synonyms: Breed, Bring, Bring about, Bring on, Catalyze, Cause, Create
antonyms: Impede, Limit, Restrict, Abolish, Demolish, Destroy

englishMeaning: To father or produce offspring, to cause or bring about. An archaic form of “begets,” typically found in older English texts like the King James Bible. synonyms: Generate, Produce, Father, Create, Cause
antonyms: Destroy, Prevent, End, Stop

antonyms: Tangle, Dirty, Mess Up, Soil, Wrinkle
examples: She brushed out her hair before going to bed. The tailor brushed out the dust from the coat. He brushed out the carpet to make it look new. Please brush out the dog’s fur after washing it.
sindhiMeaning: برش يا ڪنگهي سان ڪنهن شيءِ کي صاف ڪرڻ، مٽي يا ڌوڙ ڪڍڻ يا وارن کي سنوارڻ، اهو لفظ گهڻو ڪري وارن ڪپڙن يا قالين لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو آهي

englishMeaning: To hide, ignore, or avoid dealing with a problem, mistake, or unpleasant situation, instead of facing it honestly or solving it. To pretend something did not happen or to cover it up so that others do not notice.
synonyms: Hide the truth, Cover up, Ignore the problem, Conceal, Sweep under the carpet
antonyms: Bring to light, Admit the truth, Face the problem, Expose, Deal with openly
examples: The company tried to brush the financial mistake under the rug. Instead of fixing the problem, they just brushed it under the rug. You can’t brush the truth under the rug forever, it will come out one day. She brushed her bad behavior under the rug and acted like nothing happened.
sindhiMeaning: مسئلي کي لڪائڻ يا نظرانداز ڪرڻ، ظاهر نه ڪرڻ، ڏکيو يا شرمناڪ معاملو لڪائي ڇڏڻ، ڪنهن غلطي، مسئلي يا شرمناڪ ڳالهه کي ظاهر ڪرڻ بدران ان کي لڪائڻ يا ان تي ڳالهائڻ کان پاسو ڪرڻ تہ جيئن ٻين کي علم نہ ٿئي
urduMeaning: کسی غلطی، مسئلے یا حقیقت کو چھپانا یا نظرانداز کرنا، کسی غلطی، برائی یا مسئلے کو تسلیم کرنے کے بجائے اسے چھپانا تاکہ دوسروں کو علم نہ ہو،

englishMeaning: To revise or practice something again to become better at it.
synonyms: Review, Revise, Refresh, Relearn, Polish Up
antonyms: Forget, Neglect, Ignore, Overlook
examples: I need to brush up my English before the interview. She brushed up her driving skills after many years. The teacher advised the students to brush up their grammar. He brushed up on computer basics for the new job.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڳالهه يا صلاحيت کي ٻيهر ياد ڪرڻ يا نئين سر سکڻ

englishMeaning: To review, refresh, or improve your existing knowledge or skill in a subject that you have learned before but may have forgotten.
synonyms: Review, Revise, Refresh, Relearn, Polish Up
antonyms: Forget, Neglect, Ignore, Overlook
examples: I need to brush up on my English before the interview. She brushed up on her driving skills before taking the test. He is brushing up on history for his upcoming exam. You should brush up on your computer skills to get that job.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءَ کي ٻيهر ياد ڪرڻ يا ٻيهر مشق ڪرڻ لاءِ، جيئن ڄاڻ يا مهارت کي بهتر بڻائي سگهجي

englishMeaning: Speaking or behaving in a very direct, brief, and unfriendly way. So short and abrupt that it may seem rude, even if not intended.
synonyms: Abrupt, Blunt, Curt, Direct, Short, Rude
antonyms: Polite, Courteous, Gentle, Kind, Considerate
examples: The manager’s brusque reply made the employee feel uncomfortable. He spoke in such a brusque tone that people thought he was angry. Her brusque manners hide a very kind heart. The doctor was brusque, but he gave clear instructions.
sindhiMeaning: بي لحاظ، اوچتو، رُکڙو، بي تڪلف، ڳالهه ۾ نرمي يا لحاظ نه هجي، سڌو سنئون ڳالهه ڪرڻ بغير ڪنهن خوش اخلاقي يا نرمي جي

englishMeaning: A person or animal that behaves in a cruel, violent, or uncontrolled way. It often suggests lack of reason or compassion. Extremely cruel, violent, or savage in behavior or action.
synonyms: Savage, Beast, Bully, Ruffian, Barbarian
antonyms: Gentle person, Civilized person, Humanitarian, Kind soul
examples: He behaved like a brute during the argument. The brute force of the storm destroyed the village. No one liked him because he treated people like a brute. The guard used brute strength to open the jammed gate.
sindhiMeaning: وحشي، درندو، بي رحم ماڻهو جيڪو عقل بدران زور ۽ تشدد استعمال ڪري

englishMeaning: Related to the pleasant aspects of the countryside or rural life. Things associated with the countryside, rural scenery, or simple country life. It often evokes peaceful, pastoral, and charming rural settings.
synonyms: Pastoral, Rural, Rustic, Countryside, Country-like
antonyms: Urban, City, Metropolitan, Industrial, Cosmopolitan
examples: The artist painted a bucolic landscape with grazing sheep. They enjoyed a bucolic weekend away from the city noise. The novel depicts a bucolic life in the mountains. Her poems often celebrate bucolic scenes and country simplicity.

englishMeaning: To move slightly or make something move a little. To change one’s opinion or position slightly (usually when someone refuses to change). To give way or yield under pressure.
synonyms: Shift, Give way, Alter, Relent, Stir
antonyms: Stay, Remain, Resist, Stand firm, Hold, Persist, Refuse
examples: I pushed the door, but it wouldn’t budge. He refused to budge from his decision. The car was stuck in the mud and didn’t budge an inch. Despite all the arguments, she didn’t budge from her opinion.

englishMeaning: To reduce impact or soften effect. To protect something by lessening force. To separate and prevent conflict or damage. To store data temporarily before processing. A person or thing that reduces damage between two forces. An additional amount kept to avoid problems. Memory used to hold data temporarily. A solution that keeps pH level stable.
synonyms: Cushion, Soften, Shield, Protect, Absorb, Barrier, Reserve, Safeguard
antonyms: Expose, Intensify, Increase, Aggravate, Amplify, Exposure, Risk, Vulnerability, Danger, Pressure
examples: Trees buffer the town from strong winds. The manager tried to buffer the team from criticism. The app buffers data before playing the video. The bushes acted as a buffer against the strong wind. We added extra time as a buffer for delays. The video paused because the buffer was full. The company kept cash as a buffer during the crisis.
sindhiMeaning: اثر يا ڌڪ گهٽ ڪرڻ، ن شين وچ ۾ نرم رڪاوٽ بڻجڻ، بچاءُ لاءِ اثر گهٽ ڪرڻ، عارضي طور ڊيٽا محفوظ ڪرڻ، ٻن شين جي وچ ۾ نقصان گهٽ ڪندڙ بچاءُ، مسئلن کان بچڻ لاءِ رکيل اضافي مقدار، عارضي طور ڊيٽا رکڻ واري ياداشت، اهڙو محلول جيڪو پي ايڇ کي مستحڪم رکي، ٽولن وچ ۾ تڪرار گهٽ ڪندڙ ماڻهو
urduMeaning: اثر یا جھٹکا کم کرنا، عارضی طور پر ڈیٹا محفوظ کرنا، دو چیزوں کے درمیان نرم رکاوٹ بننا، کسی چیز کو بچانے کے لیے اثر کم کرنا، کوئی چیز جو اثر یا جھٹکے کو کم کرے، اضافی مقدار جو مشکل سے بچنے کے لیے رکھی جائے، عارضی طور پر ڈیٹا رکھنے والی میموری، ایسا محلول جو پی ایچ کو مستحکم رکھے

englishMeaning: An area or space created to separate two things and reduce conflict, risk, or pressure. A neutral or protective area between two groups, places, or situations. It helps prevent direct contact, reduces tension, or provides safety. It can be physical, social, environmental, or even emotional.
synonyms: Cushion, Barrier, Protective area, Neutral zone, Safety zone, Shield
antonyms: Direct contact, Exposure, Connection, Overlap, Integration
examples: The trees were planted as a buffer zone between the highway and the houses. The countries agreed to create a buffer zone to avoid military conflict. Keeping savings acts as a financial buffer zone during emergencies. The manager created a buffer zone in the schedule to handle delays.
sindhiMeaning: حفاظتي حد، وچ وارو علائقو بچاءُ واري جڳهه، محفوظ فاصلو، ٻن شين يا علائقن جي وچ ۾ حفاظتي يا ڌار رکڻ وارو علائقو، اهڙو وچ وارو علائقو جيڪو تڪرار گهٽ ڪرڻ حفاظت مهيا ڪرڻ يا سڌي رابطي کي روڪڻ لاءِ ٺاهيو ويندو آهي، اهو سرحدي سماجي يا ماحولياتي مقصد لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو آهي

englishMeaning: To hit repeatedly or to strike with force, especially by wind or waves. To strike or hit something repeatedly and forcefully. A meal where people serve themselves from a variety of dishes placed on a table. It can also mean a long table or counter where food is placed.
synonyms: Strike, Hit, Batter, Pound, Assail, Feast, Banquet, Self service meal, Sideboard, Food counter
antonyms: Protect, Shield, Defend, Support, Table service, Set meal
examples: We enjoyed a delicious buffet at the wedding. The hotel offers a breakfast buffet every morning. Strong winds buffeted the small boat all night. The company was buffeted by financial problems last year.

antonyms: Stay, Approach

She spent her time building castles in the air instead of taking real action.

englishMeaning: To use something as a foundation or basis to develop further. To take an existing idea, achievement, or situation and develop it further or improve it. It often implies progress based on something already established.

synonyms: Accumulate, Strengthen, Develop, Enhance

englishMeaning: To swell, stick out, or expand beyond usual limits. It is often used for objects, body parts, or even numbers and statistics. A rounded swelling or protrusion on a surface, object, or body. It can be physical, like a bulge in a wall or pocket, or figurative, like a bulge in prices or population.

englishMeaning: To limit somebody, something’s freedom, rights, power, etc. To draw a circle around another shape.

englishMeaning: The act of limiting somebody, something's freedom, rights, power, etc. Something that limits or encloses. A surrounding substance. An inscription, as around a coin or medal. Something that limits one's freedom of action or choice.

antonyms: Allowance, Freedom, Infinity, Liberation, Permission

englishMeaning: To cleverly avoid a rule, law, or difficulty, often in a way that is not straightforward or honest. To bypass an obstacle or overcome a challenge by ingenuity rather than confrontation.
synonyms: Evade, Bypass, Avoid, Sidestep, Outwit
antonyms: Obey, Confront, Face, Follow, Comply
examples: The company tried to circumvent the new regulations by creating a subsidiary abroad. She found a way to circumvent the traffic jam by taking a narrow side road. englishMeaning: An insulting term for a boy or man who is seen as weak, timid, or not traditionally masculine.

englishMeaning: In ancient times, a citadel was the strongest part of a city, often surrounded by walls. It served as the last defense point in case of invasion. Figuratively, it can describe something that protects important values or ideas.
synonyms: Fortress, Stronghold, Castle, Bastion, Fort, Keep
antonyms: Open field, Weak point, Vulnerability, Unprotected area
examples: The soldiers took refuge in the citadel when the enemy attacked. The citadel stood proudly on the hill overlooking the city. The university is regarded as a citadel of learning and wisdom. During the war, people sought safety within the walls of the citadel.
sindhiMeaning: قلعو، مضبوط قلعو، حفاظت جو هنڌ، شهر يا علائقي ۾ ٺهيل اهڙو مضبوط قلعو جيڪو دشمن کان بچاءَ لاءِ ٺاهيو ويندو آهي، مجازي طور تي، ڪو به مضبوط ادارو يا جڳهه جيڪا ڪنهن قدر يا علم جي حفاظت ڪري ٿي

englishMeaning: A reference to a source of information, or an official notice given for recognition or for a legal matter. Reference to a source used in writing or speech. An official award for bravery or achievement.  A formal notice to appear in court. Formal praise recorded in writing.

antonyms: Plagiarism, Concealment, Omission
examples: The report included a citation for every statistic. She received a citation from the governor for her service. The police issued a citation for parking in a restricted area. Always provide a citation when you use someone else's ideas.
sindhiMeaning: ڪو به ماخذ ڪتاب يا بيان جيڪو حوالو طور ڏنو وڃي، بهادري يا سٺي ڪم تي ڏنل سرڪاري ساراه، عدالت ۾ پيش ٿيڻ لاءِ ڏنل نوٽيس، لکيل حوالو، ڪتاب مان نقل ڪيل جملي جو ٽڪرو، سرڪاري واکاڻ جو دستخطي بيان، عدالتي سڏ نامه

englishMeaning: To mention something as evidence or support. To quote, refer to, or mention a source, example, rule, case, or fact in order to explain a point or support an argument. To officially call someone to appear in court or before authorities. To praise someone formally, especially for bravery or good work. To point out or list something as an example. It is often used in academic writing, legal discussions, speeches, and reports.
synonyms: Quote, Refer to, Mention, Name, Invoke
antonyms: Ignore, Overlook, Discount, Drop, Omit
examples: She cited three research papers to support her argument. The teacher asked the students to cite reliable sources in their essays. Lawyers often cite previous court cases during trials. He cited his busy schedule as the reason for not attending the meeting.
sindhiMeaning: حوالو ڏيڻ يا مثال طور ذڪر ڪرڻ، ڪنهن شخص کي عدالت ۾ طلب ڪرڻ جو حڪم ڏيڻ، ڪنهن جي ساراهه ڪرڻ يا شاباشي ڏيڻ، ڪنهن ڳالهه کي مثال طور بيان ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ڳالهه کي ثابت ڪرڻ يا وضاحت ڪرڻ لاءِ ڪتاب شخص واقعو قانون يا ڪنهن به مواد مان حوالو ڏيڻ يا مثال بيان ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: حوالہ دینا یا مثال کے طور پر ذکر کرنا، کسی شخص کو عدالت یا حکام کے سامنے پیش ہونے کا نوٹس دینا، کسی کی تعریف یا سرکاری سطح پر تحسین کرنا، کسی بات کو مثال یا ثبوت کے طور پر پیش کرنا، کسی دلیل بات یا وضاحت کو مضبوط بنانے کے لیے کسی کتاب شخص واقعے قانون یا مواد کا حوالہ دینا یا اس کا ذکر کرنا

englishMeaning: Related to a city, town, citizenship, or the duties of citizens. Something connected with a city, town, community life, public affairs, or the responsibilities and rights of citizens. It is often used for public duties, social participation, local government, and community welfare.
synonyms: Municipal, Public, Community, Civil, Local, Social
antonyms: Private, Personal, Individual, Nonpublic, Domestic
examples: Civic responsibility includes obeying laws and helping the community. The mayor spoke about improving civic services in the city. Schools should teach students about civic duties and voting rights. Her civic engagement helped bring positive change to the neighborhood.

englishMeaning: To suddenly stop talking, usually due to fear, shyness, or secrecy.
synonyms: Silence, Shut up, Stop talking
antonyms: Speak, Talk, Confess

antonyms: Allow, Tolerate, Overlook, Ignore

synonyms: Enforce, Control, Restrict, Regulate

synonyms: Be silent, Shut up, Hush

antonyms: Open, Public, Overt, Transparent, Known

Exaggerated, false, or nonsensical statements that are often used to attract attention, gain applause, or impress an audience rather than to convey truth or useful information. synonyms: Nonsense, Rubbish, Baloney, Hype, Gibberish, Bunk
antonyms: Truth, Sense, Fact, Sincerity, Honesty
examples: His speech was full of claptrap and had no real value. The advertisement used claptrap to attract customers. People quickly realized that his promises were just claptrap. She ignored the claptrap and focused on facts.

englishMeaning: A device or action used to hold things tightly together. A small object or fastener used to hold two things together, such as parts of a bag, necklace, or clothing. To grip or hold something tightly with hands or fingers. To embrace someone tightly in arms (hold closely).

antonyms: Release, Let go, Loose, Free, Unfasten
examples: She fastened the necklace with a golden clasp. The bag has a broken clasp. He clasped her hand before she left. The soldier clasped the weapon tightly in his hands.

englishMeaning: To make a loud rattling sound. To produce a sharp, repeated noise when hard objects hit each other or a hard surface. A sharp, continuous noise made when hard objects strike each other, such as dishes, tools, or shoes hitting a hard surface. It can also mean to make such a noise while moving or falling.
synonyms: Rattle, Clank, Bang, Crash, Jangle
antonyms: Silence, Quiet, Calm, Stillness
examples: The plates fell and made a loud clatter on the floor. She heard the clatter of footsteps coming down the stairs. The tools clattered as he dropped them on the table. A sudden clatter woke everyone in the room.

englishMeaning: A group of words with a subject and verb, or a section of a legal document. A group of words that usually contains a subject and a verb and forms part of a sentence. antonyms: Whole, Entire document, Main sentence
examples: The contract includes a clause about payment terms. This sentence has a dependent clause. Every clause in the agreement must be followed. The lawyer explained the meaning of each clause clearly.

englishMeaning: Fear of small or enclosed spaces. An anxiety disorder in which a person experiences intense fear or panic when in confined, crowded, or enclosed spaces. It can trigger physical symptoms like sweating, rapid heartbeat, or shortness of breath.

antonyms: Spaciousness comfort, Openness, Agoraphobia (opposite type of phobia: fear of open spaces)
examples: She could not ride in the small elevator because of her claustrophobia. His claustrophobia made it hard for him to travel on crowded trains. The doctor explained techniques to manage claustrophobia during MRI scans. Visiting the narrow cave triggered his claustrophobia.

englishMeaning: Clean living shows good character. Hygiene brings health and respect. A clean environment creates positivity. Purity and neatness reflect morality. Clean habits are signs of discipline

antonyms: Dirtiness, Untidiness, Filthiness, Uncleanliness, Negligence
examples: Our teacher always reminds us that cleanliness is next to godliness, so we should keep our classroom neat and tidy. My mother believes that cleanliness is next to godliness and makes us clean the house every weekend. englishMeaning: Something that is not clear or confusing. A situation, explanation, or statement that is confusing, obscure, or difficult to understand.
synonyms: Confusing, Unclear, Obscure, Puzzling

antonyms: Strong, Healthy, Sturdy, New, Well built

englishMeaning: To openly and strongly criticize something because you believe it is wrong, harmful, unfair, or unacceptable. It is often used in formal or public contexts such as politics, social issues, policies, or public behavior.

antonyms: Praise, Approve, Support, Commend, Applaud

englishMeaning: To convert secret or coded information into readable or understandable form. To unlock, decode, or translate encrypted information, messages, files, or data so that it can be understood. It is commonly used in computer security, communication systems, and secret codes.

antonyms: Encrypt, Encode, Conceal, Hide, Obscure
examples: The engineer decrypted the secured file successfully. Police experts decrypted the secret message quickly. The software can decrypt protected data in seconds. Scientists decrypted the ancient coded manuscript after many years.

englishMeaning: Converting coded, encrypted, or hidden information back into its original readable form. The process of unlocking or decoding protected information by using a key, password, software, or method so the original message or data can be understood. It is commonly used in computer security, banking systems, messaging apps, military communication, and digital privacy.
synonyms: Decoding, Unlocking, Interpretation, Unscrambling, Translation, Revealing, Recovery
antonyms: Encryption, Encoding, Concealment, Hiding, Locking, Scrambling
examples: The technician completed the decryption of the secured file successfully. Decryption helps users read encrypted messages safely. The police used advanced software for the decryption of hidden data. Without the correct password, decryption of the document was impossible.
sindhiMeaning: ڳجهي يا ڪوڊ ٿيل معلومات کي ٻيهر سمجهڻ جهڙي شڪل ۾ آڻڻ، ڪوڊ کولڻ، ڳجهي معلومات ظاهر ڪرڻ، محفوظ ڊيٽا کي پڙهڻ لائق بڻائڻ، لڪل پيغام سمجهڻ، انڪرپٽ ٿيل مواد کي کولڻ
urduMeaning: خفیہ یا کوڈ شدہ معلومات کو دوبارہ قابلِ فہم بنانا ہے، خفیہ کوڈ کھولنا، محفوظ معلومات کو سمجھنا، انکرپٹ شدہ ڈیٹا کو پڑھنا، پوشیدہ پیغام ظاہر کرنا، کوڈ شدہ مواد کی تشریح کرنا

englishMeaning: Strong commitment to a goal or activity. Act of devoting time, effort, or oneself to something. Formal opening statement in a book, speech, or work. Religious or ceremonial act of offering something to a sacred purpose.

antonyms: Praise, Honor, Respect, Compliment, Admire, Glorify, Appreciate
examples: The politician claimed that the newspaper tried to defame him with false allegations. Spreading fake rumors on social media can defame innocent people. He filed a case against those who attempted to defame his reputation. It is wrong to defame someone without knowing the truth.

englishMeaning: To pass waste matter from the body through the anus.  To remove solid waste from the digestive system through the anus. To empty or cleanse of impurities in a general sense. In older usage, to purify or clear something unwanted. In biology, to eliminate waste materials from an organism.
synonyms: Excrete, Eliminate, Pass stool, Void
antonyms: Retain, Constipate, Withhold

antonyms: Constipation, Retention

englishMeaning: A shortage or lack of something, especially money. Financial loss or shortfall. Lack of resources. Insufficient amount. Gap between demand and supply.

antonyms: Obey, Submit, Follow, Surrender, Comply

englishMeaning: To lose or remove water or moisture from something or someone. To cause the body or a substance to lose more water than is taken in. When the human body loses too much fluid, it becomes dehydrated and is unable to function properly. Also used in food science and industry to describe the process of removing water from food to preserve it.
synonyms: Dry out, Desiccate, Parch, Evaporate, Drain, Deplete fluids, Wither, Shrivel
antonyms: Hydrate, Moisturise, Rehydrate, Saturate, Replenish, Quench, Soak

synonyms: Scatter, Disperse, Vanish, Fade, Waste
antonyms: Collect, Gather, Accumulate, Concentrate, Preserve
examples: The crowd began to dissipate after the event ended. His nervousness dissipated once the interview started. Their energy dissipated after hours of hard work. Smoke from the fire slowly dissipated into the sky. The explanation helped dissipate their doubts. Friction causes mechanical energy to dissipate as heat.

englishMeaning: A way of living focused too much on entertainment, drinking, or luxury, often leading to moral or physical weakness. A state in which attention is scattered and not focused on serious matters. The process of spreading something over a wide area until it loses strength or concentration. Gradual weakening of emotions, anger, fear, or excitement over time.
synonyms: Waste, Squandering, Extravagance, Decay, Disappearance
antonyms: Conservation, Preservation, Saving, Accumulation, Retention
examples: His dissipation of family wealth left him bankrupt. The dissipation of heat from the engine prevents overheating. Years of dissipation affected his health badly. The dissipation of fog made the road visible again. Too much dissipation distracted him from his studies.

urduMeaning: فضول خرچی یا ضائع کرنا، آہستہ آہستہ ختم ہو جانا، عیش و عشرت میں زندگی گزارنے سے اخلاقی یا جسمانی کمزوری، ذہنی انتشار یا توجہ کا بٹ جانا، کسی چیز کا پھیل جانا اور طاقت کھو دینا، جذبات یا احساسات کا آہستہ آہستہ کم ہو جانا

englishMeaning: To mix into a liquid and become part of it. To end or break apart. To become incorporated into a liquid so that it forms a solution. To officially end or disband something like a group or partnership. To lose strength or intensity. A smooth transition where one image fades out while another fades in. A gradual blending or merging of one thing into another
synonyms: Melt, Disintegrate, Fade, Break up, Liquefy
antonyms: Solidify, Form, Build, Combine, Unite
examples: Sugar dissolves quickly in hot tea. The fog began to dissolve as the sun rose. The company decided to dissolve the partnership. His anger slowly dissolved into sadness. The director used a dissolve to move between scenes. The film opens with a slow dissolve from black.
sindhiMeaning: پگهرجڻ/ ٽٽڻ، ختم ٿيڻ/ ورهائجي وڃڻ، ڪنهن مايع ۾ ملي ڪري مڪمل طور شامل ٿي وڃڻ، آهستي آهستي ختم ٿي وڃڻ يا گم ٿي وڃڻ، ڪنهن اداري يا گروهه کي ختم ڪرڻ، حالت يا احساس جو ڪمزور ٿي وڃڻ، فلم يا وڊيو ۾ هڪ منظر جو آهستي ختم ٿي ٻئي ۾ تبديل ٿيڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ جو آهستي آهستي ٻي ۾ ملي وڃڻ

englishMeaning: To persuade someone not to do something. To convince or advise someone against doing something, usually by giving reasons or warnings so that the person changes their mind. Dissuade is commonly used in formal or advisory situations where someone tries to stop another person from making a risky or unwise decision.
synonyms: Discourage, Deter, Persuade against, Advise against, Prevent
antonyms: Encourage, Persuade, Motivate, Urge, Influence
examples: I tried to dissuade him from quitting his job. The teacher dissuaded the students from cheating in the exam. Her friends dissuaded her from traveling alone at night. The doctor dissuaded him from smoking.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي ڪنهن ڪم ڪرڻ کان روڪڻ يا منع ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ماڻهوءَ کي دليل ڏئي يا سمجهاڻي ڏئي ڪنهن ڪم ڪرڻ کان روڪڻ يا سندس ارادو بدلائڻ، هي لفظ اڪثر صلاح يا نصيحت ۾ استعمال ٿيندو آهي جڏهن ڪنهن کي غلط يا نقصان ڏيندڙ ڪم کان روڪيو وڃي

englishMeaning: To pull or twist out of shape; to give a misleading or false account of something. To change the original form, meaning, or nature of something in an inaccurate or deceptive way.
synonyms: Warp, Twist, Misrepresent, Deform, Falsify
antonyms: Clarify, Straighten, Correct, Represent accurately
examples: The mirror distorted their reflections in a funny way. The media often distorts facts to attract more viewers. Stress can distort your perception of reality. He distorted the truth to avoid taking blame.

englishMeaning: To put someone in a state of anxiety, sorrow, or difficulty. A state of extreme worry, sorrow, or physical discomfort caused by a difficult situation.
synonyms: Suffering, Anguish, Hardship, Trouble, Agony, Worry
antonyms: Comfort, Relief, Ease, Happiness, Peace
examples: She was in deep distress after hearing the bad news. The ship sent a distress signal during the storm. Financial problems distressed him greatly. The abandoned animals were in distress.

englishMeaning: Active during the day or happening every day. Relating to the daytime. Occurring every day. Animals or plants active during daylight hours. Daily recurring cycle
synonyms: Daily, Daytime, Day active, Everyday, Circadian
antonyms: Nocturnal, Night active, Nightly
examples: Humans are mostly diurnal and sleep at night. The diurnal temperature changes were significant in the desert. Many birds have diurnal feeding habits. The scientist studied the diurnal cycle of plant growth.

englishMeaning: The ability of an investment, asset, or risk to be diversified to reduce exposure. The characteristic of an investment, project, or financial portfolio that allows it to be spread across different assets, sectors, or regions to lower overall risk. It measures how effectively risks can be mitigated through diversification.
synonyms: Diversifiable nature, Spreadability, Risk-distribution potential, Portfolio flexibility
antonyms: Non-diversifiable, Concentrated, Undiversifiable, Inflexible
examples: The diversifiability of her investments allowed her to reduce potential losses. Diversifiability is key when constructing a balanced financial portfolio. Not all risks have high diversifiability; some are systemic. The company focused on diversifiability to enter multiple markets safely.

englishMeaning: Capable of being spread or varied to reduce risk or dependence. Something, especially investments, risks, or activities, that can be distributed among different options or categories to minimize potential loss or to create variety.
synonyms: Diversifiable, Spreadable, Varied, Distributable, Allocable
antonyms: Non-diversifiable, Concentrated, Fixed, Undividable
examples: The risk in this portfolio is largely diversifiable. Diversifiable investments help protect against market fluctuations. By choosing diversifiable strategies, companies reduce financial exposure. Not all risks are diversifiable; some are inherent to the industry.
sindhiMeaning: ورهايو وڃي سگهندڙ (ورڇ يا خطري کي گهٽائڻ لاءِ ورهائڻ جي قابل)، ڪنهن شيءِ کي مختلف حصن يا موقعن ۾ ورهائي سگهندڙ جيئن خطرو گهٽجي يا متنوعيت وڌي، سيڙپڪاري کي مختلف شعبن ۾ ورهائڻ سان نقصان جو امڪان گهٽجي ٿو
urduMeaning: قابلِ تقسیم یا متنوع بنانے کے قابل، کسی شے کو مختلف حصوں یا مواقع میں بانٹ کر خطرہ کم کرنا یا تنوع پیدا کرنا ممکن ہو، سرمایہ کاری کو مختلف شعبوں میں تقسیم کرنے سے نقصان کا امکان کم ہوتا ہے

englishMeaning: The process of varying products, investments, or activities to reduce risk or expand opportunities. The act of introducing variety in business, finance, agriculture, or other areas to minimize risks, increase stability, and explore multiple growth opportunities. It can involve investing in different industries, creating new product lines, or spreading resources across sectors.
synonyms: Variation, Expansion, Assortment, Spread, Heterogeneity, Multiplicity
antonyms: Uniformity, Sameness, Concentration, Specialization
examples: The company pursued diversification by entering the renewable energy market. Farmers practiced diversification by growing multiple crops instead of relying on a single one. Diversification of investments can protect your savings from market fluctuations. The restaurant’s diversification into catering helped increase its revenue.
sindhiMeaning: ڦهلاءُ، ڪاروبار يا سيڙپڪاري ۾ خطرن کي گهٽائڻ لاءِ مختلف شعبن ۾ ورڇ يا پکيڙ، پيداوار يا سرگرمين ۾ نئون انداز آڻڻ، هڪ ئي شيءِ تي ڀروسو گهٽائڻ ۽ متبادل اختيار وڌائڻ، فصلن يا وسيلن جي ورائٽي وڌائڻ، مختلف شعبن يا سرگرمين ۾ ورڇ (خطرن کي گهٽائڻ لاءِ يا موقعن کي وڌائڻ لاءِ)
urduMeaning: تنوع، مختلف شعبوں یا سرگرمیوں میں پھیلاؤ، خطرہ کم کرنے یا مواقع بڑھانے کے لیے، مختلف شعبوں یا سرگرمیوں میں پھیلاؤ تاکہ خطرہ کم ہو، پیداوار یا کاروبار میں نئے مواقع پیدا کرنا، کسی ایک چیز پر انحصار کم کرنا اور متبادل راستے پیدا کرنا، فصلوں یا سرمایہ کاری میں ورائٹی بڑھانا

englishMeaning: Varied or including many different types. Having a wide range of different elements, activities, or forms. It often implies variety in investments, skills, products, or experiences to reduce risk or broaden scope.
synonyms: Varied, Assorted, Multifaceted, Mixed, Multidimensional
antonyms: Uniform, Limited, Narrow, Specialized, Monolithic
examples: The company has a diversified portfolio of products to serve different markets. She has a diversified skill set, including writing, coding, and graphic design. Farmers are encouraged to grow a diversified range of crops to reduce risk. The investment fund is diversified, with stocks from multiple industries.
sindhiMeaning: مختلف قسمن وارو، گهڻ رخو، متنوع، جيڪو ڪيترن قسمن يا شعبن تي مشتمل هجي جهڙوڪ ڪاروبار سيڙپڪاري يا صلاحيتن ۾ تنوع پيدا ڪرڻ، طرحين طرحين جو
urduMeaning: متنوع، مختلف النوع، کئی قسموں والا، جس میں مختلف اقسام سرگرمیاں یا شعبے شامل ہوں، جیسے کاروبار سرمایہ کاری یا مہارتوں میں تنوع

englishMeaning: Something or someone that makes things more varied or introduces variety. A person, company, or tool that adds variety, reduces risk, or broadens scope in a system, business, investment, or activity. It is often used in finance, business, agriculture, or strategy.
synonyms: Varier, Broadener, Innovator, Risk-spreader
antonyms: Monopolizer, Standardizer, Concentrator, Restrictor
examples: The company acted as a diversifier by investing in multiple industries. Introducing new crops can be a diversifier for farmers facing climate risks. Mutual funds serve as diversifiers for investors. Technology has become a diversifier in traditional business models.

urduMeaning: متنوع بنانے والا، کوئی شخص یا چیز جو کسی نظام کاروبار سرمایہ کاری یا سرگرمی میں تنوع پیدا کرے خطرہ کم کرے یا دائرہ کار کو وسیع کرے، یہ لفظ مالیات کاروبار زراعت یا حکمت عملی میں استعمال ہوتا ہے

englishMeaning: Having flowers of many kinds or of different forms. Used for plants or vegetation that produce a variety of flowers differing in size, shape, color or type. It describes botanical diversity within one plant or within a group of plants. A description for ecosystems or habitats that show floral variation, often used in ecology and botany. It can also be applied metaphorically for anything showing wide floral variety.
synonyms: Variflorous, Multifloral, Many flowered, Mixed flowering, Flower diverse
antonyms: Uniflorous, Single flowered, Uniform flowering, Monofloral
examples: The garden looked diversiflorous with dozens of species blooming together. A diversiflorous meadow attracts more insects and birds. The scientist studied a rare diversiflorous shrub found in the valley. Their field became diversiflorous after years of careful restoration.

urduMeaning: ایسے پودے یا پودوں کے مجموعے کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے جن میں طرح طرح کے یا مختلف شکلوں کے پھول پائے جائیں، یہ لفظ زیادہ تر نباتیات اور ماحولیاتی مطالعات میں اس وقت استعمال ہوتا ہے جب کسی منظر یا ماحول میں پھولوں کی بہت زیادہ اقسام موجود ہوں کبھی کبھار اسے بطور استعارہ بھی استعمال کیا جاتا ہے جہاں پھولوں کی رنگا رنگی نمایاں ہو

englishMeaning: Having leaves of different shapes or types. A plant or tree that bears more than one type of leaf, showing diversity in leaf forms or shapes. Often used in botany or horticulture.
synonyms: Varied-leaved, Heterophyllous, Multi-leaved, Polymorphic leaves
antonyms: Uniform-leaved, Monophyllous, Simple-leaved
examples: The garden featured a diversifoliate tree that attracted botanists. Diversifoliate plants can adapt better to different climates. She studied the diversifoliate patterns of the tropical forest. The new park included diversifoliate shrubs for ornamental purposes.
sindhiMeaning: مختلف پنن وارو، اهڙي ٻوٽي يا وڻ جي وصف جنهن جا پن هڪجهڙا نه هوندا يعني مختلف شڪل يا قسم جا هوندا
urduMeaning: متنوع پتیوں والا، ایسے پودے یا درخت کی خصوصیت جس کے پتے مختلف شکلوں یا اقسام کے ہوں، یہ اصطلاح عام طور پر نباتات یا باغبانی میں استعمال ہوتی ہے

englishMeaning: Having leaves of different shapes. A plant with leaves that are not uniform in shape but show noticeable variety. Used in botany to describe a plant that bears leaves of varied forms on the same stem or plant. It highlights natural variation in leaf shape due to growth stage, environment, or genetic traits. synonyms: Variable leaved, Heterophyllous, Mixed leaved, Shape varied leaves
antonyms: Uniform leaved, Monomorphic, Same shaped leaves
examples: The diversifolious shrub caught the botanist’s attention during the field survey. Many aquatic plants become diversifolious as they adapt to changing water levels. urduMeaning: ایسا پودا جس کے پتے ایک جیسے نہ ہوں بلکہ مختلف شکلوں کے ہوں، یہ لفظ زیادہ تر نباتات میں پتوں کی ساخت کے تنوع کو ظاہر کرنے کے لئے استعمال ہوتا ہے، کبھی کبھی ادبی انداز میں بھی کسی ایسی چیز کے لئے بولا جاتا ہے جس میں مختلف شکلیں یا انداز پائے جائیں

englishMeaning: Shaped in various forms. Having mixed or different shapes. Something that appears in a variety of shapes, patterns or structures. It is used for objects, natural forms, designs or anything that does not follow a single uniform shape.
synonyms: Variform, Multiform, Diverse, Manifold, Heterogeneous
antonyms: Uniform, Homogeneous, Single shaped
examples: The artist used diversiform patterns to make the painting more vibrant. Coral reefs have a diversiform structure that supports many species. The museum displayed diversiform pottery from ancient cultures. The landscape was diversiform with hills, plains and rocky cliffs.

urduMeaning: کئی شکلوں والا، مختلف صورتوں پر مشتمل، وہ چیز یا شکل جو ایک جیسی نہ ہو بلکہ کئی طرح کی صورتیں رکھتی ہو، مختلف ڈھانچوں یا شکلوں کا مجموعہ، اس لفظ کا استعمال ان چیزوں کے لئے بھی ہوتا ہے جو ساخت یا شکل میں بہت مختلف ہوں، مختلف انداز کی ظاہری صورتیں رکھنا

englishMeaning: To make something more varied or add different types. To change or expand something so it includes a wider range of types, activities, products, skills or investments. It often refers to spreading risk, improving variety or broadening options.
synonyms: Vary, Broaden, Expand, Multiply, Modify

englishMeaning: Supporting the principle that all people should have equal rights, opportunities, and treatment, regardless of gender, race, or social status

synonyms: Aubergine, Brinjal, Solanum melongena
antonyms: There are no antonyms

englishMeaning: To get rid of, reject, cancel, or refuse service to someone or something. Used when something is no longer wanted or allowed. Often heard in restaurants when an item is unavailable. Can also refer to removing a person from a place or list. It is commonly used in informal American English, especially in restaurants and casual conversation.

A diagnostic technique used in medicine and neuroscience to measure and record brain wave patterns. It helps doctors study brain function and detect conditions such as epilepsy, sleep disorders, brain injuries, and other neurological problems. The test works by detecting electrical signals produced by neurons in the brain and converting them into a visual graph called an electroencephalogram.
synonyms: EEG (Electroencephalogram test), Brain wave test, Neural activity recording, Brain electricity monitoring
antonyms: There is no direct antonym
examples: The doctor ordered an electroencephalography test to check for epilepsy. Electroencephalography helps in studying brain wave patterns during sleep. The hospital used EEG to monitor the patient after a head injury. Electroencephalography revealed abnormal brain activity in the patient.

examples: The solution to the problem remained elusive. The criminal was elusive and avoided the police for months. Happiness sometimes feels elusive in busy life. She gave an elusive answer instead of speaking directly.
sindhiMeaning: مشڪل سان هٿ ايندڙ، پڪڙ ۾ نه ايندڙ، سمجهڻ ۾ ڏکيو، لڪل رهندڙ، پڪڙ کان بچندڙ، ڏسڻ ۾ ناياب، حاصل ڪرڻ ۾ ڏکيو، هٿ نه ايندڙ، پڪڙ کان بچندڙ، هٿ نه ايندڙ، نظر کان لڪل، ڌيان کان بچندڙ، صحيح طرح بيان نه ٿي سگهندڙ
urduMeaning: مشکل سے ملنے والا، گرفت میں نہ آنے والا، سمجھنے میں مشکل، چکمہ دینے والا، نظروں سے اوجھل رہنے والا، گرفت سے بچنے والا، حاصل کرنا مشکل، توجہ سے بچنے والا

englishMeaning: Event is over. Said to indicate that a performance or situation has ended and nothing more will happen. An event, discussion, or opportunity has fully finished.
synonyms: Finished, Over, Concluded
antonyms: Start, Begin
examples: The show is over, Elvis has left the building. No more questions, Elvis has left the building. The party ended, Elvis has left the building. Once the deal closed, Elvis had left the building.

englishMeaning: To preserve a corpse for funeral or scientific purposes. To protect something from decay or destruction. To keep a memory, tradition, or honor alive. To preserve by using oils, spices, or chemicals. To preserve a dead body by treating it with chemicals or other methods to slow decay. It can also mean to preserve or keep something in memory or honor.
synonyms: Preserve, Mummify, Treat, Protect, Conserve, Safeguard, Maintain, Keep
antonyms: Decay, Decompose, Rot, Destroy, Corrupt, Neglect, Spoil, Deteriorate
examples: The funeral home embalmed the body before the public viewing. Ancient Egyptians used special techniques to embalm their dead. The book embalms the memories of a forgotten generation. Historians strive to embalm important traditions through careful documentation.
sindhiMeaning: لاش کي محفوظ رکڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي خراب ٿيڻ کان بچائڻ، ياد يا روايت کي زنده رکڻ، خوشبودار تيلن يا ڪيميائي مادّن سان سنڀالڻ، لاش کي خاص دوائن يا ڪيميائي مادّن سان محفوظ رکڻ ته جيئن اها جلدي خراب نه ٿئي، مجازي معنيٰ ۾ ڪنهن ياد يا عزت کي قائم رکڻ
urduMeaning: مردہ جسم کو محفوظ کرنا، کسی چیز کو خراب ہونے سے بچانا، یاد یا روایت کو قائم رکھنا، تیل  مصالحوں یا کیمیائی مادوں کے ذریعے حفاظت کرنا، کسی مردہ جسم کو کیمیائی طریقے سے محفوظ کرنا تاکہ وہ جلد خراب نہ ہو، مجازی طور پر کسی یاد یا عزت کو محفوظ رکھنا

englishMeaning: To impose a formal ban or restriction on the export, import, or transport of goods, or on communication or activities, usually for political, economic, or security reasons.
synonyms: Ban, Restriction, Prohibition, Blockade, Moratorium
antonyms: Permission, Approval, Free trade, Lift
examples: The government imposed an embargo on oil exports to the neighboring country. The United Nations lifted the embargo after peace agreements were signed. The company faced an embargo on its products due to safety concerns. The country decided to embargo all shipments until inspections were complete.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ملڪ ڪمپني يا شخص تي واپار سامان جي منتقلي يا سرگرميون سرڪاري طور تي روڪڻ يا پابندي لڳائڻ، واپار تي پابندي
urduMeaning: کسی ملک ادارے یا شخص پر تجارتی اشیاء آمد و رفت یا سرگرمیوں کو سرکاری طور پر روکنے یا پابندی لگانے کا عمل عموماً سیاسی یا اقتصادی وجوہات کی بنا پر، تجارتی پابندی

englishMeaning: To get onto a ship or plane. To put somebody, something onto a ship or plane.
synonyms: Go aboard, Depart,
antonyms: Disembark, Arrive
examples: They embarked the troops by night.

englishMeaning: To make somebody feel shy, uncomfortable or ashamed, especially in a social situation. To place in doubt, perplexity, or difficulties. To throw into a state of self-conscious distress.
synonyms: Mortify, Bewilder
antonyms: Comfort, Cheer
examples: Her question about my life embarrassed me. The speech was deliberately designed to embarrass the PM. It embarrassed her to meet strange man in the corridor at night.

englishMeaning: To prepare or arrange for battle. To organize troops, fortifications, or defenses for fighting; to put into a state of readiness for combat or conflict.
synonyms: Fortify, Marshal, Deploy, Arrange
antonyms: Retreat, Withdraw, Disorganize, Abandon
examples: The general embattled his forces along the river. Villagers embattled their homes against the incoming storm. They embattled the city walls to withstand the attack. Leaders embattled their arguments in the debate.
sindhiMeaning: جنگ لاءِ تيار ڪرڻ، فوج يا دفاع کي ترتيب ڏيڻ، فوج يا دفاع کي ترتيب ڏيڻ، جنگ لاءِ تيار ڪرڻ، ڪنهن جاءِ کي مضبوط ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: جنگ کے لیے تیار کرنا، فوج یا دفاع کو لڑائی کے لیے منظم یا تیار کرنا، کسی جگہ کو حملے کے لیے مضبوط کرنا

englishMeaning: To fix something firmly inside another thing. To place, fix, or insert something deeply and firmly within another object, structure, idea, or system so that it becomes a permanent or natural part of it. It is also used for including media, data, or information within digital content such as a website or document.
synonyms: Insert, Fix, Implant, Ingrain, Integrate, Incorporate
antonyms: Remove, Extract, Detach, Separate, Dislodge
examples: The engineer embedded the metal rod in concrete for strength. Good values should be embedded in the education system. She embedded a video in her presentation to explain the topic. The journalist was embedded with the army during the operation.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ کي ٻي شيءِ جي اندر مضبوطي سان لڳائڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي اهڙي طرح اندر لڳائڻ يا رکڻ جو اهو ان جو مستقل حصو بڻجي وڃي، هي لفظ خيالن نظامن يا ڊجيٽل مواد کي ويب سائيٽ يا دستاويز ۾ شامل ڪرڻ لاءِ به استعمال ٿيندو آهي
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کو مضبوطی سے اندر جمانا یا شامل کرنا، کسی چیز کو دوسری چیز کے اندر اس طرح شامل یا نصب کرنا کہ وہ اس کا مستقل حصہ بن جائے، یہ لفظ خیالات کو نظام میں شامل کرنے یا ویب سائٹ میں ویڈیو اور کوڈ شامل کرنے کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے

englishMeaning: To decorate, beautify, or add extra details to something. It can also mean adding exaggerated or imaginary details to a story to make it more interesting.
synonyms: Decorate, Adorn, Beautify, Enhance, Elaborate, Antonyms
antonyms: Simplify, Plain, Reduce, Diminish, Understate
examples: She used colorful patterns to embellish the dress. The writer embellished the story to make it more exciting. The walls were embellished with traditional artwork. He tends to embellish his achievements during interviews.

englishMeaning: Decorative details, additions, or improvements that make something more beautiful, attractive, or impressive. It can also mean adding imaginative details to a story so it sounds more interesting than the original facts.
synonyms: Decoration, Ornamentation, Adornment, Enhancement, Elaboration
antonyms: Plainness, Simplicity, Bareness, Reduction
examples: The dress had beautiful embellishments made with small pearls and beads. The writer added some embellishment to the story to make it more exciting. The palace walls were famous for their artistic embellishments. His speech contained a little embellishment, but the main idea was true.
sindhiMeaning: اهڙو سينگار سجاوٽ يا اضافو جيڪو ڪنهن شيءِ کي وڌيڪ خوبصورت دلڪش يا متاثر ڪندڙ بڻائي، ڳالهه يا ڪهاڻي کي وڌيڪ دلچسپ بڻائڻ لاءِ حقيقتن ۾ اضافي تفصيل شامل ڪرڻ جو عمل
urduMeaning: ایسی سجاوٹ آرائش یا اضافہ جو کسی چیز کو زیادہ خوبصورت دلکش یا متاثر کن بنائے، یہ کسی کہانی یا بیان میں اضافی تفصیلات شامل کرنے کو بھی کہتے ہیں تاکہ وہ زیادہ دلچسپ لگے

englishMeaning: A piece of wood or coal that is not burning but is still red and hot after a fire has died. A small piece of burning or glowing coal or wood left from a fire. In a broader sense it also means a feeling or idea that still exists weakly after the main event has ended.

antonyms: Ice, Coldness, Extinction, Water
examples: The camper carefully blew on the ember to restart the fire. A single ember glowed in the fireplace long after the flames were gone. The story left an ember of hope in her heart. Even after years, an ember of anger remained inside him.

englishMeaning: To steal money or property from one’s organization or employer. To secretly take money or property entrusted to you, usually for personal use. It involves theft or misappropriation by someone in a position of trust, such as an employee, manager, or public official.
synonyms: Misappropriate, Misapply, Peculate, Misuse
antonyms: Give, Receive, Compensate, Pay, Reimburse, Return
examples: He was found guilty of embezzling $150 000 of public funds. She embezzled thousands of dollars from the charity. It was clear that funds were being embezzled but who could be doing it? He was caught embezzling money from his clients.
sindhiMeaning: ڦٻائڻ، پيسا کائي وڃڻ، ڪنهن جي ذميواري هيٺ رکيل پيسا يا مال چوري ڪرڻ خاص ڪري نوڪري يا عهدو هئڻ دوران، غبن ڪرڻ، ذميواريءَ دوران مال يا پئسا ناجائز استعمال ڪرڻ، سرڪاري يا خانگي وسيلن جو غلط استعمال ڪرڻ، ڪنهن جي ملڪيت کي پنهنجو ڪرڻ يا لُٽي وٺڻ
urduMeaning: غبن کرنا ، خیانت کرنا ، خر دبرد کرنا ، چرالینا، فراڈ کرنا، رقم چو ری کرنا، کسی شخص کا اپنی تحویل میں دی جانے والی چیز کو ذاتی استعمال کے لیے دھوکے سے ہتھیا لینا

englishMeaning: The act of stealing money that you are responsible for or that belongs to your employer. The crime of secretly taking money that is in your care or that belongs to an organization or business you work for.
synonyms: Misapplication, Misappropriation, Peculation, Fraud
antonyms: Compensation, Pay, Reimbursement, Return
examples: She was found guilty of embezzlement. They were arrested for embezzlement of company funds. He's accused of tax evasion, embezzlement, and fraud. Their embezzlement bankrupted the firm. Their embezzlement bankrupted the firm.

englishMeaning: A symbol or sign that represents an idea, quality, group, or organization. englishMeaning: A visible or living form of an abstract idea, quality, or feeling. A perfect representation of a particular trait or concept. Someone or something that shows a quality in its purest form.

englishMeaning: To hold someone closely with affection. To accept or adopt something willingly. To hug someone as a sign of love, comfort, or greeting. To accept an idea, belief, opportunity, or change with readiness and positivity. A hug or the act of holding someone closely in the arms.

The policy embraces several ideas for environmental protection. She greeted her mother with a warm embrace. Their emotional embrace showed how much they missed each other.

englishMeaning: A person who leaves their own country to live permanently in another country. A person who moves out of their native or home country with the intention of settling in another country. The word focuses on the act of leaving one’s country, not on arriving in a new one.

englishMeaning: To leave one’s own country to live permanently in another country. To move out of your native country with the intention of settling in a foreign country, usually for better living conditions, work, education, or safety.
synonyms: Move abroad, Leave one’s country, Relocate overseas, Settle abroad
antonyms: Immigrate, Return, Come back, Stay
examples: Many people emigrate to Canada for better job opportunities. His family decided to emigrate after the economic crisis. She emigrated from Pakistan to Australia ten years ago. Thousands of workers emigrate every year in search of a stable future. He emigrated from Pakistan.
sindhiMeaning: هميشه لاءِ پنهنجو ملڪ ڇڏي ٻئي ملڪ ۾ رهڻ وڃڻ، وزگار، تعليم، بهتر زندگي يا حفاظت لاءِ پنهنجو ملڪ ڇڏي هميشه لاءِ ٻئي ملڪ ۾ وڃي آباد ٿيڻ
urduMeaning: مستقل طور پر اپنا ملک چھوڑ کر کسی دوسرے ملک میں جا کر رہنا، بہتر زندگی، روزگار، تعلیم یا تحفظ کے لیے اپنا ملک چھوڑ کر مستقل طور پر کسی دوسرے ملک میں جا کر آباد ہو نا

urduMeaning: وہ عمل جس میں لوگ اپنے آبائی ملک کو چھوڑ کر کسی دوسرے ملک میں مستقل طور پر رہائش اختیار کرے، یہ عام طور پر بہتر روزگار تعلیم تحفظ یا معیارِ زندگی کے لیے ہوتا ہے

englishMeaning: Payment or salary received for work or holding a position. Money, salary, allowance, or benefits earned from employment or office. It can include wages, bonuses, perks, or any financial gain from a job.

englishMeaning: The ability to understand and share another person’s feelings, thoughts, or experiences. Feeling with someone rather than just for them, putting yourself in their place
synonyms: Compassion, Understanding, Kindness, Sensitivity, Sympathy
antonyms: Indifference, Cruelty, Apathy, Coldness, Harshness
examples: Her empathy for the poor made her volunteer at the shelter every weekend. A good leader shows empathy toward team members facing challenges. Teachers need empathy to understand their students’ emotional needs. He listened with empathy, offering comfort without judgment.
sindhiMeaning: همدردي، احساس ڪرڻ جي صلاحيت، ٻين جي جذبن ۽ احساسن کي سمجهڻ ۽ محسوس ڪرڻ جي صلاحيت، جڏهن ڪو شخص ٻئي جي تڪليف خوشي يا حالتن کي پنهنجو سمجهي ساڻس گڏ محسوس ڪري

englishMeaning: Special importance given to something. Giving extra attention, importance, or stress to a particular idea, word, or action so that it stands out clearly.

urduMeaning: کسی بات پر خاص زور، کسی خیال لفظ یا عمل پر زیادہ توجہ یا زور دینا تاکہ وہ بات نمایاں ہو جائے

englishMeaning: To give special importance to something. To give special attention. To highlight, stress, or make something more noticeable or important in speech or writing.

It happens when a line breaks before the sentence or phrase is finished, and the thought continues onto the next line. This creates a smooth flow, builds suspense, and keeps the reader moving forward.
synonyms: Run-on line, Overflow, Continuation
antonyms: End-stopped line, Complete line, Closed line
