examples: He is an epicure who travels the world to taste different cuisines. As an epicure, she only dines at the finest restaurants. The dinner party was designed to impress every epicure present. Being an epicure, he values quality over quantity in food.
sindhiMeaning: نفيس کاڌي ۽ پيتي جو شوقين ماڻهو، عيش ۽ آرام پسند ماڻهو، نفيس ذوق وارو شخص، لذيذ ۽ خاص شين جو قدر ڪندڙ، جيڪو سٺي معيار جي کاڌي پيتي ۽ ذائقي جو وڏو شوقين هجي، اهو ماڻهو نفيس شين کي پسند ڪري ٿو ۽ زندگي جي آرامده ۽ لذيذ پهلوئن مان لطف اندوز ٿئي ٿو
urduMeaning: عمدہ کھانے اور پینے کا شوقین شخص، عیش و عشرت پسند شخص، نفیس ذوق رکھنے والا انسان، لذیذ چیزوں کا قدر دان، جو عمدہ اور لذیذ کھانوں اور مشروبات کا شوقین ہو، ایسا شخص نفیس ذائقوں اور اعلیٰ معیار کی چیزوں کو پسند کرتا ہے اور زندگی کی آسائشوں سے لطف اٹھاتا ہے

englishMeaning: A sudden increase in the number of cases of a disease in a particular area or among a specific group of people. A situation in which a disease spreads quickly and affects many individuals within a community, region, or population at the same time. The term can also be used for rapid spread of non medical problems such as misinformation, crime, or social issues.
synonyms: Pandemic, Contagious
antonyms: Endemic, Enzootic
examples: Car theft is now reaching epidemic proportions. An epidemic of measles broke out, and over 200 children died. Effectively, tobacco companies will be exporting an epidemic of smoking-related diseases, the campaign suggests. The city faced an epidemic of dengue during the rainy season. Social media misinformation became an epidemic among teenagers.
sindhiMeaning: وبا، تيزي سان پکڙجندڙ بيماري ڪنهن علائقي ۾ بيماري جو اوچتو ڦهلاءُ، وڏي پيماني تي پکڙجندڙ بيماري، سماجي يا رويي واري خرابين جو تيزي سان پکڙجڻ، اوچتو ۽ وسيع پيماني تي بيماري جو ظاهر ٿيڻ، ڪنهن مسئلي جي تيزي سان وڌڻ، ڪنھن شيءِ جو معاشري ۾ بي قابو پکڙجڻ
urduMeaning: وبائی مرض، وبا، تیزی سے پھیلنے والی بیماری، کسی علاقے میں اچانک بیماری کا پھیلاؤ، کسی مسئلے کا وسیع پیمانے پر پھیل جانا، وبائی بیماری، معاشرتی یا سماجی برائی کا تیزی سے پھیلنا، غیرمعمولی اور وسیع پیمانے پر بیماری کا ظہور، بیماری یا مسئلے کی تیزی سے افزائش، کسی چیز کا معاشرے میں بے قابو پھیلاؤ

englishMeaning: A sudden clear understanding or realization. A moment when a person suddenly understands something important or sees a situation in a new and meaningful way.  An intuitive grasp of reality through something as simple as a common occurrence. In a religious sense, it refers to the manifestation of a divine being.
synonyms: Realization, Insight, Awakening, Revelation
antonyms: Confusion, Misunderstanding, Ignorance, Unawareness
examples: She had an epiphany while reading the report and finally understood the problem. His travel experience led to an epiphany about what truly matters in life. During the meeting, the solution came to her as an epiphany. The teacher’s explanation gave the students an epiphany about the concept.
sindhiMeaning: اوچتو سمجهه يا ڄاڻ جو لمحو، اهو لمحو جڏهن ماڻهو کي اوچتو ڪنهن اهم ڳالهه جي گهري سمجهه ملي ٿي يا سوچ مڪمل طور تبديل ٿي وڃي ٿي، الهامي سڃاڻپ، ناگهاني ظهور، حقيقت جو انڪشاف، تجلي، غيبي اڳڪٿي يا خبر
urduMeaning: اچانک سمجھ یا ادراک کا لمحہ، وہ لمحہ جب انسان کو اچانک کسی اہم حقیقت کی گہری سمجھ حاصل ہو جائے یا سوچ کا زاویہ بدل جائے، تجلی، وحی، انکشافِ حقیقت، نادیدہ حقیقت کا اچانک ادراک، ظہورِ قدسی

englishMeaning: Excessive watering of the eyes. A medical and rhetorical term. In medicine, it refers to excessive tearing caused by irritation, infection, or blockage of tear ducts. In rhetoric, it means repetition of a word or phrase at the end of successive sentences for emphasis.
synonyms: Tearing, Watery eyes, Excessive lacrimation, End repetition, Terminal repetition
antonyms: Dry eyes, Anaphora, Beginning repetition
examples: The patient complained of epiphora due to blocked tear ducts. Cold wind often causes temporary epiphora in winter. The poet used epiphora to give rhythm to his speech. Repeating the phrase at the end of each line is a form of epiphora.
sindhiMeaning: اکين مان گهڻو پاڻي وهڻ، اکين مان غيرمعمولي طور پاڻي وهڻ کي چيو ويندو آهي جيڪو نالين جي بندش يا اکين جي بيماري سبب ٿيندو آهي، ادبي معنيٰ ۾ جملن جي آخر ۾ ساڳيو لفظ ورجائڻ کي چيو ويندو آهي
urduMeaning: آنکھوں سے زیادہ پانی بہنا، آنکھوں سے غیر معمولی آنسو بہنے کو کہتے ہیں جو نالیوں کی بندش یا جلن کی وجہ سے ہوتا ہے، ادبی اصطلاح میں جملوں کے آخر میں الفاظ کی تکرار کو کہتے ہیں

englishMeaning: Happening in separate or disconnected parts or episodes. Something occurring occasionally or in irregular intervals rather than continuously. Often used for events, memories, or storytelling that happens in distinct segments.
synonyms: Intermittent, Irregular, Occasional, Sporadic
antonyms: Continuous, Regular, Constant, Unbroken
examples: His memory of childhood was episodic and incomplete. The TV series is episodic, with each episode telling a separate story. Rainfall in this region is episodic and unpredictable. The patient experienced episodic headaches over several months.
sindhiMeaning: قسمن ۾ ورهائيندڙ، وقفي طور ٿيندڙ، قسطوار
urduMeaning: قسط وار، وقفے وقفے سے ہونے والا، حادثاتی طور پر پیش آنے والا

englishMeaning: A rhetorical device in which the same word or phrase is repeated at the end of successive sentences or clauses.
synonyms: Epiphora, Rhetorical repetition, Terminal repetition
antonyms: Anaphora, Beginning repetition, Initial repetition
examples: We demand justice for the poor, justice for the weak, justice for all. She believed in love, lived for love, and died for love. The people wanted change in the streets, change in the homes, change in the nation. He worked with passion, spoke with passion, and led with passion.
sindhiMeaning: هڪ ادبي طريقيڪار جنهن ۾ جملي يا فقرن جي آخر ۾ ساڳيو لفظ يا فقره بار بار ورجايو وڃي
urduMeaning: ایک بلاغتی اسلوب جس میں جملوں یا فقروں کے آخر میں ایک ہی لفظ یا فقرہ بار بار دہرایا جاتا ہے

englishMeaning: A perfect example of a quality, type, or characteristic. A person or thing that represents the highest standard or embodiment of something.
synonyms: Personification, Model, Ideal, Quintessence
antonyms: Opposite, Antithesis, Counterexample
examples: She is the epitome of kindness, always helping those in need. His dedication to work is the epitome of professionalism. The Taj Mahal is considered the epitome of Mughal architecture. He is the epitome of courage in the face of danger.

englishMeaning: Mental calmness and composure, especially in difficult situations. The ability to remain emotionally stable and composed under pressure, stress, or adversity.
synonyms: Composure, Serenity, Calmness, Tranquillity, Poise
antonyms: Anxiety, Agitation, Distress, Panic, Turmoil
examples: She faced the tragedy with remarkable equanimity. His equanimity during the crisis inspired everyone around him. It takes great equanimity to remain calm during a storm. She accepted the criticism with equanimity and grace.
sindhiMeaning: ذهني سڪون ۽ پُرسڪوني، خاص طور تڪليف يا دٻاءُ جي صورتحال ۾ جذباتي استحڪام ۽ صبر
urduMeaning: ذہنی سکون اور متانت، خاص طور پر مشکل حالات میں جذباتی استحکام اور صبر و ضبط

englishMeaning: Unclear or having more than one possible meaning. Something that is ambiguous, uncertain, or open to more than one interpretation. It is often used for statements, answers, or behavior that avoid a clear commitment or definite meaning.
synonyms: Ambiguous, Vague, Uncertain, Indistinct, Dubious
antonyms: Clear, Definite, Certain, Unambiguous, Explicit
examples: His answer was equivocal, so no one understood his real opinion. The politician gave an equivocal response to avoid controversy. Her feelings about the decision were equivocal and confused. The evidence was equivocal and did not clearly prove anything.

englishMeaning: Work-lover, someone passionate about working. A person who loves work, is highly enthusiastic about working, and finds satisfaction in productivity.
synonyms: Workaholic, Industrious person, Diligent worker, Hardworking individual
antonyms: Lazy person, Slacker, Idler, Procrastinator
examples: John is an ergophile who often spends extra hours at the office. The company appreciates ergophiles because they boost overall productivity. Unlike his peers, Tom is an ergophile and finds joy in challenging projects. Being an ergophile, she volunteers for tasks that others avoid.
sindhiMeaning: ڪم جو شوقين، ڪم سان پيار ڪندڙ شخص، جيڪو ڪم ۾ دلچسپي ۽ محنت سان مصروف رهڻ پسند ڪري ٿو
urduMeaning: کام پسند شخص، کام سے محبت کرنے والا شخص، جو محنت اور کام کرنے میں خوشی محسوس کرتا ہو

englishMeaning: A person who argues merely for the sake of conflict or victory, not for truth. Relating to arguments that are intended to win rather than to reach the truth. Characterized by disputing, controversy, or argument for argument’s sake.
synonyms: Argumentative, Disputatious, Contentious, Combative, Quarrelsome, Polemical
antonyms: Cooperative, Agreeable, Conciliatory, Peaceful, Harmonious, Logical
examples: His eristic debating style won him many arguments but few friends. The discussion turned eristic when both sides stopped listening and just tried to outsmart each other. She avoided eristic conversations because they led nowhere productive. An eristic thinker enjoys challenging others, even without a clear purpose.

englishMeaning: To slowly wear away, destroy, or reduce something by natural forces like water, wind, or by gradual influence. It can refer to physical wearing of land or the slow weakening of power, trust, values, or systems.
synonyms: Blackmail, Coercion, Intimidation, Shakedown, Racket
antonyms: Charity, Donation, Gift, Voluntary payment, Generosity
examples: Heavy rain can erode the soil on hillsides. Years of corruption began to erode public trust in the government. Strong ocean waves slowly erode the coastline. Constant criticism can erode a person's confidence.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ جو آهستي آهستي ختم يا گهٽجي وڃڻ، عام طور تي پاڻي هوا يا موسم جي اثر سان زمين يا پٿر جي ڳرڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿئي ٿو، سماجي يا اخلاقي قدرن اعتماد يا اختيار جو آهستي آهستي ڪمزور ٿيڻ
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کا آہستہ آہستہ گھس جانا، کم ہونا یا ختم ہوناعموماً پانی ہوا یا موسم کی وجہ سے زمین یا پتھروں کے گھسنے کے لئے استعمال ہوتا ہے، اعتماد طاقت یا اقدار کے بتدریج کمزور ہونے کے لئے بھی بولا جاتا ہے

englishMeaning: A person who has deep knowledge gained through extensive study and reading. Someone scholarly, well educated, and intellectually refined.
synonyms: Learned, Scholarly, Knowledgeable, Intellectual, Well read, Wise
antonyms: Ignorant, Uneducated, Illiterate, Uninformed, Simple
examples: The professor is an erudite scholar known for his vast knowledge of history. She gave an erudite explanation of climate change during the seminar. His erudite writing style impressed readers around the world. The panel included several erudite thinkers from different fields.
sindhiMeaning: عالم، گهڻي علم وارو، پڙهيل لکيل ماڻهو، اهڙو ماڻهو جنهن وٽ گهڻو علم هجي ۽ مطالعي وسيلي ڄاڻ حاصل ڪئي هجي
urduMeaning: علم والا، عالم، بہت پڑھا لکھا شخص، ایسا شخص جو گہری معلومات رکھتا ہو اور مطالعہ کے ذریعے علم حاصل کیا ہو

englishMeaning: To burst out suddenly, especially with force, emotion, or activity. To explode or burst out suddenly, like a volcano or liquid. To suddenly show strong emotions like anger, laughter, or excitement. To begin suddenly, especially conflicts, protests, or noise. To break out on the skin, like rashes or pimples. To come out forcefully (lava, smoke, sound)
synonyms: Explode, Burst, Break out, Blaze up, Flare up, Detonate
antonyms: Calm down, Subside, Settle, Suppress, Contain
examples: The volcano erupted after years of silence. The crowd erupted in cheers when the team won. Violence erupted in the city after the protest. She erupted in anger when she heard the news.
sindhiMeaning: اوچتو ڦاٽڻ يا زور سان نڪرڻ، اوچتو ڌماڪي سان ڦاٽڻ جيئن آتش فشان، اوچتو جذبات ظاهر ٿيڻ، اوچتو شروع ٿيڻ خاص طور تي تڪرار، چمڙي تي داڻا يا ڦٽ نڪرڻ، اوچتو ظاهر ٿيڻ يا سرگرم ٿيڻ،
urduMeaning: اچانک پھٹ پڑنا یا زور سے نکلنا، اچانک پھٹنا جیسے آتش فشاں، اچانک جذبات ظاہر ہونا، اچانک شروع ہونا خاص طور پر جھگڑا یا ہنگامہ، جلد پر دانے یا خارش نکل آنا، اچانک ظاہر ہونا یا سرگرم ہونا

englishMeaning: To increase in intensity, seriousness, or size. To become more intense, serious, or severe. It is often used for conflicts, problems, costs, or situations that grow quickly.
synonyms: Increase, Intensify, Rise, Grow, Expand, Amplify
antonyms: Decrease, Reduce, Decline, Lower, Calm, Ease
examples: The argument began to escalate after the meeting. Prices may escalate during the holiday season. The manager stepped in before the issue could escalate. Tensions escalated between the two teams.
sindhiMeaning: تيزي سان وڌڻ، وڌيڪ سنجيده بڻجڻ، مٿين سطح تي وڃڻ، تڪرار وڌڻ، ڪنهن ڳالهه جو شدت سنجيدگي يا سطح ۾ وڌي وڃڻ، عام طور تي تڪرار مسئلو يا خرچ وڌڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو آهي
urduMeaning: تیزی سے بڑھنا، زیادہ سنگین ہونا، اونچی سطح پر جانا، تنازع بڑھ جانا، کسی صورتحال مسئلے یا تنازع کا شدت یا سنگینی میں بڑھ جانا

englishMeaning: A rise or increase in intensity, seriousness, or scale. A situation where something becomes more intense, serious, or larger in scale over time. It is often used for conflicts, prices, problems, or tensions that keep increasing.
synonyms: Increase, Rise, Intensification, Amplification, Growth, Expansion
antonyms: Reduction, Decrease, Decline, Reduction in intensity, De-escalation
examples: The escalation of prices has made life difficult for many families. There was an escalation in the conflict between the two countries. The manager tried to stop the escalation of the issue in the office. Emotional escalation during arguments can lead to misunderstandings
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن به شيءَ جو آهستي آهستي وڌڻ (خاص ڪري تڪرار قيمتن يا مسئلن ۾ شدت اچڻ)، واڌارو، شدت ۾ اضافو، ڪنهن شڪايت کي مٿي اختيارين تائين پهچائڻ يا ڪنهن معاملي کي وڌيڪ اهم سطح تي کڻڻ به آهي
urduMeaning: شدت یا اضافہ، کسی چیز کا بڑھ جانا، کسی چیز کا بتدریج بڑھ جانا (خاص طور پر جھگڑے قیمتوں مسائل یا کشیدگی میں اضافہ ہونا)، کسی شکایت کو اوپر کے افسران تک لے جانا یا کسی مسئلے کو زیادہ سنجیدہ سطح پر پہنچانا بھی ہوتا ہے

englishMeaning: A moving staircase that carries people between floors. A motor driven moving staircase found in malls, airports, stations and large buildings. It helps people travel between floors without climbing regular stairs. A system or process that increases or rises step by step, often used metaphorically. A mechanical device designed to move people efficiently in busy places.
synonyms: Moving staircase, Moving stairway, Travelator stair system, Automatic stairs
antonyms: Stairs, Ladder
examples: The mall installed a new escalator near the main entrance. The escalator stopped working, so everyone had to use the stairs. She stood on the escalator while it carried her to the second floor. The airport has several escalators to manage the heavy crowd.
sindhiMeaning: هلندڙ ڏاڪڻ جيڪي ماڻهن کي مٿين يا هيٺين منزل تي وٺي وڃي، برقي طاقت سان هلندڙ ڏاڪڻ جيڪي مسلسل هلنديون رهن ٿيون ۽ ماڻهن کي بغير ڏاڪڻ چڙهڻ يا لهڻ جي مختلف منزل تائين پهچائين ٿيون، اهڙو نظام جيڪو تدريجي طور وڌندو وڃي يا مٿي چڙهندو وڃي، اها مشين جيڪا ماڻهن کي وڏن هنڌن تي وڌيڪ آساني سان کڻي وڃي
urduMeaning: چلتی سیڑھیاں جو لوگوں کو اوپر یا نیچے منزلوں تک لے جاتی ہیں، ایک برقی چلنے والی سیڑھی جو مسلسل حرکت کرتی ہے اور لوگوں کو بغیر محنت کے مختلف منزلوں تک پہنچاتی ہے، عام طور پر شاپنگ مالز ایئرپورٹس اور بڑی عمارتوں میں ہوتی ہے،

englishMeaning: A thin slice of boneless meat, usually veal, chicken, or pork, often flattened and cooked quickly by frying or grilling. A boneless piece of meat that is sliced very thin and usually tenderized. It is commonly coated with flour, breadcrumbs, or seasoning and then fried or grilled quickly. It is popular in European cuisine, especially French and Italian dishes.
synonyms: Cutlet, Schnitzel, Thin slice of meat, Fillet slice
antonyms: Thick steak, Whole cut of meat, Bone-in meat piece
examples: I ordered a chicken escalope with fries for dinner. The chef prepared a veal escalope with lemon sauce. She prefers a lightly fried escalope over grilled meat. The restaurant is famous for its crispy pork escalope.
sindhiMeaning: گوشت جو سنهو ٽڪرو جيڪو عام طور تي چکن بيف يا ويل مان هوندو آهي ۽ ان کي تلڻ يا گرل ڪرڻ سان پچايو ويندو آهي، گوشت جو اهڙو سنهو ۽ بغير هڏي وارو ٽڪرو جنهن کي نرم ڪري مصالحا ڏئي يا ڪوٽنگ ڪري تري يا گرل ڪيو ويندو آهي (اهو يورپي کاڌن ۾ عام استعمال ٿئي ٿو)
urduMeaning: باریک کٹی ہوئی گوشت کی تہہ جو عموماً چکن بیف یا ویل کی ہوتی ہے اور تل کر یا گرل کر کے پکائی جاتی ہے، گوشت کا ایک باریک اور بغیر ہڈی والا ٹکڑا ہوتا ہے جسے نرم کر کے مصالحہ لگا کر یا کوٹنگ کے ساتھ تل کر یا گرل کیا جاتا ہے (یہ یورپی کھانوں میں بہت استعمال ہوتا ہے)

englishMeaning: A fun, daring, or adventurous act, often slightly risky or mischievous. An adventure that is exciting, bold, or slightly irresponsible. It often involves playful or mischievous behavior, something done for thrill rather than seriousness.
synonyms: Adventure, Mischief, Prank, Frolic, Exploit, Caper
antonyms: Seriousness, Obedience, Caution, Routine
examples: They went on a late-night escapade to explore the old castle. The children’s escapade caused laughter rather than trouble. His mountain-climbing escapade became the highlight of the trip. She always remembers their summer escapade with a smile.
sindhiMeaning: شرارت ڀري يا خطري واري راند جهڙو عمل، مزيدار مهم، هلڪي شرارت، جرئتمند پر بي پرواهه قدم، راند جهڙي خطري واري ڪوشش، اها ڪارروائي جيڪا ڪجهه شرارت جرئت يا خطري سان ڀرپور هجي ۽ مزيدار مهم لڳي
urduMeaning: دلچسپ یا قدرے خطرناک شرارت والا عمل، دلچسپ مہم، شرارتی حرکت، بے باکی والا عمل، ہلکی پھلکی خطرناک مہم، ایسا عمل جو مہم جوئی شرارت یا معمولی خطرے پر مبنی ہو اور مزے کے لیے کیا جائے

englishMeaning: To get free from danger or confinement. To break free from a place, person, or situation, especially from danger, control, or confinement. It can also mean avoiding something unpleasant or forgetting worries for a short time. The act of getting away or a way to get free. Running away from danger or prison. Avoiding stress, worries, or reality. Something getting out accidentally.
synonyms: Flee, Break free, Get away, Run away, Evade
antonyms: Stay, Remain, Be captured, Surrender, Be trapped
examples: The prisoner managed to escape from the jail at night. She reads books to escape from daily stress. The gas began to escape from the pipe. They found a secret escape through the tunnel.
sindhiMeaning: ڀڄي نڪرڻ، بچي وڃڻ، خطري يا قيد مان ڀڄڻ، ذهني سڪون لاءِ پري ٿيڻ، اوچتو نڪري وڃڻ، بچاءُ جو رستو، ڪنهن خطري قيد يا ڏکئي حالت مان ڀڄي نڪرڻ يا پاڻ کي آزاد ڪرائڻ، اهو پڻ ذهني طور پري ٿيڻ يا پريشانين کان بچڻ لاءِ به استعمال ٿيندو آهي
urduMeaning: بھاگ نکلنا، بچ جانا، کسی خطرے قید یا مشکل حالت سے نکل جانا یا خود کو آزاد کر لینا، یہ ذہنی طور پریشانیوں سے بچنے یا وقتی طور پر دور ہونے کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے

englishMeaning: Relating to death, judgment, and the final destiny of the soul and of humankind. Concerned with the end of the world or the ultimate climax of history. It is a term primarily used in theology and philosophy.
synonyms: Apocalyptic, Messianic, Final, Ultimate, Doomful, Prophetic
antonyms: Beginning, Historical, Generative, Initial, Prototypical, Commencing
examples: The preacher delivered an eschatological sermon about the end of days. Many ancient cultures had complex eschatological myths regarding the afterlife. The movie explores eschatological themes through a post-apocalyptic setting. His research focuses on the eschatological beliefs of medieval scholars.
sindhiMeaning: آخرت بابت، قيامت جي علم متعلق، موت ۽ فيصلي جي ڏينهن بابت، حشر جو
urduMeaning: علمِ آخرت سے متعلق، قیامت کے بارے میں، حشر سے متعلق، انجامِ کائنات کے متعلق

englishMeaning: In a manner relating to the final events in the history of the world or of humankind. It refers to the theological study of the end times, death, and judgment. This adverb describes actions or perspectives focused on the ultimate destiny of humanity.
synonyms: Apocalyptically, Terminally, Finally, Ultimately, Prophetically
antonyms: Historically, Physically, Materially, Presently
examples: The author framed his narrative eschatologically to emphasize the final judgment. The prophet spoke eschatologically about the coming of a new era. Many ancient texts are interpreted eschatologically by modern scholars. He viewed the global crisis eschatologically rather than politically.
sindhiMeaning: قيامت يا پڇاڙيءَ جي لحاظ کان، عاقبت جي حوالي سان، آخرت جي نظرئي مطابق، پڇاڙيءَ جي علم موجب
urduMeaning: قیامتی طور پر، عقبیٰ کے حوالے سے، حشر کے متعلق، انجامِ کار کے لحاظ سے

englishMeaning: The part of theology concerned with death, judgment, and the final destiny of the soul and of humankind. It is the study of 'last things' or the ultimate end of the world. Different religions have distinct eschatologies involving concepts like resurrection or nirvana.
synonyms: Doomsday theory, Belief in the end times, Finality, Revelation, Apocalypticism
antonyms: Genesis, Archeology, History, Beginning
examples: The professor specialized in Christian eschatology and the Book of Revelation. Different cultures have unique myths regarding their eschatology. Islamic eschatology involves a detailed description of the Day of Judgment. The student wrote a thesis on the eschatology of ancient Norse mythology.
sindhiMeaning: قيامت جو علم، پڄاڻيءَ جو علم، عاقبت جو علم، آخرت جو بيان
urduMeaning: علمِ قیامت، حشریات، عقائدِ آخرت، انجامِ جہاں کا مطالعہ

englishMeaning: To deliberately avoid or stay away from something. To consciously choose not to do something or to avoid something, usually because it is considered wrong, harmful, unnecessary, or undesirable. It often reflects a thoughtful or moral decision.
synonyms: Avoid, Shun, Abstain, Refrain, Reject, Give up
antonyms: Embrace, Accept, Adopt, Welcome, Indulge
examples: He decided to eschew junk food to improve his health. The writer eschewed complicated language to make the book easy to understand. She eschews gossip and prefers meaningful conversations. Many people eschew violence and choose peaceful solutions.
sindhiMeaning: ڄاڻي واڻي ڪنهن شيءِ کان پاسو ڪرڻ، رد ڪرڻ يا ڇڏڻ، ڪنهن عادت يا عمل کان پاسو ڪرڻ، پنهنجي مرضي سان ڪنهن شيءِ کان پري رهڻ، خاص طور تي جڏهن اها شيءِ غلط نقصانڪار يا غير ضروري هجي
urduMeaning: جان بوجھ کر کسی چیز سے پرہیز کرنا، ترک کرنا یا چھوڑ دینا، کسی عادت یا عمل سے بچنا، اپنی مرضی سے کسی چیز سے دور رہنا، خاص طور پر جب وہ چیز غلط نقصان دہ یا غیر ضروری ہو

englishMeaning: To accompany or guide someone for protection, courtesy, or direction. To go with someone to provide protection or show respect. To guide or lead a person to a place. A person, group, or vehicle that accompanies another for safety. In social situations, a person who accompanies someone to an event.
synonyms: Accompany, Guide, Lead, Attend, Chaperone, Companion, Guide, Attendant, Guard, Protector
antonyms: Abandon, Leave, Desert, Ignore, Neglect
examples: The guard escorted the visitors to the main hall. She was escorted home after the event. Police escorted the convoy through the city. He came as her escort to the wedding.
sindhiMeaning: ساٿ ڏيڻ يا ڪنهن کي حفاظت يا عزت سان وٺي وڃڻ، رستو ڏيکارڻ يا ڪنهن کي منزل تائين پهچائڻ، اهڙو ماڻهو يا ٽولو جيڪو ڪنهن سان گڏ هجي حفاظت لاءِ، محفل يا تقريب ۾ ساٿ ڏيڻ وارو شخص
urduMeaning: کسی کو حفاظت یا احترام کے ساتھ ساتھ لے جانا، راستہ دکھانا یا کسی کو منزل تک پہنچانا، وہ شخص یا گروہ جو حفاظت کے لیے ساتھ ہو، کسی تقریب میں ساتھ جانے والا شخص

englishMeaning: "Escribe" is a Spanish word. It comes from the verb "escribir" which means "to write" in English. It is used when someone tells another person to write something. It is commonly used as a command in Spanish. It can refer to writing a letter, message, note, book, article, or any form of text.
synonyms: Write, Record, Note, Draft, Compose, Author, Pen, Inscribe, Document, Jot down
antonyms: Erase, Delete, Ignore, Read, Forget, Remove, Omit, Destroy
examples: Please escribe your full name on the form. She escribe letters to her friend every week. The teacher asked the students to escribe a short story. He likes to escribe notes during meetings.
sindhiMeaning: لکو، تحرير ڪريو، نوٽ ڪريو، قلمبند ڪريو، عبارت لکو، دستاويز تيار ڪريو، بيان لکو، لکائي ڪريو
urduMeaning: لکھو، تحریر کرو، نوٹ کرو، قلم بند کرو، عبارت لکھو، دستاویز تیار کرو، بیان لکھو، لکھائی کرو

englishMeaning: To place money, property, or documents with a third party until certain conditions are met. A legal arrangement in which money, property, or important documents are held by a neutral third party on behalf of two other parties involved in a transaction. The third party releases the asset only after all agreed conditions are satisfied. Commonly used in real estate transactions, online purchases, business agreements, and financial dealings to protect both buyer and seller.
synonyms: Trust account, Deposit, Safekeeping, Custody, Security holding
antonyms: Direct payment, Immediate release, Withdrawal, Unsecured transfer
examples: The buyer placed the deposit in escrow until the house inspection was complete. The lawyer held the documents in escrow for both parties. The payment will remain in escrow until the service is delivered. The funds were released from escrow after all conditions were met. The company escrowed the funds until the contract was finalized. We will escrow the payment until the service is delivered.
sindhiMeaning: رقم ملڪيت يا دستاويز ٽئين ڌر وٽ شرطون پوريون ٿيڻ تائين رکڻ، امانت طور رکيل رقم يا ملڪيت جيڪا ڪنهن ٽئين ڌر وٽ رکي وڃي جيستائين شرط پوريون نه ٿين، ملڪيت يا اثاثا ورثاء لاءِ ٽئين ڌر وٽ رکيا وڃن جيستائين قانوني ضرورتون پوريون نه ٿين
urduMeaning: رقم جائیداد یا دستاویزات کو تیسرے فریق کے پاس رکھنا جب تک کہ شرائط پوری نہ ہوں، وہ رقم جائیداد یا دستاویزات جو کسی تیسرے فریق کے پاس امانت کے طور پر رکھی جائیں جب تک طے شدہ شرائط پوری نہ ہوں، جائیداد یا اثاثے وارثین کے لیے تیسرے فریق کے پاس رکھی جائیں جب تک قانونی شرائط پوری نہ ہوں

englishMeaning: Hard to understand, secretive, or for a limited audience. Likely to be understood by a small number of people with a specialized knowledge or interest. Intended to be understood by only a small number of people with specialized knowledge or interest. Something obscure, abstract, or hard to understand.
synonyms: Obscure, Mysterious, Abstract, Cryptic, Arcane, Secret, Hidden, Profound
antonyms: Clear, Obvious, Simple, Common, Popular, Accessible, Public
examples: The professor’s lecture on quantum mechanics was so esoteric that only a few students could follow it. Specialist dictionaries may be required to understand some of the more esoteric texts. His esoteric interests set him apart from his contemporaries. She has a somewhat esoteric taste in clothes.
sindhiMeaning: پوشيده، راز وارو، خاص ماڻهن لاءِ، ڏکيو سمجهڻ ۾ (اصول تقرير عقيدو وغيره)، ڳجھو، اندروني، باطني، خاص سلسلي ۾ شامل ماڻهن جو، صرف خاص ماڻهن لاءِ سمجھ جوڳو
urduMeaning: پوشیدہ، خفیہ، خاص لوگوں کے لئے مخصوص، مشکل فہم، صرف مخصوص دلچسپی کے حامل افراد کی سمجھ میں آنے والا، کسی نظام کا خفيہ پہلو

englishMeaning: Great respect and approval, a good opinion of somebody. The regard in which one is held. To respect and admire somebody, something very much.
synonyms: Admiration, Appreciation
antonyms: Abhorrence, Antipathy, Aversion, Contempt
examples: She is held in high esteem by her colleagues.  Over the years, he has earned our affection and esteem. Many of these qualities are esteemed by managers. He was esteemed as a dedicated and imaginative scholar. We esteem it a privilege to have you with us.

englishMeaning: Extremely hungry; greedy or eager for food, wealth, or gain.
synonyms: Ravenous, Voracious, Covetous
antonyms: Satisfied, Content, Generous, Full
examples: After a long day without food, the travelers were esurient and ready to eat anything. The esurient businessman wanted more profits, even at the cost of ethics. Children came esurient to the dinner table after playing outside all day. His esurient eyes looked at the dessert table with uncontrollable desire.
sindhiMeaning: ڀوڪيو، تمام گهڻو خواهشمند يا لالچ ۾ مبتلا، هڙي خواهش جيڪا ضرورت کان وڌيڪ هجي
urduMeaning: بھوکا، لالچی، حریص، ایسی خواہش جو ضرورت سے زیادہ ہو

englishMeaning: Without an end, Existing or continue for ever, Happening often & seeming never to stop
synonyms: Everlasting, Permanent, Immortal
antonyms: Sempiternal, Ephemeral, Mortal
examples: She's an eternal optimist (=She always expects that the best will happen). I am tired of your eternal arguments. Women try to look eternally young.

englishMeaning: Something very delicate, refined, or light that seems too perfect for this world. It can refer to physical appearance, music, beauty, atmosphere, or even a person’s manner that feels heavenly or spiritual rather than earthly.
synonyms: Delicate, Heavenly, Angelic, Light, Airy, Spiritual
antonyms: Earthly, Heavy, Solid, Harsh, Coarse
examples: The bride looked ethereal in her white dress. The singer’s voice had an ethereal quality that touched everyone’s heart. A soft mist gave the mountains an ethereal appearance. The painting captured an ethereal light that made the scene magical.
sindhiMeaning: نهايت نازڪ، هلڪو يا آسماني جهڙو، غير زميني، پاڪيزه، اها اهڙي خوبصورتي يا ڪيفيت بيان ڪري جيڪا دنياوي کان وڌيڪ روحاني لڳي
urduMeaning: نہایت نازک، ہلکا یا آسمانی سا، چیز یا کیفیت جو بہت نازک، لطیف، پاکیزہ یا آسمانی محسوس ہو، یہ ایسی خوبصورتی یا ماحول کو ظاہر کرتا ہے جو دنیاوی سے زیادہ روحانی لگے

englishMeaning: Polite and proper behavior in social or professional situations. A set of rules or accepted behavior in society, organizations, or specific situations that show respect, good manners, and proper conduct.
synonyms: Manners, Politeness, Decorum, Propriety, Courtesy
antonyms: Rudeness, Impoliteness, Bad manners, Disrespect
examples: You should learn table etiquette before attending a formal dinner. Good telephone etiquette creates a positive impression. He showed excellent etiquette during the meeting.

englishMeaning: The study of the origin and history of words and how their meanings have changed over time. The branch of linguistics that explores where words come from, how they were formed, and how their spelling, pronunciation, and meaning have evolved over time. It often traces words back to older languages such as Latin, Greek, Arabic, Sanskrit, or other root languages.
synonyms: Word origin study, Linguistic history, Word history, Origin of words
antonyms: Modern usage only, Current meaning study, Contemporary language use
examples: The etymology of the word “school” comes from the Greek word scholē, meaning leisure or learning. Studying etymology helps students understand the deeper meaning of words. The teacher explained the etymology of “alphabet” during the lesson. Many English words have interesting etymology from Latin and French origins.
sindhiMeaning: لفظن جي اصل ۽ انهن جي تاريخي تبديلين جو مطالعو، اهو علم جنهن ۾ لفظن جي اصل/ انهن جي ٺهڻ ۽ وقت سان گڏ انهن جي معنيٰ / اچار ۽ لکڻ ۾ ٿيندڙ تبديليون پڙهجن، هي علم گهڻو ڪري قديم ٻولين جهڙوڪ لاطيني يوناني عربي يا سنسڪرت تائين لفظن جي پاڙن کي ڳولي ٿو
urduMeaning: الفاظ کی اصل اور ان کی تاریخی تبدیلیوں کا علم، وہ علم جس میں الفاظ کی اصل/ ان کی تشکیل اور وقت کے ساتھ ان کے معنی/ تلفظ اور ہجے میں آنے والی تبدیلیوں کا مطالعہ کیا جاتا ہے، یہ اکثر قدیم زبانوں جیسے لاطینی یونانی عربی یا سنسکرت تک الفاظ کی جڑوں کا سراغ لگاتا ہے

englishMeaning: A man who has been castrated, especially in the past, often employed in royal courts to guard women or serve in special roles. A male whose reproductive organs have been removed or rendered inactive. Historically, eunuchs were often trusted servants in royal households, particularly assigned to guard harems or serve queens because they were considered safe and loyal. In a broader or figurative sense, the term can also refer to a man who lacks power, vitality, or masculinity.
synonyms: Castrated man, Impotent man, Court servant, Chamberlain
antonyms: Virile man, Strong man, Potent male
examples: In ancient kingdoms, a eunuch was often appointed to guard the royal harem. The king trusted the eunuch with important responsibilities in the palace. Some historical records describe eunuchs as powerful advisors. He was mocked as a eunuch because he failed to show courage in difficult situations.
sindhiMeaning: کدڙو، هيجڙو، نامرد، خصي ڪيل مرد خاص طور تي جيڪو بادشاهن جي درٻار ۾ خدمتون انجام ڏيندو هو
urduMeaning: ہیجڑا، خواجہ سرا، کھسرا،خصی کیا گیا مرد خاص طور پر وہ جو بادشاہوں کے دربار میں خدمات انجام دیتا تھا

englishMeaning: To put an animal or person to death painlessly, especially to relieve suffering from an incurable or painful disease. It is often called “mercy killing.”
synonyms: Mercy kill, Put to sleep, Put down, End suffering humanely, Assist in dying
antonyms: Revive, Resuscitate, Save, Preserve life
examples: The veterinarian decided to euthanize the dog to end its suffering. The hospital obtained consent to euthanize the terminally ill patient. It was a difficult choice for the family to euthanize their old cat. Some countries have strict laws about when a doctor can euthanize a patient.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن بيمار زخمي يا ناقابلِ علاج جانور يا انسان کي آرام سان موت ڏيڻ جيئن کيس وڌيڪ تڪليف نه ٿئي، رحم واري موت ڏيڻ، اهو عمل اخلاقي طبي ۽ انساني همدردي جي بنيادن تي ڪيو ويندو آهي
urduMeaning: کسی شدید بیمار یا ناقابلِ علاج انسان یا جانور کو آرام سے موت دینا تاکہ وہ مزید تکلیف نہ اٹھائے، ایک ایسا طبی عمل جس کا مقصد تکلیف کو ختم کرنا ہو نہ کہ ظلم

englishMeaning: To avoid something intentionally, especially by using cleverness or trickery. To escape or avoid something (law, responsibility, danger) by cleverness or trick. To avoid answering a question directly. To stay away from something unpleasant or difficult. To avoid capture or punishment.
synonyms: Avoid, Escape, Dodge, Elude, Shirk, Sidestep
antonyms: Face, Confront, Accept, Meet, Acknowledge
examples: The thief tried to evade the police. She evaded my question about her salary. The company evaded paying taxes for years. He evaded responsibility for the mistake.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ کان هوشياري سان بچڻ يا نڪرڻ، سوال کان پاسو ڪرڻ، ذميواري يا خطري کان بچڻ، چڪمو ڏيڻ، گرفتار ٿيڻ يا سزا کان بچڻ، ڳالهه کي ٽارڻ، ذميواري کان پاسو ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: کسی چیز سے جان بوجھ کر بچنا یا چکمہ دینا، سوال کا سیدھا جواب نہ دینا، قانون ذمہ داری یا خطرے سے بچ نکلنا، گرفتاری یا سزا سے بچ جانا، بات کو گھما پھرا کر جواب دینا، فرض یا ذمہ داری سے پہلو تہی کرنا

englishMeaning: Avoiding something such as a question, duty, or responsibility. The act of escaping or avoiding a duty, question, rule, or problem, often in a clever or indirect way. It may also refer to avoiding taxes, laws, or responsibilities.
synonyms: Avoidance, Escape, Dodging, Circumvention, Elusion
antonyms: Confrontation, Acceptance, Compliance, Admission, Facing
examples: The politician’s answer sounded like evasion rather than a clear response. His constant evasion of responsibility annoyed the whole team. The thief managed evasion by hiding in the crowded market. The government is taking strict action against tax evasion.
sindhiMeaning: ٽال مٽول، گسائڻ، بهانو ڪرڻ يا لنوائڻ جو عمل، گول مول جواب، حيلو بهانو، بچڻ يا پاسو ڪرڻ، ڪنهن سوال ذميواري يا قانون کان هوشياري سان بچڻ يا ٽالڻ، ذميواري کان پاسو ڪرڻ، ٽيڪس يا قانون کان غير قانوني بچاء
urduMeaning: ٹال مٹول، حیلہ بازی، بچ نکلنے کا عمل، بچ نکلنا ، عذر، ذمہ داری یا قانون سے چالاکی سے بچ نکلنا یا جواب دینے سے گریز کرنا، خطرے یا گرفت سے بچ نکلنا، ٹیکس یا قانون سے غیر قانونی بچاؤ

englishMeaning: Avoiding giving a direct answer or response. A person, reply, or behavior that tries to avoid giving clear or honest information. It often involves indirect answers, changing the topic, or hiding the truth.
synonyms: Avoiding, Indirect, Vague, Elusive, Dodging, Unclear
antonyms: Direct, Honest, Clear, Straightforward, Open
examples: He gave an evasive answer when asked about the missing money. The politician remained evasive during the interview. She was evasive about her plans for the future. His evasive behavior made everyone suspicious.
sindhiMeaning: سڌي جواب کان بچڻ وارو، ذميواري کان بچڻ وارو، غير واضح يا اڻ سڌو، سوال کان پاسو ڪندڙ، ڳالهه کي گول ڪندڙ، اهو لفظ اهڙي ماڻهو جواب يا روئيي لاءِ استعمال ٿئي ٿو جيڪو سڌو سنئون جواب ڏيڻ کان پاسو ڪري ۽ ڳالهه کي گول ڪري يا لڪائي
urduMeaning: سیدھا جواب دینے سے بچنے والا، ذمہ داری سے بچنے والا، غیر واضح یا مبہم، سوال سے بچنے والا، بات گھمانے والا، یہ لفظ ایسے شخص جواب یا رویے کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے جو صاف اور سیدھا جواب دینے سے گریز کرے بات کو گھمائے یا حقیقت چھپائے

englishMeaning: The day or evening before an important event or festival. Evening before a festival or holiday. A poetic or literary word for evening or the time before night. The beginning of something or the moment before an important change. Also the first woman in the Bible.
synonyms: Evening, Nightfall, Preceding day, Vigil
antonyms: Morning, Dawn, Daybreak, Beginning of the day
examples: The family gathered together on the eve of the festival. The country was on the eve of an important election. Many people attend church services on Christmas Eve. The scientist made a discovery on the eve of his retirement.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن خاص ڏينهن يا عيد کان اڳ واري شام، ادبي انداز ۾ شام يا رات شروع ٿيڻ کان اڳ وارو وقت، مذهبي روايت موجب حضرت آدم عليه السلام جي زال ۽ دنيا جي پهرين عورت، ڪنهن نئين دور يا واقعي جي شروعات کان اڳ وارو وقت

englishMeaning: A possible event or situation that may happen in the future. A possible outcome or circumstance that might occur, especially one that people prepare for or consider in planning. It often refers to uncertain situations that could arise later.

antonyms: Certainty, Impossibility, Improbability, Assurance

sindhiMeaning: هنگامي صورتحال، امڪاني صورت، نتيجو، اِتفاق، امڪان، اهڙو ممڪن واقعو جيڪو اڳتي هلي ٿي سگهي، اهڙو امڪاني حال يا واقعو جيڪو مستقبل ۾ پيش اچي سگهي، ماڻهو گهڻو ڪري اهڙين حالتن لاءِ اڳواٽ منصوبابندي ڪندا آهن

antonyms: Immediately, Instantly, Promptly, At once
examples: She hopes to get a job on the local newspaper & eventually work for it. After many attempts, she eventually solved the difficult puzzle. word: Every cloud has a silver lining
englishMeaning: Even in difficult or bad situations, there is always something positive or hopeful.
synonyms: Hope, optimism
antonyms: Hopelessness
examples: Although she lost her job, she soon realized that every cloud has a silver lining when she found a better opportunity. The long power outage was frustrating, but every cloud has a silver lining; the neighbors spent time together and built stronger friendships.

englishMeaning: Every situation has both good and bad aspects. Nothing in life is completely good or completely bad. Every situation, decision, or person has advantages and disadvantages. We should understand both sides before judging.
synonyms: Look at both sides of the picture, Every situation has pros and cons, There are two sides to every story, Nothing is one-sided
antonyms: One-sided view, Biased opinion, Partial judgment, Narrow thinking
examples: Losing a job feels bad, but it can also open doors to better opportunities, Every coin has two sides. Social media connects people, but it can also waste time, Every coin has two sides. Moving to a new city is difficult, but it brings new experiences, Every coin has two sides. Exams are stressful, but they help students improve knowledge, Every coin has two sides.

englishMeaning: To break or come apart physically. To lose control emotionally or mentally. To stop functioning properly or completely fail. To become weak, disorganized, or destroyed.
synonyms: Break down, Collapse, Fall apart, Crumble, Disintegrate, Shatter, Lose control
antonyms: Hold together, Remain strong, Stay calm, Endure, Persevere
examples: After hearing the sad news, she completely fell to pieces. The old bridge fell to pieces after years of neglect. When the company lost its main investor, the whole project fell to pieces. He tried to stay strong, but during the speech he fell to pieces.
sindhiMeaning: ٽڪرا ٽڪرا ٿي وڃڻ، ڪمزور ٿي وڃڻ، قابو وڃائي ڇڏڻ، مڪمل طور ناڪام ٿي وڃڻ

englishMeaning: To be included within a particular category, group, or classification. To belong to or be classified as part of a specific group, law, rule, or category. To come under the influence or control of something or someone.
synonyms: Belong to, Be classified
antonyms: Exclude, Escape
examples: This case falls under the category of fraud. This topic falls under the subject of psychology. His actions fall under criminal behavior. The city falls under federal jurisdiction. Many young people fall under the influence of social media.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن درجي، قانون، قاعدي يا ضابطي ۾ شامل ٿيڻ يا ڪنهن جي اثر، ڪنٽرول يا اثر هيٺ اچڻ
urduMeaning: کسی خاص زمرے قانون یا ضابطے کے تحت آنا، کسی کے اثر و اختیار میں آ جانا

englishMeaning: To attack suddenly or violently. To turn one’s attention to something suddenly. To come upon or happen to someone unexpectedly (for example a burden or duty). To start eating something eagerly.
synonyms: Assault, Strike, Charge, Seize, Pounce on, Come upon, Happen to
antonyms: Defend, Protect, Avoid, Withdraw, Ignore, Neglect
examples: The soldiers fell upon the enemy camp at night. The responsibility of caring for the family fell upon his shoulders. The hungry travelers fell upon the food as soon as it arrived. His eyes fell upon an old photograph on the table.

englishMeaning: To fail to keep up with others in progress, work, or performance. To move slower than others, fail to make progress at the same rate, or not complete something on time.
synonyms: Lag, Trail, Delay
antonyms: Keep up, Advance, Progress
examples: He fell behind in rent. The runner fell behind the group. She fell behind in her studies after being sick for a month. If you don’t practice regularly, you’ll fall behind the others. The company fell behind on its payments. He fell behind because he didn’t understand the new topic.
sindhiMeaning: پوئتي رهجي وڃڻ، رفتار ۾ گهٽ هجڻ، ٻين جي ڀيٽ ۾ پوئتي رهجي وڃڻ، ڪم يا پڙهائي ۾ رفتار گهٽ هجڻ يا وقت تي ڪجهه مڪمل نه ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: پیچھے رہ جانا، سست پڑ جانا، کسی چیز کو مقررہ وقت پر مکمل نہ کرنا

englishMeaning: Capable of making mistakes. Describes a person, system, or belief that is not perfect and can be wrong or make errors
synonyms: Imperfect, Error prone, Mistaken, Unreliable
antonyms: Infallible, Perfect, Flawless, Unerring
examples: Even experienced doctors are fallible and can make mistakes. Humans are fallible, which is why learning never stops. The plan failed because it was designed by fallible judgment. He admitted that his memory is fallible under pressure.
sindhiMeaning: غلطي ڪرڻ جي صلاحيت رکڻ وارو، اهڙو شخص يا شيءِ جيڪا مڪمل نه هجي ۽ ان مان غلطي ٿيڻ جو امڪان هجي

englishMeaning: The negative results or consequences of an event or action. The side effects, aftereffects, or repercussions following an event, especially one that is harmful or controversial. It can also literally mean radioactive particles that settle after a nuclear explosion.
synonyms: Aftereffect, Consequence, Repercussion, Result, Outcome, Side effect
antonyms: Benefit, Advantage, Gain, Success, Blessing
examples: The political scandal caused widespread fallout within the party. Many people were affected by the economic fallout of the pandemic. Scientists measured the radioactive fallout after the test. The decision had serious fallout for the local community.
sindhiMeaning: نتيجا، اثر، ڪنهن واقعي يا ڪارروائي کان پوءِ ٿيندڙ منفي اثر يا نقصان خاص ڪري ته اهو ڪاوڙ يا نقصان پهچائيندڙ هجي، ريڊيو ايڪٽو ذرات جو ڇنڊڇاڻ پڻ چئبو آهي
urduMeaning: نتیجہ، اثر، کسی واقعے یا کارروائی کے بعد پیدا ہونے والے منفی نتائج یا اثرات خاص طور پر نقصان دہ یا متنازعہ اثرات، نیوکلیئر دھماکے کے بعد موجود ریڈیائی ذرات

englishMeaning: An act that is done to mislead people by making it appear that someone else did it. A deceptive action in which a person, group, or country carries out an act but makes it look as if another person, group, or country is responsible. This term is often used in politics, war, intelligence, media discussion, and security matters. Its purpose is usually to confuse people, create blame, justify retaliation, or gain support for a certain action.
synonyms: Deception, Frame-up, Set-up, Hoax operation, Disinformation tactic, Cover operation, Staged attack
antonyms: Truth, Honesty, Open action, Direct responsibility, Transparency, Genuine act
examples: The analyst warned that the attack might be a false flag intended to blame a rival group. Some historians study whether certain incidents were planned as false flag operations. The report found no evidence that the event was a false flag. Spreading unverified claims about a false flag can create confusion and fear.
sindhiMeaning: اهڙو عمل جيڪو ماڻهن کي ڌوڪي ۾ رکڻ لاءِ ڪنهن ٻئي جي نالي سان ڪيو وڃي، اهڙو فريب وارو عمل جنهن ۾ ڪو ماڻهو ٽولو يا ملڪ پاڻ ڪو ڪم ڪري ٿو پر اهڙو ڏيک ڏئي ٿو ڄڻ اهو ڪنهن ٻئي ڪيو هجي، هي لفظ گهڻو ڪري سياست جنگ جاسوسي سلامتي ۽ ميڊيا جي بحثن ۾ استعمال ٿيندو آهي، ان جو مقصد عام طور ماڻهن کي گمراهه ڪرڻ الزام ڪنهن ٻئي تي وجهڻ بدلي يا ڪارروائي لاءِ جواز پيدا ڪرڻ يا ڪنهن خاص مقصد لاءِ حمايت حاصل ڪرڻ هوندو آهي
urduMeaning: ایسا عمل جو دھوکا دینے کے لیے اس طرح کیا جائے کہ لگے یہ کسی اور نے کیا ہے، ایک فریب پر مبنی عمل جس میں کوئی شخص گروہ یا ملک خود کوئی کارروائی کرتا ہے لیکن ایسا ظاہر کرتا ہے جیسے یہ کسی اور نے کی ہو، یہ اصطلاح زیادہ تر سیاست جنگ خفیہ کارروائیوں سلامتی اور میڈیا کی بحث میں استعمال ہوتی ہے، اس کا مقصد عموماً لوگوں کو گمراہ کرنا الزام کسی اور پر ڈالنا جوابی کارروائی کے لیے جواز پیدا کرنا یا کسی خاص مقصد کے لیے حمایت حاصل کرنا ہوتا ہے

englishMeaning: To make false or incorrect. To lie about or alter information. To deliberately alter information, documents, or facts to make them untrue or misleading. It can also mean misrepresenting the truth in statements, records, or evidence.
synonyms: Forge, Fabricate, Misrepresent, Doctor, Alter
antonyms: Verify, Confirm, Authenticate, Validate, Prove true
examples: He tried to falsify his academic records to get the job. The company was accused of falsifying financial statements. She falsified her signature on the contract. Politicians sometimes falsify data to support their claims.

englishMeaning: A writing style, alphabet, or set of characters that someone already knows or recognizes. Something written in a way that feels ordinary, known, or understandable. Can also be used figuratively for a “pattern” or “narrative” someone has seen before.
synonyms: Common pattern
antonyms: Unexpected event
examples: The old manuscript was written in a familiar script, so the historian could easily read it. Children learn faster when they read in a familiar script before moving to new styles. The letter was in a familiar script, reminding me of my grandmother’s handwriting. For Urdu speakers, Nastaliq is the most familiar script compared to Roman Urdu.

englishMeaning: A severe shortage of food that causes widespread hunger and suffering among people, often due to drought, war, crop failure, or economic crisis.
synonyms: Starvation, Hunger, Scarcity, Food shortage, Dearth
antonyms: Abundance, Plenty, Sufficiency, Surplus
examples: The country faced a terrible famine after years of drought. Thousands of people migrated to the city to escape the famine. Relief organizations provided food aid to famine-affected areas. Famine not only destroys lives but also weakens the economy.
sindhiMeaning: قحط، ڏڪار، اهڙي حالت، جڏهن کاڌي پيتي جي شيئن جي سخت کوٽ هجي، ۽ ماڻهو بک، بيمارين ۽ بدحالي جو شڪار ٿين
urduMeaning: قحط، ایسی حالت جب کھانے پینے کی اشیاء کی شدید کمی ہو جائے اور لوگ بھوک و افلاس کا شکار ہوں

englishMeaning: To suffer from extreme hunger or to make someone very hungry. To experience severe hunger due to lack of food or to cause someone to suffer from extreme hunger. It emphasizes an intense state of starvation rather than just ordinary hunger.
synonyms: Starve, Hunger, Deprive, Malnourish
antonyms: Feed, Nourish, Satisfy, Fill
examples: The prisoners were famished after days without food. The famine caused many villages to famish. He felt famished after the long hike. The neglected pets were famished and weak.

englishMeaning: To move or spread inward toward a central point. In computer science or electronics: the number of input signals or connections going into a single component (like a logic gate). To gather people, things, or energy toward one point or area.
synonyms: Gather in, Close in
antonyms: Scatter, Spread out, Disperse
examples: After the performance ended, the audience began to fan in toward the exit. The soldiers fanned in to secure the central area. In this circuit, the logic gate has a high fan-in capacity. As the rain started, the tourists fanned in under the shelter.

englishMeaning: To spread out or move in different directions from a single point, similar to how the ribs of a fan open outward.
synonyms: Disperse, Scatter
antonyms: Gather, Assemble
examples: The police officers fanned out across the field to search for clues. The crowd fanned out as the concert ended. He fanned out the cards on the table for everyone to see. The rescue teams fanned out in different directions after the earthquake.
sindhiMeaning: پکڙجڻ، ڦهلجڻ، منتشر ٿيڻ، هڪ هنڌ کان مختلف طرفن ۾ پکڙجي وڃڻ

englishMeaning: Everywhere. From long distances and close by. Refers to places both far away and nearby. Often used to express wide coverage or people from many places. In all directions, including distant and close places.
synonyms: All around
antonyms: Nowhere, Locally only, In one place
examples: People came from far and near to see the festival. His fame spread far and near because of his honesty. The news was heard far and near. They searched far and near for the lost child.

englishMeaning: Over a large area or distance, everywhere. in many different places.
synonyms: Broadly
antonyms: Limited
examples: His fame spread far and wide. The news of his success spread far and wide. People came from far and wide to see the festival. Her fame reached far and wide across the country. They searched far and wide for the missing child.

englishMeaning: A type of comedy that uses exaggeration, ridiculous situations, and absurd characters to make people laugh. It can also mean something that is so badly organized, false, or ridiculous that it seems like a joke.
synonyms: Comedy, Mockery, Absurdity, Sham, Joke, Ridiculousness, Travesty
antonyms: Seriousness, Reality, Tragedy, Sincerity
examples: The play was a farce filled with silly misunderstandings and exaggerated acting. The trial was a complete farce; justice was never served.

englishMeaning: Silly or unreasonable, often in a way that is humorous. Something ridiculous, absurd, or laughably foolish, often like a farce (a type of comedy where events are exaggerated and nonsensical).
synonyms: Absurd, Ridiculous, Preposterous, Laughable, Comical, Nonsensical
antonyms: Serious, Sensible, Reasonable, Logical
examples: The meeting turned into a farcical display of shouting and confusion. Such a farcical situation could never happen in Germany. It was a farcical trial. It is preposterous, ridiculous, almost farcical. The whole situation has become farcical. There were farcical scenes at the meeting.

englishMeaning: A release of gas from the bowels through the anus, often making a sound or smell. (informal, humorous). To release gas from the bowels through the anus.
synonyms: Emit gas
antonyms: There are no antonyms
examples: He accidentally farted in the classroom and everyone laughed. A loud fart broke the silence during the meeting. Children often find fart jokes funny. He tried to hold in a fart during the lecture.

englishMeaning: To attract and hold someone’s attention strongly. To charm or enchant someone.  To make someone very curious. To strongly attract interest or admiration. To capture someone’s interest or attention so deeply that they feel attracted, curious, or amazed. It often involves a sense of charm, beauty, or mystery.
synonyms: Attract, Captivate, Charm, Enchant, Intrigue
antonyms: Bore, Repel, Disinterest, Dull, Disgust
examples: The magician fascinated the audience with his amazing tricks. She is fascinated by ancient history and cultures. The child was fascinated by the colorful butterflies. His story fascinated everyone in the room.

englishMeaning: A lifestyle that is full of excitement, luxury, and pleasure but often careless or risky.
synonyms: Recklessness
antonyms: Simplicity
examples: He spent his youth in fast living and never saved any money. Fast living can lead to health problems and regret later in life. Many celebrities are known for their fast-living lifestyle. She gave up fast living and chose a peaceful, simple life.
sindhiMeaning: جلدي، شوخ ۽ عياش زندگي، جيڪا مزن ۽ خرچ سان ڀرپور هجي پر گهڻي دير قائم نه رهي

englishMeaning: Hard to satisfy. Showing refinement or delicacy in taste. Sensitive to imperfections. Very attentive to detail, meticulous, or hard to please. Showing excessive care about cleanliness or correctness. Demanding, particular, or critical.
synonyms: Meticulous, Picky, Fussy, Exacting, Particular
antonyms: Careless, Unconcerned, Sloppy, Indifferent, Easygoing
examples: She is fastidious about her appearance and always dresses perfectly. The chef was fastidious when it came to plating the dishes. He is fastidious in checking every detail of the report before submission. Fastidious readers often notice even minor mistakes in a book.

englishMeaning: Almost no possibility. it’s an ironic way to express hopelessness or disbelief about something happening. (Used to show strong doubt or disbelief that something will happen),
synonyms: No chance, Hardly possible, Not likely, Impossible, Slim chance
antonyms: Good chance, High possibility, Likely, Certain, Definite
examples: You think he’ll lend you money? Fat chance!. Fat chance of getting tickets for that concert, it’s been sold out for weeks!. They said they would apologize, fat chance of that happening!. Fat chance he’ll finish the work on time; he hasn’t even started yet!.
sindhiMeaning: بي اميد ٿيڻ، امڪان نه هجڻ، نه ٿيڻ جهڙو ڪم (جڏهن ڪنهن ڳالهه ٿيڻ جو ڪو امڪان نه هجي يا اهو ممڪن نه لڳي)

englishMeaning: Causing death or leading to serious failure or disaster. Something that results in death or causes very serious and irreversible damage. It can also mean something that leads to a complete failure or major negative outcome, especially in decisions or mistakes.
synonyms: Deadly, Lethal, Mortal, Destructive, Dangerous, Catastrophic, Harmful
antonyms: Harmless, Safe, Benign, Protective, Non-lethal
examples: The accident was fatal for the driver. A fatal mistake in the experiment ruined the results. Lack of safety measures can lead to fatal injuries. The doctor confirmed the disease could be fatal if untreated.
sindhiMeaning: موتمار، تباه ڪند، قاتل، نحس، مھلڪ، جيوگھاٽڪ، ھلاڪت خيز، اهڙو عمل يا حالت جيڪا موت جو سبب بڻجي يا وڏي تباهي آڻي، اهو لفظ ان وقت به استعمال ٿئي ٿو جڏهن ڪا غلطي يا فيصلو مڪمل ناڪامي جو سبب بڻجي
urduMeaning: جان لیوا، مہلک، تباہ کن، ایسا عمل یا حالت جو موت کا سبب بنے یا کسی بڑے نقصان یا ناکامی کا باعث ہو، یہ لفظ عام طور پر خطرناک یا مہلک صورتحال کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے

englishMeaning: A  person who believes that everything is decided by fate and cannot be changed. Someone who thinks that events in life are already decided by fate, destiny, or a higher power. Such a person may believe that human effort cannot change what is meant to happen. Sometimes, a fatalist accepts problems passively because he or she thinks, “Whatever has to happen will happen”.
synonyms: Determinist, Predestinarian, Believer in destiny, Believer in fate, Necessitarian, Defeatist, In some contexts, Resigned person, In some contexts
antonyms: Believer in free will, Non fatalist, Optimist, In some contexts, Activist, In some contexts, Self determined person, Free thinker, In some contexts, Person who believes in personal choice
examples: He is a fatalist who believes that no one can escape destiny. As a fatalist, she accepted the loss without trying to change the situation. The old man was not a planner, but a fatalist who trusted fate completely. A fatalist may think that success and failure are already written in life.
sindhiMeaning: تقدير پرست، قسمت تي يقين رکندڙ ماڻهو، اهڙو ماڻهو جيڪو سمجهي ٿو ته زندگيءَ جا واقعا اڳواٽ تقدير ۾ لکيل آهن، هو مڃي ٿو ته انسان جي ڪوشش به قسمت کي بدلائي نٿي سگهي، ڪڏهن ڪڏهن اهڙو ماڻهو مشڪلاتن کي خاموشيءَ سان قبول ڪري وٺندو آهي ڇو ته هن جي نظر ۾ جيڪو ٿيڻو آهي اهو ضرور ٿيندو
urduMeaning: تقدیر پرست، قسمت پر یقین رکھنے والا شخص، وہ شخص جو یہ سمجھتا ہے کہ زندگی کے واقعات پہلے سے تقدیر میں لکھے ہوئے ہیں، وہ مانتا ہے کہ انسان کی کوشش بھی قسمت کو نہیں بدل سکتی، کبھی کبھی ایسا شخص حالات کو خاموشی سے قبول کر لیتا ہے کیونکہ اس کے خیال میں جو ہونا ہے وہ ہو کر رہے گا

englishMeaning: Believing that all events are fixed by fate and cannot be changed by human actions. A fatalistic person thinks that whatever happens in life is already decided by destiny, luck, or fate, and people cannot avoid or change it. This attitude may cause a person to accept situations without trying to improve them.
synonyms: Pessimistic, Resigned, Defeatist, Passive, Destiny-bound, Doom-minded
antonyms: Optimistic, Hopeful, Determined, Confident, Self-reliant, Proactive
examples: He became fatalistic after losing his job several times. Her fatalistic attitude stopped her from trying again. Many people felt fatalistic during the difficult economic crisis. The old man was fatalistic and believed that everything happens for a reason.
sindhiMeaning: قسمت تي ڀروسو ڪندڙ، تقدير کي حتمي سمجهندڙ، اهو خيال ته زندگي جون سڀ ڳالهيون اڳواٽ مقرر ٿيل آهن ۽ انسان انهن کي تبديل نٿو ڪري سگهي، تقدير پسند، قسمت جو پابند، حالتن کي اڻٽار سمجهندڙ، تبديلي کان نااميد سوچ وارو
urduMeaning: قسمت پرست، تقدیر کے آگے بے بس سمجھنے والا، یہ یقین رکھنا کہ ہر چیز پہلے سے لکھی ہوئی ہے اور انسان اسے بدل نہیں سکتا ، تقدیر پسند، قسمت کے تابع، بے اختیار سوچ رکھنے والا، حالات کو بدلنے سے ناامید

englishMeaning: Extreme tiredness resulting from mental or physical exertion or illness. It also refers to the weakening of a material caused by repeated stress. It describes a state where one's capacity for work is significantly reduced.
synonyms: Exhaustion, Weariness, Lethargy, Lassitude, Burnout
antonyms: Energy, Vigor, Refreshment, Liveliness, Strength
examples: She was suffering from severe fatigue after the long journey. Metal fatigue was identified as the primary cause of the bridge's failure. The soldiers were overcome by heat and fatigue during the drill. Chronic fatigue can be a symptom of various underlying health issues.
sindhiMeaning: ٿڪ، ماندگي، لورا، بيزاري، مانداڻو، ذهني يا جسماني ٿڪاوٽ، ڪم جي زيادتي سبب ٿڪجڻ.
urduMeaning: تھکان، تھکاوٹ، ماندگی، بیزاری، محنت و مشقت کے باعث ہونے والی کمزوری۔

englishMeaning: Something that is not genuine but is made to imitate or resemble the real thing. It is commonly used for materials, fashion, design, or behavior that copies something authentic.
synonyms: Fake, Artificial, Imitation, Synthetic, Mock
antonyms: Genuine, Real, Authentic, Original, Natural
examples: She wore a jacket made of faux leather. The room had a faux marble finish on the walls. His faux confidence was easy to detect. They decorated the house with faux flowers.
sindhiMeaning: جيڪي اصل نه هجن پر اصل جهڙيون ڏسڻ يا محسوس ٿيڻ لاءِ ٺاهيون وڃن، گهڻو ڪري ڪپڙن فرنيچر سينگار يا روين لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو آهي
urduMeaning: جو اصلی نہ ہوں مگر اصل جیسی دکھائی دینے یا محسوس ہونے کے لیے بنائی جائیں، یہ لفظ عموماً کپڑوں ڈیزائن آرائش یا رویے کے لیے بولا جاتا ہے

englishMeaning: An action, remark, or behavior that is socially awkward, improper, or tactless, often causing embarrassment.
synonyms: Mistake, Blunder
antonyms: Politeness, Courtesy
examples: Forgetting her guest’s name was a real faux pas. Wearing sneakers to the wedding was a fashion faux pas. He committed a faux pas by interrupting the speaker. Making jokes at the funeral would be a serious faux pas.

englishMeaning: To try to please somebody by praising them or paying them too much attention. To seek attention and admiration (from) by cringing and flattering. To show affection in a solicitous or exaggerated way usually with over. A deer less than one year old. A light yellow-brown color.
synonyms: Fuss, Drool, Toady
antonyms: Despise, Disdain, Scorn
examples: He seemed unaware of the girl’s fawning admiration. Why is everybody fawning over him as if he were a national hero? People fawn over you when you're famous. The fawn ran to the top of the ridge.

englishMeaning: To give someone excessive praise or attention, often to gain favor.
synonyms: Flatter, Adulate
antonyms: Ignore, Insult
examples: She fawns over her boss all the time. Don’t fawn over celebrities. The students fawned over their teacher. He dislikes people who fawn over others.
sindhiMeaning: چاپلوسي ڪرڻ، وڌي چڙهي تعريف ڪرڻ، ڪنهن کي خوش ڪرڻ لاءِ بنا ضرورت جي مهرباني ڏيکارڻ
urduMeaning: خوشامد کرنا، ضرورت سے زیادہ تعریفیں کرنا، کسی کو خوش کرنے کے لیے بڑھ چڑھ کر پیش آنا

englishMeaning: Showing excessive flattery or praise to gain favor. Acting overly submissive or obedient. Trying to please someone in an insincere way. Behaving like a servant to impress someone.
synonyms: Kowtowing, Obeisant, Obsequious, Sycophantic, Toadyish
antonyms: Unsubmissive, Unservile, Sincere
examples: The assistant gave a fawning smile to impress the boss. His fawning behavior made everyone uncomfortable. She spoke in a fawning tone to gain special treatment. The employee was criticized for his fawning attitude.
sindhiMeaning: چاپلوسي ڪندڙ، حد کان وڌيڪ خوشامد ڪندڙ، راضي ڪرڻ لاءِ جهڪندڙ، غلامي جهڙو رويو اختيار ڪندڙ
urduMeaning: خوشامدی، حد سے زیادہ تعریف کرنے والا، چاپلوس، خوش کرنے کے لئے جھکنے والا

englishMeaning: To disturb the composure of someone. To disconcert or cause to feel confused or worried. To make someone feel nervous or uneasy, typically by something unexpected. To affect the confidence or self-possession of a person. It is often used in negative sentences (e.g., 'not fazed').
synonyms: Abash, Bewilder, Daunt, Disconcert, Dismay, Fluster, Perturb, Rattle, Unnerve, Upset
antonyms: Calm, Comfort, Compose, Encourage, Help, Soothe, Hearten
examples: She was so confident that the difficult questions did not faze her at all. Even though the dog barked loudly, the little boy wasn't fazed. The sudden change in the schedule did not faze the experienced manager. High pressure situations rarely faze professional athletes. He seemed completely unperturbed, as if nothing could faze him.
sindhiMeaning: گهٻرائڻ، پريشان ڪرڻ، حيران ڪرڻ، بي آرام ڪرڻ، حواس خطا ڪرڻ، ذهني طور متاثر ڪرڻ، ڪنهن کي سندس پراعتماديءَ تان هٽائڻ يا منجهائڻ. ڪنهن اهڙي ڳالهه يا واقعي سبب جنهن سان طبيعت ۾ مونجهارو پيدا ٿئي.
urduMeaning: پریشان کرنا، گھبرانا، حواس باختہ کرنا، ہمت پست کرنا، بے چین کرنا، الجھن میں ڈالنا۔ کسی شخص کے سکون یا خود اعتمادی کو کسی ناگوار یا غیر متوقع واقعے سے متاثر کرنا۔

englishMeaning: The state of being bothered, worried, or disturbed by something unexpected. It describes a person who has lost their calm or focus due to an external pressure. It is the past participle form acting as an adjective.
synonyms: Daunted, Disconcerted, Nonplussed, Rattled, Perturbed
antonyms: Disturbed, Rattled, Agitated, Unconfident, Flustered
examples: She looked slightly fazed by the criticism she received. He remained unphased even though everyone else felt fazed by the news. The new intern felt fazed by the complexity of the software. I was a bit fazed when the audience started shouting.
sindhiMeaning: گھٻرايل، پريشان ٿيل، حواس باخته، منجهيل، پريشان حال.
urduMeaning: گھبرایا ہوا، پریشان، بدحواس، مضطرب، حواس باختہ۔

englishMeaning: The state or quality of being possible, practical, or able to be done successfully. The likelihood that a plan, idea, or project can be carried out effectively. An assessment of whether something can be achieved given available resources, time, and conditions. Often used in business and engineering studies to evaluate proposed projects before implementation.
synonyms: Practicality, Possibility, Viability, Workability, Practicability, Achievability
antonyms: Impracticality, Impossibility, Inviability, Unworkability
examples: The engineers studied the feasibility of building a bridge over the river. A feasibility report must be submitted before the project starts. The committee doubted the feasibility of the new education plan. We are conducting a feasibility study for the proposed solar power plant. The feasibility of the idea depends on the available budget.
sindhiMeaning: ممڪن هجڻ، عمل ۾ اچڻ جي صلاحيت، ڪنهن منصوبي جي قابل عمل هجڻ جي حالت، اهو جائزو ته ڪو ڪم ٿي سگهي ٿو يا نه، ڪنهن رٿا جي عملي طور تي ٿي سگهڻ جي ڪيفيت، ممڪنيت
urduMeaning: ممکن ہونا، قابل عمل ہونا، کسی منصوبے کے عملی طور پر ممکن ہونے کی حالت، یہ جائزہ کہ کوئی کام ہو سکتا ہے یا نہیں، کسی تجویز کے قابل عمل ہونے کی کیفیت، امکانیت

englishMeaning: Capable of being done, accomplished, or carried out successfully. Possible to do easily or conveniently under the given circumstances. Likely to work or to be effective in practice. Reasonable and likely to succeed. Used for plans, ideas, solutions, or projects that can realistically be put into practice.
synonyms: Possible, Practical, Viable, Workable, Achievable, Realistic, Doable
antonyms: Impossible, Impractical, Unworkable, Unrealistic, Unachievable
examples: Is it feasible to complete this project within a month? The plan seems feasible if we get enough funding. Solar power is now a feasible alternative to conventional energy. We must find a feasible solution to the traffic problem. The proposal is feasible but requires careful planning.
sindhiMeaning: ممڪن، قابل عمل، عملي طور تي ٿي سگهڻ جوڳو، اهڙو منصوبو يا رٿا جيڪا حقيقت ۾ پوري ٿي سگهي، ڪارگر ۽ مناسب، اهڙو ڪم جيڪو موجوده حالتن ۾ ٿي سگهندو هجي
urduMeaning: ممکن، قابل عمل، عملی طور پر ہو سکنے والا، ایسا منصوبہ یا تجویز جو حقیقت میں پوری ہو سکے، کارگر اور مناسب، ایسا کام جو موجودہ حالات میں کیا جا سکے

englishMeaning: In a way that is possible or practical. Refers to doing something in a manner that can realistically be achieved or carried out given the circumstances, resources, or conditions.
synonyms: Practically, Realistically, Viably, Achievable
antonyms: Impractically, Impossibly, Unfeasibly, Unrealistically
examples: We could feasibly finish the project by Friday if everyone works extra hours. The plan seems risky but feasibly achievable. It is not feasibly possible to travel across the desert without proper supplies. She argued that the budget could feasibly cover all necessary expenses.
sindhiMeaning: ممڪن طور تي، قابلِ عمل طور تي، مناسب طور تي، ٿي سگهي ٿو
urduMeaning: ممکنہ طور پر، عملی طور پر، حقیقت میں، انجام دینے کے قابل

englishMeaning: A large or special meal, especially for a lot of people and to celebrate something. To eat a large amount of food with great pleasure. To enjoy some unusual pleasure or delight.
synonyms: Banquet, Buffet
antonyms: Deficiency, Inadequacy
examples: The evening was a real feast for music lovers. The women were busy preparing the wedding feast.
sindhiMeaning: دعوت، ضيافت، طعام کارائڻ، عرس، ميلو، خوشيءَ جو ڏينهن، مجلس
urduMeaning: تہوار، جشن

englishMeaning: Waste matter discharged from the bowels. Solid or semisolid excretory matter eliminated from the digestive tract through the anus. It consists of undigested food, bacteria, cells, and waste products. It is a key indicator in medical diagnostics and environmental studies.
synonyms: Stool, Excrement
antonyms: Intake, Ingestion
examples: The doctor tested the patient’s feces. The doctor collected a feces sample for testing. Farmers often use animal feces as natural fertilizer. Proper disposal of human feces is crucial for sanitation. Scientists studied the feces of wild animals to understand their diet.
sindhiMeaning: گندگي، فضلو، پاخانو، گوبر، گهڻو گندو مواد
urduMeaning: فضلہ، پاخانہ، گندہ مواد

englishMeaning: Weak, lacking strength (physical or mental). Without force, effectiveness, or convincing power. Frail or faint in intensity (sound, effort, light, etc).
synonyms: Weak, Frail, Fragile
antonyms: Strong, Robust
examples: He gave a feeble attempt to lift the box. He was too feeble to lift the box. The argument was feeble and unconvincing. A feeble light shone through the window.
sindhiMeaning: ڪمزور، ناتوان، بيوس، هلڪو، اهڙو دليل يا ڳالهه جيڪا مضبوط نه هجي، اهڙي روشني يا آواز جيڪا مدهم ۽ بيجان هجي، جيڪو جسماني يا ذهني طاقت ۾ ڪمزور هجي

englishMeaning: To gain strength, energy, advantage or benefit from something, especially negative emotions or situations.
synonyms: Exploit, Depend
antonyms: Avoid, Ignore
examples: Some people feed off drama. The media feeds off scandals. They feed off each other’s energy. Parasites feed off their hosts. Some rumors feed off fear and uncertainty. The company feeds off the demand for quick online shopping.
sindhiMeaning: طاقت يا فائدو حاصل ڪرڻ، تيار ٿيڻ يا ڪنهن ڳالهه تي دارومدار رکڻ، حالت، احساس يا ٻئي ماڻهو جي عمل مان فائدو يا طاقت حاصل ڪرڻ (جانور يا انسان کاڌي مان توانائي حاصل ڪن)
urduMeaning: فائدہ اٹھانا، طاقت حاصل کرنا، کسی چیز پر انحصار کرنا یا اس سے فائدہ اٹھانا، کسی حالت، جذبے یا صورتِ حال سے طاقت یا فائدہ حاصل کرنا، کسی چیز سےخوراک یا توانائی حاصل کرنا

englishMeaning: To eat or live on a particular type of food. To use something as a source. To eat or get nourishment from something. It can also mean to gain strength, energy, or motivation from a particular thing or situation.
synonyms: Consume, Nourish
antonyms: Starve, Reject
examples: Lions feed on other animals. The project feeds on innovation. The fire feeds on oxygen. They feed on hope.

englishMeaning: To make someone eat more to become healthier or stronger. To become tired, annoyed, or bored with something unpleasant or repetitive.
synonyms: Fatten, Nourish
antonyms: Starve, Deprive
examples: She’s trying to feed up her son. They feed up the animals before winter. He was fed up before training. The doctor said to feed him up. I’m fed up with this terrible weather. She’s fed up with doing all the work alone.
sindhiMeaning: وڌيڪ خوراڪ ڏيڻ، طاقت لاءِ کاڌو کارائڻ، تنگ اچڻ، بيزار ٿيڻ، دل ڀرجي وڃڻ
urduMeaning: موٹا کرنا، زیادہ کھلانا، طاقت کے لیے خوراک دینا، تنگ آنا، اکتا جانا، بیزار ہونا

englishMeaning: To feel sad or unhappy. To experience sadness, low mood, or emotional heaviness, often without a clear reason or because of disappointment, loneliness, or stress
synonyms: Feel sad, Feel down, Feel low, Be unhappy, Be depressed lightly
antonyms: Feel happy, Feel cheerful, Feel joyful, Be in high spirits, Feel upbeat
examples: She felt blue after missing her family for so long. I always feel blue when it rains all day. He was feeling blue because his plans did not work out. Music helps me when I start to feel blue.
sindhiMeaning: اداس محسوس ڪرڻ، دل ۾ اداسي، مايوسي يا دل ڀرجي وڃڻ جو احساس، ڪڏهن بغير ڪنهن خاص سبب جي
urduMeaning: اداس محسوس کرنا، دل کی اداسی، مایوسی یا دل گھبرانے کا احساس، اکثر تنہائی یا پریشانی کی وجہ سے

englishMeaning: To feel unimportant or embarrassed. Describes emotional discomfort when someone feels inferior or ashamed.
synonyms: Feel inferior, Feel ashamed
antonyms: Feel important, Feel confident
examples: His words made me feel small. She felt small after the criticism. I felt small in front of the experts. He tried not to make others feel small.

englishMeaning: To understand the current mood, trends, or situation of a group, place, or activity. Being aware of what is really happening in a particular situation. It involves sensing opinions, emotions, or changes in a group, society, market, or environment. It is often used in leadership, business, media, and social contexts.
synonyms: Understand the mood, Gauge the situation, Read the room, Stay in touch, Be aware
antonyms: Be unaware, Misjudge the situation, Ignore reality, Be out of touch
examples: A good leader must feel the pulse of the people before making decisions. Journalists try to feel the pulse of society through interviews and reports. The company regularly surveys customers to feel the pulse of the market. Teachers should feel the pulse of their students to improve learning.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ يا حالتن جي موجوده حالت رجحان يا احساس کي سمجهڻ، حالتن کان واقف رهڻ، عوامي راءِ کي سمجهڻ، تبديلي جي رخ کي محسوس ڪرڻ، حقيقت سان جڙيل رهڻ
urduMeaning: کسی صورتحال ماحول یا لوگوں کے موجودہ رجحان اور کیفیت کو سمجھنا، حالات سے باخبر رہنا، عوامی رائے کو سمجھنا، تبدیلی کے رخ کو محسوس کرنا، حقیقت سے جڑے رہنا

englishMeaning: To touch someone in a sexual or inappropriate way (informal, often negative).
synonyms: Grope, Touch, Fondle
antonyms: Respect, Ignore
examples: He was accused of feeling up a colleague. She complained that someone felt her up. Don’t feel up others. The man was arrested for feeling up a passenger.

englishMeaning: To have the energy, strength, or confidence to do something.
synonyms: Manage, Cope
antonyms: Avoid, Refuse
examples: I don’t feel up to going out tonight. Do you feel up to hiking? She didn’t feel up to talking. He feels up to working again.

englishMeaning: To feel sad, unhappy, or depressed.
synonyms: Depressed
antonyms: Cheerful
examples: After hearing the sad news, she was feeling blue all day. He often feels blue when he is away from his family. Rainy days sometimes make people feel blue without any reason. She tried to cheer up her friend who was feeling blue after the exam results.

englishMeaning: To pretend that you have a particular feeling or that you are ill, tired, etc. To give a false appearance of. Make believe with the intent to deceive.
synonyms: Postulate, Dissemble, Simulate, Bluff
antonyms: Tell Truth, Be Honest, Be True
examples: He survived the massacre by feigning death. She feigned sleep to avoid having to answer. He feigned sickness so he wouldn’t have to go to school. He feigned that he was not feeling well so that he could leave the party early.
sindhiMeaning: ايجاد ڪرڻ، خيال ڪرڻ، مڪر ڪرڻ، پنهنجو ٺاهڻ، بهانو ڪرڻ، ٻيائي يا ٺڳي ڪرڻ، مڪر عُذر يا حيلي بهاني کان ڪم وٺڻ، ڍونگ ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: جوڑنا، گھڑنا، بنانا، ایجاد کرنا، بہانا بنانا، حیلہ کرنا

englishMeaning: A structure (usually made of wood, wire, or metal) that encloses an area, marking a boundary. A means of protection or separation. To avoid giving a direct answer, or to argue in a clever way. A person who buys and sells stolen goods.
synonyms: Barrier, Wall, Enclosure
antonyms: Opening, Gap
examples: They built a fence around the garden. The farmer built a fence around his field. She fenced off the garden to protect the flowers. The politician kept fencing with reporters’ questions.
sindhiMeaning: باڙو، ڪاٺ، لوهي تار يا سرن جي ٺهيل ديوار يا حد بندي، جيڪا ڪنهن جاءِ کي گهيرڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿئي، حد يا روڪاوٽ جو نشان، اهڙو جواب ڏيڻ جيڪو سڌو نه هجي يا ڳالهه کي ٽار
urduMeaning: باڑ، لکڑی، تار یا دیوار سے بنی ہوئی چیز جو کسی زمین یا علاقے کو گھیرنے کے لیے استعمال ہو، کسی چیز یا جگہ کی سرحد یا حد بندی، سوال کا براہِ راست جواب دینے سے بچنا یا چالاکی سے بحث کرنا

englishMeaning: To defend or protect oneself. To take care of oneself without help (manage, survive). To ward off, repel, or resist.
synonyms: Defend, Resist, Protect
antonyms: Surrender, Yield
examples: He had to fend for himself in the city. He had to fend off the attackers. After losing his job, he had to fend for himself. She skillfully fended off difficult questions.

englishMeaning: To take care of yourself without help from anyone else. To manage your own needs or survive independently.
synonyms: Manage alone, Be independent, Sustain oneself
antonyms: Depend on others, Eely on support, Need assistance, Be looked after
examples: After his parents died, he had to fend for himself at a young age. The refugees had to fend for themselves in the wilderness. When you move to a new city, you learn to fend for yourself. She’s strong enough to fend for herself without anyone’s help.

englishMeaning: To defend yourself or protect something from an attack, problem, or unwanted situation, To avoid or resist something harmful or unpleasant.
synonyms: Defend, Repel, Resist, Ward off, Avoid, Prevent, Protect against
antonyms: Attract, Invite, Allow, Welcome
examples: He tried to fend off the dog with a stick. The company managed to fend off bankruptcy through a new investment. She wore a mask to fend off the flu. The politician fended off his critics with a strong explanation.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن حملي، تڪليف، تنقيد يا خطري کان بچائڻ، پاڻ بچائڻ، خطرو ٽارڻ، حملو روڪڻ
