englishMeaning: Literacy, of a flam or candle, to burn in unsteady way, long curved channel of metal, plastic under edge of roof carrying away water
synonyms: Drain
antonyms: Congeal
examples: The line of intersection forming a descending gutter which runs to the outlet.

englishMeaning: An intense fear of women. A psychological condition in which a person has an irrational, persistent, and overwhelming fear of women. This fear may cause anxiety, panic, avoidance behavior, and difficulty in social or professional interactions.
synonyms: Fear of women, Female related phobia, Specific social phobia involving women
antonyms: Confidence with women, Comfort around women, Social ease with women
examples: His gynophobia made it difficult for him to speak to female colleagues. Therapy helped her brother manage his gynophobia over time. Gynophobia can affect personal relationships if left untreated. The psychologist explained that gynophobia is different from simple shyness.
sindhiMeaning: عورتن جو شديد خوف، هڪ ذهني حالت جنهن ۾ ماڻهو کي عورتن کان غير منطقي ۽ تمام گهڻو خوف محسوس ٿئي جيڪو پريشاني ۽ سماجي مسئلا پيدا ڪري سگهي ٿو
urduMeaning: عورتوں کا شدید خوف، ایک نفسیاتی حالت جس میں کسی شخص کو عورتوں سے غیر منطقی اور مستقل خوف ہوتا ہے جس کی وجہ سے گھبراہٹ اور سماجی مشکلات پیدا ہو سکتی ہیں

englishMeaning: A person who wanders or roams from place to place. To travel or roam from place to place.
synonyms: Nomad, Wanderer, Rover, Vagabond, Traveller
antonyms: Settler, Resident, Homebody, Permanent inhabitant
examples: The old stories described a gypsy family traveling across many countries. She had a gypsy spirit and loved exploring new places every year. The festival included music inspired by traditional gypsy culture. He lived like a gypsy, moving from town to town for work.
sindhiMeaning: خانه بدوش، رولو قوم، جوڳي ماڻهو، هڪ هنڌ کان ٻئي هنڌ گهمندڙ ماڻهو، آزادي پسند مسافر طبيعت وارو ماڻهو
urduMeaning: خانہ بدوش، مسلسل سفر کرنے والا شخص، آزاد مزاج اور گھومنے پھرنے والا انسان

englishMeaning: To train or condition a person or animal to become familiar and comfortable with a situation, environment, or activity through repeated exposure. It can also mean to adapt mentally or physically to something over time.
synonyms: Accustom, Adapt, Condition, Familiarize, Inure
antonyms: Alienate, Unsettle, Disorient, Disturb, Shock
examples: Parents should habituate children to healthy eating habits early in life. The trainer habituated the dog to loud noises. It takes time to habituate yourself to a new work environment. Soldiers are habituated to strict discipline during training.
sindhiMeaning: عادي بڻائڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ سان مانوس ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: عادی بنانا، کسی چیز کا خوگر کرنا

englishMeaning: An inherited disorder in which the blood’s ability to form clots is impaired. This happens because of the absence or low levels of clotting factors, leading to prolonged bleeding even from minor injuries.
synonyms: Bleeding disorder, Coagulation disorder
antonyms: Normal blood clotting, Hemostasis
examples: The boy was diagnosed with haemophilia at an early age. People with haemophilia must avoid activities that could cause injury. Treatment for haemophilia often includes injections of clotting factor. Haemophilia can be life-threatening if not managed carefully.
sindhiMeaning: هڪ جينياتي بيماري جنهن ۾ رت صحيح نموني جمڻ ۾ ناڪام ٿئي ٿو جنهن سبب ٿورو يا گهڻو زخم به گهڻو رت وهڻ لڳي ٿو
urduMeaning: ایک موروثی مرض جس میں خون کا جمنا متاثر ہوتا ہےجس کے نتیجے میں معمولی چوٹ بھی زیادہ خون بہا سکتی ہے

englishMeaning: A medical condition where the blood does not clot properly. Someone with deficiency in clotting factors, which makes even minor injuries lead to excessive bleeding. The term can also describe traits or things related to this condition.
synonyms: Bleeder, Clotting disorder patient, Blood disorder patient
antonyms: Healthy blood clotter, Non-haemophiliac
examples: The haemophiliac required careful medical supervision after a small cut. He learned how to manage life as a haemophiliac. Being a haemophiliac made him cautious about contact sports. Advances in medicine have improved treatment options for haemophiliacs.
sindhiMeaning: اهڙو ماڻهو جنهن ۾ رت آساني سان نه ڄمندو آهي، رت وهڻ واري بيماري ۾ مبتلا ماڻهو، اهڙو شخص جنهن کي رت ڄمائڻ واري علاج جي ضرورت هجي، اهڙو مريض جيڪو گهڻي رت وهڻ جي خطري ۾ هجي
urduMeaning: ایسا شخص جس میں خون صحیح طرح جمتا نہیں ہے، خون بہنے کی بیماری میں مبتلا شخص، ایسا فرد جسے خون جمانے کے علاج کی ضرورت ہو

englishMeaning: To greet or acclaim someone enthusiastically. To call out to attract attention, like stopping a vehicle. To come from a particular place. Small balls or pellets of ice that fall from the sky during a storm. A greeting or salute. To greet, salute, or praise someone with respect or excitement.
synonyms: Greet, Welcome, Acclaim, Call, Summon, Salute, Ice pellets
antonyms: Ignore, Dismiss, Reject, Avoid
examples: Large hail damaged many cars during the storm. People hailed the scientist as a national hero. She hailed a taxi outside the airport. He hails from a small village in Sindh. Hail, Caesar! The crowd shouted loudly. Hail, brave warriors!. The king welcomed them. Hail! The champion of the tournament arrives.
sindhiMeaning: انهن برف جهڙن سخت داڻن کي چوندا آهن جيڪي طوفان دوران ڪڪرن مان زمين تي ڪرن، ڪنهن کي سلام ڪرڻ، وڏي خوشي سان ڀليڪار ڪرڻ، ڪنهن کي آواز ڏئي سڏڻ، ڪنهن جي اصليت يا جڳهه ظاهر ڪرڻ لاءِ به استعمال ٿئي ٿو
urduMeaning: برف جیسے سخت دانوں کو کہتے ہیں جو طوفانی بادلوں سے زمین پر گرتے ہیں، کسی کو پکارنا، خوشی سے استقبال کرنا یا کسی گاڑی وغیرہ کو آواز دے کر روکنا بھی ہوتا ہے، یہ کسی کے کسی جگہ سے تعلق ظاہر کرنے کے لئے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے

englishMeaning: Calm, peaceful, and happy, often referring to a time in the past. A period or situation that is calm, stable, and free from trouble. It is often used nostalgically to talk about earlier times that are remembered as happier or more peaceful than the present. A mythical bird linked with calm seas.
synonyms: Peaceful, Calm, Tranquil, Serene, Happy
antonyms: Turbulent, Chaotic, Troubled, Stormy, Unsettled
examples: She often talks about the halcyon days of her childhood. The town enjoyed a halcyon period before rapid development began. They longed for a return to the halcyon calm of earlier years. The lake looked halcyon in the early morning light.
sindhiMeaning: سڪون ڀريو يا خوشحال وقت، اهڙو وقت يا حالت جيڪو سڪون خوشحالي ۽ بي فڪري سان ڀريل هجي، اڪثر اهو لفظ ماضي جي خوشگوار ڏينهن لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو آهي
urduMeaning: پرسکون اور خوشگوار وقت، ایسا دور یا حالت جو پُرسکون خوشحال اور بے فکری سے بھرپور ہو، عام طور پر یہ لفظ ماضی کے سنہرے دنوں کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے

englishMeaning: To haul, drag, or pull someone or something with effort or force, often against resistance. This can be used literally (physical pulling) or figuratively (forcing someone to do something). Someone who is in good health, robust, and free from illness or weakness, often used especially for older adults.
synonyms: Healthy, Robust, Strong, Vigorous, Fit, Drag, Pull, Haul, Tug, Wrest
antonyms: Sick, Weak, Frail, Feeble, Push, Release, Let go, Free
examples: The police haled the suspect into the station. Workers haled the heavy logs up the hill. She was haled before the committee for questioning. They haled the boat ashore during the storm. The doctor declared her hale after the checkup. They were a hale couple, full of energy. He remained hale despite years of hard work.
sindhiMeaning: صحتمند، طاقتور، ڇڱو ڀلو، تازو توانو، ڇڪڻ، زور سان ڪڍڻ، گِھِلڻ، تندرست، مضبوط، ڏٽو موٽو
urduMeaning: زبردستی کھینچنا، کھینچنا، لے جانا، صحت مند، طاقتور

englishMeaning: To see, hear, feel, or experience something that is not actually present. It often happens due to illness, mental stress, drugs, extreme fear, or lack of sleep. The mind creates false sensory experiences that feel real to the person.
synonyms: Imagine falsely, Delude, See illusions, Misperceive
antonyms: Perceive reality, See clearly, Be aware, Recognize truth
examples: He began to hallucinate after staying awake for three days. The patient hallucinated voices that were not real. High fever can cause a person to hallucinate. She hallucinated shadows moving in the room.
sindhiMeaning: وهم ڏسڻ يا اهڙو احساس ڪرڻ جيڪو حقيقت ۾ موجود نه هجي، بيماري نشي ذهني دٻاءُ يا ننڊ جي کوٽ سبب ماڻهو اهڙيون شيون ڏسي يا ٻڌي سگهي ٿو جيڪي اصل ۾ نه هجن
urduMeaning: ایسی چیزیں دیکھنا سننا یا محسوس کرنا جو حقیقت میں موجود نہ ہوں، یہ عموماً بیماری ذہنی دباؤ نشہ یا نیند کی کمی کی وجہ سے ہوتا ہے

englishMeaning: A false experience where a person sees, hears, or feels something that is not real. A mental condition in which a person perceives sights, sounds, smells, or sensations that do not exist in reality. It often happens due to illness, mental stress, drugs, lack of sleep, or extreme fear. The experience feels real to the person even though it is not actually happening.
synonyms: Illusion, Delusion, False perception, Mirage
antonyms: Reality, Truth, Actuality, Fact
examples: The patient reported visual hallucinations during the illness. Lack of sleep can cause hallucinations. He heard voices, but they were only hallucinations. The drug induced hallucination faded after treatment.
sindhiMeaning: اهڙو وهم جيڪو حقيقت ۾ موجود نه هجي، اهڙي ذهني حالت جنهن ۾ ماڻهو اهڙيون شيون ڏسي يا ٻڌي جيڪي حقيقت ۾ موجود نه هونديون آهن، اهو بيماري نشي ذهني دٻاءَ يا ننڊ جي کوٽ سبب ٿي سگهي ٿو
urduMeaning: ایسی کیفیت جس میں انسان غیر حقیقی چیزیں محسوس کرے، ایک ذہنی حالت جس میں انسان ایسی آوازیں سنتا یا چیزیں دیکھتا ہے جو حقیقت میں موجود نہیں ہوتیں، یہ بیماری ذہنی دباؤ منشیات یا نیند کی کمی کی وجہ سے ہو سکتی ہے

englishMeaning: A small village or a group of houses in the countryside, smaller than a town and usually without its own church or local government. A very small settlement, often rural, consisting of only a few houses or families. It is smaller than a village and typically lacks major facilities like a school or marketplace.
synonyms: Settlement, Community, Rural area, Countryside dwelling
antonyms: City, Town, Metropolis, Urban area
examples: The old hamlet lies hidden among the hills. He grew up in a quiet hamlet far from the city. The earthquake destroyed several houses in the mountain hamlet. Tourists visited the charming hamlet for its traditional culture.
sindhiMeaning: اهڙو ننڍڙو ڳوٺ يا وسند، جيڪو تمام ٿورو آبادي وارو هجي، عام طور تي ڳوٺ جي ڀيٽ ۾ به ننڍڙو هوندو آهي، ۽ اڪثر ڪري ان ۾ چرچ، اسڪول يا بازار نه هوندي آهي
urduMeaning: ایسا چھوٹا گاؤں یا بستی جو عام گاؤں سے بھی چھوٹا ہوتا ہے، عموماً دیہی علاقے میں واقع ہوتا ہے اور اس میں کوئی مسجد، اسکول یا بازار نہیں ہوتا

englishMeaning: To hinder, obstruct. To prevent something from happening easily. To hold back progress or movement. A large basket, usually with a lid, used for carrying food, clothes, or laundry. A gift basket containing food and drinks.
synonyms: Hinder, Obstruct, Basket, Container
antonyms: Aid, Assist, Support, Encourage, Facilitate
examples: Heavy rain hampered their progress. Heavy traffic hampered our journey. Lack of funds hampered the project. She brought a picnic hamper full of fruit and snacks. The hotel sent us a complimentary gift hamper.
sindhiMeaning: روڪڻ، رڪاوٽ وجهڻ، آڙ بڻجڻ، ٽوڪري، وڏو ٽوڪر جيڪو کاڌي يا ڪپڙن لاءِ هوندو آهي، تحفي جي ٽوڪري
urduMeaning: رکاوٹ ڈالنا، روکنا، آڑ بننا، کپڑوں یا کھانے کی بڑی ٹوکری، تحفے کی ٹوکری

englishMeaning: To distribute items among a group of people so that everyone receives one.
synonyms: Distribute, Pass around, Share
antonyms: Collect, Gather, Withhold
examples: She handed around the chocolates during the party. Please hand around these leaflets to the audience. They handed around the forms for everyone to fill out. The teacher handed around the answer sheets.
sindhiMeaning: هٿ سان ورهائڻ يا ماڻهن ۾ ورهائڻ، تقسيم ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: ہاتھ سے سب میں بانٹنا یا تقسیم کرنا

englishMeaning: To return something to its rightful owner after borrowing or using it.
synonyms: Return, Restore, Give back
antonyms: Keep, Hold, Retain
examples: She handed back the book after reading it. Please hand back the documents once checked. The students handed back the borrowed materials. He handed back the pen he had borrowed.
sindhiMeaning: واپس ڪرڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي ان جي اصلي مالڪ کي واپس ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: واپس کرنا، کسی چیز کو اصل مالک کو لوٹانا

englishMeaning: To pass something, such as knowledge, tradition, or property, from one generation to another.
synonyms: Transmit, Inherit, Bequeath
antonyms: Take away, Withhold, Stop
examples: These customs were handed down from our ancestors. The old watch was handed down to him by his grandfather. Stories are handed down through oral tradition. Values are often handed down in families.
sindhiMeaning: نسلن تائين پهچائڻ، منتقل ڪرڻ، وراثت طور ڏيڻ، اڳين نسل کان ايندڙ نسل ڏانهن منتقل ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: نسل در نسل منتقل کرنا، عدالت کا فیصلہ سنانا، وراثت میں دینا، اگلی نسل کو منتقل کرنا

englishMeaning: To formally submit something, such as an assignment, document, or resignation, for official consideration or record.
synonyms: Submit, Present, Deliver
antonyms: Withhold, Keep, Retain
examples: She handed in her homework before the deadline. Please hand in your resignation letter by Friday. Students must hand in the forms at the office. He handed in his ID card before leaving the company.
sindhiMeaning: جمع ڪرائڻ، پيش ڪرڻ، سپرد ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: جمع کرانا، پیش کرنا، سپرد کرنا

englishMeaning: To be very close or work together in complete agreement, often for a shared goal or purpose. This idiom is used when two or more people, organizations, or groups are very closely connected or cooperate so smoothly that their actions seem almost unified.
synonyms: In close cooperation, In partnership, In alliance
antonyms: In conflict, At odds, In opposition, Working separately
examples: The two companies worked hand in glove on the project. The manager and his assistant worked hand in glove to complete the project on time. The two companies are hand in glove in developing the new technology. The politician was hand in glove with the businessmen involved in the scandal. Teachers and parents should work hand in glove for children’s better education.
sindhiMeaning: ٻه ماڻهو يا تنظيمون تمام ويجهو هم آهنگ ۽ گڏجي ڪم ڪن
urduMeaning: دو لوگ یا ادارے بہت قریب اور ہم آہنگی سے کام کر یں

englishMeaning: To give credit or praise to someone for their effort or achievement.
synonyms: Acknowledge, Praise, Compliment, Appreciate
antonyms: Criticize, Blame, Condemn, Ignore
examples: You have to hand it to her, she did a great job. I’ll hand it to John; he always works hard. You must hand it to the team for their dedication. We should hand it to them, they never gave up.
sindhiMeaning: ڪجهه ڪرڻ تي ڪنهن جي تعريف ڪرڻ، ڪنهن جي قابليت يا ڪاميابي جي تعريف ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: کسی کی تعریف یا پذیرائی کرنا، ماننا پڑے گا، تسلیم کرنا پڑے گا، کسی کی صلاحیت یا کامیابی کو سراہنا

englishMeaning: To pass or transfer responsibility or control of something to another person.
synonyms: Delegate, Transfer, Assign, Pass on
antonyms: Retain, Keep, Withhold, Maintain
examples: The manager handed off the project to his assistant. You can hand off the task when you’re finished. The quarterback handed off the ball to the running back. I’ll hand off this report once I review it.
sindhiMeaning: ذميواري يا ڪنٽرول ڪنهن ٻئي ڏانهن منتقل ڪرڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي هٿ سان ٻي کي ڏيڻ، مداخلت نه ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: ذمہ داری اختیار یا کنٹرول کسی اور کو منتقل کرنا، اتھ سے کسی چیز کو آگے دینا، مداخلت نہ کرنا

englishMeaning: To pass or give something to someone, especially knowledge or information.
synonyms: Pass on, Transfer, Convey, Transmit
antonyms: Withhold, Retain, Keep, Conceal
examples: The teacher handed on her experience to the new staff. He handed on the family traditions to his children. Please hand on this document to the manager. Wisdom is often handed on from generation to generation.
sindhiMeaning: ڄاڻ يا معلومات ڪنهن کي ڏيڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي اڳتي ڏيڻ، منتقل ڪرڻ يا ڪنهن ٻئي تائين پهچائڻ
urduMeaning: کسی کو علم یا معلومات دینا، کسی چیز کو آگے دینا، منتقل کرنا یا کسی دوسرے تک پہنچانا

englishMeaning: To transfer the possession or control of something to another person, often formally or under obligation.
synonyms: Transfer, Surrender, Deliver
antonyms: Keep, Retain, Withhold
examples: The manager handed over the documents to the director. He was forced to hand over the keys to the police. The power was handed over peacefully after the elections. Please hand over the package at the reception.
sindhiMeaning: حوالي ڪرڻ، هٿ ۾ ڏيڻ، قبضي مان ڇڏائي ڪنهن ٻئي کي ڏيڻ، سپرد ڪرڻ، ڪنھن شيءِ يا ذميواريءَ جو ڪنھن ٻئي شخص کي ڏيڻ
urduMeaning: سپرد کرنا، حوالے کرنا، قبضہ چھوڑ کر کسی اور کے حوالے کرنا، کسی چیز یا ذمے داری کو کسی دوسرے کو دینا

englishMeaning: Used when a person wants to emphasize that they are telling the absolute truth. It is a strong expression of honesty, sincerity, or promise. (It’s similar to saying “I swear to God.”)
synonyms: I’m telling the truth
antonyms: Lying, Deceitful, Dishonest, Falsehood, Untruth
examples: Hand to God, I didn’t take your book Hand to God, I have never met that person before. Hand to God, everything I said is true. Hand to God, I was at home the whole time.
sindhiMeaning: خدا جي قسم، سچيءَ دل سان قسم، خدا جو قسم کڻي چوان ٿو(هي لفظ سچائي ۽ ايمانداري تي زور ڏيڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿئي ٿو)
urduMeaning: خدا کی قسم،خدا گواہ ہے،میں سچ کہہ رہا ہوں (یہ ایمانداری اور سچائی پر زور دینے کے لیے کہا جاتا ہے)

englishMeaning: Living without savings, Whatever one earns (by the hand) is immediately spent on necessities (for the mouth). There’s nothing left for future savings. Having no savings and struggling to meet daily needs. It describes a person or family who earns just enough to get by, often in poverty or financial hardship.
synonyms: Poor, Barely surviving, Struggling financially
antonyms: Wealthy, Comfortable, Prosperous
examples: Many poor families in the village live a hand-to-mouth life. After losing his job, he was forced to live hand to mouth for several months. Despite working hard, some people remain hand to mouth because of rising prices. Farmers often live a hand-to-mouth existence during dry seasons.
sindhiMeaning: فقط گذر بسر، اهڙي حالت جنهن ۾ ماڻهو فقط پنهنجي روزاني ضرورت پوري ڪرڻ لاءِ ڪمائي ٿو، پر بچت يا اضافي پئسا ناهن، اهڙي زندگي جيڪا غربت تنگدستي يا محدود وسيلن سان گذري ٿي
urduMeaning: بس گزارا کرنا، بمشکل گزارا کرنا، وہ حالت جس میں آدمی جو کماتا ہے، وہی روز مرہ کے اخراجات میں خرچ ہو جاتا ہے، کچھ بھی بچت نہیں ہوتی

englishMeaning: To surrender yourself to the authorities, especially the police.
synonyms: Surrender, Submit, Yield, Confess

englishMeaning: Boring, dull, routine, Lacking excitement, variety, or interest. Repetitive and boring due to routine. Dull and ordinary with nothing special. Monotonous in nature, especially daily life or work.
synonyms: Boring, Dull, Monotonous, Tedious, Routine
antonyms: Exciting, Interesting, Thrilling, Lively, Engaging
examples: His job became humdrum after doing the same tasks every day. She wanted to escape her humdrum routine and travel the world. The movie started well but turned humdrum in the middle. Life in the small town felt humdrum to him.
sindhiMeaning: بيزار/ سستو/ هڪجهڙو، بيزار ڪندڙ جنهن ۾ ڪا دلچسپي نه هجي، روزمره جهڙو ۽ ورجاءُ وارو، سادو ۽ بي رنگ، هڪجهڙائي سبب بي مزو، اڳڪٿي لائق ۽ بنا تبديلي، ٿڪائيندڙ يا اوٻاڻو، بي جان يا بي روح
urduMeaning: بور/ پھیکا/ معمولی، بور کرنے والا جس میں کوئی دلچسپی نہ ہو، روزمرہ اور ایک ہی طرح کا، پھیکا اور غیر دلچسپ، یکسانیت کی وجہ سے اکتاہٹ پیدا کرنے والا، قابلِ پیش گوئی اور بغیر تبدیلی، تھکا دینے والا، بے جان اور بے اثر

englishMeaning: Wise people stay humble. Real education teaches respect. Knowledgeable people avoid arrogance. Learning develops modest behavior. Intelligence with humility earns respect.
synonyms: Modesty shows wisdom, Wisdom brings humility, Knowledge creates modesty, True learning removes arrogance, Humble wisdom
antonyms: Arrogance, Pride, Vanity, Conceit, Overconfidence
examples: The professor spoke kindly to every student because humility reflects knowledge. Despite his success, he remained polite and calm, proving that humility reflects knowledge. Great scientists often listen carefully to others because humility reflects knowledge. A wise leader understands mistakes and learns from them because humility reflects knowledge.
sindhiMeaning: نوڙت علم جي نشاني آهي، سچو عالم هميشه عاجز هوندو آهي، علم انسان کي نرم دل بڻائي ٿو، دانائي سان ادب ۽ نوڙت پيدا ٿيندي آهي، وڏائي اڻڄاڻائي جي نشاني ٿي سگهي ٿي
urduMeaning: عاجزی علم کی عکاسی کرتی ہے، حقیقی علم انسان کو جھکنا سکھاتا ہے، دانا انسان تکبر نہیں کرتا، علم کے ساتھ شائستگی آتی ہے، عاجزی سمجھدار انسان کی پہچان ہے

englishMeaning: A smooth, creamy food made mainly from mashed chickpeas blended with tahini, olive oil, lemon juice, and garlic. It is commonly eaten as a dip or spread.
synonyms: Chickpea dip, Chickpea spread, Garbanzo bean paste, Middle Eastern dip
antonyms: There is no direct antonym
examples: I ate hummus with warm pita bread for lunch. She spreads hummus on her sandwich instead of butter. Hummus is a healthy snack rich in protein and fiber. They served hummus with fresh vegetables at the party.
sindhiMeaning: هڪ نرم ۽ ڪريمي کاڌو جيڪو چڻن تل جي پيسٽ زيتون جي تيل ليمون ۽ ٿوم مان ٺاهيو ويندو آهي، اهو عام طور تي ڊِپ يا اسپريڊ طور کائبو آهي
urduMeaning: ایک نرم اور کریمی غذا جو چنے تل کے پیسٹ زیتون کے تیل لیموں اور لہسن سے تیار کی جاتی ہے، یہ عموماً ڈِپ یا اسپریڈ کے طور پر استعمال ہوتی ہے

englishMeaning: Funny or amusing; causing laughter. Having or showing a sense of humor, able to make others laugh, playful in nature, amusing in a lighthearted way.
synonyms: Amusing, Funny, Cerebral
antonyms: Humorless, Unamusing, Uncomic
examples: She has a humorous way of telling stories that always makes us laugh. His humorous comments lightened the tense meeting. The movie was full of humorous scenes that kept everyone entertained. A humorous personality often helps in making friends easily.
sindhiMeaning: خوش مزاجي، چرچائي، مزي جھڙو، کلائيندڙ، مذاق جي حِس رکندڙ
urduMeaning: خوش طبع، مزاحیہ، ہنسی مذاق والا

englishMeaning: To agree with somebody’s wishes, even if they seem unreasonable, in order to keep the person happy. The quality in something that makes it funny, The ability to laugh at things that are funny.
synonyms: Comedy, Comic, Mood
antonyms: Agony, Anguish
examples: She thought it best to humour them rather than get into an argument. She ignored his feeble attempt at humour. I can't stand people with no sense of humour. She has her very own brand of humour. The remarks were made in good humour.

englishMeaning: The rich, dark organic matter in soil that forms when plants, leaves, and animals decompose. It improves soil fertility, increases moisture retention, supports beneficial microorganisms, and helps plants grow stronger. Humus plays a key role in agriculture, forestry, and environmental sustainability.
synonyms: Organic matter, Compost, Leaf mold, Soil organic material
antonyms: Mineral soil, Sand, Clay without organic content, Barren soil
examples: Farmers add compost to increase the humus content of the soil. Humus helps the soil retain water during dry seasons. Forest floors are rich in humus due to fallen leaves. The presence of humus improves soil structure and fertility.
sindhiMeaning: نباتياتي مٽي، نامياتي ڀاڻ، مٽي جو نامياتي زرخيز عنصر، زمين ۾ ڳريل نباتاتي مواد، مٽيءَ جو اهو زرخيز ۽ ڪارو نامياتي حصو جيڪو ٻوٽن پنن ۽ جاندارن جي گرڻ سڙڻ سان ٺهي ٿو، اهو مٽيءَ جي زرخيزي وڌائي ٿو پاڻي کي محفوظ رکي ٿو فائديمند جراثيمن جي واڌ ويجهه ۾ مدد ڪري ٿو ۽ ٻوٽن کي صحتمند وڌڻ ۾ سهارو ڏئي ٿو
urduMeaning: تُراب، نباتی مٹی، نباتی کھاد، مٹی کا وہ زرخیز اور سیاہ نامیاتی حصہ جو پودوں پتوں اور جانداروں کے گلنے سڑنے سے بنتا ہے، یہ مٹی کی زرخیزی بڑھاتا ہےنمی کو محفوظ رکھتا ہے مفید جراثیم کی افزائش میں مدد دیتا ہے اور پودوں کی بہتر نشوونما میں اہم کردار ادا کرتا ہے

englishMeaning: To bend your body forward, especially your back or shoulders. To make a decision based on instinct rather than facts. An intuitive feeling, guess, or suspicion without concrete evidence. The act of bending forward, often with shoulders or back rounded. Someone who looks worried or tense because of posture.
synonyms: Bend, Stoop, Crouch, Lean forward, Intuition, Suspicion, Feeling, Guess, Inkling
antonyms: Straighten, Stand upright, Extend, Certainty, Fact, Knowledge, Proof
examples: It seemed that the doctor's hunch had been right. I have a hunch that Jane likes me. My hunch is that the burglars are still in the area. Her hunches were confirmed the next day. I had a hunch that you might be here. We hunched round the fire to keep warm. She leaned forward, hunching over the desk. He hunched his shoulders and thrust his hands deep into his pockets.
sindhiMeaning: جسم اڳتي جھڪائڻ (خاص ڪري پٺ ۽ ڪلهن کي)، ٿوھو يا ڪُٻ ڪڍڻ، احساس جي بنياد تي فيصلو ڪرڻ، هڪ اڻڄاتل احساس يا اندازو بغير ڪنهن ثبوت جي، دٻاءُ يا پريشانيءَ ۾ جسم جي جھڪاءُ جي وضاحت ڪرڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو آهي
urduMeaning: جسم کو آگے جھکانا (خاص طور پر کمر یا کندھوں کو)، جسم کا اوپری حصہ جھکانا، کسی چیز کے بارے میں بغیر ثبوت کے اندیشہ یا حدس، جسمانی جھکاؤ یا کمر کے موڑ کو دباؤ یا پریشانی کے اظہار کے لیے استعمال کیا جاتا ہے

englishMeaning: Everything is fine, satisfactory, or going well. A situation, condition, or state of affairs that is completely satisfactory, without problems, or proceeding smoothly. Often informal and conversational.
synonyms: Fine, Okay, All right, Smooth, Satisfactory
antonyms: Awry, Problematic, Bad, Troublesome, Off
examples: After fixing the car, everything was hunky dory. He thought the meeting went well and that everything was hunky dory. After a short argument, things were hunky dory between them. The project started with a few delays, but now it’s hunky dory.
sindhiMeaning: هر شيءَ ٺيڪ آهي، سڀ حالتون خوشگوار آهن، ڪابه پريشاني ناهي، ڪم يا زندگي سٺي ۽ آسان حالت ۾ آهي، سڀ ڪجهه ٺيڪ ۽ مطمئن ڪندڙ آهي
urduMeaning: سب کچھ بالکل ٹھیک ہے، کوئی مسئلہ نہیں، حالات خوشگوار ہیں، سب کچھ آسان اور مطمئن کن صورت میں ہے، ہر کام بغیر کسی رکاوٹ کے بہتر چل رہا ہے

englishMeaning: To search carefully and persistently to find something hidden or not immediately obvious.
synonyms: Seek, Discover, Unearth
antonyms: Ignore, Overlook
examples: I hunted out my old notes. They hunted out the lost files. She hunted out the best restaurant. Let’s hunt out a solution.

englishMeaning: A violent storm with very strong winds, especially in the western Atlantic Ocean. A tropical cyclone with winds of 74 miles (119 kilometers) per hour or greater that is usually accompanied by rain, thunder, and lightning, and that sometimes moves into temperate latitudes. A state of noisy, confused activity.
synonyms: Cyclone, Tornado, Typhoon, Storm
antonyms: Calm, Hush, Peace, Quiet, Quietude
examples: A powerful hurricane hit the Florida coast. Hurricane Sandy devastated the area. After a hurricane comes a rainbow. The hurricane left a trail of destruction behind it.
sindhiMeaning: طوفان، واچوڙو، سامونڊي طوفان، وڏو سامونڊي واچوڙو
urduMeaning: طوفانی آندھی، ہوا کا تیز چھکڑ، طوفان بادوباراں، تیز و تند ہوا، ہنگامہ برپا کر دینا، آندھی

englishMeaning: Done in haste or very quickly. Doing something quickly, rapidly, or in a rush because of limited time, pressure, excitement, fear, or urgency.
synonyms: Quickly, Rapidly, Hastily, Swiftly, Speedily, Fast, Briskly, In haste
antonyms: Slowly, Calmly, Carefully, Patiently, Gradually, Leisurely
examples: She hurriedly packed her bag before leaving for school. The driver hurriedly moved the car after hearing the warning. He hurriedly finished his homework before dinner. The staff hurriedly evacuated the building during the emergency.
sindhiMeaning: جلديءَ سان, تڪڙ ۾, اُٻهرائي سان, تيزيءَ سان
urduMeaning: جلدی سے, عجلت میں, تیزی کے ساتھ, گھبراہٹ یا جلد بازی میں

englishMeaning: The care, cultivation, and breeding of crops and animals. The careful management and conservation of resources. Skill in managing or using something efficiently
synonyms: Farming, Agriculture, Cultivation, Management, Stewardship
antonyms: Neglect, Waste, Mismanagement, Destruction
examples: Modern husbandry focuses on sustainable farming methods. He studied animal husbandry to improve dairy production. Good husbandry ensures that the land remains fertile for generations. The family practiced careful husbandry of their savings.

urduMeaning: کاشتکاری، کھيتی باڑی، زراعت، کھیتوں اور مویشیوں کی دیکھ بھال، وسائل کا دانشمندانہ انتظام، کسی چیز کے محتاط اور مؤثر استعمال کی مہارت

englishMeaning: To move or work rapidly and energetically. To urge someone to act quickly. To obtain something by energetic effort or sometimes by trickery. Busy, energetic activity. A state of commotion. Aggressive effort to achieve something.
synonyms: Rush, Hurry, Work hard, Push, Drive, Bustle, Strive
antonyms: Idle, Dawdle, Linger, Relax, Loaf, Slack
examples: She had to hustle to finish the project on time. Street vendors hustle tourists for tips. The team’s hustle on the field won them the match. He hustled his way through the crowded station to catch the train.
sindhiMeaning: تيزي سان ڪم ڪرڻ، ڌڪڻ يا زور وٺرائڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ حاصل ڪرڻ جي ڪوشش ڪرڻ، مشغوليت، سرگرمي، تيزي سان هلڻ يا ڪم ڪرڻ جو عمل
urduMeaning: تیزی سے کام کرنا، زور دینا، جلدی میں کچھ حاصل کرنا، مصروفیت، ہلچل، سرگرمی، محنت سے کام کرنے کا عمل

englishMeaning: Busy, noisy activity and fast movement, usually in a crowded place. An environment full of energy, movement, and noise where many people are active at the same time. It is often used for markets, cities, offices, or events where there is constant motion and lively interaction.
synonyms: Activity, Commotion, Bustling atmosphere, Liveliness, Rush
antonyms: Calm, Quiet, Stillness, Peacefulness
examples: The hustle and bustle of the city never stops, even at night. She moved to the countryside to escape the hustle and bustle of urban life. The market was full of hustle and bustle during the festival. He enjoys the hustle and bustle of working in a busy office.
sindhiMeaning: شور شرابو ۽ هلهه چلھ، ماڻهن جي رش ۽ گهڻي سرگرمي، شهرن يا مارڪيٽن ۾ بي انتها گهمڻ ڦرڻ ۽ هلچل، گهماگهمي/ شور ۽ مصروفيت، اهڙي جڳهه تي ماڻهو تيزي سان اچ وڃ ڪندا آهن ۽ ماحول زندهه ۽ مصروف هوندو آهي
urduMeaning: چہل پہل، بہت زیادہ ہلچل، شور شرابا اور بھیڑ بھاڑخاص طور پر شہروں بازاروں یا رش والے مقامات پر، مصروف زندگی، متحرک ماحول، مسلسل سرگرمی، ہجوم اور شور والا ماحول

englishMeaning: Something made by combining two different things. Biology: offspring of two different species or varieties. Technology: a system combining two different technologies. Vehicle: a car using both fuel and electricity. General: a mixture of different ideas or styles.
synonyms: Blend, Mixture, Combination, Crossbreed, Fusion
antonyms: Pure, Original, Single, Unmixed, Separate
examples: This plant is a hybrid of two rare species. He drives a hybrid car to save fuel. The course uses a hybrid learning model with online and classroom sessions. Her music is a hybrid of classical and modern styles.
sindhiMeaning: ملاوٽيل يا ٻن مختلف شين مان ٺهيل، حياتيات: ٻن مختلف نسلن مان پيدا ٿيل جاندار، ٽيڪنالاجي: ٻن نظامن جو گڏيل استعمال، گاڏي: ايندھن ۽ بجلي ٻنهي سان هلندڙ گاڏي، عام: مختلف خيالن يا اندازن جو ميلاپ
urduMeaning: ملا جلا یا دو مختلف چیزوں سے بنا ہوا، حیاتیات: دو مختلف نسلوں سے پیدا ہونے والی مخلوق، ٹیکنالوجی: دو نظاموں کا مشترکہ استعمال، گاڑی: پٹرول اور بجلی دونوں پر چلنے والی گاڑی، عام: مختلف خیالات یا انداز کا امتزاج

englishMeaning: To cause a person, animal, or substance to absorb or be supplied with water or moisture. To restore or maintain the water balance in the body or a substance. As a noun in chemistry, a compound containing water molecules chemically combined in a definite ratio. To keep the body adequately supplied with fluids to maintain health and proper function.
synonyms: Moisturise, Water, Soak, Saturate, Replenish, Quench, Nourish, Refresh
antonyms: Dehydrate, Dry, Desiccate, Parch, Drain, Deplete, Wither
examples: Doctors advised the athlete to hydrate well before and after the race. You should hydrate your skin daily using a good moisturiser. It is important to hydrate yourself by drinking plenty of water in hot weather. The plant needs to be hydrated regularly during the dry season. She drank several glasses of water to hydrate herself after the long walk.
sindhiMeaning: پاڻي پيارڻ، رطوبت ڏيڻ، نمي ڀرڻ، جسم ۾ پاڻي جي گهٽتائي پوري ڪرڻ، ترٻيل ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: پانی پلانا، نمی دینا، جسم میں پانی کی کمی پوری کرنا، تر کرنا، سیراب کرنا

englishMeaning: Fear of water. An extreme or irrational fear of water. Medically, it also refers to a symptom of rabies in humans, causing difficulty in swallowing water or fear of drinking.
synonyms: Aquaphobia, Water fear
antonyms: Love of water, Aquaphilia
examples: His hydrophobia made swimming impossible. The doctor explained that hydrophobia is a symptom of rabies. She developed hydrophobia after nearly drowning as a child. Awareness campaigns help prevent rabies, which can cause hydrophobia.
sindhiMeaning: پاڻيءَ جو ڊپ، پاڻي کان شديد ڊپ خاص طور تي جڏهن اهو رابيز جي علامت طور ظاهر ٿئي ٿو
urduMeaning: پانی کا خوف، پانی سے شدید یا غیر معقول خوف، عام طور پر ریبیز کی علامت کے طور پر ظاہر ہوتا ہے

englishMeaning: To promote, praise, or advertise something in an exaggerated and exciting way to attract attention or increase interest. To make something seem more exciting, important, successful, or impressive than it may actually be. It is often used in advertising, social media, movies, products, events, games, or public discussions.
synonyms: Promote, Advertise, Publicize, Exaggerate, Boost, Praise highly, Build excitement for, Glorify
antonyms: Downplay, Criticize, Understate, Ignore, Dismiss, Minimize
examples: The company hyped up its new smartphone before the launch. Social media influencers hyped the movie up for weeks. He keeps hyping up the event as if it will change everyone’s life. The game was heavily hyped up, but many players were disappointed later.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ جي تمام گهڻي تعريف يا مشهوري ڪرڻ ته جيئن ماڻهن جو ڌيان ۽ دلچسپي وڌي وڃي، وڏي مشهوري ڪرڻ، وڌائي بيان ڪرڻ، ماڻهن ۾ جوش پيدا ڪرڻ، ڌيان ڇڪائڻ لاءِ تعريف ڪرڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي حقيقت کان وڌيڪ اهم ڏيکارڻ، اهو اڪثر اشتهارن فلمن شين پروگرامن ۽ سوشل ميڊيا ۾ استعمال ٿيندو آهي
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کی بہت زیادہ تعریف یا تشہیر کرنا تاکہ لوگوں کی دلچسپی اور توجہ بڑھے، بہت زیادہ تشہیر کرنا، بڑھا چڑھا کر پیش کرنا، لوگوں میں جوش پیدا کرنا، غیر معمولی تعریف کرنا، کسی چیز کو حقیقت سے زیادہ اہم دکھانا، یہ لفظ اکثر اشتہارات فلموں مصنوعات اور سوشل میڈیا میں استعمال ہوتا ہے

englishMeaning: Extreme exaggeration used for emphasis or effect. A way of speaking or writing that makes something sound better, more exciting, more dangerous, etc than it really is.
synonyms: Exaggeration, Overstatement, Amplification
antonyms: Understatement, Minimization, Restraint
examples: The film is being promoted with all the usual hyperbole. He’s not usually given to hyperbole. I have told you a million times to be careful. This bag weighs a ton. She cried a river after watching the movie. He was so hungry that he could eat a horse.
sindhiMeaning: وڌاءُ، اٺاءُ، وڌايل بيان، اهڙو اظهار جنهن ۾ ڳالهه کي جان بوجھ ڪري تمام گهڻو وڌايو وڃي ته جيئن زور اثر يا احساس پيدا ٿئي، ان کي لفظي معنيٰ ۾ نٿو ورتو وڃي
urduMeaning: مبالغہ، اِغراق، غلو، حد سے زيادہ تعريف، ایک ادبی انداز جس میں بات کو جان بوجھ کر حد سے زیادہ بڑھا چڑھا کر بیان کیا تاکہ زور اثر یا احساس پیدا ہو، اسے لفظی طور پر نہیں لیا جاتا

englishMeaning: Exhibiting unusual or excessive concern with or indulgence in sexual activity. Extremely or excessively sexual or given to sexual activities. Having an abnormally high or excessive interest in sexual activity, fantasies, or behavior. It often describes a condition where sexual thoughts or actions become overwhelming, frequent, or difficult to control.
synonyms: Concupiscent, Goatish, Horny, Hot, Itchy lasciviously lecherous, Lewd
antonyms: Frigid, Undersexed
examples: The movie unfairly portrayed the character as being hypersexual, which was not true to her personality. Some people wrongly label teenagers as hypersexual when they are simply curious about relationships. The doctor explained that hypersexual behavior could be a symptom of certain mental health conditions. The article criticized the fashion industry for creating hypersexual images of women.

examples: Negotiations have reached an impasse. An arbitrator was called in to break the impasse. She had reached an impasse in her career. The committee faced an impasse over budget allocation. We are at an impasse and need a new strategy to solve the problem. The peace talks ended in an impasse after both sides refused to compromise. The project reached an impasse due to lack of funding. After hours of debate, the committee found itself at an impasse.
sindhiMeaning: اهڙي رڪاوٽ واري حالت جتي اڳتي وڌڻ ممڪن نه هجي، ڳالهين ۾ ٺپ صورتحال، بند رستو يا بي نتيجا موڙ، ڪم يا عمل ۾ اڳتي وڌڻ جي ناڪامي، ذهني يا جذباتي جمود، ٻن ڌرين يا ماڻهن وچ ۾ ڳالهين فيصلي يا معاملي ۾ اهڙي رڪاوٽ جو ڪو به اڳتي قدم نه وڌائي سگهي، ٻئي ڌريون پنهنجي موقف تي قائم هجن ۽ حل جو ڪو رستو نظر نه اچي

englishMeaning: To formally accuse a public official of wrongdoing. To officially charge a public official with misconduct or illegal actions while in office. It can also mean to question the truth or validity of something such as a statement or evidence.
synonyms: Accuse, Charge, Indict, Prosecute, Question
antonyms: Acquit, Defend, Exonerate, Clear, Justify
examples: The parliament decided to impeach the president for corruption. The lawyer tried to impeach the witness's credibility. Lawmakers voted to impeach the governor after the scandal. The defense attempted to impeach the evidence presented in court.
sindhiMeaning: سرڪاري عهديدار تي رسمي الزام لڳائڻ، قانوني طور الزام مڙهڻ، ڪنهن ڳالهه جي ساک يا سچائي تي شڪ ڪرڻ، شاهدي جي سچائي تي سوال ڪرڻ، ڪنهن سرڪاري عهديدار تي سندس عهدو دوران غلط ڪم يا غيرقانوني عمل لاءِ رسمي الزام لڳائڻ۔ اهو پڻ ڪنهن ڳالهه يا ثبوت جي سچائي تي سوال اٿارڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو آهي
urduMeaning: کسی سرکاری عہدیدار پر باضابطہ الزام لگانا، قانونی طور پر فردِ جرم عائد کرنا، کسی چیز کی ساکھ کو نقصان پہنچانا یا سوال اٹھانا، گواہی کی درستگی پر سوال اٹھانا، کسی سرکاری عہدیدار پر اس کے عہدے کے دوران بدعنوانی یا غیر قانونی عمل کا باضابطہ الزام لگانا،اس کا مطلب کسی بیان یا ثبوت کی سچائی پر شک کرنا بھی ہو سکتا ہے

englishMeaning: Capable of being questioned, accused, or charged with wrongdoing. Something or someone described as impeachable can be legally or morally challenged. It may refer to a person whose actions can lead to formal charges, or to evidence or statements that can be doubted or discredited.
synonyms: Accusable, Chargeable, Blameworthy, Questionable, Challengeable
antonyms: Unimpeachable, Irrefutable, Blameless, Above reproach, Trustworthy
examples: The official’s actions were clearly impeachable under the law. His testimony was found to be impeachable due to contradictions. Any misuse of public funds is considered impeachable conduct. The lawyer argued that the witness’s statement was impeachable.
sindhiMeaning: قابلِ احتساب، جنهن تي الزام لڳائي سگهجي، اعتراض لائق، شڪي، ڀروسو ڪرڻ جهڙو نه، اهڙو ماڻهو يا عمل جنهن کي قانوني يا اخلاقي طور چيلينج ڪري سگهجي يا جنهن خلاف ڪارروائي ٿي سگهي، اهو لفظ اهڙن ثبوتن لاءِ به استعمال ٿئي ٿو جيڪي شڪ هيٺ اچي سگهن ٿا
urduMeaning: قابلِ مواخذہ، جس پر الزام لگایا جا سکے، قابلِ اعتراض، مشکوک، ناقابلِ اعتماد، ایسا شخص یا عمل جس پر قانونی یا اخلاقی طور پر اعتراض کیا جا سکے، جس کے خلاف باقاعدہ کارروائی ہو سکتی ہو، یہ لفظ ایسے ثبوت یا بیان کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے جس پر شک کیا جا سکے

englishMeaning: A formal process to accuse a public official of wrongdoing. A formal legal process by which a legislative body brings charges against a high-ranking public official, such as a president or judge, for misconduct or violation of law. It may lead to removal from office after trial.
synonyms: Accusation, Charge, Indictment, Prosecution, Allegation
antonyms: Acquittal, Exoneration, Clearance, Vindication
examples: The parliament started impeachment proceedings against the president. The judge faced impeachment due to corruption charges. The lawyer attempted the impeachment of the witness's credibility. The constitution explains how impeachment works in detail.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن سرڪاري عملدار تي الزام هڻڻ جي قانوني ڪارروائي، هڪ قانوني عمل جنهن ۾ پارليامينٽ يا قانون ساز اداري طرفان ڪنهن اعليٰ سرڪاري عملدار جهڙوڪ صدر يا جج تي بدعنواني يا قانون جي ڀڃڪڙي جا الزام لڳايا وڃن جنهن کان پوءِ ان کي عهدو ڇڏڻ تي مجبور ڪيو وڃي، اهو لفظ ڪنهن ڳالهه جي سچائي يا اعتبار تي سوال ڪرڻ لاءِ به استعمال ٿئي ٿو
urduMeaning: کسی سرکاری عہدیدار پر الزام لگانے کا باقاعدہ عمل، ایک قانونی عمل جس کے ذریعے پارلیمنٹ یا قانون ساز ادارہ کسی اعلیٰ سرکاری عہدیدار جیسے صدر یا جج پر بدعنوانی یا قانون کی خلاف ورزی کے الزامات عائد کرتا ہے جس کے نتیجے میں اسے عہدے سے ہٹایا بھی جا سکتا ہے، یہ لفظ کسی بیان یا ثبوت کی سچائی پر سوال اٹھانے کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے

englishMeaning: Perfect, without any faults or errors. Flawless in behavior, appearance, or quality. Free from mistakes or wrongdoing.
synonyms: Flawless, Perfect, Spotless, Exemplary, Faultless, Unblemished
antonyms: Faulty, Imperfect, Defective, Flawed, Inadequate
examples: Her performance in the play was impeccable and earned a standing ovation. The chef’s presentation of the dish was impeccable, impressing all the guests. He has impeccable manners and always treats everyone with respect. The report was impeccable, leaving no room for criticism.

englishMeaning: In a way that is perfect, flawless, without any fault, mistake, or flaw.  With the highest standards of correctness, neatness, or behavior.
synonyms: Admirably, Correctly, Excellently, Exquisitely, Faultlessly, Fitly, Flawlessly, Ideally, Superbly, Superlatively, Supremely, Wonderfully
antonyms: Flawed, Imperfectly, Partially
examples: The airport was new, impressive, and impeccably clean. Her work is well written and impeccably researched. Medical practitioners tend to be impeccably honest, devoted to their patients, and incredibly hardworking. His logic is impeccably straightforward. He was impeccably polite. His mother was always impeccably groomed. He had behaved impeccably both times.

synonyms: Hinder, Obstruct, Block, Delay, Thwart, Restrict, Slow down
antonyms: Facilitate, Aid, Assist, Promote, Encourage, Advance
examples: Heavy traffic can impede emergency vehicles from reaching the hospital on time. His lack of experience may impede his chances of promotion. Snowstorms often impede travel during winter. Political disagreements can impede the progress of important legislation.

synonyms: Vital, Compulsory, Mandatory, Behest, Requirement
antonyms: Unnecessary, Unneeded, Unwanted, Undesired, Appeal

englishMeaning: Too small, slight, or subtle to be noticed or detected. So slight, gradual, or tiny that it cannot be seen, heard, or felt easily. It is below the level of human perception.
synonyms: Unnoticeable, Invisible, Subtle, Indiscernible, Faint, Unperceivable
antonyms: Noticeable, Visible, Obvious, Detectable, Clear, Apparent
examples: The change in his behavior was almost imperceptible. There was an imperceptible movement in the curtain. The temperature dropped in an imperceptible way during the night. Her smile had an imperceptible sadness behind it.

englishMeaning: To remain undamaged or never decay. To stay everlasting. To resist destruction. To avoid decline. To stay unharmed, unchanged, or undestroyed over time. It refers to anything that does not fade, rot, weaken, or disappear. It can be used for memories, values, objects, or anything that endures without losing its quality.
synonyms: Endure, Last, Survive, Persist, Remain, Stay intact, Never fade
antonyms: Perish, Decay, Disappear, Fade, Deteriorate, Break down
examples: Great ideas often imperish even after centuries. His love for knowledge will imperish in every stage of life. Ancient traditions can imperish despite social changes. True friendships sometimes imperish through the hardest times.

It can also refer to inserting devices or objects into a body or system.

antonyms: Removal, Extraction, Detachment, Dislodgment
examples: The doctor explained the implantation of the pacemaker. Implantation of the embryo occurs a few days after fertilization. The company focused on the implantation of new safety protocols. Dental implantation can restore missing teeth effectively.

englishMeaning: Something that indicates or suggests a meaning, conclusion, or relation without stating it directly. In logic and mathematics it can also mean a condition or expression that guarantees another statement is true.

antonyms: Explicit statement, Direct expression, Clear declaration, Open explanation
examples: The statement acted as an implicant of a deeper political intention. In Boolean algebra, each implicant represents a condition that makes the function true. His silence became an implicant that something was wrong. The evidence served as an implicant of the larger theory.

To shrink violently inward (physical). To experience a sudden loss of stability or structure (emotional or social).

examples: The old submarine imploded under the pressure of deep water. The company began to implode after years of internal conflict. His plans imploded when the funding was suddenly withdrawn. The building was designed to implode safely during demolition.

englishMeaning: Impossible to defeat, capture, or enter; very strongly defended. sindhiMeaning: ناقابلِ تسخير، جيڪو فتح يا ٽوڙڻ ناممڪن هجي، اهڙو مضبوط قلعو جاءِ يا خيال جيڪو دشمن لاءِ فتح ڪرڻ يا نقصان پهچائڻ ناممڪن هجي، صرف فوجي يا جسماني حفاظت تائين محدود ناهي پر مضبوط خيالن ۽ دليلن لاءِ به استعمال ٿئي ٿو

englishMeaning: An art movement that focuses on capturing the visual impression of a moment, especially the effects of light and color, rather than detailed realism. A style of painting developed in the 19th century, mainly in France. Artists try to capture how a scene looks at a particular moment, especially how light changes its appearance. The focus is on quick brush strokes, natural light, and everyday scenes instead of precise details.
synonyms: Impressionist art, Impressionistic style, Modern art movement, Real-time painting style (contextual)
antonyms: Realism, Naturalism, Academic art, Detailed classical painting
examples: Impressionism changed the way artists painted light and shadow. Monet is famous for his contribution to Impressionism. The museum has a large collection of Impressionism artworks. Impressionism focuses more on feeling than on fine detail.
sindhiMeaning: هڪ اهڙي فن تحريڪ جنهن ۾ ڪنهن منظر جي تفصيل بدران روشني ۽ رنگن جا تاثر ڏيکاريا ويندا آهن، اڻويهين صدي ۾ فرانس ۾ شروع ٿيل هڪ فن تحريڪ آهي، هن ۾ مصور منظر کي ان لمحي جيئن نظر اچي ٿو تيئن ڏيکارڻ جي ڪوشش ڪندا آهن خاص طور تي روشني ۽ قدرتي رنگن تي ڌيان ڏنو ويندو آهي

englishMeaning: Unplanned or spontaneous. Done without being planned, prepared, or rehearsed. Spontaneous or improvised action or speech. Occurring suddenly, often unexpectedly.

antonyms: Out of trouble, Safe, Secure, Free, Untroubled

antonyms: Isolation, Separation, Disconnection, Silence, Noncommunication

antonyms: Deliver, Send, Release, Pass, Allow
examples: The defender intercepted the pass and ran towards the goal. Police intercepted the smuggled goods at the border. She intercepted the letter before it reached him. The missile was intercepted mid-air by the defense system. His intercept of the football changed the game. The spy's intercept of the secret letter prevented a disaster. The missile intercept saved the city.

antonyms: Encourage, Comfort, Reassure, Support, Calm, Strengthen
examples: The manager tried to intimidate the workers into accepting lower wages. Big dogs sometimes intimidate small children. He was intimidated by the strict teacher and stayed quiet. She refused to be intimidated by their threats.

englishMeaning: A substance that affects the mind or body and causes drunkenness, loss of control, or altered mental state. Any chemical substance, especially alcohol or drugs, that temporarily changes how the brain works. It can reduce awareness, slow reactions, and affect judgment. antonyms: Sobriety, Sobering agent, Clear-minded substance (contextual), Non-alcoholic substance
examples: Alcohol is a common intoxicant used in many countries. The doctor warned him about the harmful effects of intoxicants. Some plants contain natural intoxicants that affect the nervous system. Driving under the influence of any intoxicant is illegal.

examples: It was ironic that the fire station burned down. She found it ironic that the health coach was always unhealthy. It is ironic that he failed the safety test. The weather was ironic because it rained on the day they planned a beach picnic.

englishMeaning: In a way that is opposite to what is expected or intended, often in a surprising or funny way. synonyms: Surprisingly, Unexpectedly, Contradictorily, Paradoxically, In an ironic way
antonyms: Predictably, Expectedly, Naturally, Obviously, Normally
examples: Ironically, the fire station burned down during a fire. He studied hard for the exam but, ironically, he failed it. Ironically, the doctor who advised healthy eating died of a heart attack. She was afraid of water, but ironically became a swimming coach.

englishMeaning: A narrow strip of land connecting two larger land areas, usually with water on either side. antonyms: Peninsula, Island
examples: The Isthmus of Panama connects North and South America. Ancient civilizations often built cities along an isthmus for trade advantages. The soldiers defended the narrow isthmus against enemy forces. Ships pass through the canal that cuts across the isthmus.
sindhiMeaning: هڪ تنگ زميني پٽي جيڪا ٻن وڏن زمينن کي ڳنڍي ٿي ۽ ٻن پاڻيءَ وارن حصن کي الڳ ڪري ٿي
urduMeaning: ایک تنگ زمین کا ٹکڑا جو دو بڑے زمینی علاقوں کو جوڑتا ہے اور دو پانی کے حصوں کو الگ کرتا ہے

word: It takes two to make a quarrel
englishMeaning: A quarrel or fight usually happens because both sides contribute to the disagreement. One person alone cannot continue an argument if the other refuses to participate. Arguments grow when both people react emotionally. Disagreements need participation from both sides. Peace can be maintained if one person stays calm. Shared anger often creates conflict.
synonyms: Both sides are responsible, It takes two to tango, Conflict needs participation from both sides, Mutual disagreement, Shared responsibility in conflict
antonyms: One-sided blame, Innocent party, Peaceful understanding, Mutual harmony, Silent patience
examples: Ahmed and Ali kept insulting each other in class because it takes two to make a quarrel. My teacher advised us to stay calm during arguments because it takes two to make a quarrel. sindhiMeaning: تاڙي هڪ هٿ سان نه وڄندي آهي، جهيڙو ٿيڻ لاءِ ٻن ماڻهن جو شامل هجڻ ضروري هوندو آهي، جهيڙو ٻنهي ڌرين جي ردعمل سبب وڌندو آهي، جيڪڏهن هڪ ماڻهو خاموش رهي ته تڪرار گهٽجي سگهي ٿو، ڪاوڙ جو جواب ڪاوڙ سان ڏيڻ جهيڙي کي وڌائيندو آهي، صبر ۽ برداشت سان امن قائم رهي سگهي ٿو
urduMeaning: تالی ایک ہاتھہ سے نہیں بجتی، لڑائی یا جھگڑا ہونے کے لیے دونوں فریقوں کا شامل ہونا ضروری ہوتا ہے، جھگڑا دونوں کے ردعمل سے بڑھتا ہے، اگر ایک شخص خاموش رہے تو لڑائی رک سکتی ہے، غصے کا جواب غصے سے دینے سے تنازع بڑھتا ہے، صبر اور برداشت امن پیدا کرتے ہیں

englishMeaning: A situation or conflict usually involves two people, and both are responsible for it. Many actions, arguments, relationships, or problems cannot happen because of just one person. synonyms: Both sides are responsible, It needs cooperation from both sides, Shared responsibility, Two-way involvement
antonyms: One-sided responsibility, Only one person is guilty, Single-handed effort, One-way action
examples: The couple keeps blaming each other, but it takes two to tango. If the project failed, remember it takes two to tango between manager and worker. Don’t blame only him for the fight; it takes two to tango. In every argument, it takes two to tango, so both should reflect on their actions.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن به تڪرار يا تعلق ۾ ٻه ماڻهو شامل هوندا آهن ۽ ٻئي برابر ذميوار هوندا آهن، هڪ ماڻهو اڪيلو ذميوار نه هوندو آهي، هي اصطلاح عام طور تي رشتن يا تڪرارن ۾ استعمال ٿيندي آهي ته ٻنهي ڌرين جو حصو هوندو آهي
urduMeaning: کسی بھی تنازعہ تعلق یا مسئلے میں دونوں افراد برابر ذمہ دار ہوتے ہیں، ایک اکیلا ذمہ دار نہیں ہوتا، یہ کہاوت اکثر رشتوں اور جھگڑوں میں استعمال ہوتی ہے تاکہ یہ واضح کیا جا سکے کہ دونو افراد کی شراکت ہوتی ہے

englishMeaning: To repeat. To say or do something repeatedly. To repeat a process or action, often to improve or refine it.

examples: The designer iterated the app interface until it looked perfect. Software developers iterate their code to fix bugs and improve performance. The teacher iterated the instructions to ensure every student understood. During the meeting, she iterated her key points several times.
sindhiMeaning: دهرائڻ، ڪنهن شيءَ کي ٻيهر ورجائڻ، عمل کي بهتر بڻائڻ لاءِ ٻيهر انجام ڏيڻ

englishMeaning: The process of repeating something, usually to improve it or reach a desired outcome. A single repetition or version in a sequence of attempts. In computing, a step in a loop or repeated process. An instance of doing something again in a systematic way.
synonyms: Repetition, Version, Cycle, Revision, Loop
antonyms: Original, First attempt, Single instance, Unique

sindhiMeaning: ورجائڻ يا ٻيهر عمل ڪرڻ جو عمل، هڪ مرحلو يا ورجن جيڪو ورجائڻ سان پيدا ٿئي، ڪمپيوٽنگ ۾ هڪ لوپ جو هڪ قدم، ڪنهن ڪم کي منظم طريقي سان ٻيهر ڪرڻ

englishMeaning: Traveling from place to place, especially for work. Traveling worker. Wandering person. Nomadic professional. Moving preacher or teacher. Someone who moves regularly from one location to another, often without staying long, usually for employment, trade, or duty

antonyms: Settled, Stationary, Fixed, Permanent, Resident

englishMeaning: A planned route or schedule of a journey. A document or plan that outlines the sequence of places to visit, activities to do, and the timing of each step during a trip. It helps travelers organize their journey efficiently.

englishMeaning: To poke, hit, or prod quickly, often repeatedly, usually with a finger, stick, or object. To criticize, tease, mock, or make sharp comments about someone or something repeatedly.

englishMeaning: Feeling tired, bored, or no longer interested due to too much experience. A person who has lost enthusiasm, excitement, or freshness because of overuse, repeated experiences, or emotional exhaustion.
synonyms: Weary, Bored, Exhausted, Disenchanted, Tired
antonyms: Fresh, Enthusiastic, Energetic, Excited, Interested
examples: After years of the same job, he felt jaded and unmotivated. She looked jaded after attending too many social events. The traveler was jaded by constant delays and long journeys. He sounded jaded when talking about politics.

englishMeaning: Unrefined natural sugar made from sugarcane juice or palm sap, usually brown in color, used widely in Asia and Africa for cooking and sweetening. It is less processed than white sugar and retains more minerals.
synonyms: Brown sugar, Unrefined sugar

urduMeaning: دبانا، بڑھنے سے روکنا یا نیچے رکھنا، کسی چیز کو قابو میں رکھنا تاکہ وہ زیادہ نہ ہو جیسے خرچ شور یا جذبات، اس کا مطلب یہ بھی ہو سکتا ہے کہ خود کو نمایاں ہونے سے بچانا یا خطرے سے بچنے کے لیے نیچے رہنا

englishMeaning: To prevent oneself or someone from doing something. To avoid doing something oneself. To withhold something from someone. To protect or shield someone or something from harm or trouble. To refrain from expressing a feeling or action.
synonyms: Prevent, Hinder, Stop
antonyms: Allow, Permit
examples: I couldn’t keep from laughing. Keep from touching the hot stove. She kept herself from crying. We must keep from wasting time.

englishMeaning: To remain inside or to continue having something such as contact, control, or possession. To hold back feelings or speech. To include or keep something in mind. To not share information.
synonyms: Contain, Confine, Retain
antonyms: Release, Free
examples: The teacher kept the students in after class. I kept in my anger. Keep the cat in during the night. He kept in his feelings. Please keep in touch while you are abroad. The news was kept in to avoid panic.
sindhiMeaning: اندر رکڻ، ٻاهر نه وڃڻ ڏيڻ، اندر رهڻ، لاڳاپو برقرار رکڻ، راز ۾ رکڻ، ذهن ۾ رکڻ يا شامل ڪرڻ، احساسن يا ڳالهين کي قابو ۾ رکڻ
urduMeaning: اندر رکھنا، باہر نہ جانے دینا، اندر رہنا، رابطہ برقرار رکھنا، جذبات یا باتوں کو قابو میں رکھنا، ذہن میں رکھنا یا شامل کرنا، راز میں رکھنا

englishMeaning: To stay away from something or not touch or step on it. (Used especially on warning signs to protect property, plants, or unsafe areas.)
synonyms: Avoid, Stay away, Abstain
antonyms: Approach, Indulge

sindhiMeaning: پري رهڻ، هٿ نه لڳائڻ، نه هلڻ يا نه ڇهڻ، لاڳاپو نه رکڻ، پاسو ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: دور رہنا، ہاتھ نہ لگانا، نہ چلنا یا نہ چھونا، پرہیز کرنا، استعمال نہ کرنا، دخل نہ دینا

englishMeaning: To prevent entry; not allow someone to enter a place. To stay away from something; avoid participation or involvement. To exclude from participation or influence. To resist or prevent something from affecting.
synonyms: Stay away, Avoid, Exclude, Block, Bar
antonyms: Enter, Join, Allow in, Participate, Include
examples: Keep out of the restricted area for your safety. He tried to keep out of the argument between his friends. Please keep out strangers from the private garden. She keeps out of trouble by following the rules.

englishMeaning: To follow, stick with, or stay on something. To continue doing something consistently, follow a rule, plan, schedule, or path, or to restrict oneself to a particular topic, route, or routine.
synonyms: Follow, Adhere, Abide
antonyms: Ignore, Disobey
examples: Keep to the path. Try to keep to your budget. He kept to the topic. Please keep to your word.
sindhiMeaning: پابند رهڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ تي قائم رهڻ، پيروي ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ڪم رستي قانون يا شيءَ سان مستقل طور تي لڳل رهڻ يا ان جي پيروي ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: پابند رہنا، کسی چیز پر قائم رہنا، عمل کرنا، کسی کام قانون منصوبہ یا راستے پر مستقل طور پر عمل کرنا یا اس کے پابند رہنا

englishMeaning: To maintain or continue at the same level. To continue doing something at the same rate, pace, or standard; to remain informed about something. To not fall behind.
synonyms: Maintain, Continue, Match pace
antonyms: Fall behind, Stop
examples: Keep up the good work!. She can’t keep up with the others. Keep up your studies. Prices are kept up by demand.
sindhiMeaning: جاري رکڻ، ساڳئي رفتار سان هلڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي جاري رکڻ يا رفتار، معيار يا ڄاڻ ۾ پوئتي نه رهڻ
urduMeaning: جاری رکھنا، ایک ہی رفتار پر چلنا، برقرار رکھنا، کسی کام یا معیار کو قائم رکھنا یا کسی معلومات میں پیچھے نہ رہنا

englishMeaning: Neat and well-groomed. Refers to someone or something that is clean, tidy, orderly, and well-maintained in appearance.
synonyms: Neat, Tidy, Well-groomed, Smart, Spruce
antonyms: Untidy, Messy, Unkempt, Sloppy, Disheveled
examples: She always looks kempt, even after a long day at work. The kempt garden showed the gardener’s dedication. His kempt appearance impressed the interview panel. The hotel rooms were kempt and ready for guests.

englishMeaning: The extreme or irrational fear of thunder and lightning. A specific phobia in which a person experiences intense fear, anxiety, or panic when they hear thunder or see lightning. The fear may occur during storms or even at the thought of stormy weather. It can lead to avoidance behavior, stress, and physical symptoms like sweating or trembling.
synonyms: Astraphobia, Brontophobia, Fear of storms, Lightning fear, Thunder anxiety
antonyms: Fearlessness, Courage, Calmness during storms, Bravery, Composure
examples: She suffers from keraunophobia and hides in a closed room during thunderstorms. His keraunophobia became worse after he experienced a severe lightning strike as a child. People with keraunophobia often check weather reports frequently to avoid storms. Despite his keraunophobia, he tries to stay calm when thunder starts at night.
sindhiMeaning: گوڙ ۽ بجليءَ کان حد کان وڌيڪ يا غير معقول خوف، هي هڪ نفسياتي خوف آهي جنهن ۾ ماڻهو گوڙ واري موسم يا بجليءَ جي چمڪ کان شديد ڊپ محسوس ڪري ٿو ۽ پريشاني ۾ مبتلا ٿي سگهي ٿو
urduMeaning: گرج چمک اور بجلی (آسمانی بجلی اور گرج) سے حد سے زیادہ اور غیر ضروری خوف، یہ ایک نفسیاتی کیفیت ہے جس میں فرد بادلوں کی گرج یا بجلی کی چمک سے شدید خوف محسوس کرتا ہے حتیٰ کہ موسم کا اندازہ ہوتے ہی گھبراہٹ شروع ہو سکتی ہے

englishMeaning: A situation in which people become upset, confused, or angry over something, usually something minor. It often involves loud disagreement, disorder, or unnecessary excitement about a small issue.
synonyms: Commotion, Uproar, Fuss, Hubbub, Ruckus, Disturbance
antonyms: Calm, Peace, Harmony, Order, Quiet
examples: There was a kerfuffle in the office after the email was sent to the wrong person. The children caused a kerfuffle when they started arguing over the toy. A small pricing error created a huge kerfuffle among customers. The politician tried to calm the kerfuffle caused by his statement.

englishMeaning: The correct explanation or solution to a mystery, problem, or puzzle. Something that allows entry, control, or access to a place, system, or opportunity. A guide that explains symbols, signs, or codes in a chart, map, or text.
synonyms: Vital to, Fundamental to, Central to
antonyms: Irrelevant to, Unimportant to, Insignificant to, Minor to
examples: The witness gave the key to the mystery. Communication is the key to a healthy relationship. Education is the key to a better future. Practice is the key to mastering any skill. Confidence is the key to public speaking. Use the key to understand the map symbols.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن راز، مسئلي يا ڳجهارت جو حل يا وضاحت، ڪنهن جاءِ يا موقعي تائين پهچ حاصل ڪرڻ جو ذريعو، نقشو يا چارٽ ۾ نشانين جي وضاحت ڪندڙ فهرست
urduMeaning: کسی راز، مسئلے یا پہیلی کا حل یا وضاحت، کسی جگہ یا موقع تک رسائی حاصل کرنے کا ذریعہ، قشے یا چارٹ میں علامتوں کی وضاحت کرنے والی فہرست

englishMeaning: To make someone more alert, focused, or energetic. To increase tension or anticipation in a situation. To enter data or information into a system (less common, in computing context). To stimulate emotions or reactions in a group or individual.
synonyms: Stimulate, Excite, Energize, Provoke, Intensify, Alert
antonyms: Calm, Relax, Soothe, Depress, Dull
examples: The speaker keyed up the audience with an inspiring story. The tension in the courtroom keyed up as the verdict was announced. He keyed up all the customer orders into the system before lunch. The trainer keyed up the athletes before the championship.
sindhiMeaning: جوش ۾ آڻڻ، تيار ڪرڻ، چست ڪرڻ، جذبات يا ڪشش وڌائڻ، معلومات يا ڊيٽا داخل ڪرڻ (ڪمپيوٽر ۾)، گروپ يا فرد ۾ جوش يا جذبو پيدا ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: جوش دلانا، تیار کرنا، چوکنا کرنا، جذبات یا تناو بڑھانا، معلومات یا ڈیٹا داخل کرنا (کمپیوٹر میں)، گروپ یا فرد میں جوش یا ردعمل پیدا کرنا

englishMeaning: To discuss or talk about an idea informally before making a decision. To move or travel from one place to another without a clear purpose. (British informal) To spend time aimlessly or casually.

examples: We kicked about the idea of moving abroad. They kicked about some business plans. The topic was just kicked about at lunch. Let’s not just kick about, let’s decide.
sindhiMeaning: ڳالهائڻ، بحث ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ڳالهه تي غير رسمي طرح بحث يا صلاح ڪرڻ، ڪنهن جاءِ تي بي مقصد يا بي رخ گهمڻ
urduMeaning: کسی خیال یا منصوبے پر غیر رسمی گفتگو کرنا، بغیر مقصد کے اِدھر اُدھر گھومنا یا وقت گزارنا

englishMeaning: To resist or protest something. Relax after hard work. To react strongly or forcefully. Can also mean to return money illegally (bribe).
synonyms: Resist, Oppose, Defy, Rebel
antonyms: Accept, Obey, Comply, Agree
examples: He always kicks against authority. They kicked against the unfair decision. Children often kick against strict rules. She kicked against her parents’ expectations.
sindhiMeaning: مخالفت ڪرڻ يا بغاوت ڪرڻ، مزاحمت ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: مخالفت کرنا یا بغاوت کرنا، احتجاج یا مزاحمت کرنا

englishMeaning: To sit comfortably and rest without stress. Money given secretly in return for favor or business. To react suddenly or violently (machine/gun). To respond strongly or aggressively.
synonyms: Relax, Rest, React, Recline
antonyms: Work, Strain, Calm down, Freeze
examples: After work, I just want to kick back and watch TV. The horse kicked back when someone touched it. The manager was accused of kicking back money to suppliers. Let’s kick back and enjoy the weekend.

urduMeaning: سکون سے بیٹھنا اور آرام کرنا، خفیہ طور پر فائدہ کے بدلے پیسے دینا، مشین یا ہتھیار کا پیچھے کی طرف زور سے جانا، سخت ردعمل دینا

englishMeaning: To begin to take effect or start working (often used for medicines, plans, systems, or reactions). To contribute or add something, especially money or effort.
synonyms: Begin, Start
antonyms: Cease, End
examples: The painkillers kicked in after ten minutes. The law will kick in next month. The new system kicked in smoothly. His training kicked in during the emergency.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ جو اثر شروع ٿيڻ (جهڙوڪ دوائن، قانونن يا نظام جو)، ڪنهن ڪم ۾ مدد يا حصو ڏيڻ (پئسن يا ڪوشش جي صورت ۾)
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کا اثر ظاہر ہونا، جیسے دوا یا نظام کا عمل میں آنا، کسی کام میں پیسے یا مدد کے طور پر حصہ ڈالنا

englishMeaning: To begin or start something. To indicate the start of an event, activity, process, or action. It can also mean to remove something by kicking, or in informal contexts, to get angry.
synonyms: Launch, Commence, Initiate, Open

synonyms: Expel, Dismiss
antonyms: Admit, Welcome
examples: He was kicked out of school. They kicked out the rude customer. The tenant was kicked out for not paying rent. She kicked him out of the car. The teacher kicked the noisy students out of the class.

englishMeaning: To overturn or knock something down accidentally. En relax after hard work. To react strongly or forcefully. Can also mean to return money illegally (bribe).
synonyms: Overturn, Knock down, Tip over
antonyms: Set upright, Lift, Balance
examples: He kicked over the bucket of paint by mistake. The child kicked over his toys. The engine kicked over but didn’t start. She kicked over the stool while dancing.

urduMeaning: لات مار کر کسی چیز کو گرا دینا یا مشین کو چلانا، شروع ہونا، اچانک ردِعمل دینا یا بغاوت کرنا

englishMeaning: To die. A very informal idiom used to say that someone has died. It is often used in a humorous or indirect way instead of saying “die” directly.
synonyms: Pass away, Die, Breathe last, Depart this life, Perish
antonyms: Be born, Come to life, Survive, Live, Exist
examples: My old neighbor finally kicked the bucket at the age of ninety. The car was so old that it looked like it would kick the bucket any day. He joked that his phone would kick the bucket after years of use. Many soldiers kicked the bucket during the war.

englishMeaning: To cause trouble or anger by doing or saying something that upsets many people. To create a situation full of problems, anger, or conflict that is difficult to control afterward.

antonyms: Calm the situation, Restore peace, Avoid conflict, Settle issues

By questioning the leader’s decision, she kicked the hornet’s nest. Posting that controversial comment online was like kicking the hornet’s nest.
sindhiMeaning: اهڙو ڪم ڪرڻ يا ڳالهه چوڻ جنهن سان ماڻهن ۾ غصو، جهيڙو يا تڪرار پيدا ٿئي، ڪنهن حساس يا خطرناڪ معاملي کي چھيڙڻ ۽ ان سان تڪليف يا ڏکيائي پيدا ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: ایسا عمل یا بات کرنا جس سے لوگوں میں غصہ، ہنگامہ یا تنازعہ پیدا ہو جائے، کسی خطرناک یا حساس مسئلے کو چھیڑ کر حالات کو بگاڑ دینا

englishMeaning: To cause trouble or start a disturbance. Du relax after hard work. To react strongly or forcefully. Can also mean to return money illegally (bribe).
synonyms: Complain, Protest, Agitate, Rise
antonyms: Calm down, Settle, Soothe, Lower
examples: The students kicked up a fuss about the new rules. The wind kicked up a lot of dust. The kids kicked up when asked to go to bed early. Prices kicked up after the announcement.

urduMeaning: شور مچانا یا مسئلہ کھڑا کرنا، جھگڑا کھڑا کرنا، تنازع یا فساد پیدا کرنا، سخت احتجاج کرنا

englishMeaning: To give a strong or energetic start to a process, activity, or project, often to overcome inertia or delay. It can also mean jump-starting something to make it function efficiently.
synonyms: Initiate, Energize, Launch, Activate, Jump-start, Stimulate
antonyms: Stop, Halt, Delay, Slow, Postpone
examples: The manager tried to kick-start the new marketing campaign with a big launch event. I need a strong cup of coffee to kick-start my day. The government launched a program to kick-start economic growth in rural areas. A short motivational speech helped kick-start the team’s energy before the match.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڪم يا منصوبي کي زور سان شروع ڪرڻ، جيئن اهو جلدي اڳتي وڌي يا مؤثر طور تي ڪم ڪرڻ لڳي
urduMeaning: کسی کام، منصوبے یا سرگرمی کو طاقت یا توانائی کے ساتھ شروع کرنا تاکہ وہ تیزی سے آگے بڑھے یا مؤثر طور پر کام کرے

word: Kill two birds with one stone
englishMeaning: To achieve two goals or solve two problems with a single action or effort. Doing one thing that brings double benefit.
synonyms: Do double work, Be efficient

examples: He killed two birds with one stone by shopping and visiting friends. By driving my friend to the airport and doing some shopping on the way back, I killed two birds with one stone. She improved her English and made new friends at the same time, killing two birds with one stone. Walking to work helps me exercise and save money on transport, it’s like killing two birds with one stone.
sindhiMeaning: هڪ ئي ڪم سان ٻه فائدا حاصل ڪرڻ، هڪ ئي ڪوشش سان ٻه مقصد پورا ڪرڻ، ھڪڙي تير سان ٻہ شڪار

englishMeaning: A person who has the same ideas, feelings, interests, or nature as another person. A person who feels very similar to you in thoughts, emotions, values, interests, or attitude. It is used for someone with whom you feel a natural connection, understanding, or closeness because both of you think or feel in much the same way.
synonyms: Like minded person, Soulmate, Kindred soul, Kindred mind, Kindred heart, Kindred being, Kindred companion, Kindred friend, Bosom friend, Kindred one

examples: When I met Sara, I felt I had found a kindred spirit because we both loved books and quiet places. In a new city, finding a kindred spirit made her feel less lonely and more understood.
sindhiMeaning: اهڙو ماڻهو جيڪو اوهان جهڙا خيال احساس يا دلچسپيون رکي، هم خيال ماڻهو، هم مزاج شخص، دل سان ويجهو ماڻهو، ساڳي طبيعت وارو، ساڳين دلچسپين وارو دوست

englishMeaning: The fear of zombies or fear of the dead moving. It is a specific phobia where a person feels extreme anxiety or panic at the thought or sight of zombies or animated corpses. Fear of zombies or moving dead.
synonyms: Zombie phobia, Fear of the undead, Necrophobia
antonyms: Fearlessness, Courage, Bravery
examples: He could not watch horror movies because of his kinemortophobia. Kinemortophobia made her avoid Halloween events with zombie costumes. Even a cartoon with zombies triggered his kinemortophobia. The documentary on ancient burial practices worsened his kinemortophobia.

englishMeaning: Related to motion or movement. Something that is produced by movement or is connected with physical motion. It is commonly used in science, especially physics, to describe energy that an object has because it is moving.
synonyms: Moving, Dynamic, Active, Motional
antonyms: Static, Still, Stationary, Motionless

englishMeaning: A marriage between a man and a woman arranged to hide one or both partners’ true sexual orientation, usually for social, cultural, or professional reasons. Such marriages were more common in the past when social stigma, legal restrictions, or career risks made it difficult for LGBTQ individuals to live openly. The term is often associated with early Hollywood, politics, or conservative societies where public image was very important.
synonyms: Marriage of convenience, Sham marriage, Cover marriage, Strategic marriage, Protective marriage
antonyms: Love marriage, Genuine marriage, Romantic marriage, Open same sex marriage
examples: The actor entered into a lavender marriage to protect his career in a conservative era. Historians believe several celebrities in the early film industry had lavender marriages. Their lavender marriage allowed both partners to maintain their public image. In some societies, a lavender marriage was seen as a safer option than coming out openly.

sindhiMeaning: بي مقصد بيهڻ، بي مقصد گهمڻ، بيڪار بيهڻ، سست رفتاري سان هلڻ، ضرورت کان وڌيڪ بيهڻ يا بي مقصد گهمڻ، بنا ڪم جي هنڌ هنڌ رلڻ، انتظار يا بيزاري ۾ وقت ڪڍڻ، شڪي انداز ۾ هڪ هنڌ تي رهڻ

englishMeaning: To look around. To turn your eyes around, to observe the surroundings, or to search around in different directions.
synonyms: Glance, Search

She paused in the garden to look about, enjoying the beauty of the flowers. When he entered the old house, he looked about to see if anyone was inside.

sindhiMeaning: چوڌاري ڏسڻ، ماحول جو جائزو وٺڻ، ڳولڻ، آس پاس جا ماحول ڏسڻ
urduMeaning: چاروں طرف دیکھنا، اِدھر اُدھر دیکھنا، ارد گرد جائزہ لینا، تلاش کرنا

englishMeaning: To think about and plan for the future. Refers to anticipating future events, opportunities, or challenges, and preparing for them mentally, emotionally, or practically. It implies foresight, planning, and proactive thinking rather than reacting only when events occur.
synonyms: Plan ahead, Anticipate, Foresee, Prepare, Strategize
antonyms: Ignore, Neglect, Procrastinate, Overlook, React
examples: We must look ahead to future challenges. She’s always looking ahead in her career. It’s time to look ahead rather than dwell on the past. Investors look ahead before making decisions.

englishMeaning: To explore a new place. To search casually. To observe surroundings. To turn your head or eyes in different directions to see what is nearby.
synonyms: Observe, Scan, Search, Explore
antonyms: Ignore, Overlook, Stay focused
examples: We looked around the old city during our trip. I looked around the room but couldn’t find my phone. It’s good to look around before making a big decision. We looked around the city before deciding where to eat.

englishMeaning: To direct your eyes towards someone or something. To consider, think about, or examine carefully. To regard someone/something in a particular way. To read, check, or review something.
synonyms: Observe, Watch
antonyms: Ignore, Overlook
examples: Look at that beautiful painting. The doctor will look at your injury. We need to look at the problem from another angle. Please look at my essay and give feedback.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ يا ماڻهو ڏانهن نظر ڪرڻ، غور سان ڏسڻ ۽ پرکڻ، اهو جسماني نظر وجهڻ سان گڏوگڏ سوچڻ ۽ تجزيو ڪرڻ لاءِ به استعمال ٿئي ٿو

englishMeaning: To turn your eyes aside or ignore. To turn your eyes in another direction or to avoid seeing or noticing something. It can also mean to ignore something unpleasant or embarrassing.
synonyms: Ignore, Avoid, Disregard
antonyms: Notice, Observe, Face
examples: She looked away when the injured animal appeared on the screen. He looked away to hide his tears. You cannot look away from the truth forever. The child looked away shyly when the teacher smiled at him.
sindhiMeaning: رخ موڙڻ، نظر ڦيرائڻ، ڪنھن ڳالهه منظر کان پاسو ڪرڻ، نظر يا چهرو ٻي پاسي ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: منہ یا نظر دوسری طرف کر لینا، کسی چیز سے گریز کرنا، نظر ہٹا لینا یا رخ موڑ لینا، نظرانداز کرنا، چشم پوشی کرنا

englishMeaning: Think carefully about the possible results before taking any action. A person should think carefully, examine the situation, and understand the risks before making a decision or taking action. It advises people not to act in haste or excitement because careless decisions may lead to trouble, loss, or regret.
synonyms: Think before acting, Be cautious, Act wisely, Use caution, Consider carefully, Be careful, Use good judgment
antonyms: Act rashly, Jump to conclusions, Be reckless, Act without thinking, Rush blindly
examples: Before investing all his savings in a new business, Ali remembered to look before he leaped. She accepted the job offer without checking the company properly, and later realized she should have looked before she leaped. Buying a house is a major decision, so it is wise to look before you leap. Students should look before they leap when choosing a career path.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن به ڪم ڪرڻ کان اڳ چڱيءَ طرح سوچي سمجهي فيصلو ڪرڻ، ڪنهن به قدم کڻڻ کان اڳ حالتن فائدن ۽ نقصانن بابت غور ڪرڻ گهرجي، جلدي يا بنا سوچ جي فيصلا ڪرڻ نقصان جو سبب بڻجي سگهي ٿو
urduMeaning: کسی بھی کام کو کرنے سے پہلے اچھی طرح سوچ سمجھ لینا، کسی بھی قدم یا فیصلے سے پہلے اچھی طرح غور و فکر کرنا چاہیے، جلد بازی میں کیے گئے فیصلے نقصان یا پچھتاوے کا باعث بن سکتے ہیں

englishMeaning: To try to find someone or something. To search, seek, or expect.
synonyms: Search, Seek
antonyms: Ignore, Miss
examples: I am looking for my keys; I think I lost them in the car. She is looking for a new job in Karachi. They are looking for a solution to the problem. We are looking for someone who can speak English, Sindhi, and Urdu.

englishMeaning: To feel excited or pleased about something that is going to happen in the future. Anticipate with pleasure.
synonyms: Anticipate, Await eagerly, Be excited about, Expect with pleasure
antonyms: Dread, Fear, Be anxious about, Avoid
examples: I look forward to meeting you. She looks forward to her holidays. We’re looking forward to your visit. They look forward to good news.

englishMeaning: To make a short visit to someone, usually informally. To inspect or check on a person, place, or situation. To appear in a place, often unexpectedly.
synonyms: Visit briefly, Check on, Drop by, Call on
antonyms: Ignore, Avoid, Bypass, Neglect
examples: I’ll look in on my parents this evening. Can you look in on the baby while I cook? She looked in at the shop while passing by. The manager looked in to see if everything was okay
sindhiMeaning: مختصر ملاقات ڪرڻ، ڪنهن جي گھر يا جاءِ تي مختصر طور وڃڻ، ڪنهن يا ڪنهن حالت جي جاچ ڪرڻ، ڪنهن جاءِ تي اچڻ، اڪثر اڻڄاڻايل طريقي سان
urduMeaning: مختصر ملاقات کرنا، کسی کے گھر یا مقام پر مختصر طور پر جانا، کسی شخص یا حالت کی جانچ کرنا، کسی جگہ پر اچانک یا غیر متوقع طور پر نمودار ہونا

englishMeaning: To search for something where it is not actually present or cannot be found. To waste time or effort searching for something in an unsuitable or incorrect location or situation. It is often used when someone is not able to find a solution or answer because they are focusing on the wrong source or direction.
synonyms: Misguided search, Wrong approach, Searching in vain, Misplaced effort, Off track
antonyms: Looking in the right place, Correct approach, Accurate search, Proper direction, Right focus
examples: He has been looking for his keys in the kitchen, but he is looking in the wrong place. If you are blaming your teammates, you are looking in the wrong place. She was looking for happiness in money, but she was looking in the wrong place. You are looking in the wrong place if you think success comes without effort.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ کي اهڙي هنڌ ڳولڻ جتي اها موجود ئي نه هجي، جڏهن ڪو ماڻهو ڪنهن شيءِ کي اهڙي هنڌ يا طريقي سان ڳولي رهيو هجي جتي اها ملي ئي نه سگهي ۽ هو غلط رخ ۾ ڪوشش ڪري رهيو هجي، جتي ڪو ماڻهو اصل مسئلي کي سمجهڻ بدران غلط سبب تي ڌيان ڏئي رهيو هجي

englishMeaning: To examine, investigate, or study something carefully in order to understand it or find out the truth.
synonyms: Explore, Scrutinize, Check
antonyms: Neglect, Ignore
examples: The police will look into the matter. The committee will look into the causes of the recent flood to prevent it in the future. She promised to look into the matter and get back with a solution. The teacher decided to look into why so many students failed the test.
sindhiMeaning: جاچڻ، تحقيق ڪرڻ، غور سان ڏسڻ، ڄاڻڻ لاءِ غور سان ڏسڻ

antonyms: Look out of place
examples: He really looks the part of a CEO. You need to look the part for the audition. She looked the part of a princess at the ball. He doesn’t look the part of a teacher.
