sindhiMeaning: ڳولهڻ، معلومات ڏسڻ، ڪنهن ڪتاب ڊڪشنري يا آن لائن ذريعن ۾ ڄاڻ ڳولڻ، حالتون بهتر ٿيڻ يا ڪنهن جي موڊ يا صورتحال کي سڌارڻ، اکيون ڪنهن شيءِ ڏانهن ڪرڻ

word: Look what the cat dragged in
englishMeaning: A playful or sarcastic way of saying that someone has arrived, especially when they are unexpected, late, or not welcome. An informal and humorous expression used when someone shows up in a place after being absent or late. synonyms: Long time no see, Well, Look who’s here, Who do we have here, Guess who showed up
antonyms: Glad to see you, Welcome, Nice to meet you, Happy you arrived
examples: Look what the cat dragged in! We thought you forgot about us. Well, look what the cat dragged in, the late guest has finally arrived. Look what the cat dragged in, haven’t seen you in months!. Oh, look what the cat dragged in, Mr always-late is here again.

englishMeaning: To take care of someone or something.
synonyms: Care for, Tend

englishMeaning: To think about or remember the past, To turn one’s eyes backward.

englishMeaning: To respect or admire someone.
synonyms: Respect, Admire

englishMeaning: To form a circle or repeat. To bend or twist something into a circular shape, or to cause an action, sound, or process to repeat continuously. A circular or curved shape. antonyms: Line, End, Break, Stop, Straight Path

englishMeaning: To return to an earlier point or topic. To go back physically to a previous place, or to return in conversation, thinking, planning, or communication to something discussed or done before.
synonyms: Return, Go back, Revisit, Come back
antonyms: Move forward, Proceed, Advance, Continue
examples: We need to loop back to the main issue before making a decision. The road loops back to the village after the bridge. Let me loop back to you once I confirm the details. The discussion looped back to budget concerns again.

englishMeaning: To include someone in information or a process. To intentionally involve someone by sharing information, keeping them informed, or making them part of a discussion, decision, or activity, especially in work or planning contexts

antonyms: Exclude, Leave Out, Omit, Ignore, Keep in the dark
examples: Please loop me in on any updates about the project. She looped the finance team in before finalizing the budget. Make sure to loop the manager in if the plan changes. He was looped in late, so he missed the earlier discussion.

englishMeaning: To come out of a loop, cycle, or repeated pattern. To exit or break free from a repeated cycle, process, or circular movement. synonyms: Break out, Exit, Come out, Escape, Stop repeating
antonyms: Loop in, Repeat, Continue, Cycle, Reenter
examples: The program will loop out once the condition is met. She felt relieved when she finally looped out of the same daily routine. Pull the wire gently so it can loop out without breaking. The system failed to loop out and kept repeating the same command.
sindhiMeaning: لوپ مان ٻاهر نڪرڻ، ورجاءَ واري چڪر مان آزاد ٿيڻ، ڪنهن کي ڳالهه ٻولهه مان ڪڍي ڇڏڻ

antonyms: Skip, Ignore, Bypass, Single pass
examples: We need to loop over all the files to check for errors. The program will loop over each item in the list until it finds a match. She likes to loop over her notes before exams. The robot will loop over its instructions until the task is complete.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنھن عمل کي ورجائڻ يا هر شيءِ کي هڪ هڪ ڪري ڏسڻ، ڪنهن لسٽ يا سيڪونس ۾ هر عنصر کي هڪ هڪ ڪري پروسيس ڪرڻ، عام طور تي ڪمپيوٽر پروگرامنگ يا منظم ڪم ۾

englishMeaning: Uneven or not balanced on one side. Tilted, heavier, or larger on one side than the other. It can refer to physical objects, situations, or comparisons that are unfair or unequal.
synonyms: Uneven, Tilted, Off-center, Asymmetrical, Skewed, Biased
antonyms: Balanced, Even, Symmetrical, Fair, Straight
examples: The painting looked lopsided because it was hung too high on one side. The election results were lopsided, favoring one party heavily. His smile was slightly lopsided, giving him a quirky look. The table is lopsided because one leg is shorter than the others.

englishMeaning: Talkativeness, the habit of speaking a lot. A tendency to talk continuously or excessively. It often describes someone who enjoys speaking at length, sometimes more than necessary or expected.
synonyms: Talkativeness, Verbosity, Garrulity, Chattiness, Volubility
antonyms: Silence, Reticence, Taciturnity, Quietness, Reserve

englishMeaning: To get money, food, etc from somebody else instead of paying for it yourself. To walk slowly with no particular purpose. To be somewhere not doing very much.
synonyms: Beg, Scrounge, Borrow, Loaf, Wander, Hang about, Parasite
antonyms: Pay, Earn, Buy, Contribute, Work, Provide
examples:
He's happy to mooch around the house all day.
We had coffee then mooched down to the beach. He's always mooching off his friends. He always mooches cigarettes.

antonyms: Independent, Self-reliant, Hard-working, Contributor, Giver, Supporter
examples: Don’t be such a moocher; pay for your own meal. He lost many friends because he was known as a moocher. One of my brothers was a moocher and drug addict.

synonyms: Propose, Put forward, Argue
antonyms: Irrefutable, Censor

sindhiMeaning: قابل بحث،صلح جوڳو، زير بحث، تڪراري، تقرير ڪرڻ، بحث ڪرڻ، تڪرار ڪرڻ

englishMeaning: A foolish or stupid person. A person of subnormal intelligence. A rude way to refer to somebody that you think is very stupid.

antonyms: Intellect, Intellectual, Sage, Thinker, Genius
examples: Don't leave it there, you moron!. Some moron smashed into the back of my car yesterday. They're a bunch of morons. The people responsible for this are mindless morons.

englishMeaning: Something that will die or cannot live forever. Anything living that is subject to death. Causing death or capable of causing death. A human, especially in contrast to a divine being. Very strong or extreme (mortal fear, mortal hatred). It can also describe something severe, extreme, or related to human weakness and limitations.
synonyms: Human, Earthly, Perishable, Fatal, Deadly, Severe
antonyms: Immortal, Eternal, Undying, Imperishable
examples: All humans are mortal, so life should be valued. The hero received a mortal wound during the battle. She felt a mortal fear when the earthquake started. The story reminds us that even kings are mortal.
sindhiMeaning: جيڪو مرڻ وارو هجي يا هميشه لاءِ نه رهي سگهي، جيڪو موت جو سبب بڻجي سگهي، عام انسان جيڪو خدا يا ديوتا نه هجي، انتهائي شديد يا سخت، هر اها شي يا انسان جنھن کي مرڻو يا ختم ٿيڻو آھي (فنا/فاني)، اهو لفظ انساني ڪمزوري يا سخت خطري لاءِ به استعمال ٿئي ٿو

englishMeaning: The state of being mortal or subject to death. The number of deaths in a given population. Human weakness or vulnerability. A reminder that life is temporary. antonyms: Immortality, Eternal life, Survival
examples: Doctors are studying the rise in mortality among young adults. The story reminds us of human mortality. Better healthcare has reduced child mortality in many countries. The flood caused a high mortality rate in the affected villages.

englishMeaning: A bowl-shaped tool used for crushing or grinding substances. A type of explosive weapon that fires shells at a high angle. A mixture used in building to bind bricks or stones. antonyms: Loose material, Separation, Detacher, Disconnector

englishMeaning: To use property as security for a loan. A loan taken to buy property, where the property itself is used as security until the loan is fully paid. A legal agreement in which a bank or financial institution lends money to a person to buy a house or land. The borrower agrees to repay the loan in installments. If they fail to repay, the lender has the right to take the property.
synonyms: Loan, Home loan, Pledge, Lien, Hypothecation (formal)
antonyms: Release, Freehold, Discharge, Redeem, Unencumbered ownership
examples: He took a mortgage to buy his first house. The bank approved her mortgage application last week. They are still paying off their mortgage after ten years. She mortgaged her property to start a business.

englishMeaning: To cut a hole or cavity into a material so another piece can fit tightly into it.  A rectangular hole or slot cut into a piece of wood, metal, or other material. englishMeaning: To make someone feel extremely embarrassed, ashamed, or humiliated. To check or curb one’s natural inclinations. To cause someone to feel self-conscious or humbled. To suppress or put an end to something unpleasant.

antonyms: Praise, Honor, Compliment, Encourage

englishMeaning: To cut a hole or cavity into a material so another piece can fit tightly into it.  A rectangular hole or slot cut into a piece of wood, metal, or other material. englishMeaning: To provide someone with a reason or incentive to act or behave in a certain way. To stimulate enthusiasm, drive, or interest in a person.

englishMeaning: Hair grown on the upper lip of a man.  Facial hair on the upper lip.

sindhiMeaning: عام ماڻهو، اهڙو ماڻهو جيڪو جادوي طاقت نه رکي ٿو ۽ جادوي دنيا کان واقف نه آهي، عام ڳالهه ۾، اهو ڪنهن به شعبي ۾ اڻڄاتل يا ناپوھ جو ماڻهو ٿي سگهي ٿو
urduMeaning: عام انسان، وہ شخص جس کے پاس جادوی صلاحیتیں نہیں ہوتیں اور وہ جادوی دنیا سے ناواقف ہوتا ہے، عام طور پر، یہ کسی خاص شعبے میں تجربہ نہ رکھنے والے شخص کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے

englishMeaning: A mule is an animal born from a male donkey and a female horse. It can also mean a stubborn person or someone who illegally carries goods.
synonyms: Animal, Stubborn person, Smuggler
antonyms: Flexible person, Agreeable person, Law enforcer, Officer
examples: The mule carried heavy loads across the mountains. Farmers prefer mules because they are strong and patient. He is as stubborn as a mule when making decisions. The police arrested a mule at the airport for smuggling drugs.
sindhiMeaning: هڪ جانور جيڪو گهوڙي ۽ گڏهه مان پيدا ٿئي ٿو، هڪ مضبوط ۽ محنتي جانور جيڪو بار کڻڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو آهي، مجازي طور ضدّي ماڻهو کي به چيو ويندو آهي، غير قانوني شيون کڻندڙ ماڻهو لاءِ به لفظ استعمال ٿئي ٿو
urduMeaning: خچر ایک جانور جو گھوڑی اور گدھے سے پیدا ہوتا ہے، خچر ایک طاقتور اور محنتی جانور جو وزن اٹھانے کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے، مجازی طور پر ضدی انسان کو بھی خچر کہا جاتا ہے، یہ لفظ غیر قانونی سامان لے جانے والے شخص کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے

englishMeaning: To think about something carefully and at length; to ponder or consider deeply. Also means to heat and spice wine or cider.
synonyms: Ponder, Contemplate, Consider, Reflect, Deliberate
antonyms: Ignore, Dismiss, Decide hastily, Overlook
examples: She mulled over the job offer for several days. He sat quietly, mulling the decision in his mind. They enjoyed a cup of mulled wine by the fireplace. She needs time to mull before making a final choice.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڳالهه تي ڊگهو سوچڻ يا غور ڪرڻ، وائن کي گرم ڪري مسالا ملائڻ
urduMeaning: کسی بات پر غور کرنا، سوچنا یا جائزہ لینا، شراب کو گرم کر کے مسالے ملانا

englishMeaning: To think carefully and at length about something before making a decision. To consider all aspects of a situation or problem slowly and thoroughly.
synonyms: Ponder, Deliberate, Consider, Reflect, Weigh up
antonyms: Rush, Decide hastily, Act impulsively
examples: I need a few days to mull over your proposal. She mulled over the decision before accepting the new job. He mulled over every possible outcome before acting. Take your time and mull over all the options.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن فيصلي کان اڳ ڪنهن ڳالهه تي ڊاهيءَ سان غور ڪرڻ، سڀ پاسا سوچڻ
urduMeaning: کسی فیصلے سے پہلے کسی بات پر گہرائی سے سوچنا، تمام پہلوؤں کا جائزہ لینا

englishMeaning: Involving more than two countries, parties, or groups. Agreements, discussions, or actions that include multiple sides, nations, or organizations, rather than just two. Often used in diplomacy, trade, or international relations.
synonyms: Many-sided, Multiple-party, Collective, Joint
antonyms: Bilateral, Unilateral, One-sided
examples: The UN promotes multilateral cooperation among nations. A multilateral trade agreement benefits all participating countries. Climate change requires a multilateral approach to find effective solutions. Multilateral negotiations were held to resolve the border dispute.
sindhiMeaning: گهڻ طرفي (گهڻن ڌرين سان لاڳاپيل)، ڪنهن معاهدي ڳالهين يا عمل جو جيڪو صرف ٻن نه پر ڪيترن ڌرين ملڪن يا گروپن سان شامل هجي، عام طور تي بين الاقوامي معاملن تجارت يا سفارتڪاري ۾ استعمال ٿئي ٿو
urduMeaning: کثیر الجہتی (چند سے زیادہ فریقین میں شامل)، وہ معاہدہ بات چیت یا کارروائی جو صرف دو نہیں بلکہ کئی ممالک جماعتوں یا فریقین کے مابین ہو، عام طور پر بین الاقوامی تعلقات تجارت اور سفارتکاری میں استعمال ہوتا ہے

englishMeaning: To preserve a dead body by embalming, drying, or other methods to prevent decomposition. To make something dry, shriveled, or preserved for a very long time. Figuratively, to make a person, object, or idea inactive, rigid, or lifeless.
synonyms: Embalm, Preserve, Dry, Conserve, Cure, Desiccate, Maintain, Protect
antonyms: Decay, Decompose, Rot, Perish, Corrupt, Deteriorate, Spoil, Disintegrate
examples: The ancient Egyptians learned how to mummify their dead rulers. Archaeologists discovered a chamber where priests used special oils to mummify bodies. The dry desert climate helped mummify the remains naturally. Years of isolation seemed to mummify the old traditions, leaving them unchanged.
sindhiMeaning: لاش کي مصالح لڳائي رکڻ، لاش کي اهڙي طريقي سان محفوظ ڪرڻ جو اهو ڊگهي عرصي تائين خراب نه ٿئي، ڪنهن شيءِ کي سڪائي يا محفوظ حالت ۾ رکڻ، مجازي معنيٰ ۾ ڪنهن شيءِ کي بي جان  جامد يا غير فعال بڻائڻ
urduMeaning: مسالہ لگا کر لاش کو محفوظ کرنا، مردہ جسم کو خاص طریقے سے محفوظ کرنا تاکہ وہ گل سڑ نہ جائے، کسی چیز کو خشک کرکے لمبے عرصے تک محفوظ رکھنا، مجازی طور پر کسی چیز کو جامد  غیر متحرک یا بے جان بنا دینا

englishMeaning: Dark, gloomy, or unclear. Something that is difficult to see through, understand, or interpret. It can describe physical darkness like water or metaphorical obscurity like a situation or story that is confusing or suspicious.
synonyms: Dark, Cloudy, Gloomy, Obscure, Dim, Muddy
antonyms: Clear, Bright, Transparent, Obvious, Lucid
examples: The river water was murky after the heavy rain. His explanation of the incident was murky and confusing. The alley was murky and filled with shadows. The political situation became murky after the announcement.
sindhiMeaning: اونداهو، ڌندلا، جنهن کي صاف ڏسڻ يا سمجهڻ مشڪل هجي، جهڙوڪ گندو پاڻي اونداهي جڳهه مشڪوڪ صورتحال
urduMeaning: دھندلا، مبہم، وہ چیز جو صاف نظر نہ آئے یا سمجھ میں نہ آئے، جیسے گندلا پانی اندھیرا ماحول یا مشکوک حالت

englishMeaning: A soft, low, unclear sound or speaking quietly. A quiet, gentle, and continuous sound that is not clear. It can also mean speaking in a very soft voice so that words are not fully clear. It is often used for natural sounds like wind, water, or crowd noise, and also for people speaking secretly or softly.
synonyms: Whisper, Mumble, Mutter, Murmur sound, Hum, Rustle, Gossip (context-based)
antonyms: Shout, Scream, Yell, Roar, Cry loudly, Exclaim
examples: The children began to murmur in the classroom during the lesson. I could hear the murmur of the river at night. The crowd started to murmur when the decision was announced. She murmured a soft apology and walked away.
sindhiMeaning: ڪُرڪَڻ، سُس پُس ڪرڻ، سرسراھٽ، ڀُڻ ڀُڻ ڪرڻ، مسلسل آواز، ڪنجهڻ، هلڪي آهستي آواز يا ڀڻڀڻ، هلڪي آهستي ۽ صاف نه ٻڌجندڙ آواز، اهو لفظ تڏهن به استعمال ٿئي ٿو جڏهن ڪو ماڻهو آهستي ڳالهائي يا ڪا به آواز نرم انداز ۾ نڪري
urduMeaning: سرسراہٹ، دھیمی نرم اور غیر واضح آواز یا آہستہ بولنا، ہلکی نرم اور غیر واضح آواز یا آہستہ آہستہ بولنا جسے پوری طرح سمجھنا مشکل ہو

englishMeaning: An intense and irrational fear of mice or rats. A person with musophobia may feel extreme panic, disgust, or terror at the sight or thought of rodents.
synonyms: Fear of mice, Rodent phobia, Murophobia
antonyms: Fearlessness, Rodent fondness
examples: Her musophobia made her scream at the sight of a mouse. He refused to enter the old warehouse because of his musophobia. Musophobia is one of the most common animal phobias. She avoided the basement due to her musophobia.
sindhiMeaning: مائوسن يا چُئن کان شديد ۽ غير منطقي خوف، اهڙو شخص هنن جاندارن کي ڏسي يا سوچي به ڏاڍو پريشان ٿي وڃي ٿو
urduMeaning: چوہوں سے شدید اور غیر منطقی خوف، اس فوبیا میں مبتلا شخص چوہا دیکھ کر یا اس کے خیال سے ہی بہت گھبرا جاتا ہے

englishMeaning: Hair grown on the upper lip of a man.  Facial hair on the upper lip.
synonyms: Whiskers, Facial hair, Mustachio
antonyms: Clean shaven, Smooth faced
examples: He grew a thick mustache over the winter. The actor’s mustache made him look older. He twirled his mustache thoughtfully. Mustache styles vary across cultures.

englishMeaning: A process in which the genetic material of a person, a plant or an animal changes in structure when it is passed on to children, etc, causing different physical characteristics to develop, a change of this kind. (Biology) an organism that has characteristics resulting from chromosomal alteration. A change or alteration in form or qualities. A change in the form or structure of something.
synonyms: Transfiguration, Transformation
antonyms: Fixation, Stabilization
examples: These cells have been affected by mutation. The genetic material has suffered a mutation. It is well known that radiation can cause mutation. This essay examines the mutation of ethnic politics into nationalist politics. The sculpture series underwent several mutations as the artist experimented with different materials and techniques.
sindhiMeaning: تبديل، ڦيرگهير، مٽ سٽ، تبديلي، ڄڻ يا جنسي تبديلي، ترميم، جينياتي تبديلي، صوتي تبديلي، ڦيرڦار، ادل بدل
urduMeaning: تغیر تبدیلی خلیوں کی جینیز میں تغیرات پیدا کرنے کا فعل، داخل خارج ،انتقال تبدیلی، تغیر

englishMeaning: Forcible or passive resistance to lawful authority. To rise against or refuse to obey or observe authority. Open fighting against authority (as one's own government). To rise up against established authority.
synonyms: Rebel, Revolt, Insurgency
antonyms: Obey, Counterinsurgency
examples:
There were rumours of mutiny among the troops. The crew mutinied and murdered the ship's captain.
The troops mutinied against their officers.
sindhiMeaning: بلوو، فساد، فساد ڪرڻ، غدر، بغاوت، شورش، بغاوت ڪرڻ، سرڪشي، کُلي بغاوت، بلوو ڪرڻ، فوجين يا جھازين جي پنهنجي آفيسرن خلاف بغاوت
urduMeaning: بلوہ، غدار، بغاوت کرنا، حکمران کے خلاف اُٹھ کھڑے ہونا ،غدربرپا کرنا، سرکشی ، فوجی بغاوت کرنا

englishMeaning: A strong sensation of fatigue, extreme strain, or emotional reaction like uncontrollable laughter. It can also convey the idea of aging or facial sagging. Context matters to understand whether it’s physical, emotional, or humorous.
synonyms: Exhausted, Worn out
antonyms: Feel firm, Energized, Refreshed
examples: After hiking for 10 hours, I felt like my cheeks were falling off. I laughed so hard at the joke that my cheeks were falling off. Sitting in the freezing wind made me feel like my cheeks were falling off. After working all night, my cheeks were falling off from sheer exhaustion.
sindhiMeaning: اهو مذاق يا جذباتي انداز ۾ چيو ويندو آهي جڏهن ڪو ماڻهو ايترو کلندو يا مرڪندو آهي جو سندس ڳل سور ڪرڻ لڳن يا ٿڪجي وڃن، اهو تمام گهڻي خوشي يا کل کي ظاهر ڪري ٿو، ٿڌي موسم ۾ ڳلن جو سن يا سخت ٿي وڃڻ
urduMeaning: یہ مزاحیہ انداز میں بولا جاتا ہے جب کوئی شخص بہت زیادہ ہنستا یا مسکراتا ہے اور اس کے گالوں میں درد یا تھکن محسوس ہونے لگتی ہے، یہ شدید خوشی یا ہنسی کو ظاہر کرتا ہے، سرد موسم میں گالوں کا سن یا سخت ہو جانا

englishMeaning: Do as I say, or leave. A strict expression used when someone insists that things must be done their way, or others are free to leave. This idiom shows a rigid attitude where a person refuses to compromise. It means only one option is acceptable: follow their decision, rules, or instructions. If someone disagrees, they can step aside or leave. It often describes controlling or authoritarian behavior in personal, work, or social situations.
synonyms: Self-willed, Dictatorial, Domineering, Authoritarian, Inflexible
antonyms: Cooperative, Flexible, Democratic, Understanding, Open-minded
examples: The manager’s attitude was my way or the highway, which made his employees frustrated. You can’t run a successful team with a my way or the highway attitude. His father was very strict; it was always my way or the highway at home. If she keeps saying my way or the highway, no one will want to work with her. Leaders who listen are respected more than those who believe in my way or the highway. During the project meeting, Tom’s my way or the highway stance created conflict among team members.
sindhiMeaning: ڳالهه رڳو منهنجي پسند مطابق هلندي نه ته پوءِ وڃو، اهو اظهار ڪنهن اهڙي شخص لاءِ ڪم اچي ٿو جيڪو لچڪ ڏيکارڻ لاءِ تيار ناهي، اهو چوڻ ته شيون صرف منهنجي طريقي سان هلنديون، جيڪڏهن اوهان راضي نه آهيو ته پوءِ مسئلو توهان جو آهي يا اوهان ڇڏيو، ڪنهن هٺيلي شخص لاءِ جيڪو چوي ٿو ته منهنجو حڪم مڃو نه ته نڪري وڃو، ڪڏهن ڪڏهن مزاح ۾ به استعمال ٿيندو آهي ته ڪو ماڻهو ڏاڍو ضدي ٿي ويو آهي
urduMeaning: بات صرف میرے طریقے سے ہوگی ورنہ آپ جا سکتے ہیں، یہ محاورہ کسی ایسے شخص کے رویے کو ظاہر کرتا ہے جو کسی بات پر سمجھوتا نہیں کرنا چاہتا، مطلب یہ ہے کہ فیصلہ حکم یا طریقہ صرف میرا چلے گا اگر کسی کو اعتراض ہے تو وہ الگ ہو سکتا ہے، کسی ضدی یا حکم چلانے والے شخص کے انداز کو ظاہر کرتا ہے، طنز یا مذاق میں بھی کہا جاتا ہے کہ کوئی اپنی بات منوانے پر تلا ہوا ہے

englishMeaning: A hired ruffian or unscrupulous person who carries out orders without question. Originally the name of a legendary warrior race who followed Achilles in Greek mythology.
synonyms: Henchman, Stooge, Lackey, Follower, Minion
antonyms: Leader, Independent thinker, Rebel, Dissenter
examples: The dictator's myrmidons carried out every cruel order without hesitation. He was merely a myrmidon doing his master's dirty work. The police chief's myrmidons intimidated witnesses. History remembers those myrmidons as accessories to great crimes.
sindhiMeaning: اهو شخص جيڪو بنا سوال جي حڪم بجا آڻي، گهڻو ڪري بد نيتي يا ظالماڻي ڪمن لاءِ، يونان ڏند ڪٿا ۾ اڪلز جي پٺيان هلندڙ جنگجوءَ جي قبيلي جو نالو
urduMeaning: وہ شخص جو بغیر سوال کے احکامات بجا لائے، اکثر ظالمانہ کاموں کے لیے، یونانی داستان میں اکیلیس کے پیروکار جنگجو قبیلے کا نام

englishMeaning: A bush with shiny leaves, pink or white flowers and blue-black berries. A small tree with shiny green leaves, pleasant-smelling white flowers and blue-black fruit.
synonyms: Myrtus, Evergreen shrub, Aromatic plant
antonyms: Deciduous shrub, Non-aromatic plant
examples: The most common plants are olives, maritime pines, oaks, myrtles, junipers. The garden was full of blooming myrtle bushes. Myrtle leaves are used to make fragrant oils. She wore a wreath of myrtle on her wedding day. The ancient symbol of peace often included myrtle branches.
sindhiMeaning: ولايتي ميندي، خوشبودار ٻوٽو، سُرهن پتن ۽ اچن گلن وارو سدا بهار ٻوٽو، ڪارن واگڻائي بيضوي پيرن وارو
urduMeaning: حنا، مہندی، جِنس مائرٹس کا ایک خوشبودار پودا،خوشبودار سفید پھول ارغوانی پھل تین میٹر تک بلند ہوتا ہے اور مغربی ایشیا میں پایا جاتا ہے

englishMeaning: Difficult to understand or explain. Full of secrets or unknown facts. Causing curiosity because of being unclear. Strange or unexplained in nature.
synonyms: Secretive, Enigmatic, Unfathomable, Puzzling, Cryptic, Unknown
antonyms: Clear, Obvious, Understandable, Simple, Known
examples: The old house has a mysterious atmosphere at night. He received a mysterious phone call without any number. There is a mysterious light in the sky every evening. The disappearance of the document is still mysterious.
sindhiMeaning: پراسرار، ڳجهو، راز ڀريو، سمجهه کان ٻاهر، اهڙي شيءِ جنهن جو اصل سبب معلوم نه هجي، جيڪا ڳجهي ۽ سمجهه کان ٻاهر هجي
urduMeaning: ار، رازدار، اسرار آمیز، ناقابلِ فہم یا غیر واضح، ایسی چیز جس کی حقیقت چھپی ہوئی ہو، جس کا سبب معلوم نہ ہو

englishMeaning: In a strange or unexplained manner. In a way that causes curiosity or wonder. Without any obvious reason or explanation. In a secretive or puzzling way. In a manner connected with mystery, secrecy, or the unknown.
synonyms: Secretly, Strangely, Puzzlingly, Curiously, Unexplainedly, Enigmatically, Cryptically, Oddly, Inexplicably, Wonderingly
antonyms: Clearly, Obviously, Openly, Plainly, Evidently, Transparently, Understandably, Explicitly, Directly, Certainly
examples: The documents mysteriously disappeared from the office overnight. She smiled mysteriously but did not reveal her secret. The lights mysteriously turned on even though nobody was home. The ancient treasure mysteriously vanished centuries ago.
sindhiMeaning: پراسرار طريقي سان، اهڙي نموني جو سبب يا حقيقت واضح نه هجي، حيرت انگيز ۽ سمجهڻ ۾ ڏکيو انداز سان، ڳجهي يا راز ڀريي نموني، اهڙي طرح جو ماڻهن ۾ تجسس پيدا ڪري
urduMeaning: پراسرار انداز میں، ایسے طریقے سے جس کی وجہ معلوم نہ ہو، حیران کن اور سمجھ سے باہر انداز میں، خفیہ یا رازدارانہ طور پر، ایسا انداز جو تجسس اور حیرت پیدا کرے

englishMeaning: The quality of being enigmatic or puzzling. A sense of secrecy or concealment. An unexplained or strange nature. A condition that arouses curiosity and wonder. The characteristic of being difficult to interpret or understand. Hidden meaning or unknown purpose. An aura of intrigue surrounding someone or something.
synonyms: Mystery, Enigma, Secrecy, Intrigue, Obscurity, Uncertainty, Puzzle, Cryptic nature, Unexplainedness, Hiddenness, Ambiguity, Secretiveness
antonyms: Clarity, Openness, Transparency, Certainty, Plainness, Obviousness, Simplicity, Understanding, Explicitness, Directness
examples: The mysteriousness of the old abandoned house attracted many visitors. Her mysteriousness made everyone curious about her life. The mysteriousness surrounding the incident remains unsolved. The novel gains excitement from the mysteriousness of its main character.
sindhiMeaning: رازداري، پراسراريت، ڳجهارت وارو هجڻ، ڀيد ڀريو هجڻ، ڻڄاتل يا سمجهه کان ٻاهر هجڻ جي حالت، اها خاصيت يا حالت جنهن ۾ ڪا شيءِ  شخص  واقعو يا ڳالهه راز ڀري  ڳجهي  يا سمجهڻ ۾ ڏکي لڳي، اهڙي شيءِ ماڻهن ۾ تجسس ۽ حيرت پيدا ڪري ٿي
urduMeaning: پراسراریت، رازداری، بھید بھرا پن، معمہ خیزی، پوشیدگی کی کیفیت، ایسی کیفیت یا خصوصیت جس میں کوئی شخص  چیز  واقعہ یا صورتحال پراسرار  پوشیدہ  ناقابلِ فہم یا معمہ نما محسوس ہو اور لوگوں میں تجسس پیدا کرے

englishMeaning: Something that is difficult to understand or to explain. A religious truth that one can know only by revelation and cannot fully understand.
synonyms: Secrecy

englishMeaning: Active or happening at night. Living, occurring, or active during the night rather than the day. It is commonly used for animals, habits, or activities that take place after sunset.
synonyms: Night-active, Night-loving, Night-wandering, Crepuscular (partially related, Active at twilight)
antonyms: Diurnal (active during the day), Daytime, Sunlit activity (contextual)
examples: Owls are nocturnal birds that hunt at night. He has a nocturnal lifestyle because he works night shifts. Many desert animals are nocturnal to avoid daytime heat. Bats are nocturnal creatures that use sound to navigate.

englishMeaning: To move your head slightly up and down to show agreement, greeting, or approval. To lower and raise the head gently as a signal of agreement, permission, acknowledgment, greeting, understanding, or encouragement. It can also mean getting sleepy and dropping the head forward for a moment.
synonyms: Approve, Agree, Signal, Bow, Dip, Acknowledge
antonyms: Disagree, Deny, Reject, Shake one’s head
examples: The president nodded to the crowd as he passed in the motorcade. She nodded at him to begin speaking. Her head nodded in agreement. He sat nodding in front of the fire. She answered with a slight nod of the head. She inspected my work and gave a satisfied nod.

englishMeaning: To move your head in agreement while listening. To nod repeatedly as a sign of understanding, agreement, or following the rhythm of music or conversation.
synonyms: Agree, Assent, Follow
antonyms: Disagree, Resist, Oppose
examples: She nodded along as he explained the rules. I just nodded along because I didn’t want to argue. They nodded along during the meeting to show support. He nodded along to the rhythm of the music.

englishMeaning: To fall asleep, especially unintentionally. To begin sleeping, usually while sitting up or during an activity, often briefly and without planning.
synonyms: Doze off, Drift off, Snooze, Sleep
antonyms: Stay awake, Remain alert, Be awake
examples: I nodded off during the lecture. She nodded off on the sofa while watching TV. He tends to nod off after lunch. Don’t nod off in the meeting or you’ll miss important points.

synonyms: Approve, Pass, Ratify, Sanction, Endorse
antonyms: Reject, Oppose, Block, Question, Debate
examples: The committee nodded through the budget proposal in less than five minutes. Most routine policies are nodded through during monthly meetings. The board nodded through the agreement without raising any objections. Because everyone agreed, the resolution was nodded through easily.

englishMeaning: To acknowledge or show recognition. To show approval, recognition, or respect to someone or something, often in a subtle or indirect way, such as a gesture, mention, or reference.

englishMeaning: A member of a group of people who move from place to place instead of living in one place all the time. A member of a community that moves with its animals from place to place.
synonyms: Wanderer, Migrant, Drifter
antonyms: Immobile, Nonmoving, Settled,
examples: He lived like a nomad for a few years after college, never holding a job in one place for very long. They were nomads who hunted game and tended their herds of cattle.
sindhiMeaning: خانه بدوش، گهمندڙ ڦرندڙ قوم، لاڏو، رولو، سانگي، رولاڪ، رمتو ماڻهو، سيلاني
urduMeaning: خانہ بدوش

englishMeaning: Roaming about from place to place aimlessly, frequently, or without a fixed pattern of movement. Belonging to a community that moves with its animals from place to place.
synonyms: Roaming, Itinerant, Travelling
antonyms: Immobile, Motionless,
examples: Raised in a nomadic family, she attended half a dozen different high schools.

englishMeaning: A philosophical doctrine which holds that general or abstract terms and universal concepts exist only as names and have no independent reality. The belief that only individual objects are real and that classes or categories are merely mental constructs. A theory opposing the view that universals possess true existence outside the mind. An important position in medieval and modern philosophy concerning the nature of reality and language.
synonyms: Conceptualism, Anti-realism, Particularism, Terminism
antonyms: Realism, Platonism, Universalism, Idealism
examples: Nominalism challenged the medieval belief in the real existence of universals. William of Ockham is regarded as a leading figure of nominalism. The debate between realism and nominalism shaped medieval philosophy. Modern nominalism continues to influence theories of language and logic. The professor explained nominalism with simple everyday examples.
sindhiMeaning: نام پرستي، اهو فلسفياڻو نظريو جيڪو چوي ٿو ته عام يا تجريدي تصورات صرف نالا آهن ۽ انهن جو ڪو خود مختيار وجود ڪونهي، صرف انفرادي شيون حقيقي آهن ۽ ذيلي درجا ذهني تخليق آهن، ڪليتن جي وجود کان انڪار وارو فلسفياڻو نظريو

englishMeaning: Calm and relaxed, not showing worry or interest. Someone who appears casually calm, unconcerned, or indifferent, even in situations where others might be worried or stressed.
synonyms: Unconcerned, Casual, Indifferent, Relaxed, Cool
antonyms: Anxious, Concerned, Worried, Tense, Nervous
examples: She walked into the meeting with a nonchalant attitude, ignoring the tension in the room. He gave a nonchalant shrug when asked about the missing report. Despite the chaos around him, he remained nonchalant and composed. Her nonchalant smile made everyone feel at ease.

englishMeaning: A small corner, recess, or sheltered place that feels private, quiet, or comfortable. It can be a corner in a room, a hidden place in nature, or any small area set apart from the main space.
synonyms: Corner, Recess, Alcove, Cranny, Hideaway, Corner spot
antonyms: Center, Open space, Middle, Exposed area
examples: She sat in a quiet nook of the library to read her book. The café has a cozy nook near the window where people like to relax. They found a small nook in the garden to talk privately. A reading nook was built under the stairs for the children.

englishMeaning: A situation or a pattern of behavior that is usual or expected. Standards of behavior that are typical of or accepted within a particular group or society.

englishMeaning: Standards of proper or acceptable behavior. An average level of development or achievement. Something (such as a behavior or way of doing something) that is usual or expected.
synonyms: Standard, Ethics
antonyms: End, Exception, Extreme
examples: The government claims that background radioactivity is well below international norms. These standards generally exceed the accepted industry norms.
sindhiMeaning: رواج، مقرر ڪيل پيمانو، وضع، نمونو، معيار، قاعدو، دستور، طبع، ڊول، مزاج، ڍنگ، انداز، نيم، اصول، اخلاق، مقرر يا معياري ڪم جو مقدار يا پيداوار، روايتي رويو

englishMeaning: A person who is too interested in other people’s private affairs and likes to ask questions or look into things that do not concern them. A person who interferes in other people’s business and tries to find out private information.
synonyms: Busybody, Snoop, Prying person, Meddler, Interferer
antonyms: Private person, Discreet person, Reserved person, Respectful person, Mind-your-own-business type
examples: Stop being a nosey parker and focus on your own work. My neighbor is such a nosey parker, always listening at the door. She called him a nosey parker for asking about her salary. The nosey parker tried to read my messages without permission.

englishMeaning: Fear of contracting a disease. An excessive or irrational fear of developing a specific disease. It is a psychological condition where a person constantly worries about becoming ill, even when there is no real medical evidence suggesting illness.
synonyms: Hypochondriasis, Disease phobia, Health anxiety, Illness fear
antonyms: Fearlessness of illness, Health confidence, Wellness assurance
examples: His nosophobia made him visit the doctor every week despite being healthy. She avoids crowded places due to her nosophobia of infectious diseases. The doctor reassured him to reduce his nosophobia. Nosophobia can affect daily life if not managed properly.
sindhiMeaning: بيماريءَ جو خوف، هڪ نفسياتي حالت جنهن ۾ ماڻهو ڪنهن بيماري ۾ مبتلا ٿيڻ جو انتهائي خوف محسوس ڪري ٿو جيتوڻيڪ حقيقت ۾ اهڙو ڪو خطرو موجود نه هجي

englishMeaning: An emotional state where a person reflects fondly on experiences, people, or moments from their past. It can evoke both happiness and a sense of loss. It is commonly triggered by memories, smells, music, or familiar places.

antonyms: Democracy, Republic, Anarchy, Oligarchy, Common rule
examples: Visiting my childhood home filled me with nostalgia. Old photographs often evoke nostalgia for simpler times. She felt a wave of nostalgia when she heard her favorite childhood song. The festival brought nostalgia for the days we spent together as kids.

englishMeaning: Having or bringing a sad feeling mixed with pleasure when you think of happy times in the past. Unhappy about being away and longing for familiar things or persons.
synonyms: Wistful, Dreamy, Unsentimental
antonyms: Undesirous, Undesiring
examples: I feel quite nostalgic for the place where I grew up. People who get nostalgic about childhood were obviously never children. Congrats, your announcement makes me nostalgic for our days doing political battle in Arkansas.

englishMeaning: To show no surprise, fear, or reaction in a shocking or difficult situation. To remain calm and unemotional when something surprising, strange, dangerous, or upsetting happens. A person who does not bat an eye shows no visible reaction.
synonyms: Remain calm, Stay cool, Keep a straight face, Show no reaction, Stay composed, Remain unfazed
antonyms: Panic, Overreact, Become nervous, Be shocked, Lose control
examples: She did not bat an eye when she heard the loud explosion. The teacher did not bat an eye after seeing the broken window. He told the shocking news, but his brother did not bat an eye. The brave soldier did not bat an eye during the dangerous mission.

englishMeaning: To remain calm and unemotional in a surprising, shocking, or difficult situation. To show no reaction, fear, or surprise. To stay completely unaffected by something unusual. To behave as if nothing happened.
synonyms: Remain calm, Keep cool, Stay unfazed, Stay composed, Show no reaction
antonyms: Panic, Overreact, Get frightened, Lose composure
examples: He did not bat an eyelid when he heard the bad news. The teacher did not bat an eyelid even when the students argued loudly. She saw the snake but did not bat an eyelid. My grandfather did not bat an eyelid during the storm.

englishMeaning: To care nothing. To treat something as worthless. To pay no attention. To feel no concern at all
synonyms: Not give a thought, Not give a hoot, Not bother at all, Be indifferent
antonyms: Care deeply, Be concerned, Take seriously, Value something
examples: She did not care a fig about the gossip spreading around. She did not care a fig about the criticism and kept working her way. They do not care a fig about the noise in the neighborhood. She does not care a fig about fashion trends.

word: Not my circus not my monkeys
englishMeaning: Refusing responsibility for others’ issues. A way of saying that a problem is not your responsibility. It means the situation does not belong to you, so you will not get involved. People use it to avoid unnecessary drama or issues that are created by others.
synonyms: None of my business, Not responsible
antonyms: My problem, My responsibility
examples: That argument is not my circus not my monkeys. He said not my circus not my monkeys. I avoid office drama, not my circus not my monkeys. Family fights are not my circus not my monkeys. Their drama is endless but not my circus not my monkeys.

englishMeaning: Lack of mutual understanding. Different viewpoints or expectations. Communication gap. Misalignment in thinking or planning. People involved in a situation have different understandings, expectations, or opinions, which causes confusion or disagreement. It often happens in teamwork, relationships, or communication problems.
synonyms: Misunderstood each other, Out of sync, Not aligned, Disagreeing, Not in agreement
antonyms: On the same page, In agreement, Aligned, Understanding each other, In sync
examples: The manager and the team were not on the same page about the project deadline. We realized we were not on the same page after the meeting discussion. The couple argued because they were not on the same page about saving money. If teachers and parents are not on the same page, students may get confused.

englishMeaning: Something that someone does not like or is not interested in. The phrase is used to indicate that a person does not enjoy or is not suited to a particular activity, thing, or situation. It is often informal and used in conversation.
synonyms: Not to someone’s liking, Unappealing, Unsuitable, Not for someone
antonyms: Someone’s favorite, Appealing, Enjoyable, Suitable

englishMeaning: A situation is still risky or uncertain and problems may continue. A person or situation has not yet passed all difficulties or danger. Even if some progress has been made, the outcome is not safe or settled. More trouble may still appear.
synonyms: Still in danger, Not safe yet, In a risky situation, Problems remain

englishMeaning: Freed from difficulty, blame, or obligation. No longer in trouble or responsible for something.

sindhiMeaning: بي الزام، آزاد، مشڪل مان ٻاهر، ذميواريءَ کان آزاد، ڪنهن ڏکي صورتحال الزام يا ذميواريءَ مان آزاد ٿي وڃڻ، يعني هاڻي کيس ڪو به الزام يا بوجھ نه رهيو

englishMeaning: To move away from the main topic, goal, or correct direction. It is used when someone or something is no longer focused on the main subject, plan, or goal. It can describe losing direction in conversation, work, studies, or life plans.

sindhiMeaning: اصل مقصد يا صحيح رستي کان هٽي وڃڻ، رستي کان ڀٽڪڻ، مقصد کان پري ٿيڻ، جڏهن ڪو ماڻهو يا ڪم پنهنجي اصل مقصد يا صحيح رستي کان هٽي وڃي، اهو ڳالهه ٻولهه ڪم يا منصوبن ۾ استعمال ٿئي ٿو

englishMeaning: Something that is likely to happen soon or a distant sea view. Offing refers to something that is approaching or expected in the near future. It is also used in maritime language to mean the open sea visible from the shore but still at a distance

antonyms: Distant, Past, Gone, Finished

englishMeaning: To remove a load or burden from something or someone. To take goods, weight, responsibility, or pressure away from a vehicle, place, system, or person. antonyms: Load, Take on, Carry, Accept

englishMeaning: A road that allows vehicles to leave a highway, motorway, or expressway. A way to leave a difficult situation. A safe exit from a plan, conflict, or process. synonyms: Exit ramp, Exit road, Slip road, Turnoff, Highway exit, Escape route, Way out, Exit strategy, Alternative path
antonyms: On-ramp, Entrance ramp, Entry road, Dead end, Trap, Point of no return

englishMeaning: To balance or counter the effect of something. To reduce or neutralize the effect of a cost, loss, or negative impact by an equal or opposite action. To make something stand out by contrasting it with another element. To move or position something slightly away from a main line or center Something that compensates for a loss, disadvantage, or negative effect (A balancing factor). A small distance or shift from a main position. A credit used to reduce a debt or cost. A printing method where ink is transferred from a plate to a surface.
synonyms: Compensate, Counteract, Neutralize, Make up, Adjustment
antonyms: Increase, Worsen, Intensify, Aggravate, Drawback
examples: Higher profits offset the increase in production costs. Overtime pay helped offset monthly expenses. Salary benefits are an offset to long working hours. The discount served as an offset to the delay. There is a slight offset between the two lines. Tax offsets reduced the payable amount. The book was produced using offset printing. Job security is an offset to lower pay. Higher income can offset rising living costs. The designer offset the image to the left. Dark walls offset the bright furniture.
sindhiMeaning: توازن ڪرڻ، ڪنهن نقصان، خرچ يا منفي اثر کي برابر يا گهٽ ڪرڻ لاءِ ٻيو قدم کڻڻ، تلافي ڪندڙ شيءِ، اهڙي شيءِ يا فائدو جيڪو نقصان يا گهٽتائي کي برابر ڪري، ٿوري هٽ يا فرق، مالي ترتيب يا ڪٽوتي، ڇپائي جو طريقو جنهن ۾ مس سڌي ڪاغذ تي نه لڳي، مقابلي ۾ آڻي نمايان ڪرڻ

englishMeaning: Located at sea or outside the main land area, often used for activities done abroad. Something situated away from the coast or outside a country, especially across the sea. englishMeaning: Giving a feeling that something bad or unpleasant is going to happen. Suggesting or foreshadowing danger, trouble, or disaster; indicating that something threatening or unfavorable is likely in the future

englishMeaning: Something that is not restricted to a particular gender. It can refer to clothing, roles, or activities that are meant for people of any sex. It emphasizes inclusivity and neutrality regarding gender.

englishMeaning: From every side or direction. By everyone or from all people. Universally acknowledged or agreed upon. From all quarters or sources. Used to indicate that something is admitted, accepted, or experienced by all parties involved.

englishMeaning: Occurring at irregular intervals rather than continuously. Starting, stopping, and starting again over a period of time. Intermittently or from time to time. Used to describe relationships, weather, conditions, or activities that happen with breaks in between.

synonyms: Choose, Select, Pick, Decide on, Go for, Elect
antonyms: Reject, Refuse, Avoid, Ignore
examples: He opted for the early flight to avoid traffic. (choosing a timing) She opted for a minimalist design in her new apartment. The image a company or brand creates in the public eye. How a person’s actions look to others socially. The system of lenses and light control in cameras. englishMeaning: A hopeful and positive attitude towards life and the future. The belief that good things will happen and that problems can be overcome. antonyms: Pessimism, Despair, Hopelessness, Cynicism, Gloom, Negativity

englishMeaning: A person who tends to expect favorable or good outcomes from situations. Someone who maintains a hopeful and positive attitude even in difficult circumstances. englishMeaning: To officially appoint someone to a position, especially in a religious context. To decree or order something by authority. englishMeaning: Appearing or claimed to be true, but possibly not genuine. Something presented outwardly in a certain way, giving an impression that may differ from the real situation. Often used to describe motives, reasons, or appearances that may be deceptive.

antonyms: Real, Genuine, Actual, True, Authentic
examples: His ostensible reason for visiting the office was to discuss the project, but he actually wanted to meet his friend. The ostensible purpose of the charity was to help children, though most funds went elsewhere. She maintained an ostensible calm, even though she was nervous inside. englishMeaning: Apparently or on the surface, but possibly not true in reality. Something seems to be true according to appearances, statements, or public explanation, but there is doubt that this is the real reason or truth.
synonyms: Apparently, Seemingly, On the surface, To all appearances
antonyms: Actually, Truly, Genuinely, In reality

englishMeaning: A type of medical approach based on the idea that the body’s structure and function are closely connected. It emphasizes treating health issues through physical manipulation of muscles, joints, and bones, rather than relying only on medication.

englishMeaning: A system of medical treatment that focuses on bones, muscles, and joints, using physical manipulation to improve health. synonyms: Chaos, Uproar, Turmoil, Confusion, Commotion, Bedlam, Havoc

examples: As soon as the fire alarm rang, pandemonium broke out in the building. The news of the team’s victory caused pandemonium in the streets. When the lights went out during the concert, there was total pandemonium. The sudden announcement created pandemonium in the classroom.
sindhiMeaning: اها حالت جنهن ۾ هر طرف شور، هلهلو، بي ترتيبي ۽ افراتفري هجي، ماڻهو ڪنٽرول کان ٻاهر ٿي وڃن ۽ حالتون مڪمل طور تي انتشار جو شڪار ٿين
urduMeaning: ایسی حالت یا منظر جس میں شور شرابہ، ہنگامہ، چیخ و پکار اور افراتفری ہو، اور لوگ قابو میں نہ رہیں

englishMeaning: Excessively optimistic; believing that everything in the world is as good as it possibly can be, often ignoring real problems. Derived from Dr Pangloss in Voltaire's Candide.
synonyms: Optimistic, Naive, Unrealistically positive, Rose-tinted
antonyms: Pessimistic, Realistic, Cynical, Critical
examples: His Panglossian view of the economy ignored the poverty around him. She criticised the government's Panglossian attitude to climate change. A Panglossian outlook can prevent necessary action. His Panglossian speeches were comforting but ultimately misleading.
sindhiMeaning: حد کان وڌيڪ خوش بين، اهو سمجهڻ ته دنيا ۾ سڀ ڪجهه بهترين آهي، اصل مسئلن کي نظرانداز ڪندي، وولتيئر جي ناول جي ڪردار پانگلاس تان ورتل
urduMeaning: حد سے زیادہ پر امید، یہ سمجھنا کہ دنیا میں سب کچھ بہترین ہے، اصل مسائل کو نظرانداز کرتے ہوئے، وولٹیئر کے ناول کے کردار پینگلاس سے ماخوذ

englishMeaning: Feeling sudden fear or anxiety that makes it hard to think calmly. Panicky describes a state where a person feels intense and sudden fear, worry, or nervousness. In this condition, emotions take control and rational thinking becomes difficult.
synonyms: Suddenly afraid, Very anxious, Terrified, Fearful
antonyms: Calm, Relaxed, Confident, Composed
examples: She became panicky when she realized she had lost her passport. His panicky reaction made the situation worse. The child looked panicky after hearing the loud noise. Try not to sound panicky during an emergency call.

englishMeaning: An irrational or excessive fear of everything, often leading to general anxiety, unease, or apprehension in daily life. It is a psychological condition where the person feels threatened by almost all situations or objects, even without a clear cause.
synonyms: Omniphobia, Generalized fear, Anxiety, Phobia of everything
antonyms: Courage, Fearlessness, Bravery, Confidence
examples: His panphobia made it difficult for him to leave the house. She avoided social gatherings due to her panphobia. Panphobia caused him to constantly worry about minor risks. The therapist helped him understand and manage his panphobia.

englishMeaning: A sexual orientation where a person experiences romantic or sexual attraction to others without considering gender or biological sex. Pansexual people may be attracted to men, women, transgender, non-binary, or gender-diverse individuals.
synonyms: Omnisexual, Gender-blind, All-sexual
antonyms: Heterosexual, Homosexual, Monosexual
examples: Alex identifies as pansexual and is open to dating anyone. She realized she was pansexual after reflecting on her attractions. Pansexuality challenges traditional ideas of gender-based attraction. Many pansexual individuals advocate for inclusivity in relationships.
sindhiMeaning: هڪ اهڙو جنسي رجحان جنهن ۾ ماڻهو ڪنهن جي جنس يا جنسي سڃاڻپ کان سواءِ محبت يا جنسي دلچسپي محسوس ڪن ٿا
urduMeaning: وہ جنسی رجحان جس میں انسان کسی کی جنس یا جنسی شناخت کو دیکھے بغیر رومانوی یا جنسی کشش محسوس کرتا ہے

englishMeaning: A sexual orientation where a person feels attracted to others based on personality, emotional connection, or other qualities rather than gender. Pansexual individuals may be attracted to men, women, transgender people, non-binary people, or people of any gender identity.
synonyms: Omnisexual, Gender-blind, All-sexual
antonyms: Heterosexual, Homosexual, Bisexual (narrowly defined)
examples: Alex identifies as pansexual and is open to relationships with any gender. Pansexuality emphasizes attraction to the person, not their gender. Being pansexual means Riley does not limit themselves to dating men or women only. Some pansexual people feel society misunderstands their orientation.
sindhiMeaning: ھي ماڻهو ڪنهن جي به جنس جي باري ۾ پرواهه نه ڪندا آهن، اهي شخصيت احساساتي تعلق يا ٻين خاصيتن جي بنياد تي ڪشش محسوس ڪندا آهن، مرد عورت ٽرانس يا ڪنهن به جنسي سڃاڻپ وارن ماڻهن ڏانهن ڪشش ٿي سگهي ٿي

englishMeaning: To hide real problems instead of fixing them. It describes temporary or superficial solutions that do not fix the real issue.
synonyms: Conceal flaws, Patch up temporarily
antonyms: Expose the problem, Address the issue, Fix properly, Confront directly, Resolve fully
examples: The manager tried to paper over the cracks in the team instead of addressing the real issues. Their marriage looked fine, but they were only papering over the cracks. You can’t paper over the cracks forever; one day the truth will come out. The government’s new policy papers over the cracks rather than fixing the economy.
sindhiMeaning: مسئلي کي لڪائڻ، عيب کي ڍڪڻ، ظاهري طور سٺو ڏيکارڻ (ڀتين جا درا ڍڪڻ لاءِ پيپر لڳائڻ پر درا اڃا اندر هوندا آهن)
urduMeaning: اصل مسئلہ چھپانا، وقتی حل نکالنا، دکھاوے کے لیے بہتر بنانا (دیوار کے شگافوں پر کاغذ چپکانا تاکہ وہ نظر نہ آئیں)

englishMeaning: Standard, equal level, average. A standard or typical level of quality, quantity, or achievement. It can also mean equality with a standard or expectation. Commonly used in golf to indicate the expected number of strokes.
synonyms: Standard, Average, Equal, Benchmark, Typical
antonyms: Below standard, Inferior, Subpar, Unequal, Exceptional (in some contexts)
examples: Her performance is on par with the best in the team. The restaurant’s service was not up to par. In golf, he finished the hole in par. Salaries here are on par with industry standards.
sindhiMeaning: معيار تي، برابر، اوسط سطح تي، اوسط سطح سان برابر هجڻ جي حالت کي ظاهر ڪري ٿو، گالف ۾ اهو متوقع اسٽروڪ جي تعداد لاءِ پڻ استعمال ٿيندو آهي
urduMeaning: معیار، برابر، اوسط سطح پر، کسی چیز کے معیاری یا اوسط سطح کے برابر ہونے، معیار کے مطابق ہونے کو ظاہر کرتا ہے، گالف میں یہ متوقع اسٹروک کی تعداد کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے

englishMeaning: A fundamental change in approach or underlying assumptions. A great and important change in the way something is done or thought about. A fundamental change in approach, assumptions, or way of thinking about something. A radical change in underlying beliefs or theory.
synonyms: Transformation, Revolution, Radical change, Reorientation
antonyms: Continuation, Tradition, Status quo, Consistency
examples:
The widespread use of social media represents a paradigm shift in the company's marketing strategy. The invention of the internet caused a paradigm shift in communication. Wegener's theory led to a paradigm shift in the earth sciences.
I could convince only a few of my colleagues of the need for a revolution, a paradigm shift.
sindhiMeaning: سوچ، طريقيڪار يا نظام ۾ هڪ بنيادي ۽ انقلابي تبديلي، بنيادي تبديلي، نئين انقلابي سوچ، نئين نموني يا نظام ڏانهن مڪمل رخ موڙڻ، روايتي خيالن يا اصولن کان هٽي نئين طريقي کي اختيار ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: کسی نظام، سوچ یا طریقہ کار میں بنیادی اور انقلابی تبدیلی، بُنیادی تبدیلی ، کایا پلٹ ، نئی انقلابی فِکر

englishMeaning: A statement, situation, or idea that seems impossible, opposite, or contradictory, but may actually contain a hidden truth. Something that appears confusing because it combines opposite ideas. At first, it may sound wrong or illogical, but after deeper thinking, it can reveal an important truth or reality. Paradoxes are commonly used in literature, philosophy, science, and daily life to express complex ideas.
synonyms: Contradiction, Irony, Enigma, Puzzle, Mystery, Inconsistency
antonyms: Agreement, Consistency, Logic, Harmony, Certainty, Reality
examples: Less is more is a famous paradox. The more we learn, the more we realize how little we know. He was alone in the crowd, which is a paradoxical feeling. Saving time by rushing often causes more delays, which is a paradox.
sindhiMeaning: ابتڙ ڳالهه، حيران ڪندڙ حقيقت، ظاهري تضاد، ڳجهو سچ، الٽو لڳندڙ پر صحيح خيال، تضاد سان گڏ حقيقت، اها ڳالهه يا حالت جيڪا ظاهر ۾ هڪ ٻئي جي ابتڙ يا ناممڪن لڳي پر حقيقت ۾ ان ۾ سچائي هجي، اهڙي ڳالهه  خيال يا صورتحال جيڪا شروع ۾ حيران ڪندڙ يا غلط لڳي پر وڌيڪ سوچڻ سان ان مان ڪا اهم حقيقت يا دانائي ظاهر ٿئي
urduMeaning: متضاد بات، عجیب حقیقت، بظاہر غلط مگر درست خیال، الجھا ہوا سچ، حیران کن تضاد، عجیب حقیقت، ایسی بات یا صورتحال جو بظاہر متضاد یا ناممکن لگے لیکن حقیقت میں اس میں کوئی سچائی موجود ہو، ایسی بات  خیال یا صورتحال  جو پہلی نظر میں غلط  عجیب یا ایک دوسرے کے خلاف محسوس ہو  لیکن غور کرنے پر اس میں گہری حقیقت یا دانش موجود ہوتی ہے

englishMeaning: Seemingly contradictory, Seemingly absurd, self-contradictory, or against common sense, but may contain a hidden truth. Something that has two opposite features that exist together.
synonyms: Contradictory, Absurd
antonyms: Logical, Reasonable
examples: It is paradoxical but true. It is paradoxical that the poorest people often give the most in charity. His paradoxical statement confused everyone in the meeting. The paradoxical nature of technology is that it connects us but also isolates us. The silence of the leader at a time of crisis was paradoxical.
sindhiMeaning: تضاد وارو، ابتڙ لڳندڙ، ظاهري تضاد پر حقيقت سان لاڳاپيل
urduMeaning: تضاد نما، متضاد، خلافِ قیاس، بظاہر متضاد مگر حقیقت رکھنے والا

englishMeaning: Paradoxically means in a way that seems strange, opposite, or contradictory, but may still be true or logical. It describes a situation where two opposite ideas exist together.
synonyms: Contradictorily, Ironically, Unexpectedly, Curiously, Oddly, Strangely, Inconsistently, Amazingly
antonyms: Logically, Clearly, Consistently, Normally, Predictably, Reasonably
examples: Paradoxically, the more he earned, the less satisfied he became. Paradoxically, staying calm helped her finish the work faster. The medicine paradoxically caused the same symptoms it was meant to cure. Paradoxically, people in large cities sometimes feel more lonely than villagers.
sindhiMeaning: ابتڙ نموني سان، حيران ڪندڙ طريقي سان، هڪ ٻئي جي ابتڙ انداز ۾، اهڙي طريقي سان جنهن ۾ ٻه ڳالهيون هڪ ٻئي جي مخالفت ۾ لڳن پر حقيقت ۾ صحيح يا ممڪن هجن، هي لفظ تڏهن استعمال ٿيندو آهي جڏهن ڪا ڳالهه ظاهري طور ابتڙ يا عجيب لڳي پر حقيقت ۾ صحيح هجي
urduMeaning: متضاد طور پر، حیران کن طور پر، بظاہر الٹ انداز میں، ایسی حالت یا انداز جس میں کوئی بات بظاہر غلط  عجیب یا ایک دوسرے کے خلاف لگے لیکن حقیقت میں درست ہو، یہ لفظ اس وقت استعمال ہوتا ہے جب کوئی بات بظاہر الٹ یا عجیب لگے لیکن حقیقت میں درست ہو

englishMeaning: A one sided relationship where one person feels emotionally connected to a public figure who does not know them. Often used for fans and celebrities.
synonyms: One sided attachment
antonyms: Mutual bond
examples: Many fans develop parasocial bonds with influencers. The show created parasocial closeness with its host. Parasocial connections can feel real. Social media increases parasocial behavior.

englishMeaning: To dry out completely or cause to become very thirsty or dry. Often used for crops, soil, or figuratively for thirst or desire.
synonyms: Dry, Dehydrate, Scorch, Desiccate
antonyms: Moisten, Hydrate, Soak, Drench
examples: The summer sun parched the fields, leaving them cracked. After hours of walking in the desert, he felt parched and needed water. The heat parched the fruit, making it shriveled and tough. His curiosity parched for knowledge could not be satisfied by books alone.
sindhiMeaning: سُڪائي ڇڏڻ، ڪنهن شيءَ کي تمام گهڻو خشڪ ڪرڻ (جهڙوڪ زمين ٻوٽي يا کاڌي کي سج يا گرميءَ سان سُڪل ڪرڻ)
urduMeaning: خشک کرنا، پیاسا کرنا، کسی چیز کو مکمل طور پر خشک کر دینا (جیسے زمین پودا یا خوراک کو سورج یا گرمی سے خشک کرنا)

englishMeaning: A durable material prepared from the skin of animals such as sheep or goats, used in ancient and medieval times for writing important documents, manuscripts, and religious texts. It can also refer to a formal certificate or document written on such material. In modern usage, it may describe paper that resembles this material in texture or color. Something dry, pale, or shriveled in appearance. An official document such as a diploma or legal certificate.
synonyms: Vellum, Manuscript paper, Sheepskin document, Diploma, Certificate
antonyms: Digital document, Electronic file, Modern paper
examples: The ancient manuscript was written on parchment. The king signed the treaty on fine parchment. Her face looked pale like old parchment. The diploma was printed on thick parchment paper. She proudly framed her university parchment. His skin looked like parchment after days in the sun.
sindhiMeaning: هڪ مضبوط مواد جيڪو رڍ ٻڪري يا ٻين جانورن جي کل مان ٺاهيو ويندو هو ۽ قديم دور ۾ اهم دستاويزن مذهبي ڪتابن ۽ تحريرن لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو هو، اڄڪلهه اهو لفظ اهڙي ڪاغذ لاءِ به استعمال ٿيندو آهي جيڪو ظاهر يا بناوت ۾ اهڙو لڳي، ڪا شيءِ جيڪا سڪي ڦڪي يا سڙيل جهڙي لڳي، سرڪاري سند يا ڊگري

englishMeaning: To reduce, trim, or cut something down. To remove a small amount from something, often slowly and carefully. It is commonly used for cutting the skin of fruits or vegetables, and also for reducing costs, numbers, or limits step by step.
synonyms: Trim, Reduce, Cut, Peel, Lessen
antonyms: Increase, Add, Expand, Enlarge
examples: She pared the apple before giving it to the child. The company plans to pare its expenses next year. He tried to pare down the long report to a short summary. The chef carefully pared the vegetables for the soup.
sindhiMeaning: گهٽائڻ يا ٿورو ٿورو ڪٽڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ مان ٿورو ٿورو حصو ڪٽڻ يا گهٽ ڪرڻ، جيئن ميوي جي کل لاھڻ يا خرچ گھٽائڻ
urduMeaning: کم کرنا یا تھوڑا تھوڑا کاٹنا، کسی چیز کو آہستہ آہستہ کم کرنا یا اس کا غیر ضروری حصہ کاٹ دینا، جیسے پھل کا چھلکا اتارنا یا اخراجات کم کرنا

englishMeaning: To remove small parts. To gradually remove or cut away parts of something, often little by little
synonyms: Remove, Shave off, Strip, Cut away
antonyms: Attach, Add, Build, Join
examples: She pared away the rough edges of the wooden sculpture. The chef pared away the skin of the fruit before serving. Over time, he pared away unnecessary expenses from his budget. They pared away the extra material to fit the fabric perfectly.

englishMeaning: To cut back gradually. To cut down or reduce something carefully and systematically. Often used in financial or organizational contexts to indicate trimming excess.
synonyms: Scale back, Reduce, Cut, Decrease
antonyms: Boost, Expand, Raise, Build up
examples: The company plans to pare back unnecessary expenses next quarter. She pared back her wardrobe to just the essentials. The government is paring back subsidies for certain industries. He decided to pare back his commitments to focus on family.
sindhiMeaning: آهستي آهستي ڪنهن شيءِ کي گهٽائڻ يا ڪٽڻ، خاص طور تي خرچ يا سائيز کي منظم طريقي سان گهٽائڻ
urduMeaning: بتدریج کم کرنا، کسی چیز کو آہستہ آہستہ کم کرنا یا چھانٹنا، خاص طور پر خرچ یا سائز کو منظم طریقے سے کم کرنا

englishMeaning: To reduce size, number, or amount. To make something smaller or simpler by removing unnecessary parts, costs, or details.
synonyms: Reduce, Cut back, Trim, Lessen
antonyms: Expand, Increase, Enlarge, Add
examples: The company decided to pare down its workforce to save costs. She pared down her wardrobe before moving to a smaller apartment. The editor asked the writer to pare down the article to 1,000 words. They are trying to pare down unnecessary expenses this month.
sindhiMeaning: گهٽائڻ، غير ضروري شيون ڪڍي گهٽ ڪرڻ (مثال طور خرچ ڪم يا سامان ۾ گهٽتائي ڪرڻ)

englishMeaning: A local administrative area in the Christian church that has its own church and priest. The Christian community living in a specific church area. The members of a local church congregation. A small local administrative unit in some countries such as parts of the United Kingdom or the United States.
synonyms: Church district, Congregation area, Church community, Ecclesiastical district
antonyms: Diocese (a larger church region), Metropolis, Central city district
examples: The priest visited every family in the parish during the festival. The parish built a new community hall next to the church. People in the parish gathered to help poor families in winter. She has lived in the same parish since childhood.

englishMeaning: An essential or necessary part of something. Something that cannot be separated from the whole. It refers to something that is a natural, basic, or integral element of a situation, activity, or system.
synonyms: Inseparable part, Fundamental aspect, Core component
antonyms:
Optional part, Separate element, Unnecessary addition, 
Nonessential
examples: Hard work is part and parcel of success. Stress is part and parcel of modern life. Learning from failure is part and parcel of growing up. Communication is part and parcel of a healthy relationship.
sindhiMeaning: ضروري حصو، حصو ۽ جزو، لازمي حصو، جدا نه ٿي سگهندڙ حصو
urduMeaning: لازمی حصہ، مستقل حصہ، جزوِ لازم، الگ نہ ہونے والا حصہ

englishMeaning: The act of leaving or saying goodbye. A division or separation between two things. A line made by dividing hair on the head. The end of a relationship, friendship, or period of time.
synonyms: Farewell, Separation, Departure, Goodbye, Division
antonyms: Meeting, Reunion, Gathering, Arrival, Union
examples: Their parting was full of tears and sadness. We said our parting words before she left for another country. There was a parting of ways after the disagreement. She combed her hair with a middle parting.

englishMeaning: A person who enjoys going to parties often and behaves in a very energetic, lively, and social way at social gatherings. Someone who loves nightlife, celebrations, music, dancing, and social events. Such a person usually enjoys staying out late, meeting new people, and having fun in crowded or festive environments. The phrase is informal and often used in a friendly or humorous way.
synonyms: Social butterfly, Life of the party, Extrovert, Night owl (contextual), Celebrator
antonyms: Introvert, Homebody, Reserved person, Quiet person, Stay-at-home type
examples: He is a real party animal and never misses a weekend celebration. My cousin became a party animal after joining university. She was known as a party animal during her college days. Don’t invite him if you want a quiet evening, he is a party animal.
sindhiMeaning: اهڙو ماڻهو جيڪو گهڻيون پارٽيون ڪري، خوش مزاج پرجوش ۽ سماجي ميل جول پسند ڪري، جيڪو وندر محفلن ۽ گڏجاڻين کي پسند ڪري، جيڪو گهڻو وقت دوستن سان ميل جول ۽ پارٽين ۾ گذاري
urduMeaning: ایسا شخص جو اکثر پارٹیوں میں جاتا ہے اور بہت زیادہ خوش مزاج پرجوش اور سماجی ہوتا ہے، جو تفریح محفلوں اور میل جول کو ترجیح دیتا ہے، جو زیادہ وقت گھروں سے باہر پارٹیوں میں گزارتا ہے

englishMeaning: To give or share something to each person in a group. To distribute something among a group of people, either physically or by sharing information. It can also mean to circulate something widely, sometimes gossip or news.

englishMeaning: Relating to or involving strong controversy or argument; of the nature of a polemic. Aggressively challenging or attacking established opinions or doctrines.

englishMeaning: Completely different from each other. Having nothing in common; opposite in nature, opinion, or character.
synonyms: Opposite, Unlike, Contrary
antonyms: Similar, Alike, Related
examples: Their views are poles apart. Their opinions on politics are poles apart. The twins may look alike, but their personalities are poles apart. Our goals are poles apart, you want fame, I want peace. The two cultures are poles apart in traditions and values.
sindhiMeaning: بلڪل مختلف، بلڪل ابتڙ، اهڙا ٻه ماڻهو خيال يا شيون جيڪي بلڪل مختلف هجن ۽ ڪابه مشابهت نه رکندا هجن

englishMeaning: To finish something completely, usually food, work, or a task. It can also mean to defeat someone decisively in informal contexts.

antonyms: Leave, Neglect, Abandon, Start
examples: They polished off the cake in minutes. He polished off his homework before dinner. The team polished off their rivals. We polished off the entire project today.

englishMeaning: To improve or refine something to make it look or perform better. To make something cleaner, more attractive, or more effective, especially skills, appearance, or work. It implies refining or improving something that already exists rather than creating it from scratch.

englishMeaning: A form of marriage in which a woman has more than one husband at the same time. A social or cultural practice where a single woman is legally or socially married to multiple men simultaneously. It is the opposite of polygyny

sindhiMeaning: اهڙي شادي جو نظام جنهن ۾ هڪ عورت هڪ ئي وقت ۾ ڪيترن مڙسن سان شادي ڪري ٿي

englishMeaning: A marriage system in which a man has more than one wife at the same time. Polygyny is a type of polygamy practiced in some cultures and religions where a single man is legally or socially allowed to have multiple wives simultaneously.
synonyms: Plural marriage, Multiple marriage (for men)
antonyms: Monogamy (marriage with only one spouse), Polyandry (one woman with multiple husbands)

sindhiMeaning: گهڻيون زالون ڪرڻ جو رواج، اهڙو نظام جنهن ۾ هڪ مرد وٽ هڪ وقت ۾ هڪ کان وڌيڪ زالون هجن

englishMeaning: A person who has deep knowledge in many different subjects. A person who is highly knowledgeable and skilled in many different fields such as science, literature, art, philosophy, or mathematics. This word is used for someone whose learning is broad and impressive across several areas rather than only one subject.
synonyms: Scholar, Intellectual, Savant, Genius, Learned person, Renaissance person, All-rounder

englishMeaning: Having knowledge in many different subjects. A person who is learned in multiple fields such as science, literature, arts, and philosophy, showing wide-ranging intellectual ability and curiosity.

englishMeaning: Wide knowledge or learning in many different subjects. The ability or habit of gaining deep knowledge across a wide range of disciplines such as science, arts, literature, and philosophy. A person with polymathy is called a polymath and is skilled in multiple fields rather than specializing in just one.

englishMeaning: The belief that there is more than one God. A religious belief system where multiple deities are recognized and worshiped, each often having distinct powers, responsibilities, or domains. It contrasts with monotheism, which is the belief in a single deity.

antonyms: Monotheism, Unitarianism
examples: Ancient Greeks practiced polytheism with gods like Zeus and Athena. Hinduism is often described as a form of polytheism. Many civilizations in history were polytheistic before monotheistic religions emerged. Polytheism allows worshippers to appeal to different gods for different needs.
sindhiMeaning: شرِڪ، گھڻ خدائي جو عقيدو، گھڻا ديوتائن تي ايمان يا پوڄا

antonyms: Simplicity, Modesty, Humility, Plainness, Unpretentiousness

englishMeaning: To smell bad. A very bad or strong unpleasant smell. A foul odor coming from something rotten or dirty. Informal British slang for stink or bad smell. It is an informal word used in everyday speech.

examples: There is a pong coming from the kitchen bin. His socks had a terrible pong after the game. I could smell the pong of rotten eggs in the room. The fridge has started to pong badly.

englishMeaning: A situation where different people give different and sometimes contradictory accounts of the same event because each person sees and remembers it differently. The Rashomon effect describes how individuals can experience the same incident in different ways and later explain it according to their own perspective, emotions, memories, interests, or biases. It is often discussed in psychology, journalism, law, history, literature, and social sciences.
synonyms: Subjective interpretation, Conflicting perspectives, Multiple viewpoints, Differing testimony, Perceptual bias, Contradictory accounts
antonyms: Objective truth, Consistent account, Unified perspective, Agreed narrative, Common understanding
examples: During the court case, every witness described the accident differently, showing the Rashomon effect. The siblings remembered their childhood argument in completely opposite ways because of the Rashomon effect. Journalists often encounter the Rashomon effect when interviewing several people about the same political event. In team meetings, the Rashomon effect can appear when employees recall the same discussion differently.

englishMeaning: A situation where something increases or moves forward step by step and does not easily go back to its previous lower level. A ratchet effect happens when progress, prices, habits, or systems move in one direction, usually upward, and it becomes difficult to reverse that change. It is often used in economics, business, psychology, and social behavior.
synonyms: Irreversible increase, One way growth, Upward lock, Progressive rise, Permanent escalation, Sticky increase
antonyms: Reversal, Reduction, Decline, Decrease, Flexibility, Backward movement
examples: Due to the ratchet effect, employees found it difficult to accept lower salaries after a pay increase. englishMeaning: To respond to someone’s action, feeling, or kindness by giving the same kind of response in return. It is often used for emotions such as love, respect, friendship, help, or cooperation. It can also refer to mutual exchange between two sides.
synonyms: Return, Repay, Respond, Requite, Exchange
antonyms: Ignore, Refuse, Reject, Withhold, Neglect
examples: She smiled at him, but he did not reciprocate the gesture. I helped him many times and he always reciprocated my kindness. True friendship grows when both people reciprocate trust and respect. The two countries agreed to reciprocate trade benefits.

englishMeaning: To think, believe, or consider something to be true. To calculate or count. To form an opinion or judgement about something, or to estimate/guess a value. To mean “I think” or “I suppose”. In another sense, it can mean to calculate numbers or totals.

sindhiMeaning: سمجهڻ، اندازو لڳائڻ، ڳڻپ ڪرڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ بابت راءِ قائم ڪرڻ، اندازو لڳائڻ يا حساب ڪرڻ، عام ڳالهه ٻولهه ۾ اهو لفظ “مان سمجهان ٿو” جي معنى ۾ به استعمال ٿئي ٿو

englishMeaning: Living apart from society, avoiding the company of other people, and preferring solitude. A person who prefers to stay away from social activities and large groups of people. Such a person usually enjoys privacy, solitude, and a quiet lifestyle. Being reclusive does not necessarily mean being unfriendly; it simply means preferring limited social interaction.

antonyms: Sociable, Outgoing, Friendly, Extroverted, Gregarious, Communicative
examples: The reclusive writer rarely appeared in public after publishing his famous novel. She lived a reclusive life in a small cottage near the mountains. Although reclusive, he was respected for his wisdom and knowledge. The billionaire became increasingly reclusive as he grew older.

englishMeaning: The act of restoring friendly relations after a disagreement. The process of bringing people, groups, or ideas back into agreement after conflict, misunderstanding, or hostility
synonyms: Settlement, Harmony, Peace, Agreement, Compromise
antonyms: Conflict, Disagreement, Hostility, Alienation, Discord
examples: The reconciliation between the two countries took several years of dialogue. Family reconciliation helped heal old emotional wounds. Truth and reconciliation are essential after a long period of conflict. The manager encouraged reconciliation between the coworkers to improve teamwork.

englishMeaning: The act of being saved, corrected, or brought back to a good state. The act of saving or being saved from sin, error, or evil. It also means making up for a mistake, regaining respect, or fulfilling a promise or obligation. In finance, it means reclaiming or paying off something such as a loan or bond.
synonyms: Salvation, Recovery, Deliverance, Atonement, Restoration
antonyms: Damnation, Loss, Ruin, Condemnation, Failure

antonyms: Harmful, Damaging, Destructive, Corrupting, Worsening
examples: His apology had a redemptive effect on their friendship. The charity work gave her life a redemptive purpose. The film tells a redemptive story of forgiveness and change. Helping others can be a redemptive experience after failure.

englishMeaning: The state of being excessive, unnecessary, or more than what is needed. The condition where something is repeated or present in greater quantity than required. It often describes unnecessary repetition in language, writing, ideas, or objects. It can also refer to surplus or overflow of something.
synonyms: Excess, Superfluity, Surplus, Repetition, Verbosity
antonyms: Brevity, Conciseness, Scarcity, Lack, Shortage
examples: The report contains some redundance that makes it longer than necessary. Good writing avoids redundance and keeps ideas clear and direct. The teacher asked the student to remove redundance from the essay. The speech lost its impact because of redundance in the arguments.

urduMeaning: افراط ، بہتات ، زیادتی ، فضول ، کثیر ، فضول یا زائد ہونا، غیر ضروری، تکرار، فالتو پن، اس حالت کو کہتے ہیں جب کوئی لفظ خیال یا چیز ضرورت سے زیادہ ہو یا بار بار غیر ضروری طور پر دہرائی جائے، یہ تحریر گفتگو یا مقدار میں اضافی ہونے کو ظاہر کرتا ہے

synonyms: Excess, Surplus, Superfluity, Repetition, Duplication
antonyms: Necessity, Need, Essentiality, Importance, Requirement
examples: The editor removed several sentences because they created redundancy in the paragraph. Many workers faced redundancy when the company automated its production line. The aircraft system includes redundancy to ensure safety if one component fails. Good writing avoids redundancy and keeps ideas clear and concise.

englishMeaning: Something that is unnecessary, extra, or not needed. Describes a word, idea, worker, or thing that is no longer useful, needed, or required because there is too much of it or it repeats what is already present.

antonyms: Necessary, Essential, Required, Useful, Important

antonyms: Concisely, Briefly, Efficiently, Succinctly
examples: Data are redundantly stored in multiple different locations. The report was written redundantly, repeating the same facts in several paragraphs. antonyms: Steady, Balance, Stabilize, Flat, Board, Slab
examples: He reeled after hearing the shocking news. She reeled from the punch. He bought a new fishing reel. The movie reel was damaged.

englishMeaning: To soak something thoroughly with liquid until no more can be absorbed. To fill something completely with a substance, feeling, color, sound, or influence. englishMeaning: A condition in which no more of something can be added, absorbed, or accepted. englishMeaning: A person, usually a boy or man, who is considered weak, overly sensitive, or lacking courage. It is often used as an insult. A cowardly person. Someone easily frightened. A person who avoids tough or risky situations. A term used teasingly among friends in a lighthearted way

englishMeaning: A person who doubts the truth of claims without evidence. Someone who questions accepted ideas or beliefs. A person who refuses to accept something until it is proven. A critical thinker who demands facts before belief.

antonyms: Believer, Trusting person, Faithful, Credulous person, Gullible person, Accepting person
examples: The skeptic refused to believe the story without evidence. She is a skeptic when it comes to advertisements and marketing claims. Even after the explanation, the skeptic asked for more proof. Scientists are often skeptics who test ideas before accepting them.
sindhiMeaning: شڪ ڪندڙ، سوال ڪندڙ، بغير ثبوت جي نه مڃيندڙ ماڻهو، اهڙو شخص جيڪو ڪنهن به ڳالهه دعويٰ يا عقيدي کي بغير ثبوت جي قبول نه ڪري ۽ هميشه شڪ يا سوال ڪري

englishMeaning: Having doubt about something and not easily convinced. Questioning the truth, validity, or reliability of something. Showing a cautious attitude before accepting claims or information. Not believing something until strong evidence is given

englishMeaning: In a doubtful or questioning way, not easily believing something. With suspicion about truth or honesty. In a critical thinking manner. With doubt about success or reality. With cautious disbelief.
synonyms: Doubtfully, Suspiciously, Questioningly, Unbelievingly, Doubtingly
antonyms: Confidently, Believingly, Trustingly, Surely, Faithfully

englishMeaning: Doubting or questioning the truth of something until there is enough proof. antonyms: Belief, Trust, Faith, Confidence, Acceptance, Certainty
