englishMeaning: Making use of a situation or person in an unfair way for one's own benefit. Treating people or resources in a way that takes advantage of them without fair return. Characterised by exploitation.
synonyms: Predatory, Abusive, Oppressive, Manipulative, Parasitic, Unfair
antonyms: Fair, Just, Equitable, Ethical, Generous
examples: The report exposed the exploitative practices of the company toward its overseas workers. She described the contract as exploitative and refused to sign it under any circumstances. The exploitative relationship between the two parties was finally brought to light by an investigative journalist. The charity worked to protect children from exploitative labour in the region. His exploitative approach to business relationships ultimately left him without any loyal partners.

englishMeaning: Showing no mercy or compassion for others. Cruel and harsh without any softening of attitude or treatment. Relentlessly severe or unforgiving.
synonyms: Ruthless, Pitiless, Cruel, Heartless, Brutal, Unforgiving
antonyms: Merciful, Kind, Compassionate, Lenient, Forgiving
examples: The merciless heat of the desert made the journey almost unbearable for the expedition. She faced merciless criticism from reviewers after the publication of her first novel. The merciless storm destroyed dozens of homes in the coastal village overnight. He was known for his merciless treatment of those who failed to meet his extremely high standards. The merciless enforcement of the law left no room for appeals or special circumstances.

englishMeaning: Taking advantage of opportunities as and when they arise, especially without considering principles or consequences. Done or characterised by exploiting circumstances as they arise rather than following a consistent plan. Adapting to circumstances in a manner that serves one's immediate interests.
synonyms: Self-serving, Calculating, Expedient, Exploitative, Pragmatic
antonyms: Principled, Consistent, Ethical, Honest, Straightforward
examples: The opportunistic businessman bought the property at a fraction of its value during the economic crisis. Her critics described her decision to switch parties as purely opportunistic. The virus is described as opportunistic because it primarily attacks those with weakened immune systems. He was accused of making an opportunistic claim that had more to do with money than principle. The opportunistic hiring policy allowed the company to recruit talent whenever it became available.

englishMeaning: Relating to or characteristic of a parasite. Living on or benefiting at the expense of another organism or person without giving anything in return. Taking from others without contributing anything in exchange.
synonyms: Exploitative, Freeloading, Dependent, Predatory, Bloodsucking
antonyms: Symbiotic, Mutualistic, Giving, Contributing, Productive
examples: Some fungi have a parasitic relationship with trees, drawing nutrients without providing any benefit. He was described by his former colleagues as a parasitic individual who lived off the efforts of others. The parasite enters the host body and begins a parasitic relationship that can last for years. The relationship had become entirely parasitic — she gave everything while he contributed nothing. Parasitic vines can eventually kill the trees they rely on for support.

synonyms: Excessive, Unreasonable, Outrageous, Inflated, Overpriced, Exorbitant
antonyms: Reasonable, Fair, Affordable, Modest, Justified
examples: The hotel charged an extortionate amount for a room that was basic and poorly maintained. She complained that the legal fees were extortionate and completely out of proportion to the work done. The landlord's extortionate rent increases forced several long-term tenants to move out. synonyms: Observer, Onlooker, Viewer, Watcher, Bystander, Audience member
antonyms: Participant, Performer, Competitor, Player, Contributor
examples: Thousands of spectators lined the streets to watch the annual parade pass by. The stadium was packed with spectators who had come from across the country for the final. synonyms: Officiant, Minister, Priest, Participant, Officiate
antonyms: Observer, Spectator, Bystander

antonyms: None commonly accepted

sindhiMeaning: سنگهاڙو، پاڻي ۾ ٿيندڙ هڪ سبزي جيڪا اندران اڇي ۽ ڪرنچي هوندي آهي، ايشيائي کاڌن ۾ عام استعمال ٿيندڙ ميوو، هڪ سخت ڪاري ڇوٿڙي وارو پاڻيءَ جو ميوو، سوپ ۽ مٺاين ۾ استعمال ٿيندڙ لذيذ شيءِ، تازو کائجي يا اٽو ٺاهي استعمال ڪجي ٿو
urduMeaning: سنگھاڑا، پانی میں اگنے والی ایک سبزی جو اندر سے سفید اور کرکری ہوتی ہے، ایشیائی کھانوں میں عام استعمال ہونے والا پھل، سخت سیاہ چھلکے والا پانی کا پھل، سوپ اور میٹھے پکوانوں میں استعمال ہونے والی چیز، تازہ کھایا جاتا ہے یا آٹا بنا کر استعمال ہوتا ہے

englishMeaning: A citrus fruit similar to a lemon but sweeter and less sour. A juicy green or yellowish fruit rich in vitamin C. A tropical fruit used to make refreshing drinks. A fruit known for its digestive and cooling properties. A common citrus fruit in South Asia and the Middle East.
synonyms: Mosambi, Sweet lemon, Citrus limetta
antonyms: Sour lime, Lemon
examples: A glass of fresh sweet lime juice is very refreshing. Doctors often recommend sweet lime for good digestion. She peeled a sweet lime and ate it slowly. Sweet limes are widely grown in Pakistan and India.
sindhiMeaning: مِٺو، هڪ رَسدار ترش ميوو جيڪو نمبوءَ جهڙو پر مٺو هوندو آهي، وٽامن سي سان ڀرپور سائو يا پيلو ميوو، ٺنڍي مشروب ٺاهڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿيندڙ ميوو، هاضمي ۽ ٺنڍڪ لاءِ فائديمند ميوو، ڏکڻ ايشيا ۽ وچ اوڀر جو عام سٽرس ميوو
urduMeaning: میٹھا، ایک رسیلا ترش پھل جو لیموں سے مشابہ مگر میٹھا ہوتا ہے، وٹامن سی سے بھرپور سبز یا زرد پھل، ٹھنڈے مشروبات بنانے کے لیے استعمال ہونے والا پھل، ہاضمے اور ٹھنڈک کے لیے مفید پھل، جنوبی ایشیا اور مشرقِ وسطیٰ کا عام سٹرس پھل

englishMeaning: A dark purple fruit native to South Asia, also known as jamun. A tropical fruit with sweet-sour flesh and medicinal value. A fruit that stains the tongue purple when eaten. A summer fruit used in juices and desserts. A traditional remedy for diabetes and digestive issues.
synonyms: Jamun, Black plum, Indian blackberry, Syzygium cumini
antonyms: (no direct antonym)
examples: Java plums are widely eaten during the summer season. My mother makes delicious juice from Java plums. Java plum seeds are used in herbal medicines. He enjoyed a bowl of fresh Java plums after lunch.
sindhiMeaning: جامن، هڪ ڳاڙهي واڱڻائي رنگ جو ميوو جيڪو ڏکڻ ايشيا جو مقامي آهي، مٺو کٽو ذائقو رکندڙ ۽ دوائي فائدن سان ڀرپور ميوو، اهو ميوو جيڪو کائڻ سان زبان کي واڱڻائي ڪري ڇڏي، شربت ۽ مٺاين ۾ استعمال ٿيندڙ گرمين جو ميوو، شگر ۽ هاضمي جي بيمارين لاءِ روايتي علاج
urduMeaning: جامن، ایک گہرے جامنی رنگ کا پھل جو جنوبی ایشیا کا مقامی ہے، میٹھا کھٹا ذائقہ رکھنے والا اور دوائی فوائد سے بھرپور پھل، وہ پھل جو کھانے سے زبان جامنی ہو جاتی ہے، شربت اور میٹھے پکوانوں میں استعمال ہونے والا گرمیوں کا پھل، شوگر اور ہاضمے کے مسائل کا روایتی علاج

englishMeaning: A small round dark blue fruit that grows on shrubs. A sweet berry rich in antioxidants and vitamins. A fruit used in muffins, pies, jams, and smoothies. A superfood known for its health benefits. A cultivated or wild berry native to North America.
synonyms: Bilberry, Huckleberry, Vaccinium berry
antonyms: (no direct antonym)
examples: She added fresh blueberries to her morning cereal. Blueberry muffins are a favorite in our family. Studies show that blueberries improve memory and health. The children love blueberry ice cream in summer.
sindhiMeaning: بلو بيري، هڪ ننڍو گول گهرو نيرو ميوو جيڪو ٻوٽن تي ٿيندو آهي، اينٽي آڪسيڊنٽس ۽ وٽامنن سان ڀرپور مٺو ميوو، ڪيڪ، پائيءَ ۽ جام ۾ استعمال ٿيندڙ ميوو، صحت لاءِ فائديمند سپر فوڊ، اتر آمريڪا جو مقامي جهنگلي يا ڪاشتي ميوو
urduMeaning: بلو بیری، ایک چھوٹا گول گہرے نیلے رنگ کا پھل جو جھاڑیوں پر لگتا ہے، اینٹی آکسیڈنٹس اور وٹامنز سے بھرپور میٹھا پھل، کیک، پائی اور جام میں استعمال ہونے والا پھل، صحت کے لیے مفید سپر فوڈ، شمالی امریکہ کا مقامی جنگلی یا کاشت شدہ پھل

englishMeaning: A tropical fruit with a soft, creamy sweet flesh and a green scaly skin. A fruit known for its custard-like texture inside. A member of the Annonaceae family widely grown in South Asia. A fruit rich in vitamins, minerals, and natural sugars. A dessert-like fruit often eaten fresh or in shakes.
synonyms: Sharifa, Sitaphal, Sugar apple (loose), Annona
antonyms: (no direct antonym)
examples: The custard apple has a sweet and creamy taste. She loves eating custard apple after dinner. Custard apples are available in the market during autumn. My grandmother made a delicious custard apple milkshake.
sindhiMeaning: شريفو، هڪ گرم ملڪن جو ميوو جنهن جو گودو نرم، مٺو ۽ ڪريم جهڙو هوندو آهي ۽ ڇوٿڙي سائو ۽ ٿورو ڇلن وارو هوندو، جنهن جي اندر جو ذائقو ڪسٽرڊ جهڙو مٺو ۽ خوشبودار هوندو، ڏکڻ ايشيا ۾ عام ڪاشت ٿيندڙ ميوو، وٽامنن ۽ معدنيات سان ڀرپور ميوو، تازو کائجي يا شيڪ ۾ استعمال ڪجي ٿو
urduMeaning: شریفہ، ایک گرم ممالک کا پھل جس کا گودا نرم، میٹھا اور کریمی ہوتا ہے اور چھلکا سبز اور کھردرا ہوتا ہے، جس کے اندر کا ذائقہ کسٹرڈ جیسا میٹھا اور خوشبودار ہوتا ہے، جنوبی ایشیا میں عام کاشت ہونے والا پھل، وٹامنز اور معدنیات سے بھرپور پھل، تازہ کھایا جاتا ہے یا شیک میں استعمال ہوتا ہے

englishMeaning: A hard-shelled tropical fruit with a strong aroma and tangy pulp. A fruit used to make chutneys, jams, and drinks. A fruit widely used in Ayurvedic medicine for digestion. A round brown fruit with sticky brown flesh inside. A native fruit of South Asia known for its medicinal value.
synonyms: Bael fruit, Kaith, Elephant apple, Limonia acidissima
antonyms: (no direct antonym)
examples: Wood apple chutney is a traditional dish in South Asia. He drank a glass of wood apple juice for digestion. The wood apple has a very hard outer shell. My mother often prepared wood apple sherbet in summer.
sindhiMeaning: ڪٺ بيل، هڪ سخت ڇوٿڙي وارو گرم ملڪن جو ميوو جنهن جي خوشبو تيز ۽ گودو کٽو مٺو هوندو آهي، چٽني، جام ۽ شربت ٺاهڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿيندڙ ميوو، هاضمي لاءِ آيوروديڪ دوائن ۾ استعمال ٿيندڙ ميوو، اندران چپچپي ڀوري گودي وارو ميوو، ڏکڻ ايشيا جو دوائي فائدن وارو مقامي ميوو
urduMeaning: کٹھ بیل، سخت چھلکے والا گرم علاقوں کا پھل جس کی خوشبو تیز اور گودا کھٹا میٹھا ہوتا ہے، چٹنی، جام اور شربت بنانے کے لیے استعمال ہونے والا پھل، ہاضمے کے لیے آیورویدک ادویات میں استعمال ہونے والا پھل، اندر سے چپچپے بھورے گودے والا پھل، جنوبی ایشیا کا دوائی فوائد رکھنے والا مقامی پھل

englishMeaning: A sweet tropical fruit similar to custard apple with soft segmented flesh. A fruit with a lumpy green skin and sugary pulp inside. A member of the Annona family known for its sweetness. A fruit rich in vitamin C and natural fibers. A dessert-like fruit popular in Asian and tropical countries.
synonyms: Sweetsop, Sitaphal, Annona squamosa, Sharifa
antonyms: (no direct antonym)
examples: The sugar apple is one of the sweetest tropical fruits. She enjoyed a fresh sugar apple in the garden. Sugar apple pulp is often used in ice creams. Farmers in tropical regions grow sugar apples widely.
sindhiMeaning: شوگر ايپل، هڪ مٺو گرم ملڪن جو ميوو جيڪو شريفي جهڙو هوندو آهي ۽ اندران گودو ٽڪرن ۾ ورهايل هوندو، ڇوٿڙي سائو ۽ اُڀرندڙ حصن وارو ۽ گودو مٺو ۽ خوشبودار، انونا خاندان جو مٺو ميوو، وٽامن سي ۽ فائبر سان ڀرپور ميوو، ايشيائي ۽ گرم ملڪن ۾ مقبول مٺو ميوو
urduMeaning: شوگر ایپل، ایک میٹھا گرم علاقوں کا پھل جو شریفے جیسا ہوتا ہے اور اندر سے گودا حصوں میں تقسیم ہوتا ہے، چھلکا سبز اور ابھری ہوئی سطح والا اور گودا میٹھا اور خوشبودار، اننا خاندان کا میٹھا پھل، وٹامن سی اور فائبر سے بھرپور پھل، ایشیائی اور گرم ممالک میں مقبول میٹھا پھل

englishMeaning: A large tropical fruit resembling a heart in shape, related to custard apple. A fruit with reddish-brown skin and creamy sweet flesh. A member of the Annona family grown in warm regions. A fruit rich in nutrients and used in traditional desserts. A sweet edible fruit named for its heart-like appearance.
synonyms: Ramphal, Annona reticulata, Custard apple (variant)
antonyms: (no direct antonym)
examples: The bullock's heart fruit is sweet and creamy inside. Bullock's heart is often mistaken for custard apple. Farmers grow bullock's heart trees in tropical climates. She tasted bullock's heart for the first time on her trip.
sindhiMeaning: دل جي شڪل جو وڏو گرم ملڪن جو ميوو جيڪو شريفي جي خاندان سان تعلق رکي، ڳاڙهسرو ڀورو ڇوٿڙو ۽ اندران ڪريمي مٺو گودو، گرم علائقن ۾ ڪاشت ٿيندڙ انونا خاندان جو ميوو، غذائيت سان ڀرپور ۽ روايتي مٺاين ۾ استعمال ٿيندڙ ميوو، دل جي شڪل جي مناسبت سان مشهور مٺو ميوو
urduMeaning: دل کی شکل کا بڑا گرم ممالک کا پھل جو شریفے کے خاندان سے تعلق رکھتا ہے، سرخی مائل بھورے چھلکے اور اندر سے کریمی میٹھا گودا رکھنے والا پھل، گرم علاقوں میں کاشت ہونے والا اننا خاندان کا پھل، غذائیت سے بھرپور اور روایتی میٹھے پکوانوں میں استعمال ہونے والا پھل، دل کی شکل کی مناسبت سے مشہور میٹھا پھل

englishMeaning: A flexible board used for jumping high in diving or gymnastics. Something that helps someone start or advance a career or activity. A base or opportunity for further success. A source of inspiration or motivation to begin something. A launching point for progress or achievement.
synonyms: Launchpad, Starting point, Platform, Basis, Foundation, Stepping stone, Catalyst
antonyms: Barrier, Obstacle, Hindrance, Dead end, Setback
examples: The diver leapt from the springboard into the pool. The scholarship became a springboard for her career. His first novel served as a springboard for greater success. Volunteering can be a springboard to full-time employment.
sindhiMeaning: لڏندڙ تختو جيڪو غوطه خوري يا جمناسٽڪس ۾ اڀرڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿيندو آهي، ڪنهن ڪم يا ڪيريئر شروع ڪرڻ يا اڳتي وڌائڻ ۾ مدد ڏيندڙ ذريعو، ڪاميابيءَ لاءِ بنياد يا موقعو، ڪنهن ڪم شروع ڪرڻ لاءِ حوصلي جو ذريعو، ترقيءَ لاءِ ابتدائي پليٽ فارم
urduMeaning: لچکدار تختہ جو غوطہ خوری یا جمناسٹکس میں اونچا اچھلنے کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے، کسی کام یا کیریئر کو شروع کرنے یا آگے بڑھانے میں مددگار ذریعہ، کامیابی کے لیے بنیاد یا موقع، کسی کام کے آغاز کے لیے حوصلے کا ذریعہ، ترقی کے لیے ابتدائی پلیٹ فارم

englishMeaning: In a way that affects the mind without a person being aware of it. Below the level of conscious perception. Influencing thoughts, feelings, or behavior unconsciously. In a manner not directly noticed by the senses. Through hidden or indirect signals to the subconscious mind.
synonyms: Unconsciously, Unknowingly, Indirectly, Subconsciously, Imperceptibly
antonyms: Consciously, Knowingly, Openly, Directly, Deliberately
examples: Advertisements often influence people subliminally. The music subliminally created a calm mood in the room. He was subliminally affected by the words he heard as a child. Colors can subliminally change how we feel.
sindhiMeaning: لاشعوري طور تي، اهڙي انداز ۾ جيڪو ذهن تي بنا ڄاڻ اثر انداز ٿئي، شعور جي حد کان ھيٺ، بنا احساس جي سوچن يا جذبن تي اثر وجهڻ، اهڙي طرح جو حواس بنا محسوس ڪئي متاثر ٿين، مخفي يا اڻ سڌي اشارن ذريعي دماغ تي اثر ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: لاشعوری طور پر، ایسے انداز میں جو ذہن پر بغیر جانے اثر انداز ہو، شعور کی سطح سے نیچے، بغیر احساس کے سوچ یا جذبات پر اثر ڈالنا، ایسے کہ حواس محسوس کیے بغیر متاثر ہوں، پوشیدہ یا بالواسطہ اشاروں سے ذہن پر اثر ڈالنا

englishMeaning: To end a relationship, connection, or association with someone or something. To completely stop communication or dealings with a person, group, or organization. To break off long-standing bonds, whether emotional, social, or professional. To disconnect oneself from influences, habits, or people considered harmful. To formally sever links or agreements between individuals, families, or nations.
synonyms: Sever ties, Break off, Disconnect, Part ways, End relations, Break away, Disassociate, Separate, Withdraw, Split up
antonyms: Reconnect, Bond, Unite, Join, Attach, Maintain, Preserve, Reconcile, Strengthen, Befriend
examples: After years of conflict, he decided to cut those ties with his old business partners. She had to cut those ties with friends who kept dragging her down. The two countries chose to cut those ties following the diplomatic dispute. Sometimes you must cut those ties to protect your peace of mind.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن سان لاڳاپا ختم ڪرڻ, ڪنهن سان رشتو يا ناتو ٽوڙڻ, ڪنهن سان هر قسم جو رابطو بند ڪرڻ, پراڻن تعلقات کي مڪمل طور ختم ڪرڻ, نقصانڪار ماڻهن يا عادتن کان پاڻ کي جدا ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: کسی سے تعلقات ختم کرنا, کسی سے رشتہ یا ناتا توڑ دینا, کسی سے ہر قسم کا رابطہ منقطع کرنا, پرانے تعلقات کو مکمل طور پر ختم کر دینا, نقصان دہ لوگوں یا عادتوں سے خود کو الگ کرنا

englishMeaning: To go beyond a set limit, number, or amount. To be greater or better than something expected. To surpass a standard, rule, or expectation. To perform better than someone or something else. To go past what is allowed, required, or reasonable.
synonyms: Surpass, Outdo, Overstep, Overtake, Outstrip, Transcend, Overshoot, Beat, Top, Excel
antonyms: Fall short, Lag, Fail, Underperform, Trail, Miss, Lose, Decrease, Reduce, Limit
examples: The cost of the project may exceed our initial budget. Her performance exceeded everyone's expectations. Drivers who exceed the speed limit will be fined. The demand for tickets has exceeded the supply.
sindhiMeaning: حد کان ٻاهر وڃڻ, مقرر ڪيل انگ يا مقدار کان وڌي وڃڻ, توقع کان وڌيڪ ڪم ڪرڻ يا ثابت ٿيڻ, ڪنهن معيار يا قاعدي کان اڳتي نڪري وڃڻ, ٻين کان بهتر يا مٿانهون ٿيڻ
urduMeaning: حد سے تجاوز کرنا, مقررہ تعداد یا مقدار سے بڑھ جانا, توقع سے زیادہ کر دکھانا, کسی معیار یا قاعدے سے آگے نکل جانا, دوسروں سے بہتر یا برتر ہو جانا

englishMeaning: A small, round, green vegetable that looks like a small apple in shape. A summer squash commonly used in South Asian cooking. A vegetable of the cucurbit family, valued for its light and easily digestible nature. A soft-textured gourd often cooked with lentils, meat, or spices. A nutritious vegetable frequently recommended for a healthy diet.
synonyms: Round gourd, Indian round gourd, Tinda, Baby pumpkin, Squash
antonyms: (no direct antonym)
examples: My mother often cooks apple gourd with minced meat. Apple gourd is considered light and healthy for the stomach. He bought fresh apple gourds from the vegetable market. Doctors often recommend apple gourd for patients recovering from illness.
sindhiMeaning: ميھو, هڪ ننڍي گول سائي ڀاڄي جيڪا صورت ۾ ننڍي انب جهڙي هوندي آهي, هڪ گرمين جي موسم واري ڀاڄي, هلڪي ۽ آسانيءَ سان هضم ٿيندڙ ڀاڄي, دال يا گوشت سان پچائي ويندڙ ڀاڄي
urduMeaning: ٹنڈا, ایک چھوٹی گول سبز سبزی جو شکل میں چھوٹے سیب جیسی ہوتی ہے, گرمیوں کی ایک سبزی, ہلکی اور جلد ہضم ہونے والی سبزی, دال یا گوشت کے ساتھ پکائی جانے والی سبزی

englishMeaning: A long green vegetable with a rough surface and a strongly bitter taste. A tropical vine vegetable widely used in Asian cuisines. A vegetable known for its medicinal benefits, especially for diabetes. A gourd cooked with onions, spices, or stuffed with fillings. A plant of the cucurbit family valued for both food and traditional medicine.
synonyms: Karela, Bitter melon, Balsam pear, Bitter squash
antonyms: (no direct antonym)
examples: Bitter gourd is known to help control blood sugar levels. She stuffed the bitter gourd with spices and onions. Many people dislike bitter gourd because of its strong taste. My grandmother drinks bitter gourd juice every morning.
sindhiMeaning: ڪريلو, هڪ ڊگهي سائي ڀاڄي جنهن جو ذائقو تمام ڪوڙو هوندو آهي, هڪ ڀاڄي جيڪا خاص ڪري شگر جي مريضن لاءِ فائديمند سمجهي ويندي آهي, رواجي طور تي مصالحن يا بصر سان پچائي ويندڙ ڀاڄي, دوائي فائدن واري ڀاڄي
urduMeaning: کریلا, ایک لمبی سبز سبزی جس کا ذائقہ سخت کڑوا ہوتا ہے, ذیابیطس کے مریضوں کے لیے فائدہ مند سمجھی جانے والی سبزی, عام طور پر مصالحوں یا پیاز کے ساتھ پکائی جانے والی سبزی, دوائی خصوصیات رکھنے والی سبزی

englishMeaning: A small green vegetable with a pointed shape and light stripes on its skin. A vine vegetable commonly cultivated in South Asia. A vegetable often cooked with potatoes, meat, or spices in curries. A gourd known for being easy to digest and mildly flavored. A nutritious vegetable often used in traditional dishes and remedies.
synonyms: Parwal, Parval, Green potato, Snake gourd (regional)
antonyms: (no direct antonym)

antonyms: Scatter, Distribute, Disperse, Give away, Spread, Deliver, Discard, Disburse
examples: He collects rare coins from different countries. She went to collect her children from school. The charity collects donations for flood victims. Please give me a moment to collect my thoughts.
sindhiMeaning: شيون مختلف هنڌن يا ماڻهن کان گڏ ڪرڻ، خاص قسم جون شيون شوق طور جمع ڪرڻ، ڪنهن جاءِ تي وڃي ڪنهن ماڻهو يا شيءِ کي کڻي اچڻ، پيسا  عطيا يا ٽيڪس وصول ڪرڻ، پنهنجن خيالن يا جذبن تي ٻيهر ضابطو حاصل ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: چیزوں کو مختلف جگہوں یا لوگوں سے اکٹھا کرنا، شوق کے طور پر مخصوص قسم کی چیزیں جمع کرنا، کسی جگہ جا کر کسی شخص یا چیز کو لے آنا، رقم، عطیات یا ٹیکس وصول کرنا، اپنے خیالات یا جذبات پر دوبارہ قابو پانا

englishMeaning: To search widely for food or provisions, especially in the wild. To hunt or look around for something needed. Food, especially for horses and cattle, obtained by grazing or searching. To make a search or hunt through something. To rummage for what one needs.
synonyms: Search, Hunt, Rummage, Scavenge, Seek, Explore, Comb, Root, Ferret, Fossick
antonyms: Ignore, Overlook, Abandon, Provide, Give, Supply, Store
examples: Wild animals forage for food throughout the forest. The children love to forage for berries in the summer. Farmers store forage to feed cattle during winter. He had to forage in the drawer to find his keys.
sindhiMeaning: کاڌي يا رزق جي ڳولا ۾ گهمڻ خاص ڪري جهنگل يا کليل علائقي ۾، ضرورت جي شيءِ ڳولڻ يا ڦٿڙ ڪرڻ، اهو کاڌو جيڪو گهوڙا يا مال چراگاهن مان چري حاصل ڪن، ڪنهن جاءِ تي کوٽ لوٽ ڪري ڳولڻ، پنهنجي ضرورت جون شيون ڳولڻ
urduMeaning: کھانے یا رزق کی تلاش میں گھومنا، خاص طور پر جنگل یا کھلے علاقے میں، ضرورت کی چیز تلاش کرنا یا ڈھونڈنا، وہ چارہ جو گھوڑے یا مویشی چراگاہ سے چر کر حاصل کریں، کسی جگہ تلاش یا کھوج کرنا، اپنی ضرورت کی چیزیں ڈھونڈنا

englishMeaning: To look carefully for someone or something. To examine a place or person thoroughly to find something hidden. To try to find information, usually using a computer or the internet. To explore in order to discover something. An act of looking for or trying to find something or someone.
synonyms: Look, Seek, Hunt, Explore, Investigate, Examine, Probe, Scour, Comb, Inspect
antonyms: Ignore, Overlook, Neglect, Find, Discover, Abandon
examples: The police searched the house for stolen goods. She searched the internet for a suitable recipe. Rescue teams continued to search for the missing hikers. His search for the truth took many years.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ماڻهو يا شيءِ کي غور سان ڳولڻ، ڪنهن جاءِ يا ماڻهو جي مڪمل جاچ ڪرڻ ته جيئن لڪل شيءِ ملي، ڪا معلومات ڪمپيوٽر يا انٽرنيٽ ذريعي ڳولڻ، ڪا شيءِ دريافت ڪرڻ لاءِ کوجنا ڪرڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ يا ماڻهو کي ڳولڻ جو عمل
urduMeaning: کسی شخص یا چیز کو غور سے تلاش کرنا، کسی جگہ یا شخص کی مکمل جانچ کرنا تاکہ چھپی چیز مل سکے، کوئی معلومات کمپیوٹر یا انٹرنیٹ کے ذریعے تلاش کرنا، کسی چیز کو دریافت کرنے کے لیے چھان بین کرنا، کسی چیز یا شخص کو ڈھونڈنے کا عمل

englishMeaning: To search for something by moving things around in a careless or hurried way. To look through a container or space in an untidy manner. To make a thorough but disordered search. A search made by moving things around. A collection of miscellaneous articles, especially for sale.
synonyms: Search, Ransack, Rifle, Forage, Hunt, Comb, Fossick, Delve, Poke, Root
antonyms: Arrange, Organize, Tidy, Order, Neaten
examples: She rummaged through her bag looking for the keys. He rummaged in the drawer for a pair of scissors. The children rummaged through the old boxes in the attic. They held a rummage sale to raise money for charity.
sindhiMeaning: ڪا شيءِ ڳولڻ لاءِ شيون بيترتيبيءَ سان هيڏانهن هوڏانهن ڪرڻ، ڪنهن دٻي يا جاءِ ۾ ڦهلائي ڳولڻ، مڪمل پر بيترتيب ڳولا ڪرڻ، شيون ھيڏاھن ھوڏانھن ڪري تلاش ڪرڻ، لوڏي شين کي ڳولڻ، مختلف قسم جون شيون خاص ڪري وڪري لاءِ گڏ ڪيل تلاشي
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کو تلاش کرنے کے لیے چیزوں کو بے ترتیبی سے ادھر ادھر کرنا، کسی ڈبے یا جگہ کو الٹ پلٹ کر دیکھنا، مکمل مگر بے ترتیب تلاش کرنا، چیزوں کو ہلا کر کی گئی تلاش، مختلف قسم کی چیزیں خاص طور پر فروخت کے لیے جمع کی گئی

englishMeaning: To search something very carefully and thoroughly. To examine every part of a place or document in detail. To look through a large amount of information in order to find something. To sift through material in search of a specific item. To investigate closely in order to find or verify something.
synonyms: Search, Scour, Examine, Sift, Investigate, Explore, Inspect, Probe, Rummage, Screen
antonyms: Ignore, Overlook, Skim, Neglect, Disregard
examples: The detectives combed through every file for clues. She combed through the report to find the missing figures. Investigators combed through the wreckage after the crash. He combed through his notes before the exam.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ کي تمام غور سان ۽ مڪمل طور ڳولڻ، ڪنهن جاءِ يا دستاويز جو هر حصو جاچڻ، وڏي مقدار ۾ معلومات کي جاچي ڪا خاص ڳالهه لهڻ، مواد ۾ ڪنهن خاص شيءِ جي تلاش ڪرڻ، ويجهي جاچ ڪري ڪا ڳالهه تصديق ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کو انتہائی غور اور تفصیل سے تلاش کرنا، کسی جگہ یا دستاویز کے ہر حصے کا جائزہ لینا، بڑی مقدار میں معلومات کی چھان بین کر کے مطلوبہ چیز ڈھونڈنا، کسی مواد میں مخصوص چیز کی تلاش کرنا، قریبی جانچ کے ذریعے کسی بات کی تصدیق کرنا

englishMeaning: To give money, goods, or services to a charity, organization, or person in need. To provide something voluntarily to help others. To give one's body parts, blood, or organs for medical use. To contribute something for a public or good cause. To offer help or resources without expecting anything in return.
synonyms: Give, Contribute, Present, Gift, Bestow, Grant, Endow, Provide, Offer, Hand over
antonyms: Take, Receive, Withhold, Keep, Retain, Deny, Refuse, Accept
examples: Many people donate blood to save the lives of others. He decided to donate his old clothes to the poor. The company donates a portion of its profits to charity. She wants to donate her books to the local library.
sindhiMeaning: پيسا  شيون يا خدمتون خيراتي اداري  تنظيم يا ضرورتمند کي ڏيڻ، ٻين جي مدد لاءِ رضاڪاراڻي طور ڪجهه ڏيڻ، پنهنجو رت  عضوا يا جسم جا حصا طبي مقصد لاءِ ڏيڻ، ڪنهن عوامي يا نيڪ ڪم ۾ حصو ڏيڻ، بنا ڪنهن بدلي جي مدد يا وسيلا مهيا ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: رقم  اشیاء یا خدمات کسی خیراتی ادارے  تنظیم یا ضرورت مند کو دینا، دوسروں کی مدد کے لیے رضاکارانہ طور پر کچھ عطیہ کرنا، اپنا خون  اعضاء یا جسم کے حصے طبی مقصد کے لیے دینا، کسی رفاہی یا نیک کام میں حصہ ڈالنا، بغیر کسی صلے کے مدد یا وسائل فراہم کرنا

englishMeaning: A small piece or amount of something, especially one that is left over. Discarded material, especially metal, that can be reused or recycled. To decide not to continue with something such as a plan or project. A short fight or quarrel, usually not serious. A small item cut out from a newspaper or magazine and kept.
synonyms: Piece, Fragment, Bit, Morsel, Remnant, Junk, Waste, Discard, Abandon, Quarrel
antonyms: Whole, Entire, Keep, Retain, Preserve, Continue, Save, Peace
examples: The dog ate every scrap of food from the plate. They sold the old car for scrap metal. The government decided to scrap the outdated policy. The two boys had a small scrap in the playground.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ جو ننڍو ٽڪرو يا بچيل حصو، ڦٽيل شيون خاص ڪري لوهه جيڪو ٻيهر استعمال ڪري سگهجي، ڪنهن منصوبي يا ارادي کي رد ڪري ختم ڪرڻ، ننڍو جهيڙو يا تڪرار، اخبار يا رسالي مان ڪٽي رکيل ننڍڙو ٽڪرو
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کا چھوٹا ٹکڑا یا بچا ہوا حصہ، پھینکی گئی چیز خاص طور پر لوہا جو دوبارہ استعمال ہو سکے، کسی منصوبے یا کام کو ترک کر دینا، معمولی جھگڑا یا تکرار، اخبار یا رسالے سے کاٹ کر رکھا ہوا چھوٹا حصہ

englishMeaning: A supply of something that can be used when needed. A source of help, information, or support. Materials, money, staff, and other assets used by an organization to function effectively. A country's natural wealth such as minerals, forests, or water. An ability to deal with problems in a clever and effective way.
synonyms: Asset, Supply, Reserve, Means, Source, Stock, Fund, Wealth, Material, Capability
antonyms: Lack, Shortage, Scarcity, Deficiency, Want, Deficit
examples: Water is a precious natural resource we must protect. The library is a valuable resource for students. The country has abundant mineral resources. She showed great resource in handling the crisis.
sindhiMeaning: ڪا شيءِ جيڪا ضرورت وقت استعمال ٿي سگهي، مدد  معلومات يا سهاري جو ذريعو، ڪنهن اداري لاءِ مواد  پيسا  عملو ۽ ٻيا وسيلا، ملڪ جي قدرتي دولت جهڙوڪ معدنيات  ٻيلا يا پاڻي، مسئلن کي هوشيار طريقي سان حل ڪرڻ جي صلاحيت
urduMeaning: کوئی ذخیرہ جو ضرورت کے وقت کام آئے، مدد  معلومات یا سہارے کا ذریعہ، کسی ادارے کے لیے مواد  رقم، عملہ اور دیگر ذرائع، ملک کی قدرتی دولت جیسے معدنیات  جنگلات یا پانی، مسائل کو ذہانت سے حل کرنے کی صلاحیت

englishMeaning: Something remaining after the rest has been used or dealt with. Food that has not been eaten at the end of a meal and is saved for later. A person or thing that remains from an earlier time or situation. Extra material or items that are not needed. Remaining, surplus, or unused.
synonyms: Remaining, Remnant, Surplus, Residue, Extra, Excess, Unused, Spare, Balance, Scrap
antonyms: Used, Consumed, Finished, Fresh, New, Main, Whole
examples: We had leftover rice from last night's dinner. She packed the leftovers in the fridge for tomorrow. This old rule is a leftover from the previous system. He used the leftover paint to touch up the wall.
sindhiMeaning: ڪا شيءِ جيڪا استعمال کان پوءِ بچي پوي، اهو کاڌو جيڪو ماني کائڻ بعد بچي وڃي ۽ پوءِ لاءِ رکجي، ڪو ماڻهو يا شيءِ جيڪا اڳئين وقت يا صورتحال جي بچي وئي هجي، اضافي يا بيڪار شيون جيڪي گهربل نه هجن، بچيل يا استعمال ۾ نه ايندڙ
urduMeaning: کوئی چیز جو استعمال کے بعد بچ جائے، وہ کھانا جو کھانے کے بعد بچ جائے اور بعد میں کھانے کے لیے رکھا جائے، کوئی شخص یا چیز جو پچھلے وقت یا حالت سے بچی ہو، اضافی یا فالتو چیز جس کی ضرورت نہ ہو، باقی ماندہ یا غیر استعمال شدہ

englishMeaning: The state or fact of continuing to live or exist, especially in difficult conditions. The act of remaining alive after an accident, disaster, or dangerous situation. Something that has continued to exist from an earlier time. The ability to endure hardship or adversity. The process of surviving in nature or challenging environments.
synonyms: Endurance, Existence, Persistence, Continuation, Living, Subsistence, Preservation, Longevity
antonyms: Death, Extinction, Demise, Loss, End, Destruction, Defeat
examples: Food and water are essential for human survival. His survival after the accident amazed the doctors. This old tradition is a survival from ancient times. The soldiers were trained in wilderness survival.
sindhiMeaning: زندهه يا موجود رهڻ جي حالت  خاص ڪري ڏکين حالتن ۾، ڪنهن حادثي  آفت يا خطرناڪ صورتحال بعد جيئرو رهڻ، اڳئين وقت کان بچيل ڪا شيءِ، ڏکائي يا تڪليفن کي سهڻ جي صلاحيت، قدرت يا مشڪل ماحول ۾ زندگي گذارڻ جو عمل
urduMeaning: زندہ یا موجود رہنے کی حالت، خاص طور پر مشکل حالات میں، کسی حادثے  آفت یا خطرناک صورتحال کے بعد زندہ رہنا، پہلے زمانے سے باقی رہ جانے والی چیز، مشکلات کو برداشت کرنے کی صلاحیت، فطرت یا سخت ماحول میں زندگی گزارنے کا عمل

englishMeaning: A person or animal that searches widely for food or provisions. Someone who gathers wild food from natural surroundings. A worker or soldier historically sent out to collect food and supplies. An individual who scavenges or hunts around for useful items. A creature dependent on searching rather than farming for sustenance.
synonyms: Gatherer, Hunter, Scavenger, Searcher, Collector, Seeker, Rummager, Provider
antonyms: Farmer, Cultivator, Grower, Producer, Provider (settled)
examples: The forager returned with a basket full of wild mushrooms. Ants are natural foragers that collect food for the colony. He works as a forager for a well-known restaurant. Early humans were skilled foragers before farming began.
sindhiMeaning: اهو ماڻهو يا جانور جيڪو کاڌي يا رزق جي ڳولا ۾ گهمي، اهو شخص جيڪو قدرتي ماحول مان جهنگلي کاڌو گڏ ڪري، اهو مزدور يا سپاهي جيڪو رسد ۽ کاڌو گڏ ڪرڻ لاءِ موڪليو وڃي، ڪارآمد شيون ڳولڻ وارو ماڻهو، اهو جانور جيڪو پوکي بجاءِ ڳولا ذريعي کاڌو حاصل ڪري
urduMeaning: وہ شخص یا جانور جو کھانے یا رزق کی تلاش میں گھومے، وہ شخص جو قدرتی ماحول سے جنگلی خوراک جمع کرے، وہ مزدور یا سپاہی جسے رسد اور خوراک اکٹھی کرنے کے لیے بھیجا جائے، مفید چیزیں تلاش کرنے والا شخص، وہ جانور جو کاشتکاری کے بجائے تلاش کے ذریعے خوراک حاصل کرے

englishMeaning: A person who takes advantage of any chance or situation to gain benefit, often without regard to ethics. Someone who acts to promote their own interests when the chance arises. A person who adapts their actions to circumstances for personal advantage. An animal that feeds on whatever food is available. Describing behavior aimed at personal gain rather than principles.
synonyms: Exploiter, Self-seeker, Pragmatist, Chancer, Adventurer, Careerist, Manipulator
antonyms: Idealist, Principled person, Loyalist, Altruist, Moralist
examples: The politician was seen as a shameless opportunist. She is an opportunist who never misses a chance. Foxes are clever opportunists when it comes to finding food. He proved to be a pure opportunist during the crisis.
sindhiMeaning: اهو ماڻهو جيڪو ڪنهن به موقعي يا صورتحال مان فائدو کڻي اڪثر اخلاق جي پرواهه ڪرڻ کان سواءِ، اهو شخص جيڪو موقعي ملڻ تي پنهنجو مفاد حاصل ڪري، اهو ماڻهو جيڪو ذاتي فائدي لاءِ حالتن مطابق پنهنجا ڪم بدلائي، اهو جانور جيڪو جيڪو کاڌو ملي کائي، اصولن جي بجاءِ فائدي وارو رويو
urduMeaning: وہ شخص جو کسی بھی موقع یا صورتحال سے فائدہ اٹھائے  اکثر اخلاقیات کی پرواہ کیے بغیر، وہ شخص جو موقع ملنے پر اپنے مفادات کو ترجیح دے، وہ شخص جو ذاتی فائدے کے لیے حالات کے مطابق رویہ بدل لے، وہ جانور جو دستیاب کوئی بھی خوراک کھا لے، اصولوں کے بجائے فائدے پر مبنی رویہ

englishMeaning: A person who collects rags, waste materials, or discarded items from streets or dumps for a living. Someone who searches through garbage to find items that can be sold or reused. A poor worker involved in informal recycling. A traditional occupation in many countries where people earn by gathering scraps. A person symbolizing extreme poverty and hardship.
synonyms: Scavenger, Waste collector, Recycler, Trash picker, Junk collector, Gleaner
antonyms: Employer, Wealthy person, Consumer, Producer
examples: A young rag picker was seen sorting waste near the market. Rag pickers play an important role in informal recycling. Many rag pickers live in extreme poverty. The NGO started a school for rag picker children.
sindhiMeaning: اهو ماڻهو جيڪو گهٽين يا ڪچري مان ڪپڙا  فضلو يا اڇلايل شيون گڏ ڪري گذارو ڪري، اهو ماڻهو جيڪو ڪچري مان اهڙيون شيون ڳولي جيڪي وڪامي يا ٻيهر استعمال ٿي سگهن، غير رسمي ريسائيڪلنگ ۾ ڪم ڪندڙ غريب مزدور، ڪيترن ئي ملڪن ۾ رواجي ڌنڌو جتي ماڻهو ڦٽل شيون گڏ ڪري ڪمائين، انتهائي غربت ۽ تڪليف جو نشان
urduMeaning: وہ شخص جو گلیوں یا کچرے سے کپڑے  فضلہ یا پھینکی گئی چیزیں جمع کر کے گزارا کرے، وہ شخص جو کچرے میں سے قابل فروخت یا دوبارہ استعمال ہونے والی چیزیں تلاش کرے، غیر رسمی ری سائیکلنگ میں کام کرنے والا غریب مزدور، بہت سے ممالک میں ایک روایتی پیشہ جہاں لوگ ردی جمع کر کے کماتے ہیں، انتہائی غربت اور مشقت کی علامت

englishMeaning: The decaying flesh of dead animals. Dead and rotting animal bodies, often eaten by scavengers. The remains of a dead creature left in the open. Something disgusting, decayed, or corrupt in nature. Flesh unfit for human consumption due to decomposition.
synonyms: Carcass, Corpse, Remains, Cadaver, Dead flesh, Rot, Decay, Prey
antonyms: Living flesh, Live animal, Fresh meat, Life
examples: Vultures circled above the carrion in the desert. The hunters left the carrion behind for wild animals. A foul smell rose from the carrion beside the road. Crows quickly gathered around the carrion in the field.
sindhiMeaning: مئل جانورن جو سڙيل گوشت, مري ويل جانور جو باقي بچيل جسم, اهو گوشت جيڪو کائڻ لائق نه هجي, سڙيل يا خراب ٿيل شيءِ, جانورن جي لاش کي کائيندڙ پکين لاءِ خوراڪ
urduMeaning: مردہ جانوروں کا سڑا ہوا گوشت, مرے ہوئے جانور کی باقیات, ایسا گوشت جو کھانے کے قابل نہ ہو, گلا سڑا یا خراب مادہ, گدھ اور دیگر گوشت خور جانوروں کی خوراک

englishMeaning: A person who prepares and works on land to grow crops. A farmer who tills and manages agricultural land. A tool or machine used to loosen the soil and remove weeds. A person who develops or improves something over time, such as skills, friendships, or ideas. Someone who encourages growth of qualities, habits, or relationships.
synonyms: Farmer, Grower, Planter, Tiller, Agriculturist, Peasant, Gardener, Developer, Nurturer
antonyms: Destroyer, Neglecter, Idler, Consumer, Uprooter, Waster
examples: The cultivator ploughed his fields before the monsoon rains. He bought a new cultivator to prepare the land faster. A skilled cultivator can produce healthy crops every season. She is a great cultivator of lasting friendships.
sindhiMeaning: زمين جوٽڻ ۽ فصل پوکڻ وارو ماڻهو, هاري يا زميندار, زمين کي نرم ڪرڻ ۽ گاهه صاف ڪرڻ وارو اوزار يا مشين, ڪنهن هنر يا تعلق کي وڌائيندڙ شخص, ڪنهن سٺي عادت يا سوچ کي پروان چاڙهيندڙ
urduMeaning: زمین کو کاشت کرنے والا شخص, کسان یا زمیندار, مٹی نرم کرنے اور جڑی بوٹیاں نکالنے والا آلہ یا مشین, کسی ہنر یا رشتے کو پروان چڑھانے والا, اچھی عادات یا سوچ کو فروغ دینے والا شخص

englishMeaning: To prepare land and grow crops on it. To develop or improve a skill, quality, or relationship through effort. To try to gain someone's friendship or support. To encourage the growth of something such as an idea, habit, or attitude. To refine one's mind, taste, or behavior through learning and practice.
synonyms: Grow, Farm, Plant, Till, Develop, Foster, Nurture, Encourage, Refine, Promote
antonyms: Neglect, Ignore, Destroy, Abandon, Uproot, Discourage, Hinder
examples: Farmers cultivate wheat and rice in this region. She works hard to cultivate patience in her daily life. He tried to cultivate a friendship with his new neighbor. Teachers cultivate curiosity and creativity in young students.
sindhiMeaning: زمين کي جوٽڻ ۽ فصل پوکڻ, ڪنهن هنر يا عادت کي محنت سان وڌائڻ, ڪنهن سان دوستي يا تعلق پيدا ڪرڻ, ڪنهن خيال يا سوچ کي پروان چاڙهڻ, پنهنجي ذهن ۽ رويي کي سنوارڻ
urduMeaning: زمین کو کاشت کرنا, کسی ہنر یا عادت کو محنت سے پروان چڑھانا, کسی سے دوستی یا تعلق قائم کرنا, کسی سوچ یا رجحان کو فروغ دینا, اپنے ذہن  ذوق اور رویے کو نکھارنا

englishMeaning: Not harmful or dangerous in any way. Causing no injury, offense, or unpleasant effect. Something that appears simple, mild, or inoffensive. A remark or action that does not upset or provoke anyone. Safe and gentle in nature or intention.
synonyms: Harmless, Safe, Mild, Inoffensive, Gentle, Benign, Bland, Unobjectionable
antonyms: Harmful, Dangerous, Toxic, Offensive, Harsh, Injurious, Noxious, Hurtful
examples: The medicine is innocuous and safe for children. His comment seemed innocuous, but it hurt her feelings. The snake looked dangerous but was actually innocuous. She asked an innocuous question about the weather.
sindhiMeaning: بي ضرر, نقصان کان خالي, ايترو معمولي جو ڪنهن کي نه رنجائي, نرم مزاج يا بنا خطري واري شيءِ, اهڙي ڳالهه جيڪا ڪنهن جي دل نه ڏکوئي
urduMeaning: بے ضرر, نقصان سے پاک, ایسا کہ کسی کو تکلیف نہ دے, معمولی اور بے خطر, ایسی بات جو کسی کو ناراض نہ کرے

englishMeaning: A gift of money, goods, or services given to help others. Something given voluntarily to a charity, cause, or person in need. A contribution made without expecting anything in return. An act of generosity intended to support others. The offering of blood, organs, or resources for humanitarian purposes.
synonyms: Gift, Contribution, Offering, Charity, Grant, Present, Alms, Endowment, Handout
antonyms: Loan, Purchase, Sale, Theft, Withholding, Denial, Confiscation
examples: He made a generous donation to the orphanage. Their donation helped build a new school in the village. Blood donation can save many precious lives. The charity depends entirely on public donations.
sindhiMeaning: عطيو, خيرات ۾ ڏنل رقم يا شيءِ, ڪنهن سٺي ڪم لاءِ رضاڪارانه مدد, بغير ڪنهن بدلي جي ڏنل تحفو, رت يا عضون جو عطيو
urduMeaning: عطیہ, خیرات میں دی گئی رقم یا چیز, کسی نیک کام کے لیے رضاکارانہ مدد, بغیر کسی معاوضے کے دیا گیا تحفہ, خون یا اعضا کا عطیہ

englishMeaning: Money that is owed by one person to another. Something, such as a favor or service, owed in return. A state of being under obligation to repay. A feeling of gratitude for help received from someone. A financial liability held by an individual, company, or country.
synonyms: Loan, Liability, Obligation, Arrears, Dues, Borrowing, Mortgage, Deficit
antonyms: Credit, Asset, Payment, Wealth, Surplus, Repayment, Savings
examples: He worked two jobs to pay off his debt. The country is struggling under a huge national debt. I owe you a great debt for your kind help. She finally cleared all her old debts this year.
sindhiMeaning: قرض, اڌارو ورتل رقم, ڪنهن جو احسان يا فرض جيڪو موٽائڻ گهرجي, ڪنهن جي مدد لاءِ شڪرگذاري جو احساس, مالي ذميواري
urduMeaning: قرض, ادھار لی گئی رقم, کسی کا احسان یا فرض جو لوٹانا ہو, کسی کی مدد کا احسان مند ہونا, مالی ذمہ داری

englishMeaning: The moral principles that guide a person's behavior. The branch of knowledge that studies right and wrong conduct. Rules and standards followed by a profession or group. A system of moral values shared by a society. The study of what is good, just, and fair in human actions.
synonyms: Morals, Principles, Values, Standards, Conduct, Virtue, Integrity, Righteousness
antonyms: Immorality, Corruption, Dishonesty, Vice, Wrongdoing, Wickedness, Depravity
examples: Medical ethics guide doctors in treating patients fairly. He is known for his strong professional ethics. The company was fined for violating business ethics. Ethics teaches us the difference between right and wrong.
sindhiMeaning: اخلاقيات, صحيح ۽ غلط جي اصولن جو علم, ڪنهن پيشي يا گروهه جا اخلاقي ضابطا, معاشري ۾ رائج نيڪ اصول, انسان جي ڪردار جي پرک جو علم
urduMeaning: اخلاقیات, صحیح اور غلط کے اصولوں کا علم, کسی پیشے یا گروہ کے اخلاقی ضابطے, معاشرے میں رائج نیک اصول, انسانی کردار کے اصول

englishMeaning: An arrangement to keep something for a particular person, such as a seat or room. A feeling of doubt or hesitation about something. A special area of land set aside for a specific group or purpose. A limit or condition placed on an agreement. A quota or share kept aside in jobs or education for certain groups.
synonyms: Booking, Doubt, Hesitation, Qualm, Condition, Quota, Allotment, Preserve, Sanctuary
antonyms: Cancellation, Certainty, Confidence, Openness, Rejection, Refusal, Whole
examples: I made a reservation at the restaurant for eight o'clock. She agreed to the plan without any reservation. The tribe lives on a large reservation in the north. There is a reservation for women in this program.
sindhiMeaning: بڪنگ, ڪنهن شيءِ کي اڳ ۾ محفوظ ڪرڻ, شڪ يا هٻڪ, ڪنهن مقصد يا قوم لاءِ مخصوص زمين, ڪنهن معاهدي ۾ شرط, نوڪري يا تعليم ۾ مخصوص حصو
urduMeaning: پیشگی بکنگ, کسی چیز کو محفوظ کرنا, شک یا ہچکچاہٹ, کسی مقصد یا قوم کے لیے مخصوص زمین, معاہدے میں کوئی شرط, نوکری یا تعلیم میں مخصوص کوٹہ

englishMeaning: A feeling of uncertainty about the truth of something. To lack confidence or belief in someone or something. A question or hesitation regarding a decision. A state of being unsure about what to do. Distrust or suspicion towards a person or idea.
synonyms: Uncertainty, Suspicion, Distrust, Hesitation, Skepticism, Question, Misgiving, Disbelief
antonyms: Certainty, Trust, Belief, Confidence, Faith, Conviction, Assurance
examples: I have no doubt about his honesty. She began to doubt her own decision. There is some doubt whether he will come today. Do not let doubt stop you from trying again.
sindhiMeaning: شڪ, غير يقيني حالت, ڪنهن جي سچائي تي اعتماد نه هجڻ, هٻڪ يا الجهن, ڪنهن تي بي اعتباري
urduMeaning: شک, غیر یقینی کیفیت, کسی کی سچائی پر یقین نہ ہونا, ہچکچاہٹ یا الجھن, کسی پر بے اعتمادی

englishMeaning: The quality of being honest and morally good. Strict adherence to fairness and truth. The state of standing straight or erect. Integrity in character and behavior. Fair and just conduct in all matters.
synonyms: Honesty, Integrity, Righteousness, Virtue, Morality, Goodness, Rectitude, Honor
antonyms: Dishonesty, Corruption, Wickedness, Immorality, Deceit, Crookedness, Vice
examples: His uprightness earned him great respect in society. The judge was admired for his uprightness and fairness. Uprightness should be taught to children from a young age. She is known for the uprightness of her character.
sindhiMeaning: ايمانداري, سچائي ۽ نيڪي, سڌائي, ڪردار جي پاڪائي, انصاف ۽ عدل وارو رويو
urduMeaning: ایمانداری, سچائی اور نیکی, سیدھا کھڑا ہونے کی حالت, کردار کی پاکیزگی, انصاف اور عدل والا رویہ

englishMeaning: Dishonest or illegal behavior, especially by people in power. The act of bribing or being bribed. Moral decay in society or an individual. Alteration or damage of data, text, or files. The process of decay or spoiling something pure.
synonyms: Dishonesty, Bribery, Fraud, Immorality, Depravity, Misconduct, Perversion, Decay
antonyms: Honesty, Integrity, Morality, Uprightness, Purity, Virtue, Righteousness
examples: Corruption is a serious problem in many governments. He was arrested for corruption and misuse of power. The corruption of youth harms the whole society. File corruption caused all his data to be lost.
sindhiMeaning: بدعنواني, رشوت خوري, اخلاقي زوال, ڪنهن شيءِ کي خراب ڪرڻ, ڊيٽا يا فائل جو خراب ٿي وڃڻ
urduMeaning: بدعنوانی, رشوت خوری, اخلاقی زوال, کسی چیز کو خراب کرنا, ڈیٹا یا فائل کا خراب ہونا

englishMeaning: Not morally right or acceptable. Against the accepted rules of a profession or society. Dishonest or unfair in behavior. Involving practices that violate moral standards. Contrary to principles of good conduct.
synonyms: Immoral, Dishonest, Corrupt, Wrong, Improper, Unprincipled, Shady, Unfair
antonyms: Ethical, Moral, Honest, Fair, Principled, Upright, Righteous, Just
examples: It is unethical to cheat during examinations. The doctor was punished for his unethical behavior. Spreading false news is completely unethical. Many companies avoid unethical business practices.
sindhiMeaning: غير اخلاقي, اخلاق جي خلاف, ڪنهن پيشي جي اصولن جي ڀڃڪڙي, بي ايماني وارو عمل, بدڪرداري وارو
urduMeaning: غیر اخلاقی, اخلاق کے خلاف, کسی پیشے کے اصولوں کی خلاف ورزی, بددیانتی پر مبنی, بدکرداری والا

englishMeaning: A lack of interest, concern, or sympathy. An attitude of not caring about someone or something. Emotional coldness towards a situation or person. The state of being neither for nor against something. Neglect or inattention shown to important matters.
synonyms: Apathy, Disregard, Coldness, Detachment, Unconcern, Neglect, Aloofness, Nonchalance
antonyms: Concern, Interest, Care, Sympathy, Attention, Enthusiasm, Warmth, Compassion
examples: His indifference to her feelings hurt her deeply. Public indifference allowed the problem to grow worse. She responded with cold indifference to the news. The government showed indifference toward the flood victims.
sindhiMeaning: بي پرواهي, بي نيازي, دلچسپي جو نه هجڻ, غير جانبداري, ڪنهن معاملي کي نظرانداز ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: بے پرواہی, بے نیازی, دلچسپی کا فقدان, غیر جانبداری, کسی معاملے کو نظرانداز کرنا

englishMeaning: Showing no interest, concern, or sympathy. Not caring one way or the other. Of average or mediocre quality. Emotionally detached or cold in attitude. Neither good nor bad, ordinary in nature.
synonyms: Uninterested, Apathetic, Unconcerned, Cold, Detached, Aloof, Neutral, Mediocre
antonyms: Interested, Caring, Concerned, Enthusiastic, Passionate, Warm, Attentive
examples: He was indifferent to the criticism of others. The audience remained indifferent throughout the show. The food at the restaurant was rather indifferent. She seemed indifferent to her final results.
sindhiMeaning: بي پرواهه, بي نياز, لاتعلق, معمولي درجي جو, ٿڌو رويو رکندڙ
urduMeaning: بے پرواہ, بے نیاز, لاتعلق, معمولی درجے کا, ٹھنڈے رویے والا

englishMeaning: The quality of acting without thinking of the consequences. Careless or dangerous behavior. Lack of caution in actions or decisions. A tendency to take unnecessary risks. Foolish boldness that may cause harm.
synonyms: Carelessness, Rashness, Negligence, Foolhardiness, Impulsiveness, Thoughtlessness, Imprudence
antonyms: Caution, Care, Prudence, Wisdom, Carefulness, Vigilance, Thoughtfulness
examples: His recklessness on the road caused a serious accident. The recklessness of youth often leads to regret. She was punished for her recklessness at work. The company suffered because of the manager's recklessness.
sindhiMeaning: بي پرواهي, لاپرواهي, نتيجن کان بي خبر ٿي ڪم ڪرڻ, غير محتاط رويو, بغير سوچ سمجهه جي خطري ۾ پوڻ
urduMeaning: بے احتیاطی, لاپرواہی, نتائج سے بے خبر ہو کر کام کرنا, غیر محتاط رویہ, بلا سوچے سمجھے خطرہ مول لینا

englishMeaning: The crime of cheating someone to gain money or advantage. A person who deceives others by pretending to be someone else. A deceitful act or trick. Dishonest business or financial practices. False representation intended to mislead.
synonyms: Deception, Cheating, Swindle, Trickery, Scam, Forgery, Con, Hoax, Deceit
antonyms: Honesty, Truth, Integrity, Sincerity, Fairness, Reality, Genuineness
examples: He was arrested for committing bank fraud. That online seller turned out to be a fraud. Insurance fraud costs companies billions each year. The scheme was exposed as a complete fraud.
sindhiMeaning: دوکو, فراڊ, جعلسازي, ڪنهن کي ٺڳي مال حاصل ڪرڻ, جعلي شخص يا شيءِ
urduMeaning: دھوکہ, فراڈ, جعلسازی, کسی کو ٹھگ کر مال حاصل کرنا, جعلی شخص یا چیز

englishMeaning: The quality of being evil or morally wrong. Cruel or harmful behavior toward others. An act that is deeply immoral. Sinful or unjust conduct. A state of being full of bad intentions.
synonyms: Evil, Sinfulness, Immorality, Cruelty, Vileness, Depravity, Villainy, Iniquity
antonyms: Goodness, Virtue, Kindness, Righteousness, Innocence, Morality, Purity
examples: The wickedness of his crimes shocked the whole nation. She could not tolerate the wickedness around her. Stories often teach children to reject wickedness. His wickedness finally brought him to ruin.
sindhiMeaning: بدي, برائي, ظلم, گناهه, بد نيتي
urduMeaning: بدی, برائی, ظلم, گناہ, بد نیتی

englishMeaning: The act of not being truthful or fair. Behavior involving lies, cheating, or deceit. A lack of integrity in a person's character. The tendency to hide the truth for personal benefit. Fraudulent or misleading conduct.
synonyms: Deceit, Lying, Fraud, Cheating, Insincerity, Falsehood, Trickery, Corruption
antonyms: Honesty, Truthfulness, Integrity, Sincerity, Fairness, Uprightness, Candor
examples: His dishonesty cost him his job and reputation. Dishonesty in business destroys long-term trust. She was disappointed by her friend's dishonesty. No relationship can survive constant dishonesty.
sindhiMeaning: بي ايماني, ڪوڙ ڳالهائڻ, ٺڳي, دوکو ڏيڻ, ڪردار ۾ کوٽ
urduMeaning: بے ایمانی, جھوٹ بولنا, دھوکہ دینا, فریب, کردار میں کھوٹ

englishMeaning: To cut or engrave a design on a hard surface using acid or tools. To fix something deeply in one's memory. To outline something clearly and sharply. To create a picture or pattern by scratching a surface. To mark or leave a lasting impression on something.
synonyms: Engrave, Carve, Inscribe, Incise, Imprint, Cut, Chisel, Score
antonyms: Erase, Remove, Smooth, Wipe, Efface, Delete
examples: The artist etched a beautiful design on the glass. That moment is etched forever in my memory. Workers etched the company logo onto the metal plates. Years of hardship were etched on his face.
sindhiMeaning: لوهه يا شيشي تي نقش ڪڍڻ, ڪنهن ياد کي دل ۾ چٽو ڪري ڇڏڻ, تيزاب يا اوزار سان نقاشي ڪرڻ, ڪنهن شڪل کي واضح طور تي بيان ڪرڻ, ڪا اڻ مٽ نشاني ڇڏڻ
urduMeaning: دھات یا شیشے پر نقش بنانا, کسی یاد کو دل میں گہرا نقش کر دینا, تیزاب یا اوزار سے نقاشی کرنا, کسی شکل کو واضح طور پر ابھارنا, کوئی نہ مٹنے والا نشان چھوڑنا

englishMeaning: To rub something hard with a brush or cloth to clean it. To cancel or abandon a plan or event. To remove dirt, stains, or marks by rubbing. Low, rough bushes or vegetation. A cleansing product used to exfoliate the skin.
synonyms: Clean, Wash, Rub, Scour, Cleanse, Cancel, Abandon, Call off
antonyms: Dirty, Soil, Stain, Continue, Proceed, Begin, Start
examples: She had to scrub the floor to remove the stains. They decided to scrub the mission due to bad weather. He used a brush to scrub the rusted pan clean. A gentle face scrub can keep the skin fresh.
sindhiMeaning: زور سان مانجهو ڏيڻ, برش يا ڪپڙي سان صاف ڪرڻ, ڪنهن منصوبي کي منسوخ ڪرڻ, هلڪا ٻوٽا يا جهنگ, چمڙي صاف ڪرڻ وارو ليپ
urduMeaning: زور سے رگڑ کر صاف کرنا, برش یا کپڑے سے دھونا, کسی منصوبے کو منسوخ کرنا, ہلکی جھاڑیاں یا جھاڑ, جلد صاف کرنے والا اسکرب

englishMeaning: A small cut or notch on a surface. To make a small cut on something. To steal something, especially of small value. To arrest or catch a criminal. The exact right moment to do something.
synonyms: Cut, Notch, Scratch, Chip, Steal, Pilfer, Arrest, Catch
antonyms: Repair, Smooth, Return, Restore, Release, Free
examples: He got a small nick on his chin while shaving. Someone tried to nick my wallet in the market. The police finally nicked the thief last night. She arrived just in the nick of time.
sindhiMeaning: ننڍڙو ڪٽ يا نشان, هلڪي چير ڏيڻ, ڪا ننڍي شيءِ چوري ڪرڻ, ڪنهن مجرم کي پڪڙڻ, صحيح وقت
urduMeaning: چھوٹا سا کٹ یا نشان, ہلکی سی چیر لگانا, کوئی چھوٹی چیز چرا لینا, کسی مجرم کو پکڑنا, بالکل صحیح وقت

englishMeaning: To repair something that is broken or damaged. To improve one's behavior or attitude. To heal or recover from an illness or injury. To restore a relationship after a quarrel. The act of fixing or improving something.
synonyms: Repair, Fix, Restore, Patch, Heal, Reconcile, Improve, Recover
antonyms: Break, Damage, Destroy, Ruin, Worsen, Harm, Tear
examples: She sat quietly to mend her torn dress. He promised to mend his rude behavior. The patient is slowly beginning to mend after surgery. They finally mended their long friendship.
sindhiMeaning: مرمت ڪرڻ, ٽٽل شيءِ ٺاهڻ, رويي کي سڌارڻ, بيماري کان صحتياب ٿيڻ, ٽٽل تعلق کي ٻيهر جوڙڻ
urduMeaning: مرمت کرنا, ٹوٹی چیز ٹھیک کرنا, رویے کو سدھارنا, بیماری سے صحتیاب ہونا, ٹوٹے رشتے کو دوبارہ جوڑنا

englishMeaning: A feeling of pity or sorrow for someone else's suffering. Understanding and sharing another person's emotions. Support or agreement with someone's opinion or cause. A show of kindness during difficult times. A natural connection or harmony between people.
synonyms: Compassion, Pity, Empathy, Understanding, Kindness, Concern, Support, Consolation
antonyms: Indifference, Cruelty, Coldness, Apathy, Hostility, Harshness, Antipathy
examples: She showed great sympathy for the earthquake victims. He wrote a letter to express his sympathy. Many people felt deep sympathy for the poor family. Her kind words gave him much needed sympathy.
sindhiMeaning: همدردي, ڪنهن جي تڪليف ۾ شريڪ ٿيڻ جو احساس, ڪنهن جي جذبن کي سمجهڻ, ڪنهن جي راءِ يا مقصد جي حمايت, ڏک ۾ نرمي ۽ مهرباني
urduMeaning: ہمدردی, کسی کی تکلیف میں شریک ہونے کا احساس, کسی کے جذبات کو سمجھنا, کسی کی رائے یا مقصد کی حمایت, دکھ میں نرمی اور مہربانی

englishMeaning: Bad luck or an unfortunate event. A difficult or unhappy situation. An accident or disaster that causes suffering. A stroke of bad fate affecting someone's life. Any hardship, loss, or trouble faced by a person.

sindhiMeaning: عقلمند، سمجهدار، سليقي مند، معقول، سٺي فيصلي وارو، عقل ۽ سمجهه سان ڪم ڪندڙ، حقيقت پسند، ڪنهن ڳالهه کي محسوس ڪندڙ يا ڄاڻيندڙ
urduMeaning: عقلمند، سمجھدار، سلیقہ مند، معقول، اچھے فیصلے والا، عقل اور سمجھ سے کام لینے والا، حقیقت پسند، کسی بات کو محسوس یا جاننے والا

englishMeaning: Not making provision for the future; failing to plan ahead. Careless with money and resources. Wasteful and lacking foresight. Reckless in spending or in preparing for future needs. Short-sighted and thoughtless about consequences.
synonyms: Wasteful, Careless, Reckless, Extravagant, Spendthrift, Shortsighted, Thriftless, Imprudent, Prodigal, Thoughtless
antonyms: Provident, Prudent, Thrifty, Frugal, Careful, Economical, Foresighted, Sensible, Cautious, Wise
examples: His improvident habits left him in debt. Improvident spending can ruin even the richest families. She was too improvident to save anything for old age. An improvident farmer suffers when the harvest fails.
sindhiMeaning: لاپرواهه، اڳواٽ نه سوچيندڙ، فضول خرچ، مستقبل جو خيال نه ڪندڙ، بي احتياط، پنهنجي مالي حالت تي غور نه ڪندڙ، بي سمجهه ۽ بي پرواهه
urduMeaning: لاپرواہ، پہلے سے نہ سوچنے والا، فضول خرچ، مستقبل کا خیال نہ کرنے والا، بے احتیاط، اپنی مالی حالت پر غور نہ کرنے والا، بے سمجھ اور بے پرواہ

englishMeaning: Using more of something than is needed, especially money, time, or resources. Causing loss or unnecessary use of things. Extravagant and careless in spending. Producing much waste or unused material. Not economical or efficient in habits.
synonyms: Extravagant, Prodigal, Improvident, Uneconomical, Lavish, Spendthrift, Careless, Excessive, Squandering, Reckless
antonyms: Economical, Frugal, Thrifty, Sparing, Careful, Prudent, Efficient, Saving, Provident, Sensible
examples: Leaving lights on all day is very wasteful. Their wasteful lifestyle put them into serious debt. It is wasteful to throw away food that can still be eaten. The old machine was wasteful of both fuel and time.
sindhiMeaning: فضول خرچ، وسيلن کي بيڪار ضايع ڪندڙ، حد کان وڌيڪ خرچ ڪندڙ، بي احتياط، سنڀال نه ڪندڙ، ڪم آڻڻ جي بجاءِ اجايو استعمال ڪندڙ، غير معاشي رويو رکندڙ
urduMeaning: فضول خرچ، وسائل کو بے کار ضائع کرنے والا، حد سے زیادہ خرچ کرنے والا، بے احتیاط، حفاظت نہ کرنے والا، استعمال کے بجائے ضائع کرنے والا، غیر معاشی رویہ رکھنے والا

englishMeaning: To use something carelessly, extravagantly, or without a good purpose. Material that is no longer needed and is thrown away. A wide, empty, and often barren area of land. To gradually lose strength, health, or vitality. An action or use of something that does not produce a useful result.
synonyms: Squander, Misuse, Consume, Exhaust, Trash, Rubbish, Refuse, Garbage, Desert, Wilderness
antonyms: Save, Preserve, Conserve, Economize, Use, Utilize, Protect, Maintain, Gain, Restore
examples: Do not waste your time on useless arguments. The factory dumps its waste into the river. The desert is a vast waste of sand and rock. His health began to waste after the long illness.
sindhiMeaning: ضايع ڪرڻ، اجايو خرچ ڪرڻ، ڪا شيءِ بيڪار ڪري ڇڏڻ، ڪچرو، بيڪار مواد، ويران ۽ اجاڙ زمين، جسماني طاقت جو گهٽجڻ، وقت يا وسيلن جو غلط استعمال
urduMeaning: ضائع کرنا، فضول خرچ کرنا، کسی چیز کو بیکار کر دینا، کچرا، بیکار مواد، ویران اور اجاڑ زمین، جسمانی طاقت کا گھٹنا، وقت یا وسائل کا غلط استعمال

englishMeaning: In a manner showing careful planning for the future. With wise foresight and prudent preparation. In a thrifty and economical way to avoid future difficulty. With prudent care and cautious management of resources. In a way that anticipates future needs and prepares for them.
synonyms: Prudently, Wisely, Cautiously, Thriftily, Carefully, Foresightedly, Economically, Sensibly, Judiciously
antonyms: Wastefully, Carelessly, Recklessly, Improvidently, Thoughtlessly, Extravagantly, Imprudently, Foolishly
examples: She providently saved a portion of her salary every month. The farmer providently stored grain for the dry season. He providently invested in insurance for his family's security. The company acted providently by expanding its emergency reserves.
sindhiMeaning: اڳواٽ سوچ ۽ تدبير سان، دورانديشيءَ سان، هوشيار ۽ سنڀال ڀرئي انداز سان، بچت ۽ ڪفايت سان، مستقبل جي ضرورتن کي نظر ۾ رکندي
urduMeaning: دور اندیشی سے، عقلمندی اور احتیاط کے ساتھ، سوچ سمجھ کر منصوبہ بندی کرتے ہوئے، کفایت شعاری سے، آئندہ کی ضروریات کو مدنظر رکھتے ہوئے

englishMeaning: Relating to hormones or the glands that produce them. Caused or influenced by hormones in the body. Concerning changes in the body due to hormone activity. Relating to emotional or physical changes driven by hormone levels.
synonyms: Endocrine, Glandular, Physiological, Chemical, Biological
antonyms: Non-hormonal, Unrelated, External, Mechanical, Artificial
examples: Teenagers often experience hormonal changes during puberty. Her mood swings were caused by hormonal imbalance. The doctor recommended a hormonal test to check her thyroid. Hormonal treatments can help patients with certain conditions.
sindhiMeaning: هارمونز سان تعلق رکندڙ، هارمونز جي ڪري پيدا ٿيندڙ، هارمونز جي اثر هيٺ ايندڙ جسماني تبديلين سان لاڳاپيل، جسم جي غدود واري نظام سان تعلق رکندڙ
urduMeaning: ہارمونز سے متعلق، ہارمونز کے اثر سے پیدا ہونے والا، جسمانی غدود اور ان کے افعال سے متعلق، ہارمون کی تبدیلی کی وجہ سے ہونے والا

englishMeaning: Relating to a person between thirteen and nineteen years of age. Belonging to or characteristic of teenagers. Suitable for or aimed at young people in their teens. The period of life between childhood and adulthood.
synonyms: Adolescent, Youthful, Juvenile, Young, Pubescent, Youth
antonyms: Adult, Mature, Elderly, Aged, Grown-up, Old
examples: Teenage years are often full of emotional ups and downs. The magazine focuses on teenage fashion and lifestyle. Many teenage students take part in sports activities. Parents should guide their teenage children with patience.
sindhiMeaning: نوجواني جي عمر سان تعلق رکندڙ (13 کان 19 سال)، نوجوانن جو، نوعمر ٻارن سان لاڳاپيل، نوجوانيءَ جو دور
urduMeaning: نوعمری سے متعلق (تیرہ سے انیس سال)، نوجوانوں کا، نوعمر لڑکوں اور لڑکیوں سے متعلق، نوجوانی کا دور

englishMeaning: Relating to infants or early childhood. Behaving in a childish or immature way. Silly and lacking maturity, especially in an adult. Characteristic of a very young child.
synonyms: Childish, Babyish, Immature, Juvenile, Puerile, Naive
antonyms: Mature, Adult, Grown-up, Sensible, Sophisticated, Wise
examples: His infantile behavior at the meeting annoyed everyone. The doctor specializes in infantile diseases. Stop making infantile excuses and act your age. Infantile care requires great patience and attention.
sindhiMeaning: ٻاراڻي عمر سان تعلق رکندڙ، ٻاراڻي انداز جو، ناسمجهه ۽ ٻاراڻي رويي وارو، ننڍپڻ سان لاڳاپيل
urduMeaning: بچپن سے متعلق، بچگانہ، ناسمجھ یا بچوں جیسا رویہ رکھنے والا، شیرخوارگی سے متعلق

englishMeaning: A chemical substance produced in the body that regulates the activity of cells or organs. A natural compound made by glands and carried by the blood to control body functions. Any of the chemical messengers that influence growth, mood, or metabolism. A synthetic version of such a substance used in medicine.
synonyms: Secretion, Chemical, Endocrine, Enzyme, Compound
antonyms: Inhibitor, Blocker, Antagonist
examples: Insulin is a hormone that controls blood sugar levels. The body releases stress hormones during difficult situations. Growth hormone plays an important role in children's development. Doctors sometimes prescribe hormone therapy for certain patients.
sindhiMeaning: جسم ۾ غدود مان پيدا ٿيندڙ ڪيميائي مادو جيڪو جسم جي ڪمن کي ڪنٽرول ڪري، رت ذريعي سفر ڪندڙ قدرتي پيغام رسان، واڌ ويجهه ۽ جذبات تي اثرانداز ٿيندڙ مادو، دوا طور استعمال ٿيندڙ مصنوعي هارمون
urduMeaning: جسم کے غدود سے پیدا ہونے والا کیمیائی مادہ جو جسم کے افعال کو کنٹرول کرتا ہے، خون کے ذریعے سفر کرنے والا قدرتی پیغام رساں، نمو، مزاج اور میٹابولزم پر اثر ڈالنے والا مادہ، ادویات میں استعمال ہونے والا مصنوعی ہارمون

englishMeaning: The beginning or start of something, especially something unpleasant. A powerful attack or assault. The early stage of an illness or condition. The initial appearance of a situation or event.
synonyms: Beginning, Start, Commencement, Outset, Arrival, Emergence, Dawn, Inception
antonyms: End, Conclusion, Finish, Termination, Close, Ending
examples: The onset of winter brought heavy snowfall to the region. Doctors were able to detect the onset of the disease early. The onset of the storm forced people to stay indoors. The onset of the battle was sudden and unexpected.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ جي شروعات خاص ڪري ناخوشگوار شيءِ جي، حملي جي شروعات، بيماريءَ جي پهرين نشاني، ڪنهن واقعي جي شروعاتي مرحلي
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کا آغاز  خاص طور پر ناخوشگوار چیز کا، حملے کی ابتدا، بیماری کی ابتدائی علامت، کسی صورتحال کے شروع ہونے کا لمحہ

englishMeaning: Not fully developed or grown. Behaving in a childish way that is not suitable for one's age. Lacking experience or emotional maturity. Not yet ripe or ready.
synonyms: Childish, Juvenile, Unripe, Undeveloped, Green, Inexperienced, Naive, Callow
antonyms: Mature, Ripe, Developed, Adult, Experienced, Wise, Grown
examples: His immature reaction disappointed his teachers. The fruit is still immature and should not be picked. Some adults behave in an immature manner when angry. Immature plants need special care to grow properly.
sindhiMeaning: مڪمل طور تي وڌل نه، ناپختو، ٻاراڻي رويي وارو، تجربي کان محروم، اڃا نه پڪل يا تيار
urduMeaning: ناپختہ، پوری طرح نہ بڑھا ہوا، بچگانہ رویہ رکھنے والا، تجربے سے محروم، ابھی مکمل طور پر تیار یا پکا نہ ہوا

englishMeaning: Born after the normal period of pregnancy. Occurring or delivered later than the expected time. Referring to a baby born after 42 weeks of gestation. Later than the usual or expected developmental stage.
synonyms: Overdue, Late, Delayed, Post-term
antonyms: Premature, Preterm, Early, Premature-born
examples: The postmature baby required special medical attention. Doctors monitor postmature pregnancies very carefully. A postmature infant may face certain health risks. The hospital has advanced care for postmature deliveries.
sindhiMeaning: مقرر وقت کان پوءِ پيدا ٿيل، حمل جي عام مدت کان دير سان ڄاول، 42 هفتن کان پوءِ ڄاول ٻار، مقرر وقت کان دير سان ٿيندڙ
urduMeaning: مقررہ وقت کے بعد پیدا ہونے والا، حمل کی معمول کی مدت کے بعد پیدا ہونے والا بچہ، بیالیس ہفتوں سے زیادہ حمل کے بعد پیدا ہونے والا، معمول سے تاخیر سے واقع ہونے والا

englishMeaning: Relating to puberty or the stage of reaching sexual maturity. Concerning the physical and emotional changes during puberty. Characteristic of the period of adolescence when the body matures.
synonyms: Adolescent, Pubescent, Maturing, Developing
antonyms: Prepubescent, Childish, Immature, Infantile
examples: Pubertic changes usually begin between the ages of ten and fourteen. Doctors often study pubertic development in adolescents. The pubertic stage brings both physical and emotional growth. Parents should support their children through the pubertic years.
sindhiMeaning: بلوغت جي دور سان تعلق رکندڙ، جنسي پختگيءَ جي مرحلي سان لاڳاپيل، بلوغت واري وقت جي جسماني ۽ جذباتي تبديلين سان تعلق رکندڙ
urduMeaning: بلوغت سے متعلق، جنسی پختگی کے مرحلے سے تعلق رکھنے والا، بلوغت کے دوران جسمانی اور جذباتی تبدیلیوں سے متعلق

englishMeaning: The period during which a person reaches sexual maturity. The state of being at the age of puberty. A soft covering of fine hairs on plants or animals. The onset of adolescence marked by physical changes.
synonyms: Puberty, Adolescence, Maturation, Youth, Teenage
antonyms: Childhood, Infancy, Maturity, Adulthood
examples: Pubescence brings many changes in a young person's body. Doctors study pubescence to understand growth patterns. The leaves have a soft pubescence on their surface. Emotional support is important during pubescence.
sindhiMeaning: بلوغت جو دور، جنسي پختگيءَ جو مرحلو، پوکن يا جانورن تي هلڪن وارن جي تهه، نوجوانيءَ جي شروعات
urduMeaning: بلوغت کا زمانہ، جنسی پختگی کا مرحلہ، پودوں یا جانوروں پر ملائم بالوں کی تہہ، نوجوانی کے آغاز کی حالت

englishMeaning: The process of becoming fully developed physically or mentally. The stage of ripening or reaching full growth. The development of ideas, plans, or emotions over time. The aging process that improves quality, as in wine or cheese.
synonyms: Ripening, Development, Growth, Aging, Progression, Evolution
antonyms: Immaturity, Regression, Decline, Underdevelopment
examples: The maturation of the fruit takes several weeks. Emotional maturation is as important as physical growth. The wine's maturation gives it a rich flavor. Teachers observe the maturation of their students over years.
sindhiMeaning: مڪمل جسماني يا ذهني ترقي جو عمل، پڪجڻ يا پوريءَ طرح وڌڻ جو مرحلو، خيالن يا جذبن جي وقت سان ترقي، شراب يا پنير جي پوريءَ طرح تيار ٿيڻ جو عمل
urduMeaning: مکمل جسمانی یا ذہنی نشوونما کا عمل، پکنے یا پوری طرح بڑھنے کا مرحلہ، خیالات، منصوبوں یا جذبات کی بتدریج نشوونما، شراب یا پنیر کے پکنے کا عمل

englishMeaning: Having the qualities, freshness, or energy of a young person. Looking or appearing young. Characteristic of youth or the early stage of life. Vigorous and lively in nature.
synonyms: Young, Vibrant, Energetic, Fresh, Lively, Vigorous, Juvenile, Sprightly
antonyms: Old, Aged, Elderly, Mature, Weary, Tired, Ancient
examples: She has a youthful appearance despite her age. His youthful enthusiasm inspired the whole team. The painting captured her youthful beauty. He remained youthful in spirit throughout his life.
sindhiMeaning: جوانيءَ جهڙي تازگي ۽ توانائي رکندڙ، ڏسڻ ۾ ننڍي عمر جو لڳندڙ، نوجوانيءَ جي خاصيتن سان ڀرپور، متحرڪ ۽ زندهه دل
urduMeaning: جوانی کی توانائی اور تازگی رکھنے والا، دیکھنے میں کم عمر لگنے والا، نوجوانی کی خصوصیات سے بھرپور، پرجوش اور زندہ دل

englishMeaning: A state of physical ease and freedom from pain or constraint. A feeling of relief or consolation in times of distress. Something that provides ease or contentment. To soothe or console someone in grief or worry.
synonyms: Ease, Relief, Consolation, Solace, Reassurance, Contentment, Coziness, Support
antonyms: Discomfort, Distress, Pain, Suffering, Trouble, Agony, Misery
examples: The soft cushions added comfort to the room. She tried to comfort her friend after the sad news. Modern homes provide every comfort of life. His kind words brought her great comfort.
sindhiMeaning: آرام ۽ سک جي حالت، ڏک ۾ تسلي ۽ سڪون، سهولت ڏيندڙ شيءِ، ڪنهن جي غم ۾ دلاسو ڏيڻ
urduMeaning: جسمانی آرام و سکون کی حالت، مشکل وقت میں تسلی اور راحت، سہولت فراہم کرنے والی چیز، کسی کو غم یا پریشانی میں دلاسا دینا

englishMeaning: A substance or thing that causes irritation or annoyance. Something that provokes anger or discomfort. A physical agent that inflames the skin or eyes. A minor but persistent source of trouble.
synonyms: Annoyance, Nuisance, Bother, Provoker, Aggravator, Trigger
antonyms: Soother, Reliever, Calmer, Pacifier, Comforter
examples: Smoke can be a serious irritant to the eyes. Loud music was an irritant to the neighbors. Certain chemicals act as skin irritants. Constant interruptions were an irritant during the meeting.
sindhiMeaning: چڙ يا تڪليف پيدا ڪندڙ شيءِ، ڪاوڙ يا بيچيني پيدا ڪندڙ شيءِ، چمڙي يا اکين ۾ سوز پيدا ڪندڙ مادو، ننڍي پر مسلسل پريشاني جو سبب
urduMeaning: چڑچڑاپن یا تکلیف پیدا کرنے والی چیز، غصہ یا بےچینی پیدا کرنے والی چیز، جلد یا آنکھوں میں جلن پیدا کرنے والا مادہ، معمولی مگر مسلسل پریشانی کا باعث

englishMeaning: A person or thing that makes a bad situation worse. Someone who annoys or provokes others. A factor that increases the severity of a problem.
synonyms: Irritant, Provoker, Instigator, Agitator, Troublemaker, Annoyer
antonyms: Pacifier, Peacemaker, Soother, Calmer, Mediator
examples: Loud noise was a major aggravator of his headache. The delay proved to be an aggravator in the negotiations. He was known as an aggravator among his classmates. Stress can act as an aggravator of many diseases.
sindhiMeaning: صورتحال کي وڌيڪ خراب ڪندڙ شخص يا شيءِ، ٻين کي چيڙائيندڙ يا تنگ ڪندڙ، مسئلي جي شدت وڌائيندڙ سبب
urduMeaning: صورتحال کو مزید خراب کرنے والا شخص یا چیز، دوسروں کو چڑانے یا تنگ کرنے والا، مسئلے کی شدت بڑھانے والا عنصر

englishMeaning: To make or become stronger, greater, or more extreme. To increase in degree, force, or effect. To make more concentrated or severe. To heighten emotions, efforts, or actions.
synonyms: Strengthen, Heighten, Deepen, Escalate, Increase, Boost, Magnify, Sharpen
antonyms: Weaken, Lessen, Reduce, Diminish, Soften, Ease, Decrease
examples: The storm continued to intensify throughout the night. The company decided to intensify its marketing efforts. His anger began to intensify as he listened. Doctors intensify treatment when symptoms worsen.
sindhiMeaning: وڌيڪ سخت يا شديد ڪرڻ، طاقت يا اثر ۾ اضافو ڪرڻ، وڌيڪ گهرو يا مرڪوز ڪرڻ، جذبن يا ڪوششن کي وڌائڻ
urduMeaning: مزید شدید یا سخت کرنا، طاقت یا اثر میں اضافہ کرنا، مزید مرکوز یا گہرا کرنا، جذبات یا کوششوں کو بڑھانا

englishMeaning: A substance that causes illness or death when absorbed by a living organism. Something harmful to health, happiness, or success. To harm or kill by using a toxic substance. To corrupt someone's mind or feelings.
synonyms: Toxin, Venom, Bane, Contaminant, Corrupt, Taint
antonyms: Antidote, Cure, Remedy, Purify, Cleanse, Heal
examples: The bottle contained a deadly poison. Gossip can poison friendships. Farmers use chemicals to poison harmful insects. Jealousy slowly poisoned their relationship.
sindhiMeaning: اهڙو مادو جيڪو جاندار جي جسم ۾ داخل ٿيڻ سان بيماري يا موت جو سبب بڻجي، صحت  خوشي يا ڪاميابيءَ لاءِ نقصانڪار شيءِ، زهر ڏيڻ سان نقصان پهچائڻ يا مارڻ، ڪنهن جي سوچ يا جذبن کي خراب ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: ایسا مادہ جو جاندار کے جسم میں داخل ہو کر بیماری یا موت کا سبب بنے، صحت  خوشی یا کامیابی کے لیے نقصان دہ چیز، زہر دے کر نقصان پہنچانا یا ہلاک کرنا، کسی کے ذہن یا جذبات کو بگاڑنا

englishMeaning: Relating to the epidermis, the outer layer of the skin. Concerning the surface layer of skin or plant tissue. Belonging to the outermost protective covering of an organism.
synonyms: Cutaneous, Skin, Surface, Superficial, Dermal, Outer
antonyms: Internal, Subcutaneous, Deep, Inner, Underlying
