sindhiMeaning: هڪ وڏو ڪارو سامونڊي پکي جنهن جي ڊگهي ڳچي ۽ ٽيڏي چهنب هوندي آهي ۽ مڇي جھلڻ لاءِ ٽٻي هڻي ٿو، پاڻي ۾ ترڻ ۽ مڇي شڪار ڪرڻ ۾ ماهر پکي، اهڙو لالچي ماڻهو جيڪو پنهنجي حق کان گھڻو وٺي، ادب ۾ لالچ ۽ حرص جي علامت
urduMeaning: ایک بڑا سیاہ سمندری پرندہ جس کی گردن لمبی اور چونچ خمدار ہوتی ہے اور مچھلی پکڑنے کے لیے غوطہ لگاتا ہے، پانی میں تیرنے اور شکار کرنے کا ماہر پرندہ، مجازاً ایسا لالچی شخص جو اپنے حصے سے کہیں زیادہ لے، ادب میں حرص و لالچ کی علامت

urduMeaning: ٹمٹمانا یا لرزتی ہوئی روشنی دینا، تیز اور بے ترتیب حرکت کرنا، کسی جذبے کا ہلکا اور مختصر اظہار، ٹمٹماتی روشنی یا معمولی تیز حرکت

englishMeaning: Consisting of a single musical line, melody, or track without accompaniment. Pertaining to a sound reproduction system that uses only one channel of audio. englishMeaning: A pure vowel sound that is articulated with a steady and constant tongue position throughout its duration. A single vowel phoneme that does not glide into another sound like a diphthong. A vowel characterized by a single, unchanging quality of resonance. synonyms: Pure Vowel, Single Vowel, Unglided Vowel, Static Vowel, Simple Vowel, Vocalic Sound, Phoneme, Vowel Sound, Unitary Vowel, Monophthongal Vowel, Monic Sound, Articulated Vowel

examples: The word 'sit' contains a monophthong in the middle. Most English vowels are monophthongs rather than diphthongs. Phonetic transcription often distinguishes a monophthong from a gliding vowel sound. The teacher explained how the tongue remains stationary while pronouncing a monophthong.

synonyms: Pure, Simple, Unchanging, Steady, Single-voweled, Uniform, Monophthongic, Constant, Unvaried, Static, Unmixed, Homogeneous, Pure-voweled, Singular.

examples: The vowel sound in the word 'bead' is strictly monophthongal in most dialects. Phoneticians categorize vowels based on whether they are monophthongal or diphthongal. sindhiMeaning: ٻن مقدارن جي وچ ۾ عددي نسبت، تناسب يا مقابلو، هڪ شيءِ جي ٻي جي ڀيٽ ۾ مقدار، حصن جي وچ ۾ توازن يا نسبت، شرح جيڪا ٻن انگن جو مقابلو ڏيکاري
urduMeaning: دو مقداروں کے درمیان عددی نسبت، تناسب یا موازنہ، ایک چیز کا دوسری کے مقابلے میں تناسب، حصوں کے درمیان توازن یا نسبت، وہ شرح جو دو اعداد کا موازنہ ظاہر کرے

englishMeaning: The proportional relationship between the width and the height of an image, screen, or shape. A measurement expressing how wide a picture or display is compared with how tall it is. In engineering, the ratio of the length of a wing or body to its width. A standard format used to describe screen or video dimensions.
synonyms: Proportion, Dimension ratio, Screen ratio, Format, Width-to-height ratio, Scale, Frame proportion, Display ratio, Image proportion, Geometry
antonyms: Distortion, Stretch, Disproportion, Imbalance, Skew, Deformation, Irregularity, Mismatch, Warp, Asymmetry
examples: Most modern televisions use a sixteen-by-nine aspect ratio. The photograph was cropped, which changed its aspect ratio. Choose the correct aspect ratio before exporting the video. Older films were shot in a squarer aspect ratio than today's movies.
sindhiMeaning: تصوير يا اسڪرين جي ويڪر ۽ اوچائي جي وچ ۾ نسبت، ڊيگهه ۽ ويڪر جو تناسب، وڊيو يا ڊسپلي جي ماپ ظاهر ڪندڙ تناسب، انجنيئرنگ ۾ ڊيگهه ۽ ويڪر جو تناسب
urduMeaning: تصویر یا اسکرین کی چوڑائی اور اونچائی کے درمیان نسبت، طول و عرض کا تناسب، ویڈیو یا ڈسپلے کی پیمائش ظاہر کرنے والا تناسب، انجینئرنگ میں لمبائی اور چوڑائی کا تناسب

englishMeaning: A system of government or management in which decisions are made by technical experts rather than elected politicians. Rule by scientists, engineers, or specialists in a particular field. A society controlled by people with technical or scientific knowledge. The body of technical experts who hold such power.
synonyms: Expert rule, Meritocracy, Bureaucracy, Administration, Specialist government, Elitism, Managerialism, Governance, Regime, Officialdom
antonyms: Democracy, Populism, Mob rule, Autocracy, Anarchy, Amateurism, Laity, Monarchy, Self-rule, Demagoguery
examples: Critics argued that the reforms were pushing the country towards a technocracy. In a technocracy, policy is shaped by data rather than public opinion. The new cabinet was described as a technocracy of economists and engineers. Supporters of technocracy believe expertise produces better decisions.
sindhiMeaning: اهو نظام حڪومت جنهن ۾ فيصلا ٽيڪنيڪي ماهر ڪن، سائنسدانن ۽ انجنيئرن جي حڪمراني، ماهرن جي هٿ ۾ اقتدار وارو سماج، ٽيڪنيڪي ماهرن جو گروهه جيڪو اقتدار رکي
urduMeaning: وہ نظامِ حکومت جس میں فیصلے تکنیکی ماہرین کریں، سائنسدانوں اور انجینئروں کی حکمرانی، ماہرین کے ہاتھ میں اقتدار والا معاشرہ، تکنیکی ماہرین کا وہ گروہ جو اقتدار رکھتا ہو

englishMeaning: Relating to government or management by technical experts. Based on scientific or specialised knowledge rather than political ideology. Characterised by a cool, data-driven approach to decision-making. Belonging to or typical of a technocracy.
synonyms: Expert, Specialist, Managerial, Bureaucratic, Scientific, Administrative, Professional, Analytical, Data-driven, Meritocratic
antonyms: Populist, Democratic, Ideological, Amateur, Emotional, Unprofessional, Intuitive, Political, Lay, Unscientific
examples: The minister took a technocratic approach to solving the energy crisis. His speech was technocratic and full of statistics. A technocratic government was appointed to stabilise the economy. Voters often find technocratic language cold and difficult to follow.
sindhiMeaning: ٽيڪنيڪي ماهرن جي حڪمراني سان لاڳاپيل، سياسي نظريي بدران سائنسي ڄاڻ تي ٻڌل، انگن اکرن ۽ ڄاڻ تي مبني فيصلن وارو، ٽيڪنوڪريسي سان تعلق رکندڙ
urduMeaning: تکنیکی ماہرین کی حکمرانی سے متعلق، سیاسی نظریے کے بجائے سائنسی علم پر مبنی، اعداد و شمار پر مبنی فیصلہ سازی والا، ٹیکنوکریسی سے تعلق رکھنے والا

englishMeaning: A person who objects to something unpleasant being built or located near their own home while accepting it elsewhere. Short for the phrase 'not in my back yard'. Describing an attitude of selfish local opposition to development. Relating to protests against nearby construction or facilities.
synonyms: Objector, Protester, Obstructionist, Opponent, Blocker, Complainant, Dissenter, Campaigner, Resister, Critic
antonyms: Supporter, Advocate, Backer, Promoter, Proponent, Enabler, Champion, Sponsor, Welcomer, Facilitator
examples: Local nimbys blocked the plan to build a waste plant near the village. He supports wind power in principle but is a nimby when it comes to his own valley. The council dismissed the objections as a typical nimby reaction. Nimby campaigns have delayed several housing projects in the area.
sindhiMeaning: اهو شخص جيڪو ڪنهن ناپسنديده منصوبي کي پنهنجي گهر ويجهو ٺهڻ تي اعتراض ڪري، پنهنجي علائقي ۾ تعمير جي مخالفت ڪندڙ، خودغرض مقامي مخالفت رکندڙ ماڻهو، پنهنجي پاڙي ۾ ترقياتي منصوبي جو مخالف
urduMeaning: وہ شخص جو کسی ناپسندیدہ منصوبے کے اپنے گھر کے قریب بننے پر اعتراض کرے، اپنے علاقے میں تعمیر کی مخالفت کرنے والا، خود غرض مقامی مخالفت رکھنے والا، اپنے محلے میں ترقیاتی منصوبے کا مخالف

englishMeaning: A thick, dark, low-lying cloud layer that produces continuous rain or snow. A type of cloud formation associated with steady precipitation and grey overcast skies. A shapeless rain cloud covering the whole sky. In meteorology, a cloud genus combining stratus and rain-bearing features.
synonyms: Rain cloud, Storm cloud, Overcast layer, Cloud bank, Stratus, Grey cloud, Precipitating cloud, Cloud cover, Cloud formation, Low cloud
antonyms: Clear sky, Cirrus, Sunshine, Blue sky, Cloudlessness, Fair weather, Dry spell, Bright sky, Openness, Drought
examples: A blanket of nimbostratus brought steady rain throughout the afternoon. The pilot avoided the thick nimbostratus layer over the mountains. Nimbostratus clouds usually hide the sun completely. Forecasters expect nimbostratus and drizzle for most of the week.
sindhiMeaning: ٿلهو ۽ ڪارو هيٺاهون ڪڪر جيڪو مسلسل مينهن يا برف وسائي، لڳاتار برسات سان لاڳاپيل ڪڪرن جو قسم، سڄي آسمان کي ڍڪيندڙ بي شڪل برساتي ڪڪر، موسمياتي علم ۾ برسات آڻيندڙ ڪڪر جو هڪ قسم
urduMeaning: موٹا اور سیاہ نچلی سطح کا بادل جو مسلسل بارش یا برف برسائے، لگاتار بارش سے وابستہ بادلوں کی قسم، پورے آسمان کو ڈھانپنے والا بے شکل بارشی بادل، موسمیات میں بارش لانے والے بادل کی ایک قسم

englishMeaning: An alphabetical list of names or topics at the end of a book with page numbers. A number or figure showing the level or change of something such as prices. A sign or indicator of a particular condition or trend. To arrange information in a systematic list. To link a value such as wages to a measure such as inflation.
synonyms: List, Catalogue, Directory, Register, Table, Indicator, Gauge, Measure, Guide, Key
antonyms: Body, Text, Content, Disorder, Jumble, Confusion, Disarray, Mass, Whole, Randomness
examples: Look up the topic in the index at the back of the book. The share index fell sharply after the announcement. Rising crime is often taken as an index of social decay. The library has indexed all its new manuscripts.
sindhiMeaning: ڪتاب جي آخر ۾ ڏنل فهرست جنهن ۾ عنوان ۽ صفحن جا نمبر هجن، ڪنهن شيءِ جي سطح يا تبديلي ڏيکاريندڙ انگ، ڪنهن حالت جي نشاني يا اشارو، ڄاڻ کي ترتيب سان فهرست ۾ آڻڻ، اجرت يا قيمت کي مهانگائي سان ڳنڍڻ
urduMeaning: کتاب کے آخر میں دی گئی فہرست جس میں موضوعات اور صفحہ نمبر ہوں، کسی چیز کی سطح یا تبدیلی ظاہر کرنے والا عدد، کسی حالت کی نشانی یا اشارہ، معلومات کو ترتیب سے فہرست میں لانا، اجرت یا قیمت کو مہنگائی سے منسلک کرنا

englishMeaning: The finger next to the thumb, used for pointing. The first finger of the hand. The forefinger, commonly used to indicate direction or press buttons. In anatomy, the second digit of the human hand.
synonyms: Forefinger, First finger, Pointer, Digit, Pointing finger, Second digit, Trigger finger, Finger, Forefinger digit, Hand digit
antonyms: Thumb, Little finger, Ring finger, Middle finger, Toe, Palm, Wrist, Knuckle, Nail, Heel of hand
examples: She pointed at the map with her index finger. He tapped the screen gently with his index finger. The doctor asked him to touch his nose with his index finger. A cut on his index finger made typing painful.
sindhiMeaning: آڱوٺي جي ڀرسان واري آڱر جيڪا اشارو ڪرڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿئي، هٿ جي پهرين آڱر، شهادت جي آڱر، انسان جي هٿ جي ٻي آڱر
urduMeaning: انگوٹھے کے ساتھ والی انگلی جو اشارہ کرنے کے لیے استعمال ہوتی ہے، ہاتھ کی پہلی انگلی، شہادت کی انگلی، انسانی ہاتھ کی دوسری انگلی

englishMeaning: The practice of linking wages, pensions, or prices to a price index such as inflation. Automatic adjustment of payments in line with the cost of living. The process of compiling or arranging an index. In economics, a mechanism that protects the real value of money over time.
synonyms: Linking, Adjustment, Escalation, Pegging, Index-linking, Cataloguing, Alignment, Revaluation, Uprating, Correlation
antonyms: Freezing, Fixation, Delinking, Stagnation, Deregulation, Detachment, Cut, Reduction, Suspension, Disconnection
examples: The union demanded full indexation of salaries to inflation. Indexation of pensions protects retired people from rising prices. The government suspended indexation during the financial crisis. Indexation of the documents took the archivists several months.
sindhiMeaning: اجرتن، پينشن يا قيمتن کي مهانگائي جي انڊيڪس سان ڳنڍڻ جو عمل، خرچ جي حساب سان ادائيگين ۾ خودڪار واڌ، فهرست ٺاهڻ يا ترتيب ڏيڻ جو عمل، معاشيات ۾ پئسي جي اصل قدر بچائڻ جو طريقو
urduMeaning: اجرتوں، پنشن یا قیمتوں کو مہنگائی کے اشاریے سے منسلک کرنے کا عمل، اخراجات کے مطابق ادائیگیوں میں خودکار اضافہ، فہرست سازی یا ترتیب دینے کا عمل، معاشیات میں پیسے کی اصل قدر محفوظ رکھنے کا طریقہ

englishMeaning: To issue a bold challenge to someone. To invite a person or group into a contest or confrontation. To openly declare opposition and dare an opponent to respond. Originally, to throw down a glove as a formal challenge to a duel.
synonyms: Challenge, Defy, Dare, Confront, Provoke, Call out, Contest, Take on, Summon, Bait
antonyms: Submit, Yield, Surrender, Back down, Retreat, Concede, Withdraw, Comply, Give in, Avoid
examples: The opposition leader threw down the gauntlet by demanding an early election. She threw down the gauntlet and challenged the champion to a rematch. By publishing the report, the newspaper threw down the gauntlet to the regulators. He threw down the gauntlet, daring his rivals to match his offer.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي کليل چئلينج ڏيڻ، مقابلي لاءِ للڪارڻ، مخالفت جو اعلان ڪري جواب گهرڻ، اصل ۾ دستانو اڇلائي دوبدو مقابلي لاءِ چئلينج ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: کسی کو کھلا چیلنج دینا، مقابلے کے لیے للکارنا، مخالفت کا اعلان کر کے جواب طلب کرنا، اصل میں دستانہ پھینک کر دوبدو مقابلے کا چیلنج دینا

englishMeaning: A strong protective glove, especially one worn as part of armour. A challenge or confrontation, as in the phrase 'throw down the gauntlet'. A difficult ordeal in which a person faces criticism or danger from several sides. Historically, a military punishment in which a person ran between two rows of men who struck him.
synonyms: Glove, Mitt, Challenge, Ordeal, Trial, Test, Armour, Handguard, Confrontation, Hardship
antonyms: Bare hand, Ease, Comfort, Safety, Retreat, Surrender, Peace, Shelter, Relief, Protection
examples: The knight removed his gauntlet before shaking hands. The new policy had to run the gauntlet of public criticism. She picked up the gauntlet and accepted the challenge. He wore heavy gauntlets while welding the metal frame.
sindhiMeaning: مضبوط حفاظتي دستانو، خاص ڪري زره جو حصو، چئلينج يا مقابلو، اهڙي ڏکي آزمائش جنهن ۾ ماڻهو هر پاسي کان تنقيد يا خطري هيٺ اچي، پراڻي زماني جي سزا جنهن ۾ ماڻهو ٻن قطارن جي وچ مان لنگهندو هو
urduMeaning: مضبوط حفاظتی دستانہ، خاص طور پر زرہ کا حصہ، چیلنج یا مقابلہ، ایسی مشکل آزمائش جس میں انسان ہر طرف سے تنقید یا خطرے میں آ جائے، پرانے زمانے کی سزا جس میں شخص دو قطاروں کے درمیان سے گزرتا تھا

englishMeaning: To suddenly lose one's temper and behave in an uncontrolled way. To have a tantrum or emotional outburst, often over something minor. To become extremely upset or agitated in public. An informal British expression for making a fuss.
synonyms: Lose temper, Have a tantrum, Blow up, Flip out, Erupt, Rage, Fume, Explode, Make a scene, Storm
antonyms: Stay calm, Keep cool, Compose oneself, Relax, Tolerate, Endure, Settle, Accept, Restrain, Soothe
examples: He threw a wobbly when he heard his flight had been cancelled. The child threw a wobbly in the middle of the supermarket. Try to explain calmly instead of throwing a wobbly. She threw a wobbly over a tiny mistake in the report.
sindhiMeaning: اوچتو ڪاوڙ ۾ اچي بي قابو ٿي وڃڻ، ننڍي ڳالهه تي هنگامو ڪرڻ، عام ماڻهن اڳيان تمام گهڻو پريشان يا مشتعل ٿيڻ، برطانوي غير رسمي محاورو جنهن جو مطلب آهي فساد مچائڻ
urduMeaning: اچانک غصے میں آ کر بے قابو ہو جانا، معمولی بات پر ہنگامہ کرنا، لوگوں کے سامنے سخت پریشان یا مشتعل ہو جانا، برطانوی غیر رسمی محاورہ جس کا مطلب ہے واویلا مچانا

englishMeaning: To behave recklessly without worrying about the risks. To stop being careful and act boldly. To take a chance despite possible danger or loss. To abandon prudence in favour of daring action.
synonyms: Take a risk, Gamble, Chance it, Be reckless, Plunge in, Dare, Venture, Act boldly, Go for broke, Abandon restraint
antonyms: Be careful, Play safe, Hesitate, Take precautions, Hold back, Beware, Deliberate, Restrain, Avoid risk, Proceed cautiously
examples: He threw caution to the wind and invested all his savings in the venture. They threw caution to the wind and set off without a map. She threw caution to the wind and told her boss exactly what she thought. For once, let us throw caution to the wind and enjoy the evening.
sindhiMeaning: خطرن جي پرواهه ڪرڻ کان سواءِ بي احتياطي سان ڪم ڪرڻ، احتياط ڇڏي جرئت سان قدم کڻڻ، نقصان جي خطري باوجود موقعو وٺڻ، سمجهداري ڇڏي دليري سان ڪم ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: خطرات کی پرواہ کیے بغیر بے احتیاطی سے کام کرنا، احتیاط چھوڑ کر جرات سے قدم اٹھانا، نقصان کے خطرے کے باوجود موقع لینا، دانائی چھوڑ کر دلیری سے کام کرنا

englishMeaning: To discourage an idea or plan by criticising it. To reduce someone's enthusiasm or hope. To express doubt that spoils a proposal. To dampen excitement about a suggestion.
synonyms: Discourage, Dampen, Deter, Dishearten, Belittle, Undermine, Dissuade, Deflate, Criticise, Demotivate
antonyms: Encourage, Support, Inspire, Endorse, Promote, Cheer, Motivate, Applaud, Back, Enthuse
examples: The finance director threw cold water on the expansion plan. Please do not throw cold water on their enthusiasm so early. His remarks threw cold water on the whole celebration. The survey results threw cold water on the company's optimistic forecast.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن خيال يا منصوبي تي تنقيد ڪري حوصلو گهٽائڻ، ڪنهن جو جوش يا اميد ختم ڪرڻ، شڪ ظاهر ڪري تجويز خراب ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ڳالهه جي خوشي کي ٿڌو ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: کسی خیال یا منصوبے پر تنقید کر کے حوصلہ توڑنا، کسی کا جوش یا امید ختم کرنا، شک ظاہر کر کے تجویز کو خراب کرنا، کسی بات کے جوش کو ٹھنڈا کر دینا

englishMeaning: To fight someone physically, especially with the fists. To engage in a brawl or exchange punches. An informal expression meaning to be ready to fight. To settle a dispute through a physical fight.
synonyms: Fight, Brawl, Scuffle, Punch, Spar, Clash, Tussle, Come to blows, Grapple, Wrestle
antonyms: Make peace, Reconcile, Retreat, Talk, Negotiate, Avoid, Calm down, Settle peacefully, Withdraw, Forgive
examples: The two men were ready to throw hands outside the stadium. Instead of throwing hands, they finally sat down and talked. Security guards separated the fans before they could throw hands. He warned that anyone throwing hands would be removed from the club.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن سان هٿن سان وڙهڻ، مُڪن سان مقابلو ڪرڻ، جهيڙي ۾ پوڻ، جهڳڙو هٿن سان نبيرڻ، غير رسمي انداز ۾ لڙڻ لاءِ تيار ٿيڻ
urduMeaning: کسی سے ہاتھا پائی کرنا، مکوں سے لڑنا، جھگڑے میں پڑنا، تنازع کو ہاتھا پائی سے نمٹانا، غیر رسمی انداز میں لڑنے کے لیے تیار ہونا

englishMeaning: Extremely thin and bony, usually because of illness, hunger, or worry. Looking pale, hollow-cheeked, and worn out. Describing a place that appears bleak, bare, and grim. Having a harsh and desolate appearance.
synonyms: Thin, Emaciated, Haggard, Bony, Skeletal, Drawn, Wasted, Lean, Scrawny, Bleak
antonyms: Plump, Healthy, Robust, Stout, Chubby, Well-fed, Fleshy, Radiant, Sturdy, Inviting
examples: He looked gaunt after months of illness. Her gaunt face showed the strain of the long journey. The gaunt ruins stood alone on the hillside. Refugees arrived tired, gaunt and hungry.
sindhiMeaning: تمام سنهو ۽ هڏائون، عام طور بيماري بک يا پريشاني سبب، ڦڪو ۽ ٿڪل شڪل وارو، اهڙي جاءِ جيڪا ويران ۽ اداس لڳي، سخت ۽ اجڙيل ڏيک وارو
urduMeaning: نہایت دبلا اور ہڈیوں والا، عام طور پر بیماری بھوک یا پریشانی کی وجہ سے، زرد اور تھکا ہوا چہرہ رکھنے والا، ایسی جگہ جو ویران اور اداس لگے، سخت اور اجڑا ہوا منظر رکھنے والا

englishMeaning: To try to solve a problem simply by spending large amounts of money on it. To fund something heavily without proper planning. To use money as a substitute for real thought or effort. To invest generously in the hope of a quick fix.
synonyms: Overspend, Fund heavily, Lavish, Bankroll, Splurge, Subsidise, Pour funds into, Finance, Invest blindly, Squander
antonyms: Economise, Plan, Budget, Save, Ration, Withhold, Reform, Strategise, Cut spending, Conserve
examples: You cannot fix a broken system just by throwing money at it. The government has thrown money at the problem for years with little result. Instead of throwing money at the issue, they hired better managers. Critics say the ministry throws money at projects without measuring outcomes.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن مسئلي کي رڳو گهڻا پئسا خرچ ڪري حل ڪرڻ جي ڪوشش، بغير منصوبابندي جي وڏي رقم لڳائڻ، سوچ ۽ محنت جي بدران پئسو استعمال ڪرڻ، جلد حل جي اميد تي کليل خرچ ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: کسی مسئلے کو صرف زیادہ پیسہ خرچ کر کے حل کرنے کی کوشش کرنا، بغیر منصوبہ بندی کے بڑی رقم لگانا، سوچ اور محنت کے بجائے پیسہ استعمال کرنا، جلد حل کی امید پر کھلا خرچ کرنا

englishMeaning: The state of being extremely thin and bony. A pale, worn, and hollow appearance caused by illness or hardship. Bleakness or bareness in the look of a place. A grim and desolate quality.
synonyms: Thinness, Emaciation, Haggardness, Leanness, Boniness, Wasting, Bleakness, Frailty, Scrawniness, Desolation

englishMeaning: A long, soft feather or group of feathers, often used as a decoration. A tall column of smoke, dust, water, or gas rising into the air. A spreading trail of a substance moving through air or water. To preen or arrange feathers, or to take great pride in oneself.

To come back and have the opposite effect from the one intended. Something that rebounds unexpectedly on its originator.

antonyms: Poorly, Badly, Averagely, Mediocrely, Unremarkably, Ordinarily, Inadequately, Weakly, Dully, Modestly
examples: The students performed outstandingly in the national examination. She is outstandingly talented at mathematics. The hotel was outstandingly clean and well managed. He handled the crisis outstandingly well.
sindhiMeaning: غير معمولي بهترين انداز ۾، ايتري حد تائين جو ٻين کان واضح اڳتي هجي، نمايان ۽ شاندار نموني، غير معمولي معيار تي زور ڏيڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿيندڙ
urduMeaning: غیر معمولی بہترین انداز میں، اس حد تک کہ دوسروں سے واضح آگے ہو، نمایاں اور شاندار طور پر، غیر معمولی معیار پر زور دینے کے لیے استعمال ہونے والا

englishMeaning: A branch or post located far from the main headquarters. A remote place where an official or worker is posted. In Australia, a small settlement away from a main community. Relating to duty or travel outside one's usual station.
synonyms: Outpost, Branch, Substation, Remote post, Depot, Satellite office, Station, Settlement, Field office, Camp
antonyms: Headquarters, Main office, Centre, Base, Capital, Hub, Home station, Metropolis, Core, Head office
examples: He was posted to a remote outstation for two years. Supplies reach the outstation only once a month. The company runs three outstations along the coast. She is on outstation duty until the end of the month.
sindhiMeaning: مرڪزي دفتر کان پري واقع شاخ يا چوڪي، اهو ڏورانهون هنڌ جتي ڪو آفيسر يا ڪارڪن مقرر ٿئي، آسٽريليا ۾ مکيه آبادي کان پري ننڍي وسندي، پنهنجي مستقل جاءِ کان ٻاهر ڊيوٽي يا سفر سان لاڳاپيل
urduMeaning: مرکزی دفتر سے دور واقع شاخ یا چوکی، وہ دور دراز جگہ جہاں کوئی افسر یا کارکن تعینات ہو، آسٹریلیا میں مرکزی آبادی سے دور چھوٹی بستی، اپنے مستقل مقام سے باہر ڈیوٹی یا سفر سے متعلق

englishMeaning: To stay longer than expected, required, or welcome. To remain beyond a specific duration or time limit.
synonyms: Overstay, Linger, Remain too long, Tarry
antonyms: Depart, Leave, Vacate, Go
examples: They did not want to outstay their welcome at the host's house. It is unwise to outstay your visa in a foreign country. The guest decided to leave early so as not to outstay his invitation. She realized she had outstayed her time and quickly apologized.
sindhiMeaning: وڌيڪ وقت ترسن, حد کان وڌيڪ رهڻ, ڏينهن وڌائڻ
urduMeaning: زیادہ دیر ٹھہرنا, حد سے زیادہ قیام کرنا, ضرورت سے زیادہ رکنا

englishMeaning: Not likely to cause disagreement, argument, or public debate. Generally accepted, peaceful, or uncontested by people.
synonyms: Uncontroversial, Undisputed, Unquestioned, Accepted, Safe
antonyms: Controversial, Disputed, Contentious, Debatable
examples: The committee passed a non-controversial proposal without any opposition. He preferred to talk about non-controversial topics like the weather. The decision to repair the local park was completely non-controversial. She gave a non-controversial speech that pleased everyone in the audience.
sindhiMeaning: غير متنازعه, بي تكرار, عام قبول ٿيل
urduMeaning: غیر متنازع, بلا تنازع, متفق علیہ

englishMeaning: In a way that causes public disagreement, heated discussion, or intense debate. Done in a manner that provokes opposing views.
synonyms: Contentiously, Disputably, Questionably, Provocatively
antonyms: Uncontroversially, Indisputably, Harmoniously, Agreeably
examples: The referee controversially awarded a penalty in the final minute of the game. The mayor controversially decided to close the community center. She controversially claimed that the project was a total waste of money. The book was controversially banned in several regions.
sindhiMeaning: متنازعه طريقي سان, تڪراري انداز ۾
urduMeaning: متنازع طور پر, بحث طلب انداز میں

englishMeaning: A prolonged public disagreement or heated debate about a subject. A state of conflict, dispute, or opposition among different parties.
synonyms: Dispute, Disagreement, Contention, Debate, Dissension
antonyms: Agreement, Harmony, Consensus, Accord
examples: The new law sparked intense controversy among the public. The politician managed to avoid controversy during his campaign. There was much controversy surrounding the publication of the report. The decision to demolish the historical building caused widespread controversy.
sindhiMeaning: تڪرار, بحث, ڦيڙو, متنازعو
urduMeaning: تنازع, بحث, اختلاف, کلافت

englishMeaning: To deny the truth or validity of something. To argue against, dispute, or contradict a statement or belief. To engage in controversy over a matter.
synonyms: Dispute, Gainsay, Refute, Contradict, Challenge, Deny
antonyms: Confirm, Corroborate, Support, Agree, Accept, Verify
examples: The attorney attempted to controvert the evidence presented by the prosecution. It is difficult to controvert well-documented historical facts. She wrote an article to controvert the popular scientific myth. No one dared to controvert the judge's ruling during the trial.
sindhiMeaning: رد ڪرڻ, غلط ثابت ڪرڻ, بحث ڪرڻ, اختلاف ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: تردید کرنا, غلط ثابت کرنا, بحث کرنا, رد کرنا

englishMeaning: Stubbornly or willfully disobedient to authority. Rebellious and obstinate in resisting control. Showing a willful refusal to comply with court orders or official requests.
synonyms: Rebellious, Obstinate, Stubborn, Refractory, Willful, Disobedient
antonyms: Obedient, Compliant, Submissive, Tractable, Dutiful
examples: The contumacious witness refused to answer any of the prosecutor's questions. He was fined for his contumacious behavior in the courtroom. The teacher struggled to manage the contumacious student in class. A contumacious refusal to obey orders can lead to severe penalties.
sindhiMeaning: سرکش, گستاخ, ضدي, نافرمان
urduMeaning: سرکش, نافرمان, ضدی, منہ زور

englishMeaning: Not cause for dispute or disagreement. Generally accepted and unlikely to provoke conflict or debate. Safe, mild, and accepted by most people without opposition.
synonyms: Undisputed, Accepted, Indisputable, Safe, Unexceptionable
antonyms: Controversial, Disputed, Contentious, Debatable
examples: The proposal was accepted quickly because it was largely uncontroversial. She chose an uncontroversial topic for her presentation to avoid arguments. The candidate kept his public statements safe and uncontroversial. Park safety is an uncontroversial issue that all residents support.
sindhiMeaning: غيرمتنازعه, بي برپٽ, جنهن تي اعتراض نه هجي
urduMeaning: غیر متنازع, بلا اعتراض, مسلمہ

englishMeaning: Not based on or conforming to what is generally done or accepted. Original, unorthodox, or out of the ordinary. Departing from established rules, traditions, or social standards.
synonyms: Unorthodox, Original, Unusual, Offbeat, Atypical, Eccentric
antonyms: Conventional, Traditional, Orthodox, Standard, Customary
examples: She had an unconventional teaching style that resonated well with the students. His unconventional approach to business led to remarkable success. They decided to hold an unconventional wedding on a secluded beach. The artist was famous for using unconventional materials in her sculptures.
sindhiMeaning: غير روايتي, انوکو, نئون, نرالو
urduMeaning: غیر روایتی, انوکھا, عجیب, جدید

englishMeaning: The quality or state of being unconventional. Behavior, style, or opinion that does not conform to established rules, traditions, or social standards. An instance of unique or original conduct.
synonyms: Eccentricity, Originality, Peculiarity, Novelty, Singularity, Nonconformity
antonyms: Conventionality, Conformity, Orthodoxy, Tradition, Normality
examples: Her unconventionality in dress made her stand out in the crowd. The artist was famous for the unconventionality of his techniques. Despite the unconventionality of their approach, they achieved great success. She embraced her unconventionality and refused to conform to social expectations.
sindhiMeaning: غير روايتي پڻو, انوکائپ, عجائپ, نوانئپ
urduMeaning: غیر روایت پسندی, انوکھا پن, جدت, غیر روایتی انداز

englishMeaning: Not persuaded or certain about something. Having doubts or reservations regarding a claim, statement, or idea.
synonyms: Skeptical, Doubtful, Dubious, Suspicious, Incredulous, Uncertain
antonyms: Convinced, Certain, Persuaded, Confident, Sure
examples: Despite his detailed explanation, she remained unconvinced. The jury was unconvinced by the defendant's weak alibi. He listened to the pitch but walked away unconvinced. Skeptical scientists are still unconvinced by the preliminary findings.
sindhiMeaning: غير مطمئن, بي يقين, جنھن کي يقين نه ھجي, شڪي
urduMeaning: غیر مطمئن, بے یقین, شک میں مبتلا, مشکوک

englishMeaning: Completely certain about something. Fully persuaded or firm in a belief or belief system.
synonyms: Certain, Sure, Persuaded, Confident, Satisfied, Positive
antonyms: Unconvinced, Doubtful, Skeptical, Dubious, Uncertain
examples: I am fully convinced that this is the right decision. She was convinced of his innocence despite the accusations. The evidence was strong enough to leave everyone convinced. He was so convinced by the presentation that he invested immediately.
sindhiMeaning: مطمئن, پڪو, بي شڪ, يقين رکندڙ
urduMeaning: مطمئن, قائل, پرایقین, پرایمان

englishMeaning: Capable of causing someone to believe that something is true or real. Serving to convince or persuade through logic, evidence, or appeal. Powerful, believable, or credible.
synonyms: Persuasive, Compelling, Plausible, Believable, Credible, Cogent
antonyms: Unconvincing, Implausible, Incredible, Dubious, Weak
examples: She gave a convincing argument in favor of the new policy. The actor provided a very convincing performance as the villain. There was no convincing proof to support the claim. The team scored a convincing victory over their rivals.
sindhiMeaning: يقين ڏياريندڙ, اثرائتو, دليل سان ڀرپور, دلپذير
urduMeaning: قائل کرنے والا, مدلل, وزن دار, بااثر

englishMeaning: In a persuasive or credible manner. In a way that causes someone to believe that something is true or real. Firmly establishing belief or trust through strong evidence or argument.
synonyms: Persuasively, Credibly, Plausibly, Cogently, Forcefully
antonyms: Unconvincingly, Dubiously, Weakly, Incredibly
examples: She argued her case convincingly before the judge. The actor played the role so convincingly that everyone believed he was a real doctor. The team won the championship convincingly with a six-goal lead. He spoke convincingly about the need for immediate environmental action.
sindhiMeaning: يقين سان, يقين ڏياريندڙ طريقي سان, دلائل سان
urduMeaning: قائلانہ انداز میں, یقین دہانی کے ساتھ, دلپذیر طریقے سے

englishMeaning: A person or thing that conveys, transports, or communicates something. A continuous moving band or mechanism used for transporting objects from one place to another.
synonyms: Carrier, Transporter, Bearer, Transmitter, Conveyor belt
antonyms: Receiver, Recipient, Retainer
examples: The luggage was placed on the airport conveyor belt. He acted as the conveyor of good news to the family. The factory relies on an automated conveyor system to move heavy parts. She was the main conveyor of local traditions to the younger generation.
sindhiMeaning: پہنچائيندڙ, ليجائيندڙ, سامان کڻي ويندڙ پٽي
urduMeaning: پہنچانے والا, منتقل کرنے والا, متحرک پٹا

englishMeaning: A lawyer or specialist who prepares documents for the conveyance of property. A legal professional involved in transferring the ownership of real estate from one person to another.
synonyms: Property lawyer, Legal executive, Notary, Solicitor
antonyms: Litigator, Prosecutor
examples: We hired a licensed conveyancer to handle the legal paperwork for buying our house. The conveyancer checked the property title for any outstanding debts. You should consult a conveyancer before signing the property transfer agreement. The process was delayed because the conveyancer needed additional documents.
sindhiMeaning: ملکيت منتقل ڪندڙ وڪيل, دستاويز جوڙيندڙ
urduMeaning: جائداد کی منتقلی کا وکیل, دستاویزات تیار کرنے والا

englishMeaning: The action of transporting or carrying someone or something from one place to another. A vehicle or means of transport. The legal process of transferring property ownership from one person to another.
synonyms: Transportation, Transport, Transfer, Vehicle, Carriage, Transferral
antonyms: Retention, Holding, Stasis
examples: The conveyance of raw materials across the country takes several days. Horse-drawn carriages were once the primary mode of conveyance. The lawyer prepared the deed of conveyance for the new property owners. They arranged for the conveyance of the patient to a specialized hospital.
sindhiMeaning: منتقلي, سواري, ٽرانسپورٽ, زمين جي منتقليءَ جو دستاويز
urduMeaning: منتقلی, ذرائع نقل و حمل, جائداد کا تحریری انتقال, سواری

englishMeaning: The branch of law concerned with the preparation of documents for the transferring of property. The legal process of transferring property ownership from one person to another.
synonyms: Property transfer, Title transfer, Deed transfer, Legal transfer
antonyms: Retention, Acquisition, Withholding
examples: The lawyer specializes in residential conveyancing. The conveyancing process took longer than expected due to legal delays. Make sure to hire a qualified solicitor for conveyancing. Fees for conveyancing usually vary depending on the property value.
sindhiMeaning: ملڪيت جي منتقلي, سندسازي, قانوني منتقلي جو عمل
urduMeaning: انتقالِ ملکیت, جائیداد کی منتقلی کا قانون, دستاویزاتِ انتقال

englishMeaning: The quality or state of being convex. A convex curve or surface. Bulging or curving outward.
synonyms: Curviness, Curvature, Protuberance, Bulge, Roundedness
antonyms: Concavity, Hollowness, Indentation
examples: The convexity of the lens helps focus the light rays efficiently. Scientists measured the exact degree of convexity on the mirror. The design utilizes subtle convexity to enhance structural strength. Changes in convexity affect how light passes through the glass.
sindhiMeaning: اڀار, ٻاهرئين پاسي اڀار, محدبي
urduMeaning: تحدب, ابھار, باہر کی طرف موڑ

englishMeaning: Having a surface that curves outward like the exterior of a circle or sphere. Bulging or curving outward rather than inward.
synonyms: Curved outward, Rounded, Bulging, Prominent, Raised
antonyms: Concave, Hollow, Depressed, Sunken
examples: A convex mirror provides a wider field of view for drivers. The outer surface of an eyeball is slightly convex. Convex lenses are used in magnifying glasses and cameras. He preferred using a convex mirror to monitor the shop floor.
sindhiMeaning: اڀريل, محدب, ٻاهر نڪتل
urduMeaning: محدب, ابھرا ہوا, باہر کو مڑا ہوا

englishMeaning: Capable of being changed in form, function, or character. A car with a folding or removable roof. A currency or security that can be converted into another form.
synonyms: Changeable, Adaptable, Transformable, Flexible, Exchangeable
antonyms: Inconvertible, Fixed, Rigid, Unchangeable, Permanent
examples: They bought a sporty convertible for their summer road trips. The sofa is convertible into a full-sized bed for guests. Convertible bonds allow investors to change debt into equity. The currency is freely convertible into foreign currencies.
sindhiMeaning: مٽائي سگهجندڙ, تبديل ٿيندڙ, ڇت کليل گاڏي
urduMeaning: قابلِ تبدیل, کھلی چھت والی گاڑی, متبادل

englishMeaning: The quality or state of being convertible. The capability of a currency, asset, or security to be freely exchanged for another currency, asset, or cash without significant loss or legal restrictions.
synonyms: Exchangeability, Interchangeability, Transformability, Negotiability
antonyms: Inconvertibility, Unexchangeability, Rigidity, Permanence
examples: The convertibility of the local currency attracted international investors. Gold was once famous for its easy convertibility into cash. The economic reform program aims to maintain the full convertibility of foreign capital. Limited convertibility can hinder the growth of international trade.
sindhiMeaning: مٽا سٽا جي قابليت, تبديليءَ جي لائق هجڻ, بدلي ٿيڻ جي صلاحيت
urduMeaning: قابلِ تبدیلی ہونا, تحویل پذیری, زر کی تبادلہ پذیری

englishMeaning: To change or transform something into a different form, purpose, or system. To cause someone to change their beliefs, religion, or opinion. A person who has been persuaded to change their religious faith or another belief system.
synonyms: Transform, Alter, Adapt, Proselyte, Neophyte
antonyms: Maintain, Preserve, Keep, Reject, Apostate
examples: They plan to convert the old industrial factory into modern apartments. Solar panels convert sunlight directly into electrical energy. He decided to convert to a new religion after years of spiritual searching. As a recent convert to the cause, she speaks with great enthusiasm.
sindhiMeaning: مٽائڻ, بدلائڻ, مذہب مٽائيندڙ, نو مسلم
urduMeaning: تبدیل کرنا, بدلنا, مذہب تبدیل کرنے والا, نو مسلم

synonyms: Transformer, Adapter, Changer, Inverter
antonyms: Maintainer, Stabilizer
examples: You will need a electrical power converter when traveling abroad with electronic appliances. The media converter changed the signal from fiber optic to standard Ethernet cable. Steelmakers use a specialized converter to refine molten iron into quality steel. A catalytic converter reduces harmful emissions coming from the automobile exhaust.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنورٽر, مٽائيندڙ, تبديل ڪندڙ اوزار
urduMeaning: کنورٹر, تبدیل کرنے والا آلہ, مبدل

englishMeaning: Relating to, acting as, or involving a catalyst. Causing, accelerating, or facilitating an action, change, or event without itself undergoing any permanent chemical change.
synonyms: Accelerating, Stimulating, Motivating, Transformative, Inspiring
antonyms: Inhibiting, Retarding, Blocking, Suppressing, Delaying
examples: The catalytic converter helps lower the amount of toxic gas emitted by automobiles. Her inspiring speeches played a catalytic role in sparking the social reform movement. Complex chemical reactions often rely on catalytic agents to proceed smoothly at lower temperatures. The new investment acted as a catalytic force for local economic development.
sindhiMeaning: اثر انداز ٿيندڙ, تيز ڪندڙ, تبديلي آڻيندڙ, عمل انگیز
urduMeaning: عملِ انگیز, تحریکی, محرک, انگیزی

englishMeaning: The acceleration of a chemical reaction by a catalyst. An increase in the rate of a chemical reaction due to the participation of an additional substance called a catalyst. A process in which a reaction rate is changed by a substance that is not consumed during the reaction.
synonyms: Acceleration, Stimulation, Activation, Facilitation, Reaction speed-up
antonyms: Inhibition, Retardation, Suppression, Delay
examples: Enzymes are protein molecules that perform catalysis in biological systems. Industrial catalysis is essential for the production of synthetic fertilizers. Platinum is widely used for catalysis in automobile exhaust systems. The discovery of a new form of catalysis revolutionized organic chemistry.
sindhiMeaning: عمل انگيزی, تبديلين جي تيزي, ڪيميائي عمل جي رفتار وڌائڻ
urduMeaning: عمل انگیزی, کیمیائی عمل کو تیز کرنا, تحفیظ

englishMeaning: To cause or accelerate a reaction by acting as a catalyst. To precipitate or bring about an event or change. To act as a catalyst in a chemical process.
synonyms: Accelerate, Stimulate, Prompt, Precipitate, Provoke, Spur
antonyms: Inhibit, Hinder, Impede, Delay, Prevent
examples: Enzymes catalyse metabolic reactions inside the human cell. Her passionate speech helped to catalyse a nationwide movement for reform. High temperatures can catalyse the chemical reaction much faster. The government hopes the new tax incentives will catalyse investment.
sindhiMeaning: عمل انگیز ڪرڻ, تيز ڪرڻ, تحريڪ ڏيڻ
urduMeaning: عمل انگیزی کرنا, تیز کرنا, تحریک دینا, آگے بڑھانا

englishMeaning: A secure physical box or online directory where items or files can be deposited or shared. A cloud storage service used for file sharing and synchronization. A receptacle where documents or objects can be dropped for collection.
synonyms: Receptacle, Depository, Drop slot, Mail slot, Cloud storage, File repository
antonyms: Retrieval point, Withdrawal slot
examples: Please place your completed application forms in the drop box outside the office. You can upload the large video file directly to my Dropbox. The library has a drop box for returning books after working hours. Cloud computing makes syncing files across devices via Dropbox very easy.
sindhiMeaning: ڊراپ باڪس, فائيل جمع ڪرڻ جو باڪس, ڪلائوڊ اسٽوريج سروس
urduMeaning: ڈراپ باکس, دستاویزات جمع کرانے کا باکس, آن لائن فائل اسٹوریج

englishMeaning: A graphical user interface element where a list of options appears below an item when clicked. Relating to a menu or list that extends downward on a screen. Designed to fold or hang down when released.
synonyms: Pop-up, Pull-down, Pull-down menu, Collapsible menu
antonyms: Fixed list, Static menu, Permanent list
examples: Select your nationality from the drop-down menu on the registration form. Click on the drop-down arrow to view more options. The website interface features a clean drop-down navigation bar. The drop-down table folds neatly against the wall to save space.
sindhiMeaning: ڊراپ ڊائون مينو, هيٺ لهندڙ لسٽ
urduMeaning: ڈراپ ڈاؤن, نیچے کھلنے والی فہرست, متحرک فہرست

englishMeaning: A casual or unexpected visit. Made or done without a prior appointment or reservation. A facility or center that provides services to people without requiring an appointment.
synonyms: Casual visit, Walk-in, Unannounced visit, Impromptu call
antonyms: Scheduled visit, Appointment, Planned meeting
examples: She made a quick drop-in to say hello to her old friend. The medical clinic operates a drop-in service for minor emergencies. We bought a drop-in sink for the kitchen renovation. Drop-in visitors are always welcome at our community hub.
sindhiMeaning: اڻ سڏيو اچڻ, بنا اڳواٽ اطلاع جي اچڻ, بغير اپائنٽمنٽ جي, ڊراپ-ان

englishMeaning: An argument or set of reasons presented to oppose an idea or theory developed in another argument. A rebuttal intended to refute a previous claim or opinion.
synonyms: Rebuttal, Refutation, Objection, Counterplea, Response
antonyms: Agreement, Confirmation, Endorsement, Supporting argument
examples: The lawyer presented a strong counterargument to refute the claim. Her counterargument highlighted several critical flaws in the proposed plan. It is important to address potential counterarguments in an essay. The opponent failed to offer a convincing counterargument during the debate.
sindhiMeaning: جوابي دليل, مخالف دليل, رد عمل وارو دليل
urduMeaning: جوابی دلیل, مخالف دلیل, ردِ عمل کی دلیل

englishMeaning: An attack made in response to an attack by an opponent. A strategic offensive action launched in reaction to an enemy's advance. To launch an attack against an attacking force.
synonyms: Retaliation, Counteroffensive, Riposte, Counterstrike
antonyms: Retreat, Defense, Surrender, Submission
examples: The army launched a fierce counter-attack to reclaim the lost territory. The chess player mounted a surprising counter-attack on the king side. They were caught off guard by the sudden counter-attack. The troops prepared to counter-attack early the next morning.
sindhiMeaning: جوابي حملو, موٽ ۾ حملو, جوابي وار
urduMeaning: جوابی حملہ, جوابی وار, الٹا حملہ

englishMeaning: A weight that balances another weight. A force or influence that offsets or neutralizes an opposing force or influence. To act against something with equal force or effect.
synonyms: Counterweight, Offset, Counterpoise, Balance, Neutralize
antonyms: Imbalance, Destabilize, Aggravate, Disturb
examples: The crane uses a heavy counterbalance to keep from tipping over. Her calm personality served as a counterbalance to his hot temper. New rules were introduced to counterbalance the monopoly power. Regular exercise acts as a good counterbalance to desk job stress.
sindhiMeaning: توازن قائم ڪرڻ, برابر توازن, موٽ ۾ وزن, پڙو برابر ڪرڻ

englishMeaning: A period of the year when a particular activity, especially sport or tourism, is not taking place or is at a reduced level. It refers to the time when business or recreational activity is at a low ebb.
synonyms: Low season, Quiet period, Downtime, Slack season
antonyms: Peak season, High season, Busy period

sindhiMeaning: مرڻ تائين ڪنهن سان وفادار رهڻ، ڪنهن مقصد جي پيروي زندگيءَ جي آخر تائين ڪرڻ، ميت سان گڏ قبرستان تائين وڃڻ، اهڙي راهه تي هلڻ جيڪا موت ڏانهن وٺي وڃي
urduMeaning: مرتے دم تک کسی کا وفادار رہنا، کسی مقصد کی پیروی زندگی کے آخری لمحے تک کرنا، جنازے کے ساتھ قبرستان تک جانا، ایسی راہ پر چلنا جو موت کی طرف لے جائے

word: Have one foot in the grave
englishMeaning: To be very old or so ill that death seems near. To be close to dying. To be in a very weak or failing condition. Used humorously to say that someone is getting old.
synonyms: At death's door, Dying, Failing, On one's last legs, Near the end, Ailing
antonyms: In the prime of life, Healthy, Thriving, Robust, Full of life, Youthful
examples: He is ninety and has one foot in the grave, yet he still gardens daily. The old man looked as if he had one foot in the grave. Stop teasing me about my age; I do not have one foot in the grave yet. After the illness, she seemed to have one foot in the grave.
sindhiMeaning: موت جي ويجهو هجڻ، ڏاڍو پوڙهو يا سخت بيمار هجڻ، آخري وقت ۾ هجڻ، تمام ڪمزور ۽ بيحال هجڻ، مذاق ۾ ڪنهن کي پوڙهو چوڻ
urduMeaning: موت کے قریب ہونا، نہایت بوڑھا یا سخت بیمار ہونا، آخری وقت میں ہونا، بہت کمزور اور نحیف ہونا، مذاقاً کسی کو بوڑھا کہنا

englishMeaning: To do something that will cause serious trouble or ruin for yourself. To bring about your own downfall through your own actions. To behave in a way that guarantees future failure or punishment. To create the conditions of your own destruction.
synonyms: Bring about one's downfall, Self-destruct, Ruin oneself, Shoot oneself in the foot, Court disaster
antonyms: Save oneself, Protect one's interests, Secure one's position, Prosper, Succeed
examples: By lying to the committee, he dug his own grave. If you keep missing deadlines, you are digging your own grave. The company dug its own grave by ignoring customer complaints. She warned him that arguing with the boss was digging his own grave.
sindhiMeaning: پنهنجي تباهيءَ جو سامان پاڻ ڪرڻ، اهڙو ڪم ڪرڻ جيڪو پنهنجي لاءِ نقصانڪار ثابت ٿئي، پنهنجي هٿن سان پنهنجو نقصان ڪرڻ، پاڻ کي مصيبت ۾ وجهڻ
urduMeaning: اپنی تباہی کا سامان خود کرنا، ایسا کام کرنا جو اپنے ہی لیے نقصان دہ ثابت ہو، اپنے ہاتھوں اپنا نقصان کرنا، خود کو مصیبت میں ڈالنا

word: From the cradle to the grave
englishMeaning: For the whole of a person's life, from birth until death. Covering every stage of life without interruption. Describing care, support, or service provided throughout a lifetime.
synonyms: Lifelong, All one's life, Womb to tomb, Throughout life, Perpetually
antonyms: Temporarily, Briefly, Momentarily, Short-term, For a while
examples: The state promised welfare from the cradle to the grave. He lived in the same village from the cradle to the grave. The scheme offers health cover from the cradle to the grave. Their friendship lasted from the cradle to the grave.
sindhiMeaning: ڄمڻ کان وٺي مرڻ تائين، سڄي زندگيءَ جي عرصي ۾، حياتيءَ جي هر مرحلي تي، پوري عمر جي سنڀال يا سهولت
urduMeaning: پیدائش سے موت تک، ساری زندگی کے دوران، زندگی کے ہر مرحلے پر، پوری عمر کی دیکھ بھال یا سہولت

englishMeaning: Said of a dead person who would be shocked or angry about something happening now. Used to express that an action would deeply offend someone who has died. To indicate strong disapproval by imagining a dead person's reaction.
synonyms: Roll over in one's grave, Be appalled, Be scandalised, Be horrified, Disapprove strongly
antonyms: Rest in peace, Approve, Be pleased, Be satisfied, Rejoice
examples: Their grandfather would turn in his grave if he saw the house today. He would turn in his grave to hear the party abandon its principles. The founder must be turning in his grave over these changes. If she knew how the money was spent, she would turn in her grave.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن مري ويل شخص جو موجوده ڳالهه تي سخت ناراض ٿيڻ جو تصور، اهڙو ڪم جيڪو مرحوم کي ڏاڍو ڏک ڏئي ها، سخت ناپسنديدگي ظاهر ڪرڻ لاءِ چيو ويندڙ محاورو
urduMeaning: کسی مرحوم کا موجودہ بات پر سخت ناراض ہونے کا تصور، ایسا کام جو فوت شدہ شخص کو بہت ناگوار گزرتا، شدید ناپسندیدگی ظاہر کرنے کا محاورہ

englishMeaning: The American form of 'turn in one's grave'. Said of a dead person who would be shocked, upset, or angry at something happening now. Used to show that an action strongly violates the values of someone who has died.
synonyms: Turn in one's grave, Be appalled, Be horrified, Be scandalised, Strongly disapprove
antonyms: Rest in peace, Approve, Be pleased, Be content, Rejoice
examples: My grandmother would roll over in her grave if she heard that language. The old coach would roll over in his grave watching this performance. He is probably rolling over in his grave right now. Selling the family land would make our father roll over in his grave.
sindhiMeaning: محاوري ’ٽرن اِن ونس گريو‘ جو آمريڪي روپ، ڪنهن مرحوم جو موجوده ڳالهه تي ناراض ٿيڻ جو تصور، اهڙو عمل جيڪو مرحوم جي اصولن جي خلاف هجي، سخت ناپسنديدگي جو اظهار
urduMeaning: محاورے ’ٹرن اِن ونس گریو‘ کی امریکی صورت، کسی مرحوم کا موجودہ بات پر ناراض ہونے کا تصور، ایسا عمل جو مرحوم کے اصولوں کے خلاف ہو، شدید ناپسندیدگی کا اظہار

englishMeaning: A sum of money given to someone for a service, in addition to the standard charge. A tip given to a waiter, driver, or other service worker. A payment made to an employee at the end of service or on retirement. A voluntary gift of money as a token of appreciation.
synonyms: Tip, Bonus, Reward, Perquisite, Present, Baksheesh, Honorarium, Recompense
antonyms: Salary, Wage, Fixed charge, Fine, Penalty, Deduction
examples: A ten percent gratuity is included in the final bill. He received a generous gratuity after thirty years of service. Passengers often leave a small gratuity for the driver. The hotel staff are not permitted to ask for a gratuity.
sindhiMeaning: خدمت جي عيوض ڏنل اضافي رقم، ويٽر يا ڊرائيور کي ڏنل انعام يا ٽِپ، نوڪري ختم ٿيڻ يا رٽائرمينٽ تي ملندڙ رقم، شڪرگذاريءَ طور ڏنل رضاڪارانه تحفو، گريجويٽي
urduMeaning: خدمت کے عوض دی جانے والی اضافی رقم، ویٹر یا ڈرائیور کو دیا جانے والا انعام یا ٹِپ، ملازمت ختم ہونے یا ریٹائرمنٹ پر ملنے والی رقم، اظہارِ تشکر کے طور پر دیا گیا رضاکارانہ تحفہ، گریجویٹی

englishMeaning: Without any good reason or justification. In a way that is unnecessary and often offensive. Free of charge, without payment being required. In an uncalled-for or excessive manner.
synonyms: Needlessly, Unnecessarily, Wantonly, Unjustifiably, Freely, Without charge, Uncalled-for
antonyms: Necessarily, Justifiably, Reasonably, Deservedly, For payment, Purposefully
examples: The film was gratuitously violent from beginning to end. He gratuitously insulted a guest who had done nothing wrong. The lawyer offered her advice gratuitously to the poor family. Critics said the scene was gratuitously shocking.
sindhiMeaning: بنا ڪنهن مناسب سبب جي، اجايو ۽ غير ضروري نموني، مفت ۾ يا بنا معاوضي جي، حد کان وڌيڪ ۽ بي مقصد طريقي سان
urduMeaning: بغیر کسی معقول وجہ کے، بلاوجہ اور غیر ضروری طور پر، مفت میں یا بلا معاوضہ، حد سے زیادہ اور بے مقصد انداز میں

englishMeaning: The state of not being thankful for kindness received. A failure to show appreciation for help or favours. Unkind behaviour towards someone who has been generous to you. Lack of gratitude or thanklessness.
synonyms: Thanklessness, Ungratefulness, Unappreciation, Disregard, Selfishness
antonyms: Gratitude, Thankfulness, Appreciation, Recognition, Acknowledgement, Indebtedness
examples: He was hurt by his nephew's ingratitude after years of support. Such ingratitude towards a loyal friend is hard to forgive. The letter accused the committee of sheer ingratitude. She repaid their kindness with ingratitude.
sindhiMeaning: ناشڪري، احسان فراموشي، ڀلائيءَ جو شڪر ادا نه ڪرڻ، ڪنهن جي مدد جي قدر نه ڪرڻ، احسان جو بدلو خرابيءَ سان ڏيڻ
urduMeaning: ناشکری، احسان فراموشی، بھلائی کا شکر ادا نہ کرنا، کسی کی مدد کی قدر نہ کرنا، احسان کا بدلہ برائی سے دینا

englishMeaning: The state of continuing without interruption over a period of time. A logical and consistent connection between the parts of something. The maintenance of consistency in details across scenes of a film or story. An unbroken succession or flow of events.
synonyms: Consistency, Persistence, Flow, Succession, Cohesion, Continuance, Uninterruptedness, Connection
antonyms: Discontinuity, Interruption, Break, Disruption, Inconsistency, Gap, Cessation
examples: The new manager was appointed to ensure continuity of policy. There is little continuity between the first and second chapters. A continuity error was spotted in the final scene of the film. The family business has maintained continuity for four generations.
sindhiMeaning: بنا ڪنهن رڪاوٽ جي جاري رهڻ جي حالت، تسلسل ۽ ربط، ڪنهن شيءِ جي حصن ۾ منطقي ۽ هڪجهڙائي وارو ڳانڍاپو، فلم يا ڪهاڻيءَ ۾ تفصيلن جي هڪجهڙائي، واقعن جو مسلسل سلسلو
urduMeaning: بغیر کسی رکاوٹ کے جاری رہنے کی حالت، تسلسل و ربط، کسی چیز کے حصوں میں منطقی اور یکساں ربط، فلم یا کہانی میں تفصیلات کی یکسانیت، واقعات کا مسلسل سلسلہ

englishMeaning: Kept going without stopping or being interrupted. Resumed after a pause or break. Ongoing and still in progress. Extended further in time, space, or amount.
synonyms: Ongoing, Sustained, Persistent, Uninterrupted, Prolonged, Resumed, Maintained, Steady
antonyms: Stopped, Ended, Discontinued, Halted, Interrupted, Ceased, Abandoned
examples: We are grateful for your continued support during difficult times. The trial continued for another three weeks. The story is continued on page twelve. Continued rainfall has damaged crops across the province.
sindhiMeaning: جاري رهيل، بنا رڪاوٽ هلندڙ، وقفي کان پوءِ ٻيهر شروع ٿيل، اڃا به جاري، وقت يا مقدار ۾ اڳتي وڌايل
urduMeaning: جاری رہنے والا، بغیر رکاوٹ چلنے والا، وقفے کے بعد دوبارہ شروع کیا گیا، تاحال جاری، وقت یا مقدار میں آگے بڑھایا گیا

englishMeaning: To keep doing something without stopping. To begin again after an interruption. To remain in a particular place, state, or condition. To carry on further in a stated direction. To extend or prolong something in time or space.
synonyms: Carry on, Proceed, Persist, Resume, Endure, Maintain, Keep on, Prolong, Last
antonyms: Stop, Cease, Quit, Discontinue, Halt, Abandon, Finish, Pause, End
examples: Please continue with your work while I make a call. The meeting will continue after a short break. She continued as chairperson for another two years. The road continues for another ten kilometres.
sindhiMeaning: ڪم کي بنا رڪاوٽ جاري رکڻ، وقفي کان پوءِ وري شروع ڪرڻ، ڪنهن حالت يا جاءِ تي برقرار رهڻ، ڪنهن طرف اڳتي وڌندو رهڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي وڌائڻ يا ڊگهو ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: کام کو بغیر رکاوٹ جاری رکھنا، وقفے کے بعد دوبارہ شروع کرنا، کسی حالت یا جگہ پر برقرار رہنا، کسی سمت میں آگے بڑھتے رہنا، کسی چیز کو بڑھانا یا طول دینا

englishMeaning: The action of carrying something on without stopping. A part that follows and extends something already begun. The act of resuming after a break. Something added that makes a work or process longer.
synonyms: Extension, Prolongation, Resumption, Sequel, Persistence, Maintenance, Carrying on
antonyms: Cessation, End, Termination, Discontinuation, Stoppage, Interruption, Conclusion
examples: The novel is a continuation of the author's earlier work. They voted for the continuation of the aid programme. This meeting is a continuation of yesterday's discussion. The path is a continuation of the old railway line.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڪم کي جاري رکڻ جو عمل، اڳ شروع ٿيل شيءِ جو اڳتي وڌايل حصو، وقفي کان پوءِ ٻيهر شروع ڪرڻ، تسلسل يا اضافو
urduMeaning: کسی کام کو جاری رکھنے کا عمل، پہلے سے شروع شدہ چیز کا آگے بڑھایا ہوا حصہ، وقفے کے بعد دوبارہ آغاز، تسلسل یا اضافہ

englishMeaning: A speech sound that can be held for as long as the breath lasts, such as a fricative or nasal. Relating to a sound produced with an incomplete closure of the vocal tract. Something that continues or persists.
synonyms: Fricative, Sustained sound, Persistent, Enduring, Ongoing
antonyms: Stop, Plosive, Occlusive, Momentary, Transient
examples: The sound of 's' is a continuant in English phonetics. Students learned to distinguish continuants from stops. Nasal consonants are treated as continuants in this analysis. The teacher gave 'f' and 'v' as examples of continuant sounds.
sindhiMeaning: اهڙو آواز جيڪو ساهه هلڻ تائين جاري رکي سگهجي، اهڙو صوتي آواز جنهن ۾ وات مڪمل بند نه ٿئي، جاري رهندڙ يا برقرار رهندڙ شيءِ، لسانيات ۾ مسلسل آواز
urduMeaning: ایسی آواز جو سانس رہنے تک جاری رکھی جا سکے، ایسی صوتی آواز جس میں منہ مکمل طور پر بند نہ ہو، جاری رہنے والی یا برقرار رہنے والی چیز، لسانیات میں مسلسل آواز

englishMeaning: Repeatedly and frequently, with short breaks in between. Again and again over a long period. In a way that happens very often and seems never to end.
synonyms: Repeatedly, Frequently, Regularly, Persistently, Time and again, Recurrently, Often
antonyms: Rarely, Seldom, Occasionally, Never, Once, Infrequently
examples: He was continually interrupting the speaker with questions. The machine continually breaks down and needs repair. Prices have risen continually over the past decade. She continually reminded us about the deadline.
sindhiMeaning: بار بار ۽ وري وري، ننڍن وقفن سان مسلسل، گهڻي وقت تائين هر هر ٿيندڙ، اڪثر ۽ لڳاتار
urduMeaning: بار بار اور مسلسل، مختصر وقفوں کے ساتھ لگاتار، طویل عرصے تک بار بار ہونے والا، اکثر و بیشتر

englishMeaning: Happening repeatedly with short breaks in between. Frequent and recurring over a period of time. Constant enough to be annoying or noticeable.
synonyms: Repeated, Frequent, Recurrent, Persistent, Regular, Habitual, Incessant
antonyms: Occasional, Rare, Infrequent, Sporadic, Intermittent, Momentary
examples: His continual complaints annoyed the whole office. Continual power cuts have disrupted business in the city. She suffered continual pain in her left knee. The continual noise from the street made sleep impossible.
sindhiMeaning: بار بار ٿيندڙ، ننڍن وقفن سان لڳاتار، ڊگهي عرصي تائين ورجندڙ، مسلسل ۽ ڪوفت ڏيندڙ
urduMeaning: بار بار ہونے والا، مختصر وقفوں کے ساتھ لگاتار، طویل عرصے تک دہرایا جانے والا، مسلسل اور کوفت آمیز

englishMeaning: The state of continuing to exist or operate. The length of time something lasts. A postponement or adjournment of a court case to a later date. The act of remaining in a particular office or condition.
synonyms: Continuation, Persistence, Duration, Endurance, Maintenance, Postponement, Adjournment
antonyms: Termination, End, Cessation, Discontinuance, Stoppage, Conclusion
examples: The continuance of the project depends on further funding. The judge granted a continuance until the following month. They prayed for the continuance of peace in the region. His continuance in office surprised many observers.
sindhiMeaning: جاري رهڻ يا قائم رهڻ جي حالت، ڪنهن شيءِ جي مدت يا عرصو، عدالتي ڪيس جي ٻي تاريخ تي ملتوي ٿيڻ، ڪنهن عهدي يا حالت ۾ برقرار رهڻ
urduMeaning: جاری رہنے یا قائم رہنے کی حالت، کسی چیز کی مدت یا دورانیہ، عدالتی مقدمے کا آئندہ تاریخ تک ملتوی ہونا، کسی عہدے یا حالت میں برقرار رہنا

englishMeaning: In a way that depends on something else happening. Only if certain conditions are met. By chance rather than by necessity. In a manner that is possible but not certain.
synonyms: Conditionally, Dependently, Provisionally, Incidentally, Accidentally, Tentatively
antonyms: Absolutely, Unconditionally, Certainly, Necessarily, Definitely, Independently
examples: The bonus will be paid contingently on meeting the sales target. Funding was approved contingently upon the committee's final review. Events that occur contingently cannot be predicted with certainty. The agreement applies contingently, depending on the outcome of the vote.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ٻي ڳالهه تي دارومدار رکندي، صرف تڏهن جڏهن ڪي شرط پوريون ٿين، اتفاقي طور تي نه ڪي لازمي طور، ممڪن پر يقيني نه هجڻ واري انداز ۾
urduMeaning: کسی دوسری بات پر انحصار کرتے ہوئے، صرف اسی صورت میں جب شرائط پوری ہوں، اتفاقی طور پر نہ کہ لازمی طور پر، ممکنہ مگر غیر یقینی انداز میں

englishMeaning: Going on without any interruption or break. Forming an unbroken whole in space or time. Steady and uninterrupted in flow or extent. (Grammar) Describing a verb form that shows an action in progress.
synonyms: Constant, Unbroken, Uninterrupted, Nonstop, Steady, Perpetual, Endless, Unceasing
antonyms: Intermittent, Broken, Interrupted, Sporadic, Occasional, Irregular, Discontinuous
examples: The machine produces a continuous stream of plastic sheets. We heard a continuous humming from the generator. She has been in continuous employment since 2015. The present continuous tense describes actions happening now.
sindhiMeaning: بنا ڪنهن رڪاوٽ جي مسلسل هلندڙ، وقت يا جاءِ ۾ اڻ ٽٽل، لڳاتار ۽ هڪجهڙو، گرامر ۾ جاري فعل ظاهر ڪندڙ صورت
urduMeaning: بغیر کسی وقفے کے مسلسل جاری، وقت یا جگہ میں غیر منقطع، لگاتار اور یکساں، گرامر میں جاری فعل ظاہر کرنے والی صورت

englishMeaning: A bass part that runs throughout a piece of Baroque music, providing harmonic support. The instruments, usually a keyboard and a bass instrument, that play this part. Short for basso continuo, the continuous accompaniment in early music.
synonyms: Basso continuo, Thoroughbass, Figured bass, Accompaniment, Bass line
antonyms: Melody, Solo line, Treble part, Silence
examples: The harpsichord played the continuo throughout the concerto. A cello and organ provided the continuo for the choir. Baroque composers relied heavily on the continuo. She studied continuo playing at the conservatory.
sindhiMeaning: بيروڪ موسيقيءَ ۾ سڄي ٽڪري دوران هلندڙ بيس حصو، هارمونڪ سهارو ڏيندڙ مسلسل سنگت، اهي ساز جيڪي اهو حصو وڄائين، ’باسو ڪنٽينيو‘ جو مختصر نالو
urduMeaning: بیروک موسیقی میں پورے ٹکڑے کے دوران جاری رہنے والا بیس حصہ، ہم آہنگی فراہم کرنے والی مسلسل سنگت، وہ ساز جو یہ حصہ بجاتے ہیں، ’باسو کونٹینوو‘ کا مختصر نام

englishMeaning: Holding official qualifications or certificates for a particular role. Formally recognised as qualified by an authority. Provided with documents proving identity, status, or ability.
synonyms: Qualified, Certified, Licensed, Accredited, Authorised, Chartered, Recognised
antonyms: Unqualified, Uncertified, Unlicensed, Unaccredited, Amateur, Untrained
examples: Only credentialed teachers may apply for this position. The hospital employs fully credentialed nursing staff. She is a credentialed translator with fifteen years of experience. Credentialed journalists were allowed inside the hall.
sindhiMeaning: سرڪاري سند يا اهليت رکندڙ، ڪنهن اداري پاران باقاعده تسليم ٿيل، شناخت يا قابليت جا دستاويز رکندڙ، مستند
urduMeaning: سرکاری سند یا اہلیت رکھنے والا، کسی ادارے کی جانب سے باقاعدہ تسلیم شدہ، شناخت یا قابلیت کی دستاویز رکھنے والا، مستند

englishMeaning: A word or phrase formed by rearranging the letters of another word or phrase. A word puzzle based on rearranging letters. The result of shuffling letters to create a new meaningful word.

englishMeaning: Feeling very sad, hopeless, and without energy. Suffering from clinical depression as a medical condition. Suffering from poor economic conditions, as of an area or industry. Pushed down or lower than the surrounding surface.
synonyms: Sad, Downcast, Dejected, Miserable, Gloomy, Despondent, Low, Unhappy, Sunken, Downturned
antonyms: Happy, Cheerful, Elated, Joyful, Content, Optimistic, Prosperous, Raised, Buoyant, Upbeat
examples: He felt depressed after losing his job. She is being treated for depressed mood and anxiety. The factory closed in an economically depressed area. The depressed centre of the lid holds the seal.
sindhiMeaning: اداس ۽ مايوس، همت ۽ توانائيءَ کان خالي، طبي لحاظ کان ڊپريشن جو مريض، معاشي طور پسمانده يا ڪمزور علائقو، ڀرپاسي کان هيٺ دٻيل مٿاڇرو
urduMeaning: اداس اور مایوس، ہمت اور توانائی سے محروم، طبی اعتبار سے ڈپریشن کا مریض، معاشی طور پر پسماندہ علاقہ یا صنعت، ارد گرد سے نیچے دبی ہوئی سطح

englishMeaning: An act of attacking and robbing, causing damage or loss. Plundering or destruction carried out by armed groups. Gradual damage caused by a harmful force, often used in the plural. Serious harm done to property, land, or the environment.
synonyms: Plunder, Looting, Pillage, Ravage, Destruction, Raid, Devastation, Robbery, Damage, Spoliation
antonyms: Protection, Preservation, Conservation, Restoration, Care, Safeguarding, Repair, Defence, Maintenance, Enrichment
examples: The village suffered years of depredation by raiders. Farmers complained about the depredations of wild boar. The depredation of forests continues at an alarming rate. Historians recorded the depredations of the invading army.
sindhiMeaning: ڦرلٽ ۽ تباهيءَ جو عمل، حملو ڪري نقصان يا لٽ ڪرڻ، هٿياربندن پاران ڪيل ڦرمار ۽ ويرانگي، ڪنهن نقصانڪار قوت جو آهستي آهستي ڪيل نقصان، زمين ملڪيت يا ماحول کي پهچايل سخت نقصان

englishMeaning: A fall in the value of something over time. The reduction in the worth of an asset due to age, wear, or use. A decrease in the value of one currency against another. The act of belittling or speaking of something with little respect.
synonyms: Devaluation, Decline, Reduction, Loss of value, Markdown, Fall, Wear, Diminution, Belittlement, Disparagement
antonyms: Appreciation, Increase, Growth, Revaluation, Rise, Gain, Enhancement, Praise, Esteem, Improvement
examples: The car loses value through depreciation every year. Accountants recorded the depreciation of the machinery. The depreciation of the rupee raised import costs. He spoke with clear depreciation of their efforts.
sindhiMeaning: قدر ۾ گهٽتائي، وقت گذرڻ سان ڪنهن شيءِ جي ملهه جو گهٽجڻ، استعمال يا پراڻي ٿيڻ سبب اثاثي جي قيمت جو گهٽجڻ، هڪ ڪرنسيءَ جي قدر ٻيءَ جي مقابلي ۾ گهٽجڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي گهٽ ڀانئڻ يا ان جي بي عزتي ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: قدر میں کمی، وقت کے ساتھ کسی چیز کی قیمت کا گھٹنا، استعمال یا پرانا ہونے کے سبب اثاثے کی مالیت میں کمی، ایک کرنسی کی قدر کا دوسری کے مقابلے میں گرنا، کسی چیز کو کم اہمیت دینا یا اس کی تحقیر کرنا

englishMeaning: Recognition and enjoyment of the good qualities of someone or something. A feeling of gratitude or thankfulness. A full understanding of a situation or problem. An increase in the value of an asset or currency. A written review or assessment of a person's work.

antonyms: Ingratitude, Depreciation, Contempt, Disregard, Criticism, Indifference, Scorn, Neglect, Devaluation, Disdain
examples: She expressed her appreciation for their kind help. He has a deep appreciation of classical music. There is little appreciation of the difficulties involved. Property in this area has seen strong appreciation.
sindhiMeaning: ساراهه ۽ قدرداني، ڪنهن جي سٺين خوبين کي مڃڻ ۽ ان مان لطف وٺڻ، شڪرگذاريءَ جو احساس، ڪنهن معاملي جي مڪمل سمجهه، ڪنهن اثاثي يا ڪرنسيءَ جي قدر ۾ واڌارو، ڪنهن جي ڪم بابت لکيل جائزو
urduMeaning: قدر دانی اور سراہنا، کسی کی خوبیوں کو تسلیم کرنا اور ان سے لطف اٹھانا، شکرگزاری کا احساس، کسی معاملے کی مکمل سمجھ، کسی اثاثے یا کرنسی کی قدر میں اضافہ، کسی کے کام کے بارے میں لکھا گیا جائزہ

englishMeaning: Morally corrupt and wicked. Showing complete disregard for accepted standards of decency. Perverted in character or behaviour. Describing an act of extreme cruelty or immorality.
synonyms: Corrupt, Immoral, Wicked, Vile, Debauched, Perverted, Degenerate, Sinful, Evil, Dissolute
antonyms: Virtuous, Moral, Upright, Pure, Honourable, Decent, Righteous, Wholesome, Good, Innocent

sindhiMeaning: اخلاقي طور بگڙيل ۽ بڇڙو، شرافت جي معيارن کي بلڪل نظرانداز ڪندڙ، بگڙيل ڪردار يا رويي وارو، انتهائي ظلم يا بداخلاقيءَ وارو ڪم
urduMeaning: اخلاقی طور پر بگڑا ہوا اور بدکردار، شرافت کے معیارات کو یکسر نظرانداز کرنے والا، بگڑے کردار یا رویے والا، انتہائی ظالمانہ یا بداخلاق فعل

englishMeaning: The quality of having good judgement based on knowledge and experience. Deep understanding of what is true, right, or lasting. Accumulated learning and knowledge of a society or tradition. The soundness or sensibleness of an action or decision.
synonyms: Insight, Sagacity, Prudence, Judgement, Understanding, Knowledge, Discernment, Sense, Intelligence, Enlightenment
antonyms: Folly, Stupidity, Foolishness, Ignorance, Naivety, Recklessness, Absurdity, Imprudence, Silliness, Inexperience
examples: With age came patience and wisdom. He questioned the wisdom of selling the land now. The book collects the wisdom of village elders. She showed great wisdom in handling the dispute.
sindhiMeaning: عقل ۽ دانائي، علم ۽ تجربي جي بنياد تي صحيح فيصلو ڪرڻ جي صلاحيت، سچ ۽ صحيح ڳالهه جي گهري سمجهه، ڪنهن سماج يا روايت جو گڏ ٿيل علم، ڪنهن فيصلي جي درستگي ۽ معقوليت
urduMeaning: عقل و دانش، علم اور تجربے کی بنیاد پر درست فیصلہ کرنے کی صلاحیت، سچائی اور درستی کی گہری سمجھ، کسی معاشرے یا روایت کا جمع شدہ علم، کسی فیصلے کی درستی اور معقولیت

englishMeaning: Measuring a large distance from one side to the other. Covering a large area or range. Including a great variety of things or people. Fully open, as of eyes. Missing the target, especially in sport.
synonyms: Broad, Extensive, Vast, Spacious, Ample, Expansive, Roomy, Comprehensive, Far-reaching, Open
antonyms: Narrow, Thin, Restricted, Limited, Confined, Tight, Cramped, Small, Slim, Closed
examples: The river is very wide at this point. The store offers a wide range of products. Her eyes were wide with surprise. The shot went wide of the goal.
sindhiMeaning: ويڪرو، هڪ پاسي کان ٻئي پاسي تائين گهڻي وٿي وارو، وڏي علائقي يا دائري تي پکڙيل، گهڻي قسم جي شين يا ماڻهن کي شامل ڪندڙ، اکين جو پوريءَ ريت کليل هجڻ، نشاني کان ٻاهر لڳندڙ
urduMeaning: چوڑا، ایک طرف سے دوسری طرف تک زیادہ فاصلے والا، وسیع علاقے یا دائرے پر پھیلا ہوا، مختلف اقسام کی چیزوں یا لوگوں کو شامل کرنے والا، آنکھوں کا پوری طرح کھلا ہونا، نشانے سے باہر جانے والا

englishMeaning: Over a large area or among many people. To a great extent or degree. In many different places or by many different groups. With a large space between two points.
synonyms: Extensively, Broadly, Generally, Universally, Commonly, Greatly, Far and wide, Comprehensively, Popularly, Substantially
antonyms: Narrowly, Locally, Rarely, Slightly, Sparsely, Limitedly, Barely, Closely, Seldom, Minimally

sindhiMeaning: وڏي پيماني تي، گهڻن ماڻهن ۾ يا وڏي علائقي ۾، تمام گهڻي حد تائين، مختلف هنڌن يا گروهن ۾، ٻن نقطن جي وچ ۾ گهڻي وٿي سان
urduMeaning: وسیع پیمانے پر، بہت سے لوگوں میں یا بڑے علاقے میں، بہت زیادہ حد تک، مختلف جگہوں یا گروہوں میں، دو نقطوں کے درمیان زیادہ فاصلے کے ساتھ

antonyms: Innovation, Novelty, Modernity, Change, Departure, Break, Fashion, Newness, Unconventionality, Reform
examples: It is a family tradition to gather every Eid. The village has a long tradition of handicrafts. He was trained in the classical musical tradition. Many old traditions are slowly disappearing.
sindhiMeaning: روايت، نسل در نسل هلندڙ عقيدو رواج يا طريقو، ڊگهي عرصي کان رسمن ۽ عقيدن جو منتقل ٿيڻ، ڪنهن خاندان گروهه يا سماج ۾ جڙيل پراڻو رواج، فني مذهبي يا فڪري سلسلو جيڪو جاري رهي
urduMeaning: روایت، نسل در نسل چلا آنے والا عقیدہ رسم یا طریقہ، طویل عرصے سے رسوم و عقائد کا منتقل ہونا، کسی خاندان گروہ یا معاشرے میں قائم پرانا رواج، فنی مذہبی یا فکری سلسلہ جو جاری رہے

englishMeaning: Based on long-established customs or beliefs. Following the older, usual way of doing things. Handed down from earlier generations. Conservative in style, method, or outlook.

antonyms: Modern, Contemporary, Innovative, Unconventional, New, Progressive, Radical, Original, Untraditional, Trendy

sindhiMeaning: روايتي، پراڻن رسمن ۽ عقيدن تي ٻڌل، عام ۽ پراڻي طريقي مطابق، اڳين نسلن کان ملندڙ، انداز يا سوچ ۾ قدامت پسند
urduMeaning: روایتی، پرانی رسوم اور عقائد پر مبنی، عام اور قدیم طریقے کے مطابق، پچھلی نسلوں سے منتقل شدہ، انداز یا سوچ میں قدامت پسند

englishMeaning: According to long-established custom or practice. In the way that has been usual for a long time. As has been done by earlier generations. Historically or conventionally speaking.

antonyms: Unconventionally, Innovatively, Newly, Modernly, Radically, Untypically, Currently, Differently, Progressively, Rarely

sindhiMeaning: روايت مطابق، پراڻي رواج ۽ دستور موجب  جيئن گهڻي وقت کان ٿيندو پيو اچي، اڳين نسلن جي طريقي مطابق، تاريخي يا عام مروج انداز ۾

englishMeaning: A group of words taken from a text or speech and repeated by someone else. The act of quoting someone's words. A formal statement of the price at which work will be done or goods supplied. The current price of a share or commodity on a market.

antonyms: Original text, Paraphrase, Summary, Misquotation, Invention, Silence, Payment, Final bill, Guesswork, Omission

sindhiMeaning: اقتباس، ڪنهن ٻئي جي لکڻي يا تقرير مان ورتل جملا، ڪنهن جي چيل ڳالهه ورجائڻ جو عمل، ڪم يا سامان جي قيمت جو رسمي اندازو، بازار ۾ حصص يا شيءِ جي موجوده قيمت
urduMeaning: اقتباس، کسی تحریر یا تقریر سے لیے گئے الفاظ جو کوئی اور دہرائے، کسی کی بات نقل کرنے کا عمل، کام یا سامان کی قیمت کا رسمی تخمینہ، بازار میں حصص یا جنس کی موجودہ قیمت

englishMeaning: To repeat words that someone else has written or said. To mention something as an example or as proof. To state a price for goods or work. A phrase taken from a text or speech. A stated price or estimate.

sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ٻئي جا چيل يا لکيل لفظ ورجائڻ، مثال يا ثبوت طور ڪا ڳالهه پيش ڪرڻ، سامان يا ڪم جي قيمت ٻڌائڻ، ڪنهن لکڻيءَ مان ورتل جملو، ٻڌايل قيمت يا اندازو

urduMeaning: تبادلے کے قابل، کسی دوسری چیز سے بدلا جا سکنے والا، تجارت یا واپسی کے لائق، دوسری صورت یا کرنسی میں تبدیل ہو سکنے والا، مساوی چیز سے بدلا جا سکنے والا

sindhiMeaning: مال يا سامان، وڪري لاءِ تيار ڪيل شيون، واپاري مال جيڪو ريل يا روڊ ذريعي کڻجي، ذاتي ملڪيت يا سامان، غير رسمي طور تي معياري شيءِ يا گهربل ثبوت

englishMeaning: To attach or fasten one thing to another. To add a signature, stamp, or seal to a document. A letter or group of letters added to the beginning or end of a word. In grammar, a prefix or suffix that changes a word's meaning.

sindhiMeaning: پيچيدگي، ڪيترن ئي ڳنڍيل حصن سان جڙيل هجڻ جي حالت، اهڙي خاصيت جيڪا ڪنهن ڳالهه کي سمجهڻ ڏکيو بڻائي، ڪنهن نظام يا مسئلي جي اُلجهڻ جو درجو، ڪمپيوٽنگ ۾ ڪنهن الگورٿم لاءِ گهربل وسيلن جي ماپ
urduMeaning: پیچیدگی، کئی باہم جڑے حصوں سے بنا ہونے کی حالت، ایسی خصوصیت جو کسی چیز کو سمجھنا مشکل بنا دے، کسی نظام یا مسئلے کی الجھن کا درجہ، کمپیوٹنگ میں کسی الگورتھم کے لیے درکار وسائل کی پیمائش
