antonyms: Possess, Own, Be owed, Have no debt, Be free of obligation
examples: I owe you twenty dollars from last week. She owes her success to hard work and determination. We owe our parents gratitude for their sacrifices. He owes an apology for his rude behavior.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي پئسا ادا ڪرڻ يا واپس ڪرڻ جي ذميواري هيٺ هجڻ، ڪنهن کي ڪجهه ڏيڻ جو فرض هجڻ، خاص ڪري شڪرگذاري يا احترام، ڪنهن خاص سبب يا سبب جي ڪري ڪا شيءِ رکڻ، ڪنهن کي مدد، مهرباني، يا حاصل ڪيل احسانن لاءِ قرضدار هجڻ
urduMeaning: کسی کو پیسے ادا کرنے یا واپس کرنے کی ذمہ داری کے تحت ہونا، کسی کو کچھ دینے کا فرض ہونا، خاص طور پر شکر گزاری یا احترام، کسی خاص وجہ یا سبب کی وجہ سے کوئی چیز رکھنا، کسی کا مدد، مہربانی، یا حاصل شدہ احسانات کے لیے مقروض ہونا

englishMeaning: In a manner resembling an owl, especially looking solemn, wise, or observant. With a serious or studious appearance. In a way that suggests wisdom or thoughtfulness. Looking at something with wide, unblinking eyes like an owl.
synonyms: Wisely, Solemnly, Seriously, Studiously, Thoughtfully, Gravely, Observantly
antonyms: Carelessly, Frivolously, Casually, Inattentively, Thoughtlessly
examples: The professor peered owlishly through his thick glasses. She blinked owlishly at the bright light. He stared owlishly at the complex equation. The child looked owlishly serious while listening to the story.
sindhiMeaning: اُلو وانگر طريقي سان، خاص ڪري سنجيده، عقلمند، يا مشاهدو ڏسڻ، سنجيده يا مطالعي واري ظاهر سان، اهڙي طريقي سان جيڪو ڏاهپ يا سوچ جو اشارو ڏئي، ڪنهن شيءِ کي اُلو وانگر وسيع، اڻ جھپڪندڙ اکين سان ڏسڻ
urduMeaning: الو کی طرح طریقے سے، خاص طور پر سنجیدہ، عقلمند، یا مشاہدہ کرنے والے نظر آنا، سنجیدہ یا تعلیمی ظاہری شکل کے ساتھ، ایسے طریقے سے جو دانشمندی یا سوچ کا اشارہ دے، کسی چیز کو الو کی طرح چوڑی، غیر جھپکتی آنکھوں سے دیکھنا

englishMeaning: A person who owns something, having legal possession and rights. Someone who has purchased or acquired property, goods, or assets. A person with legal title to something. The proprietor of a business or establishment.
synonyms: Proprietor, Possessor, Holder, Master, Landlord, Keeper, Holder, Title holder
antonyms: Renter, Tenant, Lessee, Borrower, User, Non-owner
examples: The owner of the restaurant greeted us warmly. She is the proud owner of a new car. The property owner refused to sell the land. Business owners must pay annual taxes.
sindhiMeaning: اهڙو ماڻهو جيڪو ڪنهن شيءِ جو مالڪ آهي، قانوني قبضو ۽ حق رکي ٿو، ڪو به جنهن ملڪيت، سامان، يا اثاثا خريد ڪيا يا حاصل ڪيا آهن، اهڙو ماڻهو جنهن کي ڪنهن شيءِ جو قانوني لقب آهي، ڪاروبار يا اداري جو مالڪ
urduMeaning: ایسا شخص جو کسی چیز کا مالک ہو، قانونی قبضہ اور حقوق رکھتا ہو، کوئی بھی جس نے جائیداد، سامان، یا اثاثے خریدے یا حاصل کیے ہوں، ایسا شخص جس کے پاس کسی چیز کا قانونی عنوان ہو، کاروبار یا ادارے کا مالک

englishMeaning: Having legal possession of something. The act of possessing or having something as property. Acknowledging or admitting something, especially a mistake or fault. Taking responsibility for one's actions or words.
synonyms: Possessing, Having, Holding, Acknowledging, Admitting, Confessing, Accepting, Claiming
antonyms: Lacking, Denying, Rejecting, Disowning, Renouncing, Disclaiming, Renting
examples: Owning a home is a major financial commitment. He is finally owning up to his mistakes. Owning your decisions builds character and integrity. She takes pride in owning her own business.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ جو قانوني قبضو رکڻ، ملڪيت جي طور تي ڪا شيءِ رکڻ يا رکڻ جو عمل، ڪنهن شيءِ کي تسليم ڪرڻ يا قبول ڪرڻ، خاص ڪري غلطي يا غلطي، پنهنجي عملن يا لفظن جي ذميواري کڻڻ
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کا قانونی قبضہ رکھنا، ملکیت کے طور پر کوئی چیز رکھنے یا رکھنے کا عمل، کسی چیز کو تسلیم کرنا یا قبول کرنا، خاص طور پر غلطی یا قصور، اپنے اعمال یا الفاظ کی ذمہ داری لینا

englishMeaning: Done with or employing great care and thoroughness. Characterized by careful and diligent effort. Taking great pains or showing careful attention to detail. Requiring or showing meticulous effort.

antonyms: Careless, Sloppy, Hasty, Negligent, Cursory, Superficial, Reckless

sindhiMeaning: وڏي خيال ۽ مڪمليت سان ڪيل يا استعمال ڪيل، محتاط ۽ محنتي ڪوشش سان منسوب، وڏي تڪليف کڻڻ يا تفصيل ڏانهن محتاط توجهه ڏيکاريندڙ، نفيس ڪوشش جي ضرورت يا ڏيکاريندڙ

englishMeaning: In a pale manner; with little colour or brightness. Faintly or weakly, especially of light. In a way that lacks strength, intensity, or conviction.

antonyms: Brightly, Strongly, Vividly, Intensely, Boldly

antonyms: Neontology, Modern biology, Futurism, Contemporary zoology, Living species studies

synonyms: Spell, Chant, Charm, Invocation, Conjuration, Mantra, Formula, Recitation, Enchantment, Litany
antonyms: Silence, Prose, Plain speech, Disenchantment, Rebuttal, Reality, Fact, Statement, Prayerlessness, Stillness
examples: The priest murmured an incantation over the burning herbs. Old stories describe an incantation that could summon rain. Her speech became an incantation of familiar slogans. He repeated the incantation three times before dawn.
sindhiMeaning: جادوئي منتر، ٽوڻو يا ڦيڻو، جادوءَ لاءِ پڙهيل لفظ، عبادت يا رسم ۾ ورجايل ڪلمات، بار بار ورجايل بي معنيٰ لفظ
urduMeaning: جادوئی منتر، ٹونا یا افسوں، جادو کے لیے پڑھے جانے والے الفاظ، رسم میں دہرائے جانے والے کلمات، بار بار دہرائے گئے بے معنی الفاظ

englishMeaning: A proverb meaning that not knowing about a problem can keep a person happy. The idea that knowledge of unpleasant facts brings worry, so it is sometimes better not to know. A remark used when someone is untroubled only because they are unaware of the truth.
synonyms: Blissful ignorance, What you don't know can't hurt you, Blind contentment, Willful blindness, Innocence, Unawareness, Naivety, Oblivion, Carefree ignorance, Untroubled unawareness
antonyms: Knowledge is power, Forewarned is forearmed, Awareness, Enlightenment, Insight, Vigilance, Understanding, Disillusionment, Realization, Informedness
examples: He never reads the news because for him ignorance is bliss. She smiled and said ignorance is bliss when asked about the results. Sometimes ignorance is bliss, but not when your health is at stake. They kept the bad news from him, believing ignorance is bliss.
sindhiMeaning: چوڻي ته اڻڄاڻائي ۾ ئي سک آهي، حقيقت جي خبر نه هجڻ ۾ آرام آهي، ڄاڻ ڪڏهن ڪڏهن پريشاني آڻيندي آهي، بي خبر ماڻهو گهڻو ڀيرو خوش رهندو آهي، اڻڄاڻائي جو سُکُ
urduMeaning: کہاوت کہ لاعلمی میں ہی راحت ہے، حقیقت سے بے خبری میں سکون ہے، علم بعض اوقات پریشانی لاتا ہے، بے خبر شخص اکثر خوش رہتا ہے، جہالت کی راحت

englishMeaning: Perfect happiness and great joy. A state of deep peace and contentment. Spiritual joy or heavenly happiness. To experience or cause a feeling of pure delight.

antonyms: Misery, Sorrow, Agony, Despair, Grief, Unhappiness, Torment, Distress, Suffering, Anguish
examples: Their first year together was pure bliss. He closed his eyes in bliss as the music began. A quiet Sunday morning at home is my idea of bliss. The poem describes the bliss of the faithful in paradise.
sindhiMeaning: مڪمل خوشي ۽ سُکَ، دلي سڪون ۽ اطمينان، روحاني مسرت، جنت جهڙي راحت، انتهائي خوشيءَ جي ڪيفيت

englishMeaning: In disagreement or conflict with someone. Not matching or consistent with something else. In a state of dispute or opposition.
synonyms: In conflict, In disagreement, At variance, Opposed, Clashing, Quarrelling, Inconsistent, Discordant, Divided, Contradictory
antonyms: In agreement, In harmony, United, Consistent, Compatible, Reconciled, Aligned, Agreeing, At peace, Matching
examples: The two ministers have been at odds for months. His statement is at odds with the official report. She found herself at odds with her own family over the sale. The colours of the room are at odds with the furniture.
sindhiMeaning: اختلاف ۾ هجڻ، ڪنهن سان جهيڙو يا تڪرار هجڻ، هڪ ٻئي سان ٺهڪندڙ نه هجڻ، مخالفت ۾ هجڻ، ڳالهه جو نه ملڻ

englishMeaning: A small spot of light on a radar or electronic screen. A short high-pitched electronic sound. A brief and usually unimportant change or interruption in a trend. A minor problem that does not last long.
synonyms: Spot, Dot, Signal, Beep, Glitch, Hiccup, Anomaly, Fluctuation, Setback, Irregularity
antonyms: Trend, Pattern, Constancy, Continuity, Stability, Norm, Certainty, Permanence, Silence, Regularity
examples: A faint blip appeared on the radar screen. The machine gave a soft blip every few seconds. Last month's fall in sales was only a blip. Officials described the delay as a temporary blip in the schedule.
sindhiMeaning: ريڊار جي اسڪرين تي ننڍڙو نقطو، ٿوري دير جو تکو آواز، ڪنهن رجحان ۾ عارضي تبديلي، معمولي ۽ عارضي رڪاوٽ، ننڍڙو مسئلو

englishMeaning: Opening and closing the eyes quickly. Flashing on and off, as a light does. Used in informal British English as a mild word to express annoyance. Extremely, used for emphasis in informal speech.

examples: He sat blinking in the bright sunlight. A blinking red light warned us of the fault. Where is that blinking key I left here? The blinking cursor waited on the empty screen.
sindhiMeaning: اکيون ڇنڀڻ، ٽمڪندڙ روشني، بار بار ٻرڻ ۽ وسامڻ، برطانوي عام ٻوليءَ ۾ ٿوري ڪاوڙ ظاهر ڪرڻ لاءِ لفظ، زور ڏيڻ لاءِ استعمال ٿيندڙ لفظ

englishMeaning: A thin pancake, usually filled with cheese or fruit, then folded and fried. A traditional dish of Jewish and Eastern European cuisine.
synonyms: Pancake, Crepe, Blini, Fritter, Pastry, Wrap, Roll, Griddle cake, Turnover, Snack
antonyms: Main course, Soup, Salad, Beverage, Stew, Roast, Bread, Drink, Broth, Casserole

englishMeaning: A sudden and unexpected change or reversal. A trick in which one thing is secretly swapped for another. An informal term for a surprising turnaround in a situation.
synonyms: Swap, Reversal, Turnaround, Exchange, Substitution, Trick, Flip, About-face, Changeover, Ruse
antonyms: Constancy, Continuity, Stability, Retention, Permanence, Consistency, Sameness, Steadiness, Preservation, Certainty
examples: The magician pulled a clever switcheroo with the two boxes. In a surprise switcheroo, the underdog became team captain. They did a switcheroo and sent the other candidate instead. The ending of the film is a complete switcheroo.

englishMeaning: A legal expression describing the reduction or reclassification of a charge of rape to the lesser offence of fornication. A term used in court reporting when a coerced sexual offence is treated as consensual unlawful intercourse. A controversial change of charge that lowers the seriousness of a sexual offence.
synonyms: Charge reduction, Reclassification, Downgrading, Plea alteration, Legal reframing, Lesser charge, Amendment, Substitution of charge, Mitigation, Recharacterization

examples: Activists criticised the rape-to-fornication conversion of the charges. The report documented several rape-to-fornication cases in the lower courts. Lawyers argued that the rape-to-fornication shift denied the victim justice. Legal reforms aim to prevent rape-to-fornication reclassification.

englishMeaning: In mathematics, a trigonometric function of an angle, equal to the ratio of the side opposite the angle to the hypotenuse in a right-angled triangle. The curve or wave produced by this function. In anatomy and older usage, a curve, fold or hollow. Used in Latin phrases to mean 'without'.
synonyms: Trigonometric ratio, Sine function, Sinusoid, Wave function, Without (Latin)
antonyms: Cosine, Tangent, Cum (Latin: with), With

sindhiMeaning: رياضي ۾ ڪنڊ جو هڪ تڪوني تناسب، ساڄي ڪنڊ واري ٽڪنڊي ۾ سامهون واري ڀرپاسي ۽ وترجي نسبت، هن فنڪشن مان ٺهندڙ لهر يا ورڪ، لاطيني ۾ ’بغير‘ جي معنيٰ ۾ استعمال

englishMeaning: An essential condition or element without which something cannot exist or succeed. An absolutely necessary requirement. A thing that is indispensable to a plan, quality or achievement.

synonyms: Narrow-minded, Prejudiced, Biased, Insular, Parochial, Bigoted, Shortsighted, Inflexible
antonyms: Open-minded, Broad-minded, Tolerant, Liberal, Receptive, Unbiased, Enlightened

urduMeaning: پلکیں جھپک کر آنسو ہٹانا، پلکیں جھپک کر نظر صاف کرنا یا نیند بھگانا، پلکیں جھپک کر جذبات چھپانا

englishMeaning: To hold back tears by blinking the eyes. To stop oneself from crying by blinking rapidly. To restrain an emotion from showing in the eyes.
synonyms: Hold back, Fight back, Suppress, Restrain, Check, Swallow
antonyms: Let flow, Release, Weep, Sob, Break down, Give in
examples: He blinked back tears as he read the letter. She blinked back her tears and thanked the audience. The boy blinked back tears after losing the race. He blinked back the emotion and continued speaking.
sindhiMeaning: اکيون ڇنڀي ڳوڙها روڪڻ، رئڻ کان پاڻ کي بچائڻ، جذبن کي اکين ۾ ظاهر ٿيڻ کان روڪڻ
urduMeaning: پلکیں جھپک کر آنسو روکنا، رونے سے خود کو باز رکھنا، جذبات کو آنکھوں میں ظاہر ہونے سے روکنا

englishMeaning: To stop shining or working suddenly, especially of a light. To fade out or disappear after flickering. Of a signal or screen, to go dark or cease abruptly.
synonyms: Go out, Die out, Fade, Switch off, Extinguish, Vanish, Cut out
antonyms: Light up, Blink on, Switch on, Glow, Ignite, Appear
examples: The street lamp blinked out in the middle of the night. One by one the stars blinked out as dawn broke. The screen blinked out during the presentation. His torch blinked out and left them in darkness.
sindhiMeaning: اوچتو بند ٿي وڃڻ، خاص ڪري بتي جو وسامي وڃڻ، ٽمڪي پوءِ گم ٿي وڃڻ، سگنل يا اسڪرين جو اوچتو بند ٿيڻ
urduMeaning: اچانک بجھ جانا، خاص طور پر روشنی کا بند ہو جانا، ٹمٹما کر غائب ہو جانا، سگنل یا اسکرین کا یکایک بند ہو جانا

englishMeaning: To begin to shine or light up, often suddenly or with a flicker. To become active or start working, especially of a light or display.
synonyms: Light up, Switch on, Flash on, Illuminate, Start, Activate
antonyms: Blink out, Go out, Switch off, Fade, Darken, Stop
examples: The warning light blinked on as the engine started. A small green lamp blinked on inside the machine. The screen blinked on after he pressed the button. Street lights blinked on all along the road.
sindhiMeaning: اوچتو روشن ٿي پوڻ، ٽمڪي روشني ڏيڻ شروع ڪرڻ، بتي يا اسڪرين جو هلڻ شروع ٿيڻ
urduMeaning: اچانک روشن ہو جانا، ٹمٹما کر جلنا شروع کرنا، بتی یا اسکرین کا چل پڑنا

englishMeaning: To stop shining or go dark, especially of a light or indicator. To switch off suddenly or after a flicker.
synonyms: Go out, Switch off, Turn off, Die out, Shut down, Extinguish
antonyms: Blink on, Light up, Switch on, Glow, Start, Illuminate
examples: The indicator blinked off as soon as charging finished. The lights blinked off and the hall went dark. His computer screen blinked off without warning. The sign blinked off at exactly midnight.
sindhiMeaning: بتي جو وسامي وڃڻ، اوچتو بند ٿي پوڻ، ٽمڪي پوءِ بند ٿي وڃڻ
urduMeaning: بتی کا بجھ جانا، اچانک بند ہو جانا، ٹمٹما کر بند ہو جانا

englishMeaning: Unwilling to accept ideas, beliefs or ways of life different from one's own. Having a limited and intolerant outlook. Showing prejudice and a refusal to consider other opinions.
synonyms: Intolerant, Bigoted, Prejudiced, Blinkered, Insular, Parochial, Illiberal, Biased
antonyms: Open-minded, Broad-minded, Tolerant, Liberal, Progressive, Accepting, Unprejudiced
examples: He is too narrow-minded to appreciate other cultures. Narrow-minded attitudes hold a society back. She refused to work with such narrow-minded people. Travelling widely cured him of his narrow-minded views.
sindhiMeaning: تنگ نظر، ٻين جي خيالن ۽ عقيدن کي قبول نه ڪندڙ، محدود ۽ غير روادار سوچ رکندڙ، تعصب ڀريل رويو رکندڙ
urduMeaning: تنگ نظر، دوسروں کے خیالات و عقائد قبول نہ کرنے والا، محدود اور غیر روادار سوچ رکھنے والا، متعصب مزاج

englishMeaning: A panel or system used to connect and direct telephone calls within an organisation. A board with switches and instruments for controlling electric circuits. The department or staff that operates such a system.
synonyms: Exchange, Control panel, Console, Panel board, Operator desk, Distribution board
antonyms: Direct line, Dial-in line, Disconnection, Standalone phone
examples: Please call the switchboard and ask for extension four. The hospital switchboard was flooded with calls. An engineer checked the switchboard in the basement. She worked on the switchboard for many years.
sindhiMeaning: ٽيليفون ڪالون ڳنڍڻ ۽ منتقل ڪرڻ وارو نظام يا بورڊ، بجلي جي سرڪٽ ڪنٽرول ڪرڻ وارو سُئچ بورڊ، اهو شعبو جيڪو هي نظام هلائي
urduMeaning: ٹیلی فون کالیں جوڑنے اور منتقل کرنے والا بورڈ یا نظام، بجلی کے سرکٹ کنٹرول کرنے والا سوئچ بورڈ، وہ شعبہ جو یہ نظام چلاتا ہے

englishMeaning: To reduce a number of options or possibilities to a smaller and more specific set. To limit a choice or search to a few final items. To focus attention on one particular thing after eliminating others.
synonyms: Reduce to, Limit to, Restrict to, Shortlist, Focus on, Pin down, Confine to
antonyms: Broaden, Expand, Widen, Extend, Generalise, Open up
examples: We have narrowed the list down to three candidates. Police narrowed the investigation down to two suspects. She narrowed her choices down to a single university. They narrowed the problem down to a faulty wire.
sindhiMeaning: ڪيترن اختيارن کي گهٽائي ٿورن تائين محدود ڪرڻ، چونڊ کي مخصوص ڪرڻ، ٻيا امڪان ختم ڪري هڪ ڏانهن ڌيان ڏيڻ
urduMeaning: کئی امکانات کو کم کر کے چند تک محدود کرنا، انتخاب کو مخصوص کرنا، دیگر امکانات ختم کر کے ایک پر توجہ دینا

englishMeaning: To move closer to a target or goal. To focus attention or effort on one specific thing. To gradually identify the exact cause, person or answer.
synonyms: Zero in on, Home in on, Close in on, Focus on, Target, Pinpoint
antonyms: Overlook, Ignore, Digress, Wander, Broaden, Lose track of
examples: Investigators are narrowing in on the cause of the fire. The team narrowed in on a workable solution. She narrowed in on the main weakness of the argument. Researchers are narrowing in on a cure.
sindhiMeaning: مقصد يا نشاني ڏانهن ويجهو وڃڻ، ڪنهن هڪ خاص شيءِ تي ڌيان مرڪوز ڪرڻ، آهستي آهستي اصل سبب يا شخص تائين پهچڻ
urduMeaning: ہدف یا مقصد کے قریب پہنچنا، کسی ایک مخصوص چیز پر توجہ مرکوز کرنا، آہستہ آہستہ اصل سبب یا شخص تک پہنچنا

englishMeaning: A road, path or railway that climbs steeply by a series of sharp bends. A sudden reversal of direction or fortune. In British usage, a roller coaster. To turn sharply back in the opposite direction while climbing or descending.
synonyms: Zigzag, Hairpin bend, Serpentine road, Roller coaster, Reversal, Twist
antonyms: Straight road, Direct route, Level path, Steady course
examples: The bus climbed the mountain by a series of switchbacks. The trail switchbacks up the steep hillside. The season was a switchback of wins and losses. Children queued for the switchback at the fair.
sindhiMeaning: اهڙو رستو يا ريلوي لائين جيڪا تيز موڙن سان مٿي چڙهي، اوچتو رخ يا حالتن جو مٽجڻ، رولر ڪوسٽر جهڙي جهولڻ واري سواري، تيز موڙ ڏئي واپس مڙڻ
urduMeaning: ایسا راستہ یا ریلوے لائن جو تیز موڑوں کے ساتھ اوپر چڑھے، اچانک رخ یا حالات کی تبدیلی، رولر کوسٹر، تیز موڑ لے کر واپس مڑنا

englishMeaning: A pocket knife with a blade that springs out when a button is pressed. A flick knife, often associated with street crime. Anything with a folding blade that opens automatically.
synonyms: Flick knife, Pocket knife, Jackknife, Blade, Dagger, Clasp knife
antonyms: Blunt instrument, Sheathed knife, Fixed blade, Butter knife
examples: The police found a switchblade in his jacket pocket. Carrying a switchblade is illegal in many countries. He opened the parcel with a small switchblade. The film shows gangs fighting with switchblades.
sindhiMeaning: اهڙو کيسي وارو چاقو جنهن جو ڦر بٽڻ دٻائڻ سان ٻاهر نڪري، اسپرنگ وارو چاقو، پاڻمرادو کلندڙ ڦر وارو هٿيار
urduMeaning: ایسا جیبی چاقو جس کا پھل بٹن دبانے سے باہر نکلے، اسپرنگ والا چاقو، خودکار کھلنے والا پھل رکھنے والا ہتھیار

englishMeaning: Turned on so that electricity flows and a device works. Informally, alert, well informed and up to date. Aware of modern trends and quick to understand things. Mentally attentive and fully engaged.
synonyms: On, Activated, Running, Alert, Aware, Astute, Clued up, Sharp
antonyms: Switched off, Off, Inactive, Unaware, Ignorant, Dull, Out of touch
examples: The heater was already switched on when we arrived. She is a very switched on young manager. Make sure the machine is switched on before you begin. Our new teacher is switched on and full of ideas.
sindhiMeaning: آن ڪيل، بجلي هلندڙ ۽ ڪم ڪندڙ، غير رسمي طور تي هوشيار ۽ باخبر، جديد رجحانن کان واقف ۽ تيز فهم، ذهني طور مڪمل متوجه
urduMeaning: آن کیا ہوا، بجلی چالو اور کام کرتا ہوا، غیر رسمی طور پر ہوشیار اور باخبر، جدید رجحانات سے واقف اور تیز فہم، ذہنی طور پر پوری طرح متوجہ

englishMeaning: In baseball, a batter who can hit from either the right or the left side of the plate. A person who is skilled at doing two different things or working in two different roles. Informally, someone who can adapt easily to either of two options.
synonyms: Ambidextrous player, All-rounder, Versatile player, Dual-role worker, Adaptable person
antonyms: Specialist, One-sided player, Single-role worker, Inflexible person
examples: The team signed a talented switch-hitter last season. As a switch-hitter, he confuses opposing pitchers. In our office she is a switch-hitter who handles sales and design. Good switch-hitters are rare in professional baseball.
sindhiMeaning: بيس بال ۾ اهو بيٽسمين جيڪو ساڄي ۽ کاٻي ٻنهي پاسن کان بيٽنگ ڪري سگهي، اهو شخص جيڪو ٻه مختلف ڪم يا ذميواريون هلائي سگهي، غير رسمي طور تي هر حال ۾ ٺهڪي ايندڙ ماڻهو
urduMeaning: بیس بال میں وہ بلے باز جو دائیں اور بائیں دونوں طرف سے کھیل سکے، وہ شخص جو دو مختلف کام یا کردار نبھا سکے، غیر رسمی طور پر ہر حال میں ڈھل جانے والا شخص

englishMeaning: Giving pleasure or satisfaction. Making someone feel pleased because something has turned out well. Rewarding and emotionally fulfilling.
synonyms: Pleasing, Satisfying, Rewarding, Fulfilling, Heartening, Delightful, Pleasurable
antonyms: Disappointing, Frustrating, Unsatisfying, Displeasing, Depressing, Annoying
examples: It is gratifying to see your children do well. The response from readers was most gratifying. Teaching is hard work but deeply gratifying. She found the praise very gratifying.
sindhiMeaning: خوشي يا اطمينان ڏيندڙ، دل کي راحت پهچائيندڙ، اهڙو نتيجو جيڪو خوشگوار محسوس ٿئي، اجر وارو ۽ دلي تسڪين ڏيندڙ
urduMeaning: خوشی یا اطمینان دینے والا، دل کو راحت پہنچانے والا، ایسا نتیجہ جو خوشگوار محسوس ہو، پُرثمر اور دلی تسکین بخش

englishMeaning: In a way that shows thanks or appreciation. With a feeling of gratitude for kindness or help received. Thankfully and with relief.
synonyms: Thankfully, Appreciatively, Obligingly, With gratitude, Indebtedly, Warmly
antonyms: Ungratefully, Thanklessly, Ungraciously, Resentfully, Indifferently
examples: She gratefully accepted the offer of help. He gratefully sank into the chair after the long walk. We gratefully acknowledge the support of our donors. The travellers gratefully drank the cold water.
sindhiMeaning: شڪرگذاري سان، احسان مندي جو اظهار ڪندي، مدد يا مهرباني لاءِ ٿورائتو ٿي، سُک ۽ اطمينان سان
urduMeaning: شکر گزاری کے ساتھ، احسان مندی ظاہر کرتے ہوئے، مدد یا مہربانی پر ممنون ہو کر، سکون اور اطمینان سے

englishMeaning: The process of finding and hiring new people for a job or organisation. The act of enlisting new members into a group, army or cause. In biology, the addition of new individuals to a population. The activity or industry concerned with employing staff.
synonyms: Hiring, Enlistment, Employment, Enrolment, Induction, Staffing, Conscription
antonyms: Dismissal, Retrenchment, Layoff, Discharge, Retirement, Expulsion
examples: The company has started the recruitment of new engineers. Recruitment into the police force has increased this year. She works in recruitment for a large bank. Poor recruitment can weaken any organisation.
sindhiMeaning: نوڪري يا اداري لاءِ نوان ماڻهو ڀرتي ڪرڻ جو عمل، ڪنهن گروهه فوج يا مقصد ۾ نوان ميمبر شامل ڪرڻ، حياتيات ۾ آبادي ۾ نون فردن جو اضافو، ملازمن جي ڀرتي وارو ڪم يا شعبو
urduMeaning: ملازمت یا ادارے کے لیے نئے افراد کی بھرتی کا عمل، کسی گروہ فوج یا مقصد میں نئے ارکان شامل کرنا، حیاتیات میں آبادی میں نئے افراد کا اضافہ، بھرتی سے متعلق کام یا شعبہ

englishMeaning: The fact of happening again, especially of something unwanted. A repeated occurrence of an event, illness or problem. The return of a disease after a period of improvement.
synonyms: Repetition, Reappearance, Return, Relapse, Repeat, Reoccurrence, Resurgence
antonyms: Prevention, Cure, Elimination, Cessation, End, Eradication
examples: Doctors are trying to prevent a recurrence of the infection. There has been a recurrence of violence in the area. Regular checkups reduce the risk of recurrence. The recurrence of these errors is worrying.
sindhiMeaning: ٻيهر ٿيڻ، خاص ڪري ڪنهن ناپسنديده ڳالهه جو وري ورجاءُ، ڪنهن واقعي بيماري يا مسئلي جو بار بار ٿيڻ، بيماري جو صحتيابي کان پوءِ وري موٽڻ
urduMeaning: دوبارہ واقع ہونا، خاص طور پر کسی ناپسندیدہ بات کا تکرار، کسی واقعے بیماری یا مسئلے کا بار بار ہونا، بیماری کا صحت یابی کے بعد لوٹ آنا

englishMeaning: To happen again, especially repeatedly or after an interval. To come back into one's mind or thoughts. Of a symptom or illness, to return after seeming to improve. In mathematics, of digits, to repeat endlessly in a decimal.
synonyms: Reappear, Return, Repeat, Reoccur, Come back, Persist, Relapse
antonyms: Cease, Stop, End, Vanish, Disappear, Conclude
examples: The same problem recurs every winter. That thought recurred to him during the night. The fever recurred after two weeks. In this fraction the digit three recurs endlessly.
sindhiMeaning: ٻيهر ٿيڻ، خاص ڪري بار بار يا ڪجهه وقت کان پوءِ، ذهن ۾ وري اچڻ، بيماري يا علامت جو وري ظاهر ٿيڻ، رياضي ۾ انگن جو لڳاتار ورجاءُ
urduMeaning: دوبارہ ہونا، خاص طور پر بار بار یا کچھ عرصے بعد، ذہن میں دوبارہ آنا، بیماری یا علامت کا لوٹ آنا، ریاضی میں اعداد کا مسلسل دہرایا جانا

englishMeaning: Having strong, visible muscles; lean and muscular. Consisting of or resembling sinews; tough and fibrous. Difficult to chew because it is full of tough tissue. Forceful and vigorous in style or expression.
synonyms: Muscular, Wiry, Brawny, Tough, Strong, Athletic, Stringy, Robust, Vigorous
antonyms: Weak, Flabby, Frail, Soft, Tender, Feeble, Delicate
examples: The blacksmith had sinewy arms from years of work. The meat was dry and sinewy and hard to chew. She admired his lean, sinewy build. The poet is known for his sinewy prose.
sindhiMeaning: مضبوط ۽ پٺن وارو، سنهو پر طاقتور جسم رکندڙ، سخت ۽ رڳن سان ڀريل، ڏند سان چٻڻ ۾ ڏکيو گوشت، زوردار ۽ اثرائتو اسلوب
urduMeaning: مضبوط پٹھوں والا، دبلا مگر طاقتور، سخت اور ریشے دار، چبانے میں سخت گوشت، پُرزور اور مؤثر اندازِ تحریر

englishMeaning: A short or light symphony, usually simpler in structure than a full symphony. A small symphony orchestra, often with fewer players than a standard orchestra.
synonyms: Symphony, Orchestral piece, Chamber orchestra, Ensemble, Composition
antonyms: Full symphony, Grand orchestra, Solo, Silence
examples: The composer wrote a charming sinfonietta for strings. The city sinfonietta performed at the town hall. Her sinfonietta lasts only fifteen minutes. He joined the sinfonietta as a violinist.
sindhiMeaning: مختصر يا هلڪي سمفوني، عام سمفوني کان ننڍي ۽ سادي موسيقي جي تخليق، ننڍو سمفوني آرڪيسٽرا جنهن ۾ گهٽ سازندا هجن
urduMeaning: مختصر یا ہلکی سمفنی، عام سمفنی سے چھوٹی اور سادہ موسیقی، چھوٹا سمفنی آرکسٹرا جس میں کم سازندے ہوں

englishMeaning: In a way that breaks religious or moral law; wickedly. In a manner considered morally wrong or immoral. Informally, to an enjoyable degree that feels almost wrong; extremely or indulgently.
synonyms: Wickedly, Immorally, Wrongfully, Corruptly, Indulgently, Deliciously, Extremely
antonyms: Virtuously, Piously, Righteously, Morally, Innocently, Modestly
examples: He admitted that he had lived sinfully in his youth. The chocolate cake was sinfully rich. She spoke of those who behave sinfully and feel no shame. The hotel was sinfully luxurious.
sindhiMeaning: گناهه واري نموني، مذهبي يا اخلاقي قانون ڀڃيندي، بدڪاري سان، غير رسمي طور تي حد کان وڌيڪ مزيدار يا پرلطف انداز ۾
urduMeaning: گناہ آلود انداز میں، مذہبی یا اخلاقی اصول توڑتے ہوئے، بدکاری کے ساتھ، غیر رسمی طور پر حد سے زیادہ لذیذ یا پُرلطف انداز میں

englishMeaning: To make the greatest possible effort to achieve something. To try extremely hard, using all one's strength and resources. To work to the very limit of one's ability.
synonyms: Do one's utmost, Go all out, Try one's hardest, Make every effort, Pull out all the stops, Struggle hard
antonyms: Give up, Slack off, Take it easy, Neglect, Idle, Do nothing
examples: The team strained every sinew to win the final match. Doctors strained every sinew to save the patient. We will strain every sinew to finish the project on time. He strained every sinew to support his family.
sindhiMeaning: پوري طاقت لڳائي ڪوشش ڪرڻ، سر ڌڙ جي بازي لڳائڻ، هر ممڪن ڪوشش ڪرڻ، پنهنجي وس کان وڌيڪ زور لائڻ
urduMeaning: پوری طاقت لگا کر کوشش کرنا، ایڑی چوٹی کا زور لگانا، ہر ممکن جدوجہد کرنا، اپنی حد سے بڑھ کر محنت کرنا

englishMeaning: To use all one's energy and determination to do something. To make a supreme effort to achieve a goal. To push oneself mentally and physically to the limit.
synonyms: Do one's best, Strain every sinew, Exert oneself, Strive, Endeavour, Go all out
antonyms: Relax, Give up, Neglect, Loaf, Surrender, Slacken
examples: She strained every nerve to pass the entrance examination. The rescue workers strained every nerve to reach the trapped miners. He strained every nerve to keep the business alive. They strained every nerve to meet the deadline.
sindhiMeaning: سموري توانائي ۽ همت سان ڪوشش ڪرڻ، ايڙي چوٽي جو زور لڳائڻ، مقصد حاصل ڪرڻ لاءِ هر ممڪن ڪوشش ڪرڻ، ذهني توڙي جسماني طور پاڻ پتوڙڻ
urduMeaning: اپنی تمام تر توانائی اور عزم سے کوشش کرنا، ایڑی چوٹی کا زور لگانا، مقصد کے حصول کے لیے بھرپور جدوجہد کرنا، ذہنی و جسمانی طور پر انتہا تک محنت کرنا

englishMeaning: A main branch of a tree. A large limb growing from the trunk of a tree, often bearing smaller branches. In poetry, a leafy branch used as a symbol of nature or shelter.
synonyms: Branch, Limb, Arm, Twig, Offshoot, Stem
antonyms: Trunk, Root, Stump, Base
examples: A heavy bough broke under the weight of the snow. Birds nested in the highest bough of the old tree. Children sat in the shade of a spreading bough. The gardener sawed off a dead bough.
sindhiMeaning: وڻ جي وڏي ٽاري، ٿڙ مان نڪرندڙ مکيه شاخ، شاعري ۾ پنن سان ڀريل ٽاري جيڪا فطرت يا پناهه جي علامت هجي

urduMeaning: میٹھے پانی کا بڑا قدرتی بہاؤ جو سمندر جھیل یا کسی دوسرے دریا کی طرف بہتا ہے، وہ راستہ یا وادی جہاں سے یہ پانی بہتا ہے، کسی مائع یا لوگوں کا بڑا بہاؤ

englishMeaning: Water falling in drops from clouds to the ground. A fall of such water, or a period of rainy weather. To fall as rain from the sky. To fall or send down in large quantities, like rain. A large or rapid fall of something such as blows, questions, or gifts.
synonyms: Rainfall, Shower, Downpour, Drizzle, Precipitation, Deluge, Pour, Sprinkle, Torrent
antonyms: Drought, Dryness, Aridity, Sunshine, Clear weather, Dry spell
examples: Heavy rain delayed the start of the match. It began to rain soon after we left home. Reporters rained questions on the minister. The fields turned green after the first rain of the season.
sindhiMeaning: ڪڪرن مان زمين تي ڦڙن جي صورت ۾ ڪرندڙ پاڻي، برسات، مينهن پوڻ جو عرصو، آسمان مان مينهن وسڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ جو وڏي مقدار ۾ وسڻ يا وسائڻ، ڌڪن سوالن يا تحفن جي بوڇاڙ
urduMeaning: بادلوں سے زمین پر قطروں کی صورت میں گرنے والا پانی، بارش، بارش کا موسم یا وقفہ، آسمان سے بارش کا برسنا، کسی چیز کا کثرت سے برسنا یا برسانا، ضربوں سوالوں یا تحائف کی بوچھاڑ

englishMeaning: A barrier built across a river to control the level and flow of water for irrigation or navigation. A heavy and continuous firing of artillery over an area. An overwhelming and rapid succession of questions, complaints, or criticism. To direct a continuous flow of something at someone.
synonyms: Dam, Weir, Bombardment, Onslaught, Volley, Salvo, Deluge, Torrent, Battery
antonyms: Trickle, Silence, Calm, Lull, Peace, Retreat, Ceasefire
examples: The barrage regulates water supply to thousands of acres. Soldiers advanced behind an artillery barrage. She faced a barrage of criticism after the interview. Repair work on the barrage will continue until winter.
sindhiMeaning: درياهه تي ٺهيل بند جيڪو پاڻي جي سطح ۽ وهڪري کي ڪنٽرول ڪري، آبپاشي يا آمدرفت لاءِ ٺهيل بند، لڳاتار توپن جي گولاباري، سوالن شڪايتن يا تنقيد جي لڳاتار بوڇاڙ، ڪنهن تي لڳاتار ڪا شيءِ اڇلائڻ
urduMeaning: دریا پر بنایا گیا بند جو پانی کی سطح اور بہاؤ کو کنٹرول کرتا ہے، آبپاشی یا آمدورفت کے لیے تعمیر شدہ بند، توپوں کی مسلسل گولہ باری، سوالات شکایات یا تنقید کی مسلسل بوچھاڑ، کسی پر لگاتار کچھ برسانا

englishMeaning: A barrier built across a river or stream to hold back water. The body of water held back by such a barrier. To build a dam across something. To block or hold back a flow, feeling, or expression.
synonyms: Barrage, Weir, Barrier, Embankment, Dyke, Block, Obstruct, Stem, Check
antonyms: Release, Open, Free, Unblock, Discharge, Breach, Let flow
examples: The dam supplies electricity to the entire region. Engineers inspected the dam after the earthquake. Villagers dammed the stream to store water. She could no longer dam her tears.
sindhiMeaning: درياهه يا نالي تي پاڻي روڪڻ لاءِ ٺاهيل بند، بند پويان جمع ٿيل پاڻي، ڪنهن وهڪري تي بند ٻڌڻ، ڪنهن وهڪري يا جذبي کي روڪڻ يا دٻائڻ
urduMeaning: دریا یا ندی پر پانی روکنے کے لیے بنایا گیا بند، بند کے پیچھے جمع پانی، کسی بہاؤ پر بند باندھنا، کسی بہاؤ یا جذبے کو روکنا یا دبانا

englishMeaning: A large natural or artificial lake used as a source of water supply. A container or tank in which a liquid is stored. A large supply or store of something. A population or place in which an infection is maintained and from which it can spread.
synonyms: Lake, Tank, Cistern, Basin, Store, Stock, Pool, Repository, Supply
antonyms: Drain, Outlet, Shortage, Scarcity, Depletion, Emptiness
examples: The reservoir supplies drinking water to the whole city. Water levels in the reservoir fell sharply during the drought. The pen has a small ink reservoir. The country holds a vast reservoir of untapped talent.
sindhiMeaning: پاڻي جي فراهمي لاءِ ٺاهيل وڏي قدرتي يا مصنوعي ڍنڍ، مائع رکڻ وارو ٽانڪي يا برتن، ڪنهن شيءِ جو وڏو ذخيرو، اهڙي جڳهه يا آبادي جتان ڪا بيماري ڦهلجي سگهي
urduMeaning: پانی کی فراہمی کے لیے بنائی گئی بڑی قدرتی یا مصنوعی جھیل، مائع رکھنے والا ٹینک یا برتن، کسی چیز کا بڑا ذخیرہ، ایسی جگہ یا آبادی جہاں سے بیماری پھیل سکتی ہے

englishMeaning: An overflow of a large amount of water beyond its normal limits, especially over land. To cover or become covered with water. To arrive or come in overwhelming numbers or quantities. An outpouring of something such as tears, light, or emails.
synonyms: Deluge, Inundation, Torrent, Overflow, Swamp, Submerge, Surge, Spate, Outpouring
antonyms: Drought, Trickle, Drain, Dryness, Ebb, Scarcity, Shortage
examples: The flood destroyed hundreds of homes along the river. Heavy rain flooded the basement overnight. The office was flooded with job applications. Morning light flooded the little room.
sindhiMeaning: پاڻي جو حد کان وڌي زمين تي ڦهلجڻ، ٻوڏ، پاڻي سان ڀرجي وڃڻ يا ڀري ڇڏڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ جو وڏي تعداد ۾ اچڻ، لڙڪن روشني يا پيغامن جي بوڇاڙ
urduMeaning: پانی کا حد سے بڑھ کر زمین پر پھیل جانا، سیلاب، پانی سے بھر جانا یا بھر دینا، کسی چیز کا بہت بڑی تعداد میں آنا، آنسوؤں روشنی یا پیغامات کا سیلاب

englishMeaning: The highest point of achievement, development, or excellence. The peak or summit of something. The most perfect example of a particular quality or type.
synonyms: Peak, Summit, Pinnacle, Zenith, Apex, Height, Climax, Culmination, Crown
antonyms: Nadir, Bottom, Low point, Base, Trough, Depth, Rock bottom
examples: That performance was the acme of her long career. The building is considered the acme of modern design. He reached the acme of political power at forty. Their craftsmanship is the acme of patience and skill.
sindhiMeaning: ڪاميابي ترقي يا ڪماليت جي بلند ترين حد، ڪنهن شيءِ جي چوٽي، ڪنهن خوبي جو بهترين مثال
urduMeaning: کامیابی ترقی یا کمال کا بلند ترین درجہ، کسی چیز کی چوٹی، کسی خوبی کی بہترین مثال

englishMeaning: To produce offspring or young. To bring children into existence through natural reproduction. To reproduce as a species. Figuratively, to bring something new into being.
synonyms: Reproduce, Breed, Beget, Multiply, Propagate, Generate, Spawn, Father, Bear
antonyms: Abort, Sterilize, Prevent, Destroy, Kill, Extinguish, Die out
examples: Most species migrate to warmer waters to procreate. They chose not to procreate for personal reasons. Animals in the reserve procreate freely. The urge to procreate is a basic biological instinct.
sindhiMeaning: اولاد پيدا ڪرڻ، قدرتي طريقي سان ٻار پيدا ڪرڻ، نسل وڌائڻ، ڪنهن نئين شيءِ کي وجود ۾ آڻڻ
urduMeaning: اولاد پیدا کرنا، قدرتی طریقے سے بچے پیدا کرنا، نسل بڑھانا، کسی نئی چیز کو وجود میں لانا

englishMeaning: Enforcing conformity by violent or arbitrary means. Tending to force people or things into a rigid, unsuitable pattern without regard for individual differences. Marked by ruthless and inflexible standardisation.
synonyms: Rigid, Inflexible, Arbitrary, Coercive, Uncompromising, Harsh, Draconian, Restrictive
antonyms: Flexible, Lenient, Accommodating, Adaptable, Tolerant, Liberal, Yielding
examples: The school follows a procrustean approach to discipline. Such procrustean rules ignore the needs of individual students. Critics called the policy rigid and procrustean. He rejected the procrustean demands of the committee.
sindhiMeaning: زبردستي يا سختيءَ سان هڪجهڙائي مڙهيندڙ، ماڻهن يا شين کي بنا لحاظ جي سخت سانچي ۾ فٽ ڪرڻ وارو، بي رحم ۽ غير لچڪدار اصولن وارو
urduMeaning: زبردستی یا سختی سے یکسانیت مسلط کرنے والا، لوگوں یا چیزوں کو بغیر لحاظ کے سخت سانچے میں ڈھالنے والا، بے رحم اور غیر لچکدار معیار والا

englishMeaning: The act or process of producing offspring. Natural reproduction and the continuation of a species. The bringing of new life into existence.
synonyms: Reproduction, Breeding, Propagation, Generation, Multiplication, Fertility, Begetting
antonyms: Sterility, Infertility, Barrenness, Extinction, Abstinence, Celibacy
examples: Procreation ensures the survival of the species. The lecture dealt with human procreation and health. Many religions regard procreation as a sacred duty. Environmental stress can affect procreation in birds.
sindhiMeaning: اولاد پيدا ڪرڻ جو عمل، قدرتي طور تي نسل وڌائڻ ۽ برقرار رکڻ، نئين زندگي کي وجود ۾ آڻڻ
urduMeaning: اولاد پیدا کرنے کا عمل، قدرتی طور پر نسل بڑھانا اور جاری رکھنا، نئی زندگی کو وجود میں لانا

englishMeaning: Gradual growth or increase by the addition of new layers or parts. The process of things being added or joined to something over time. A thing formed or added in this way. In law, an increase of property by natural addition, such as land added by a river.
synonyms: Accumulation, Buildup, Growth, Increase, Addition, Deposit, Augmentation, Layering
antonyms: Erosion, Decrease, Reduction, Loss, Depletion, Wearing away, Shrinkage
examples: The delta grows by the slow accretion of silt. Coral reefs form through the accretion of tiny organisms. The library expanded by gradual accretion over a century. Lawyers argued about the accretion of land along the riverbank.
sindhiMeaning: نئين تہن يا حصن جي اضافي سان آهستي آهستي واڌ، وقت سان گڏ شين جو ملي وڌڻ جو عمل، اهڙي طرح ٺهيل شيءِ، قانون ۾ قدرتي طور تي ملڪيت جي واڌ جيئن درياهه سان ملندڙ زمين
urduMeaning: نئی تہوں یا اجزا کے اضافے سے بتدریج بڑھوتری، وقت کے ساتھ چیزوں کے شامل ہوتے جانے کا عمل، اس طرح بننے والی چیز، قانون میں قدرتی طور پر جائیداد میں اضافہ جیسے دریا سے ملنے والی زمین

englishMeaning: Officially recognised or approved as meeting a required standard. Given official authority or sanction to act on behalf of an organisation or country. Certified as qualified by an authorised body. Widely accepted or believed to be true.
synonyms: Certified, Authorised, Approved, Licensed, Recognised, Endorsed, Sanctioned, Validated
antonyms: Unaccredited, Unauthorised, Uncertified, Unrecognised, Banned, Disqualified, Rejected
examples: She studied at an accredited nursing college. Only accredited journalists were allowed inside the hall. The laboratory is accredited by the national testing authority. He served as the accredited representative of his government.
sindhiMeaning: سرڪاري طور تي منظور ٿيل يا مقرر معيار تي پورو لهندڙ، ڪنهن اداري يا ملڪ پاران بااختيار ٺهرايل، مجاز اداري پاران سند يافته، عام طور تي مڃيل يا تسليم ٿيل
urduMeaning: سرکاری طور پر تسلیم شدہ یا مقررہ معیار پر پورا اترنے والا، کسی ادارے یا ملک کی جانب سے بااختیار مقرر کردہ، مجاز ادارے سے سند یافتہ، عام طور پر مانا ہوا

englishMeaning: The gradual accumulation or increase of something over time. An amount of money, interest, or benefit that builds up and becomes due. In accounting, the recording of income or expenses when they are earned or incurred rather than when cash is exchanged.
synonyms: Accumulation, Buildup, Growth, Increase, Gain, Addition, Collection, Increment
antonyms: Reduction, Decrease, Loss, Depletion, Payment, Withdrawal, Deduction
examples: The accrual of interest begins from the date of deposit. Employees can check the accrual of their annual leave. The company follows the accrual method of accounting. Late payment led to a steady accrual of penalties.
sindhiMeaning: وقت سان گڏ ڪنهن شيءِ جو آهستي آهستي جمع ٿيڻ، اهو پئسو سود يا فائدو جيڪو گڏ ٿي واجب ٿئي، اڪائونٽنگ ۾ آمدني يا خرچ کي انهيءَ وقت درج ڪرڻ جڏهن اهو ٿئي نه ڪ ادائگي وقت
urduMeaning: وقت کے ساتھ کسی چیز کا بتدریج جمع ہونا، وہ رقم سود یا فائدہ جو جمع ہو کر واجب ہو جائے، اکاؤنٹنگ میں آمدنی یا اخراجات کو وقوع کے وقت درج کرنا نہ کہ ادائیگی کے وقت

englishMeaning: To adopt the customs, values, and behaviour of another culture. To help or cause a person or group to adjust to a different culture. To modify a culture through prolonged contact with another culture.
synonyms: Assimilate, Adapt, Adjust, Integrate, Blend in, Conform, Naturalise, Absorb
antonyms: Alienate, Isolate, Resist, Segregate, Reject, Estrange, Withdraw
examples: Immigrant families often acculturate within a generation. Schools help newcomers acculturate more easily. He struggled to acculturate after moving abroad. The tribe slowly acculturated to life in the city.
sindhiMeaning: ٻي ثقافت جا رسم رواج قدر ۽ طور طريقا اپنائڻ، ڪنهن ماڻهو يا گروهه کي نئين ثقافت سان هلائڻ يا ٺاهڻ، طويل رابطي سبب ثقافت ۾ تبديلي آڻڻ
urduMeaning: دوسری ثقافت کے رسم و رواج اقدار اور طور طریقے اپنانا، کسی فرد یا گروہ کو نئی ثقافت سے ہم آہنگ کرنا، طویل رابطے کے باعث ثقافت میں تبدیلی لانا

englishMeaning: To die. To stop functioning or working, especially of a machine. To give up trying and abandon an effort or hope.
synonyms: Die, Pass away, Expire, Perish, Break down, Stop working, Quit, Surrender, Succumb
antonyms: Survive, Live, Revive, Recover, Persist, Continue, Function, Endure
examples: The old man finally gave up the ghost after a long illness. My laptop gave up the ghost in the middle of the presentation. After three failed attempts, the team gave up the ghost. Their ancient car gave up the ghost on the motorway.
sindhiMeaning: مري وڃڻ، ساهه ڏيڻ، ڪنهن مشين جو ڪم ڪرڻ ڇڏي ڏيڻ يا خراب ٿي وڃڻ، ڪوشش يا اميد ڇڏي ڏيڻ
urduMeaning: مر جانا، دم توڑ دینا، کسی مشین کا کام کرنا چھوڑ دینا یا خراب ہو جانا، کوشش یا امید ترک کر دینا

englishMeaning: To revive someone from unconsciousness or apparent death. To restore breathing or heartbeat by medical means. To bring something back into use, activity, or strength again.
synonyms: Revive, Restore, Revitalise, Reanimate, Renew, Rescue, Regenerate, Bring round
antonyms: Kill, Suffocate, Abandon, Destroy, Weaken, Neglect, Let die
examples: Doctors managed to resuscitate the drowning boy. Paramedics resuscitated him at the roadside. The new manager hopes to resuscitate the failing business. Fresh investment resuscitated the local film industry.
sindhiMeaning: بيهوشي يا موت جهڙي حالت مان ڪنهن کي هوش ۾ آڻڻ، طبي طريقي سان ساهه يا دل جي ڌڙڪن بحال ڪرڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي ٻيهر فعال يا زنده ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: بے ہوشی یا موت جیسی حالت سے کسی کو ہوش میں لانا، طبی طریقے سے سانس یا دل کی دھڑکن بحال کرنا، کسی چیز کو دوبارہ فعال یا زندہ کرنا

englishMeaning: To confess or acknowledge that something is true, often reluctantly. To allow someone to enter a place. To accept someone into an institution, school, or organisation. To take a patient into hospital for treatment. To have room for something.
synonyms: Confess, Acknowledge, Concede, Accept, Allow, Grant, Enrol, Receive, Let in
antonyms: Deny, Refuse, Reject, Exclude, Bar, Dismiss, Discharge, Conceal
examples: He admitted that he had made a serious mistake. Only ticket holders will be admitted to the hall. She was admitted to the university on merit. The patient was admitted to hospital late last night.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڳالهه جي سچائي مڃڻ يا اقرار ڪرڻ، ڪنهن کي اندر اچڻ جي اجازت ڏيڻ، ڪنهن کي اداري يا اسڪول ۾ داخل ڪرڻ، مريض کي اسپتال ۾ داخل ڪرڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ لاءِ گنجائش رکڻ
urduMeaning: کسی بات کی سچائی تسلیم کرنا یا اعتراف کرنا، کسی کو اندر آنے کی اجازت دینا، کسی کو ادارے یا اسکول میں داخل کرنا، مریض کو اسپتال میں داخل کرنا، کسی چیز کی گنجائش رکھنا

englishMeaning: To inspect something carefully in order to learn about it. To study or consider a subject in detail. To check a person's health as a doctor. To test a student's knowledge formally. To question a witness in a court of law.
synonyms: Inspect, Study, Analyse, Investigate, Scrutinise, Review, Check, Assess, Probe
antonyms: Ignore, Overlook, Neglect, Skim, Disregard, Glance, Skip
examples: The mechanic examined the engine carefully. Researchers examined the effects of the new drug. The doctor examined her and prescribed rest. Students will be examined in three subjects this term.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ کي غور سان جانچڻ يا معائنو ڪرڻ، ڪنهن موضوع تي تفصيل سان غور ڪرڻ، ڊاڪٽر طور مريض جو معائنو ڪرڻ، شاگرد جو امتحان وٺڻ، عدالت ۾ گواهه کان سوال ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کا بغور جائزہ لینا یا معائنہ کرنا، کسی موضوع پر تفصیل سے غور کرنا، ڈاکٹر کے طور پر مریض کا معائنہ کرنا، طالب علم کا امتحان لینا، عدالت میں گواہ سے جرح کرنا

englishMeaning: To cut off a limb or part of the body, usually by surgery. To remove a damaged or diseased body part for medical reasons. Figuratively, to cut off or remove a part of something.
synonyms: Sever, Cut off, Remove, Excise, Detach, Lop off, Truncate, Dismember
antonyms: Attach, Join, Reattach, Preserve, Restore, Retain, Heal
examples: Surgeons had to amputate his left leg below the knee. The infection spread so fast that doctors amputated the finger. He learned to walk again after the amputated limb healed. Editors amputated the final chapter from the book.
sindhiMeaning: جراحي ذريعي جسم جو ڪو عضوو ڪٽي ڌار ڪرڻ، خراب يا بيمار عضوو طبي سبب سبب ڪڍڻ، مجازي طور تي ڪنهن شيءِ جو حصو ڪٽي ڌار ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: سرجری کے ذریعے جسم کا کوئی عضو کاٹ کر الگ کرنا، خراب یا بیمار حصہ طبی وجہ سے نکالنا، مجازی طور پر کسی چیز کا حصہ کاٹ دینا

englishMeaning: The back part of a gun barrel where the ammunition is loaded. The lower or rear part of something. Relating to a birth in which the baby's buttocks or feet come out first. The buttocks or lower rear part of the body.
synonyms: Rear, Back, Hindquarters, Buttocks, Base, Butt, Posterior, Stock
antonyms: Muzzle, Front, Head, Top, Fore, Barrel end, Vertex
examples: He loaded the cartridge into the breech of the rifle. The breech of the cannon was damaged in the blast. The baby was born in a breech position. A breech delivery often requires close medical supervision.
sindhiMeaning: بندوق جي نالي جو پويون حصو جتي گولي ڀري ويندي آهي، ڪنهن شيءِ جو هيٺيون يا پويون حصو، اهڙو ڄمڻ جنهن ۾ ٻار جا پير يا چتڙ پهرين نڪرن، جسم جو پويون هيٺيون حصو
urduMeaning: بندوق کی نالی کا پچھلا حصہ جہاں گولی بھری جاتی ہے، کسی چیز کا نچلا یا پچھلا حصہ، ایسی پیدائش جس میں بچے کے پاؤں یا کولہے پہلے نکلیں، جسم کا نچلا پچھلا حصہ

englishMeaning: A sharp piece of broken glass, pottery, metal, or similar hard material. A fragment or small broken part of something. A small remaining piece of something once whole, such as a memory or hope.
synonyms: Fragment, Splinter, Piece, Chip, Sliver, Bit, Scrap, Flake

synonyms: Recklessness, Cruelty, Malice, Licentiousness, Immorality, Extravagance, Abandon, Lawlessness
antonyms: Restraint, Discipline, Modesty, Prudence, Self-control, Care, Decency, Responsibility
examples: The report condemned the wantonness of the attack on civilians. His wantonness with money left the family in debt. She was shocked by the wantonness of the destruction. Critics accused the film of glorifying wantonness.
sindhiMeaning: بغير سبب ظلم، تشدد يا تباهي ڪرڻ جي خصلت، ضبط، نظم يا اخلاقي روڪ جي کوٽ، بي جا فضول خرچي يا لاپرواهي، بي حيائي يا بداخلاقي
urduMeaning: بلاوجہ ظلم، تشدد یا تباہی کرنے کی خصلت، ضبط، نظم یا اخلاقی روک کی کمی، بے جا فضول خرچی یا لاپروائی، بے حیائی یا بداخلاقی

englishMeaning: Lacking or absent; not present when needed. Not good enough; falling short of a required standard. Feeling or expressing a desire for something. Deficient in a particular quality.
synonyms: Lacking, Missing, Absent, Deficient, Inadequate, Insufficient, Desiring, Short
antonyms: Sufficient, Adequate, Complete, Present, Satisfactory, Ample, Full, Content
examples: The report was found wanting in several important details. Courage was the one quality he was never wanting in. She left the meeting wanting a clearer answer. Their hospitality left nothing wanting.
sindhiMeaning: غير حاضر يا موجود نه هجڻ، ضرورت مطابق نه هجڻ يا معيار تي پورو نه لهڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ جي خواهش رکندڙ، ڪنهن خاصيت ۾ گهٽتائي وارو
urduMeaning: موجود نہ ہونا یا کمی ہونا، معیار پر پورا نہ اترنا یا ناکافی ہونا، کسی چیز کی خواہش رکھنے والا، کسی خوبی میں کمی رکھنے والا

englishMeaning: To wish to enter a place, room, or building. To wish to join or become part of a group, organization, or activity. To desire involvement in a particular situation or deal.
synonyms: Wish to enter, Seek entry, Desire to join, Want in, Apply for, Seek admission
antonyms: Want out, Wish to leave, Withdraw, Refuse, Stay out, Exit
examples: The cat is scratching at the door because it wants into the house. He wants into the family business next year. Several investors want into the project before it launches. She knocked loudly, clearly wanting into the office.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن جاءِ  ڪمري يا عمارت ۾ داخل ٿيڻ جي خواهش ڪرڻ، ڪنهن گروهه  اداري يا سرگرميءَ ۾ شامل ٿيڻ جي خواهش رکڻ، ڪنهن معاملي يا سوديبازيءَ ۾ حصو وٺڻ چاهڻ
urduMeaning: کسی جگہ  کمرے یا عمارت میں داخل ہونے کی خواہش کرنا، کسی گروہ  ادارے یا سرگرمی میں شامل ہونے کی خواہش رکھنا، کسی معاملے یا سودے میں شریک ہونا چاہنا

englishMeaning: To wish to leave a place, room, or enclosed space. To wish to end one's involvement in a relationship, agreement, job, or situation. To desire release or escape from something unpleasant.
synonyms: Wish to leave, Quit, Withdraw, Back out, Pull out, Escape, Opt out, Resign
antonyms: Want in, Stay, Remain, Join, Commit, Continue, Persist
examples: The dog is barking at the door and wants out. After two difficult years, he simply wanted out of the marriage. Two partners want out of the deal before the deadline. She wanted out of the meeting as soon as it began.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن جاءِ يا بند هنڌ مان ٻاهر نڪرڻ جي خواهش ڪرڻ، ڪنهن رشتي  معاهدي  نوڪري يا معاملي مان نڪري وڃڻ چاهڻ، ڪنهن ناپسنديده صورتحال کان نجات گهرڻ
urduMeaning: کسی جگہ یا بند مقام سے باہر نکلنے کی خواہش کرنا، کسی رشتے  معاہدے  نوکری یا معاملے سے الگ ہونا چاہنا، کسی ناپسندیدہ صورتِ حال سے چھٹکارا چاہنا

englishMeaning: To lack or be without something that is needed. To be in need of a basic necessity. Used mainly in negative sentences to say that someone has everything they need.
synonyms: Lack, Need, Require, Be short of, Be deprived of, Miss, Go without
antonyms: Have, Possess, Enjoy, Be supplied with, Abound in, Own
examples: The children never wanted for anything while their grandfather was alive. He works hard so that his family will not want for food or shelter. Despite their simple life, they wanted for nothing. Many families in the region want for clean drinking water.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ضروري شيءِ جي کوٽ محسوس ڪرڻ يا ان کان محروم هجڻ، بنيادي ضرورت جي محتاجي هجڻ، عام طور نفي واري جملي ۾ چوڻ ته ڪنهن کي ڪنهن به شيءِ جي گهرج ناهي
urduMeaning: کسی ضروری چیز کی کمی ہونا یا اس سے محروم ہونا، بنیادی ضرورت کا محتاج ہونا، عام طور پر نفی کے جملے میں یہ ظاہر کرنا کہ کسی کو کسی چیز کی کمی نہیں

englishMeaning: To wish to come inside a place. To wish to be included in a plan, deal, group, or activity. To express eagerness to participate.
synonyms: Want into, Seek entry, Join, Participate, Be included, Sign up, Enter
antonyms: Want out, Opt out, Withdraw, Decline, Stay outside, Refuse
examples: The children are at the gate and want in. If the plan is really that profitable, I want in. He heard about the startup and immediately wanted in. She knocked twice to show that she wanted in.
sindhiMeaning: اندر اچڻ جي خواهش ڪرڻ، ڪنهن منصوبي  سودي  گروهه يا سرگرميءَ ۾ شامل ٿيڻ چاهڻ، حصو وٺڻ لاءِ آتو هجڻ
urduMeaning: اندر آنے کی خواہش کرنا، کسی منصوبے  سودے  گروہ یا سرگرمی میں شامل ہونا چاہنا، شرکت کے لیے بے تاب ہونا

englishMeaning: To wish to have something returned that was lost, lent, or taken away. To wish to return to a former place, job, or relationship. To desire the restoration of a previous situation.
synonyms: Reclaim, Demand return, Retrieve, Recover, Repossess, Ask for, Restore
antonyms: Give away, Relinquish, Surrender, Abandon, Forfeit, Let go
examples: I lent him my camera and now I want it back. She wants her old job back at the hospital. After the argument, he wanted her back in his life. The village wants back the land it lost years ago.
sindhiMeaning: وڃايل  اڌاري ڏنل يا کسيل شيءِ واپس گهرڻ، اڳوڻي جاءِ  نوڪري يا رشتي ڏانهن موٽڻ جي خواهش ڪرڻ، اڳوڻي حالت جي بحاليءَ جي خواهش رکڻ
urduMeaning: کھوئی ہوئی  ادھار دی گئی یا لی گئی چیز واپس مانگنا، سابقہ جگہ  نوکری یا رشتے میں لوٹنے کی خواہش کرنا، پہلی صورتِ حال کی بحالی چاہنا

englishMeaning: To wish to leave one's current club, team, or employer, especially in sport. To desire a transfer or move elsewhere.
synonyms: Seek a transfer, Wish to leave, Move on, Depart, Quit, Exit
antonyms: Stay, Remain, Sign on, Commit, Renew, Settle
examples: The striker wants away before the transfer window closes. Two senior players are said to want away this season. He made it clear in the interview that he wanted away. The manager refused to sell the midfielder even though he wanted away.
sindhiMeaning: پنهنجي موجوده ڪلب  ٽيم يا اداري کي ڇڏڻ جي خواهش ڪرڻ  خاص ڪري راندين ۾، ٻي جاءِ تي تبديلي يا منتقلي چاهڻ
urduMeaning: اپنے موجودہ کلب  ٹیم یا ادارے کو چھوڑنے کی خواہش کرنا  خاص طور پر کھیل میں، کسی اور جگہ منتقلی یا ٹرانسفر چاہنا

englishMeaning: To try to enjoy the benefits of two opposing situations or attitudes at the same time. To refuse to accept the drawbacks that come with a chosen position. To behave inconsistently in order to gain advantage from both sides.
synonyms: Have it both ways, Play both sides, Blow hot and cold, Sit on the fence, Hedge
antonyms: Choose one side, Take a stand, Commit, Accept the consequences, Be consistent
examples: You cannot want it both ways by demanding freedom and protection at once. The government wants it both ways on taxes and public spending. He wants it both ways, complaining about the rules while enjoying their benefits. Voters accused the party of wanting it both ways.
sindhiMeaning: هڪ ئي وقت ٻن مخالف صورتحالن جا فائدا وٺڻ جي ڪوشش ڪرڻ، پنهنجي چونڊيل موقف سان لاڳاپيل نقصان قبول ڪرڻ کان انڪار ڪرڻ، فائدي لاءِ ٻئي پاسا سنڀالڻ جي ڪوشش ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: ایک ہی وقت میں دو متضاد صورتوں کے فائدے حاصل کرنے کی کوشش کرنا، اپنے اختیار کردہ مؤقف کے نقصانات قبول کرنے سے انکار کرنا، فائدے کے لیے دونوں طرف کا ساتھ رکھنا

englishMeaning: To benefit from two conflicting choices, arguments, or situations at the same time. To avoid the disadvantages of a decision while keeping its advantages. To hold two inconsistent positions for personal gain.
synonyms: Want it both ways, Play both sides, Straddle the fence, Equivocate, Hedge one's bets
antonyms: Take sides, Decide, Commit, Be consistent, Accept the trade-off
examples: You can't have it both ways; either you join us or you stay home. He wants low prices and high wages, but nobody can have it both ways. The company tried to have it both ways with its environmental promises. Critics said the minister was attempting to have it both ways.
sindhiMeaning: هڪ ئي وقت ٻن مخالف ڳالهين يا صورتحالن مان فائدو وٺڻ، فيصلي جا نقصان ٽارڻ ۽ فائدا رکڻ، ذاتي مفاد لاءِ ٻه متضاد موقف رکڻ
urduMeaning: ایک ہی وقت میں دو متضاد باتوں یا صورتوں سے فائدہ اٹھانا، فیصلے کے نقصانات سے بچنا اور فوائد رکھنا، ذاتی مفاد کے لیے دو متضاد مؤقف رکھنا

englishMeaning: To wish to have no dealings, contact, or association with a person. To refuse to be involved with someone or something considered undesirable.
synonyms: Have no truck with, Avoid, Shun, Boycott, Steer clear of, Keep away from, Reject
antonyms: Associate with, Deal with, Befriend, Cooperate with, Welcome, Engage
examples: The old shopkeeper wants no truck with the new landlord. She wants no truck with people who spread rumours. Our team wants no truck with dishonest suppliers. He made it clear he wanted no truck with the scheme.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ماڻهوءَ سان ڪوبه واسطو، رابطو يا لاڳاپو نه رکڻ چاهڻ، ڪنهن ناپسنديده شخص يا شيءِ سان شامل ٿيڻ کان انڪار ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: کسی شخص سے کوئی واسطہ، رابطہ یا تعلق نہ رکھنا چاہنا، کسی ناپسندیدہ شخص یا چیز سے وابستگی سے انکار کرنا

englishMeaning: To have no dealings or relationship with a person. To refuse to accept, tolerate, or engage with someone or something. To keep completely apart from an idea or practice one disapproves of.
synonyms: Want no truck with, Shun, Avoid, Reject, Disown, Boycott, Have nothing to do with
antonyms: Engage with, Accept, Tolerate, Associate with, Support, Embrace
examples: He has no truck with gossip of any kind. The committee has no truck with members who break the rules. My grandmother had no truck with modern gadgets. They have no truck with anyone who cheats customers.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن سان ڪوبه واسطو يا لاڳاپو نه رکڻ، ڪنهن شخص يا ڳالهه کي قبول ڪرڻ يا برداشت ڪرڻ کان انڪار ڪرڻ، ناپسنديده خيال يا رواج کان بلڪل پري رهڻ
urduMeaning: کسی سے کوئی واسطہ یا تعلق نہ رکھنا، کسی شخص یا بات کو قبول یا برداشت کرنے سے انکار کرنا، ناپسندیدہ خیال یا رواج سے بالکل الگ رہنا

englishMeaning: To wish to get free from a person one finds troublesome or unwanted. To desire that someone leave, be dismissed, or be removed. To wish to end a connection with someone.
synonyms: Want shot of, Wish to remove, Get rid of, Dismiss, Expel, Oust, Be free of
antonyms: Keep, Retain, Welcome, Embrace, Hold on to, Reinstate
examples: The manager clearly wants rid of the new supervisor. They wanted rid of him long before he finally resigned. She wants rid of the tenant who never pays on time. Some board members want rid of the chairman.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن تنگ ڪندڙ يا اڻ گهربل ماڻهوءَ کان جان ڇڏائڻ چاهڻ، اهو گهرڻ ته ڪو هليو وڃي يا هٽايو وڃي، ڪنهن سان لاڳاپو ختم ڪرڻ جي خواهش رکڻ
urduMeaning: کسی تنگ کرنے والے یا ناپسندیدہ شخص سے جان چھڑانا چاہنا، یہ چاہنا کہ کوئی چلا جائے یا ہٹا دیا جائے، کسی سے تعلق ختم کرنے کی خواہش رکھنا

englishMeaning: Do not waste anything. The opening part of the proverb 'Waste not, want not', meaning that careful use of resources prevents future shortage. Used as advice to avoid extravagance.
synonyms: Save, Conserve, Economize, Be frugal, Use sparingly, Preserve
antonyms: Waste, Squander, Splurge, Throw away, Misuse, Be extravagant
examples: Waste not, and you will always have enough for tomorrow. My grandmother lived by the rule of waste not. Waste not the water you draw from the well. In hard times people learn to waste not.
sindhiMeaning: ڪجهه به ضايع نه ڪريو، چوڻي ’ضايع نه ڪريو ته محتاج نه ٿيندؤ‘ جو پهريون حصو، جنهن جو مطلب آهي ته وسيلن جو سنڀال سان استعمال اڳتي هلي کوٽ کان بچائي ٿو، فضول خرچيءَ کان بچڻ جي نصيحت
urduMeaning: کچھ ضائع نہ کرو، کہاوت ’ضائع نہ کرو تو محتاج نہ ہو گے‘ کا پہلا حصہ، یعنی وسائل کا سنبھال کر استعمال آئندہ کی تنگی سے بچاتا ہے، فضول خرچی سے بچنے کی نصیحت

englishMeaning: Do not suffer from shortage or need. The closing part of the proverb 'Waste not, want not', meaning that avoiding waste protects one from future need.
synonyms: Lack nothing, Be provided for, Have enough, Be secure, Be self-sufficient
antonyms: Want, Lack, Need, Go short, Be deprived, Suffer scarcity
examples: Waste not, want not, as my mother always reminded us. Those who save carefully will want not in old age. The saying ends with the promise that you will want not. Live simply and you will want not.
sindhiMeaning: محتاجي يا کوٽ ۾ نه پوڻ، چوڻي ’ضايع نه ڪريو ته محتاج نه ٿيندؤ‘ جو ٻيو حصو، جنهن جو مطلب آهي ته ضياع کان بچڻ ايندڙ ضرورت کان بچائي ٿو
urduMeaning: محتاجی یا کمی کا شکار نہ ہونا، کہاوت ’ضائع نہ کرو تو محتاج نہ ہو گے‘ کا دوسرا حصہ، یعنی ضیاع سے بچنا آئندہ کی ضرورت سے محفوظ رکھتا ہے

englishMeaning: To wish to withdraw from an agreement, arrangement, relationship, or commitment. To wish to leave a place or situation. To seek release from an obligation.
synonyms: Withdraw from, Back out of, Pull out of, Quit, Escape from, Opt out of, Exit
antonyms: Want into, Stay in, Commit to, Honour, Continue with, Join
examples: He wants out of the contract before the next payment is due. She wanted out of the argument as quickly as possible. Two members want out of the partnership. The player wants out of his current club.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن معاهدي  بندوبست  رشتي يا ذميواريءَ مان نڪرڻ جي خواهش ڪرڻ، ڪنهن جاءِ يا صورتحال مان نڪرڻ چاهڻ، ڪنهن فرض کان نجات گهرڻ
urduMeaning: کسی معاہدے  بندوبست  رشتے یا ذمہ داری سے نکلنے کی خواہش کرنا، کسی جگہ یا صورتِ حال سے نکلنا چاہنا، کسی پابندی سے رہائی چاہنا

englishMeaning: In need of something; lacking something that is required. Requiring attention, repair, or supply. Used in formal or literary style to express need.
synonyms: In need of, Lacking, Requiring, Short of, Deficient in, Craving, Deprived of
antonyms: Supplied with, Provided with, Full of, Having, Satisfied, Well stocked
examples: The old house is badly in want of repair. He is a man in want of good advice. The garden is in want of water after the long summer. Their argument is in want of solid evidence.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ جي ضرورت هئڻ يا ان جي کوٽ هئڻ، مرمت  سنڀال يا فراهميءَ جي گهرج هئڻ، رسمي يا ادبي انداز ۾ ضرورت ظاهر ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کی ضرورت ہونا یا اس کی کمی ہونا، مرمت  توجہ یا فراہمی کی حاجت ہونا، رسمی یا ادبی انداز میں ضرورت ظاہر کرنا

englishMeaning: To refuse to accept or take part in something. To reject an offer, idea, or behaviour completely. To make clear that one will not tolerate something.
synonyms: Have none of, Refuse, Reject, Decline, Turn down, Spurn, Repudiate
antonyms: Accept, Welcome, Embrace, Agree to, Take part in, Approve
examples: She wants none of their excuses this time. I want none of the money you made that way. The teacher wants none of that behaviour in her classroom. He wanted none of the credit for the success.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ کي قبول ڪرڻ يا ان ۾ حصو وٺڻ کان انڪار ڪرڻ، ڪنهن آڇ، خيال يا رويي کي مڪمل طور رد ڪرڻ، صاف چوڻ ته ڪا ڳالهه برداشت نه ٿيندي
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کو قبول کرنے یا اس میں شریک ہونے سے انکار کرنا، کسی پیشکش، خیال یا رویے کو مکمل طور پر مسترد کرنا، واضح کرنا کہ کوئی بات برداشت نہیں کی جائے گی

englishMeaning: To refuse to accept, allow, or tolerate something. To reject a suggestion, excuse, or behaviour firmly. To receive no share of something.
synonyms: Want none of, Refuse, Reject, Dismiss, Not tolerate, Turn down, Resist
antonyms: Accept, Allow, Tolerate, Agree to, Endorse, Share in
examples: I offered to pay, but he would have none of it. The committee will have none of this delay. She had none of the profits from the sale. Their father would have none of such rudeness at the table.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڳالهه کي قبول ڪرڻ، اجازت ڏيڻ يا برداشت ڪرڻ کان انڪار ڪرڻ، ڪنهن تجويز  بهاني يا رويي کي سختيءَ سان رد ڪرڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ مان ڪو حصو نه ملڻ
urduMeaning: کسی بات کو قبول کرنے، اجازت دینے یا برداشت کرنے سے انکار کرنا، کسی تجویز  بہانے یا رویے کو سختی سے مسترد کرنا، کسی چیز میں کوئی حصہ نہ ہونا

englishMeaning: The quality of being dull, ordinary, and lacking originality. A remark, idea, or thing that is boringly commonplace. The state of being predictable or unoriginal in thought or expression.
synonyms: Triteness, Dullness, Cliche, Platitude, Commonplace, Staleness, Ordinariness, Tedium
antonyms: Originality, Freshness, Novelty, Creativity, Inventiveness, Brilliance, Profundity
examples: The speech was full of banality and offered nothing new. She was tired of the banality of daily office conversation. Critics complained about the banality of the film's dialogue. His writing rises above the banality of ordinary travel books.
sindhiMeaning: بي مزي  عام ۽ اڻ نئين هجڻ جي حالت، اهڙي ڳالهه يا خيال جيڪو بلڪل عام ۽ بيزار ڪندڙ هجي، سوچ يا اظهار ۾ نواڻ جي کوٽ
urduMeaning: بے کیف  عام اور غیر اختراعی ہونے کی کیفیت، ایسی بات یا خیال جو بالکل عام اور بور کن ہو، سوچ یا اظہار میں جدت کی کمی

englishMeaning: Relating to the countries of the East, especially East and Southeast Asia, and their cultures. A style of art, design, or goods associated with the East. An old and now often offensive term for a person from East Asia.
synonyms: Eastern, Asian, Far Eastern, Asiatic, Eastward, Levantine
antonyms: Occidental, Western, European, American, Atlantic
examples: The museum has a fine collection of oriental ceramics. She decorated the room with oriental rugs and lanterns. Oriental spices give the dish its distinctive aroma. Many writers now avoid the word oriental when describing people.

antonyms: Acute angle, Obtuse angle, Reflex angle, Straight angle
examples: The walls meet at a right angle. Use a set square to draw a right angle. A rectangle has four right angles. The pipe was bent at a right angle.

antonyms: Acute-angled triangle, Obtuse-angled triangle, Equiangular triangle

urduMeaning: کسی کو غلطی سے کوئی اور سمجھ لینا، کسی کو کسی خاص انداز میں خیال کرنا، ایک شخص کو دوسرا سمجھ بیٹھنا، بغیر تصدیق کے کوئی بات مان لینا

englishMeaning: To become sick or unwell suddenly. To fall into illness. To be offended by something said or done. To receive a remark badly.
synonyms: Fall sick, Become ill, Sicken, Be taken unwell, Resent, Be offended, Take offence
antonyms: Recover, Get well, Stay healthy, Be pleased, Appreciate, Take kindly
examples: He took ill during the journey and had to return. She took ill soon after the wedding. Do not take it ill if I speak frankly. He took my advice ill and stopped talking to me.
sindhiMeaning: اوچتو بيمار ٿي پوڻ، بيماريءَ ۾ مبتلا ٿيڻ، ڪنهن ڳالهه تي ناراض ٿيڻ، ڪنهن جي ڳالهه کي خراب نموني وٺڻ
urduMeaning: اچانک بیمار ہو جانا، بیماری میں مبتلا ہونا، کسی بات پر ناراض ہونا، کسی کی بات کا برا مان جانا

englishMeaning: To take all or most of someone's money, often unfairly. To cheat or swindle a person out of a large sum. To defeat someone completely in a game, contest, or lawsuit. To cause someone heavy financial loss.
synonyms: Swindle, Fleece, Cheat, Defraud, Rip off, Con, Bankrupt, Trounce, Beat badly
antonyms: Compensate, Reimburse, Enrich, Repay, Deal fairly, Reward, Lose to
examples: The divorce settlement took him to the cleaners. Those online scammers took her to the cleaners. Our team was taken to the cleaners in the final. Be careful with that contract or they will take you to the cleaners.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کان سڀ پئسا ڦٻائي وٺڻ، ٺڳي ڪري وڏو نقصان پهچائڻ، ڪنهن کي مالي طور تباهه ڪري ڇڏڻ، مقابلي ۾ بري طرح شڪست ڏيڻ
urduMeaning: کسی سے سارے پیسے نکلوا لینا، دھوکہ دے کر بڑا نقصان پہنچانا، کسی کو مالی طور پر تباہ کر دینا، مقابلے میں بری طرح شکست دینا

englishMeaning: To begin to like someone or something. To start doing something as a habit. To go to a place for safety or escape. To adopt a new practice or way of life.
synonyms: Like, Grow fond of, Adopt, Begin, Resort to, Turn to, Take up, Warm to
antonyms: Dislike, Avoid, Abandon, Give up, Reject, Shun, Quit
examples: The children took to their new teacher at once. After his retirement he took to gardening. The villagers took to the hills when the flood came. She has taken to walking every morning before work.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي پسند ڪرڻ لڳڻ، ڪا ڳالهه عادت طور شروع ڪرڻ، بچاءَ لاءِ ڪنهن جاءِ ڏانهن وڃڻ، ڪو نئون طريقو يا زندگيءَ جو ڍنگ اختيار ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: کسی کو پسند کرنے لگنا، کوئی کام عادت کے طور پر شروع کر دینا، پناہ کے لیے کسی جگہ چلے جانا، کوئی نیا طریقہ یا طرزِ زندگی اپنانا

englishMeaning: To run away quickly, especially to escape danger. To flee in a hurry. To escape by running rather than facing a situation.
synonyms: Flee, Run away, Bolt, Escape, Dash off, Scamper, Take flight, Make off
antonyms: Stand firm, Stay, Face, Confront, Remain, Resist, Hold ground
examples: The thief took to his heels when the alarm rang. Seeing the police, the boys took to their heels. He took to his heels and disappeared into the crowd. The dog barked and the stranger took to his heels.
sindhiMeaning: تڪڙ ۾ ڀڄي وڃڻ، خاص ڪري خطري کان بچڻ لاءِ، جلدي ۾ فرار ٿيڻ، صورتحال کي منهن ڏيڻ بدران ڀڄي نڪرڻ
urduMeaning: تیزی سے بھاگ جانا، خاص طور پر خطرے سے بچنے کے لیے، جلدی میں فرار ہونا، صورتِ حال کا سامنا کرنے کے بجائے بھاگ نکلنا

englishMeaning: To criticise or scold someone for a fault. To call a person to account for wrongdoing. To reprimand firmly for careless or improper behaviour.
synonyms: Reprimand, Scold, Rebuke, Reproach, Censure, Chide, Admonish, Berate, Upbraid
antonyms: Praise, Commend, Applaud, Compliment, Encourage, Excuse, Overlook
examples: The manager took him to task for arriving late. She was taken to task for the errors in the report. Parents should take their children to task politely. The editor took the writer to task over false figures.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي غلطيءَ تي ڇنڊڇاڻ ڪرڻ يا جھڻڪڻ، ڪنهن کان ڪيل غلط ڪم جو حساب گهرڻ، لاپرواهي يا نامناسب رويي تي سختيءَ سان سرزنش ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: کسی کو غلطی پر ڈانٹنا یا سرزنش کرنا، کسی سے غلط کام کا جواب طلب کرنا، لاپروائی یا نامناسب رویّے پر سختی سے تنبیہ کرنا

word: Take with a grain or pinch of salt
englishMeaning: To accept a statement with doubt or reserve. To believe something only partly, allowing for exaggeration. To treat information cautiously rather than as full truth.
synonyms: Doubt, Question, Be sceptical, Distrust slightly, Treat cautiously, Not take literally
antonyms: Believe fully, Trust completely, Accept, Rely on, Take at face value

sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڳالهه کي شڪ سان قبول ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ڳالهه تي پورو ڀروسو نه ڪرڻ ۽ وڌاءَ جو خيال رکڻ، معلومات کي احتياط سان وٺڻ نه ڪي مڪمل سچ
urduMeaning: کسی بات کو شک کے ساتھ قبول کرنا، کسی بات پر پورا یقین نہ کرنا اور مبالغے کا خیال رکھنا، معلومات کو مکمل سچ کے بجائے احتیاط سے لینا

englishMeaning: To talk to someone for a very long time, often tiring or boring them. To speak at excessive length without letting the other person contribute.
synonyms: Chatter, Prattle, Ramble on, Jabber, Go on and on, Bore
antonyms: Keep quiet, Be brief, Stay silent, Listen, Hush
examples: My neighbour talked my ear off about his garden. She will talk your ear off if you let her start. He talked the poor clerk's ear off over one form. Be ready; that driver talks everyone's ear off.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن سان ايترو گهڻو ڳالهائڻ جو هو ٿڪجي پوي, ٻئي کي موقعو نه ڏيندي حد کان وڌيڪ ڳالهائڻ
urduMeaning: کسی سے اتنی زیادہ باتیں کرنا کہ وہ تھک جائے, دوسرے کو موقع نہ دیتے ہوئے بہت لمبی بات کرنا

englishMeaning: Fond of talking a great deal. Inclined to speak more than is necessary. Chatty and communicative by nature.
synonyms: Chatty, Garrulous, Loquacious, Communicative, Voluble, Gossipy, Conversational
antonyms: Quiet, Silent, Reserved, Taciturn, Reticent, Shy, Tight-lipped
examples: He becomes very talkative after a cup of tea. The talkative passenger kept everyone entertained. She is shy at first but soon grows talkative. A talkative child can be tiring at bedtime.
sindhiMeaning: گهڻو ڳالهائيندڙ, ڳالهائڻ جو شوقين, ٻڌ ٻڌ ڪندڙ, ڳالهڙيو
urduMeaning: بہت باتیں کرنے والا, باتونی, گفتگو کا شوقین, بک بک کرنے والا

englishMeaning: A record or count of a number of items, points, or scores. A mark used in counting, usually a stroke in groups of five. To count or calculate a total. To match or correspond with something else exactly.
synonyms: Count, Total, Record, Score, Reckoning, Match, Correspond, Compute, Agree
antonyms: Differ, Disagree, Conflict, Mismatch, Contradict
examples: He kept a tally of the runs scored in the match. Please tally the votes and announce the result. Her account of the incident does not tally with his. The final tally showed a clear victory for the team.
sindhiMeaning: ڳاڻاٽو، حساب، پوائنٽن يا شين جو رڪارڊ، ڳڻپ لاءِ نشان، ڳڻڻ يا جوڙ ڪڍڻ، ٻي شيءِ سان ميل کائڻ يا برابر هجڻ
urduMeaning: گنتی، حساب، پوائنٹس یا اشیاء کا ریکارڈ، گنتی کے لیے لگایا جانے والا نشان، شمار کرنا، دوسری چیز سے مطابقت رکھنا

englishMeaning: A straight line that touches a curve at a single point without crossing it. A completely different line of thought or action. The trigonometric function equal to the ratio of opposite to adjacent sides. Touching but not intersecting.
synonyms: Touching line, Contact line, Digression, Deviation, Tan (trigonometry)
antonyms: Secant, Chord, Relevant, On-topic, Perpendicular, Intersecting
examples: Draw a tangent to the circle at point P. The professor went off on a tangent during the lecture. Calculate the tangent of 45 degrees. The two circles are tangent to each other.
sindhiMeaning: هڪ سڌي لڪير جيڪا وکر کي رڳو هڪ نقطي تي ڇهي پر ڪٽي نه، سوچ يا عمل جي بلڪل مختلف طريقي، مثلثاتي فنڪشن جيڪو سامهون واري رخ جو ڀرسان واري رخ سان تناسب برابر هجي، ڇهڻ وارو پر ڪٽڻ نه وارو
urduMeaning: ایک سیدھی لکیر جو خم کو صرف ایک نقطے پر چھوئے لیکن کاٹے نہیں، سوچ یا عمل کی بالکل مختلف سمت، مثلثاتی فنکشن جو مخالف ضلع کا ملحقہ ضلع سے تناسب برابر ہو، چھونے والا لیکن کاٹنے نہ والا

englishMeaning: Two or more circles that touch each other at exactly one point without crossing. Circles that have a single common point of contact. Circles that are externally or internally tangent to each other.

antonyms: Intersecting circles, Overlapping circles, Separate circles, Non-touching circles
examples: Two tangent circles share only one point. The gears are designed as tangent circles. Tangent circles do not overlap or intersect. The diagram shows externally tangent circles.
sindhiMeaning: ٻه يا وڌيڪ دائرا جيڪي هڪ ٻئي کي بلڪل هڪ نقطي تي ڇهن پر ڪٽن نه، دائرا جن ۾ رابطي جو هڪ واحد گڏيل نقطو هجي، دائرا جيڪي هڪ ٻئي سان ٻاهران يا اندران ڇهندڙ هجن
urduMeaning: دو یا زیادہ دائرے جو ایک دوسرے کو بالکل ایک نقطے پر چھوئیں لیکن کاٹیں نہیں، دائرے جن میں رابطے کا ایک واحد مشترکہ نقطہ ہو، دائرے جو ایک دوسرے سے باہر سے یا اندر سے مماس ہوں

englishMeaning: Relating to or along a tangent. Touching a curve or surface at a single point without crossing it. Only slightly connected or related to the main subject. Diverging from a main point or course.
synonyms: Peripheral, Incidental, Divergent, Oblique, Irrelevant, Side, Digressive, Marginal
antonyms: Central, Direct, Relevant, Main, Essential, Perpendicular, Core, Focused
examples: The line is tangential to the circle at point A. His remarks were tangential to the main discussion. The professor made a tangential comment about history. The tangential velocity increases with distance from the center.
sindhiMeaning: ڇهڻ واري لڪير سان لاڳاپيل، ڪنهن وکر يا مٿاڇري کي رڳو هڪ نقطي تي ڇهڻ وارو، بنيادي موضوع سان معمولي تعلق رکڻ وارو، مکيه نقطي کان ڀڄڻ وارو
urduMeaning: مماس سے متعلق، کسی خم یا سطح کو صرف ایک نقطے پر چھونے والا، بنیادی موضوع سے معمولی تعلق رکھنے والا، اصل نکتے سے ہٹنے والا

englishMeaning: A quadrilateral whose four sides are all tangent to one inscribed circle. A four-sided figure that circumscribes a circle. A quadrilateral in which the sums of the two pairs of opposite sides are equal. Also known as a circumscribed or tangent quadrilateral.
synonyms: Circumscribed quadrilateral, Tangent quadrilateral, Circumscriptible quadrilateral
antonyms: Cyclic quadrilateral, Inscribed quadrilateral, Irregular quadrilateral
examples: In a tangential quadrilateral the sums of opposite sides are equal. A rhombus is always a tangential quadrilateral. The circle inside a tangential quadrilateral is called the incircle. He constructed a tangential quadrilateral around a given circle.

urduMeaning: وہ رباعی جس کے چاروں اضلاع ایک اندرونی دائرے کو مس کرتے ہیں, وہ چار اضلاع والی شکل جو دائرے کو گھیرتی ہے, وہ رباعی جس میں مقابل اضلاع کے دو جوڑوں کے مجموعے برابر ہوتے ہیں, جسے محیطی یا مماسی رباعی بھی کہا جاتا ہے

englishMeaning: A dark greyish brown colour. A neutral shade between grey and brown, often used in fashion and interiors. Of or having this muted brownish grey colour.
synonyms: Greyish brown, Mushroom, Beige, Fawn, Stone, Neutral, Dun
antonyms: Bright, Vivid, Bold, Colourful, White, Black

englishMeaning: Stretched or pulled tight, not slack. Showing tension, strain, or anxiety. Kept in good order and under firm control. Written or expressed concisely with no wasted words.

antonyms: Slack, Loose, Relaxed, Limp, Flabby, Baggy

urduMeaning: کھنچا ہوا یا تنا ہوا، ڈھیلا نہیں، تناؤ یا پریشانی ظاہر کرنے والا، مضبوط نظم و ضبط میں، مختصر اور جامع انداز میں لکھا ہوا

englishMeaning: Meanings that are present in great abundance. Senses of a word that are numerous and overflowing. A wealth of interpretations carried by a single expression.

antonyms: Single meaning, Literal sense, Plain meaning, Emptiness, Ambiguity-free sense

sindhiMeaning: اهڙا مطلب جيڪي وڏي تعداد ۾ موجود هجن، لفظ جا ڪيترائي ۽ ڀرپور مطلب، هڪ ئي جملي مان نڪرندڙ گهڻن مطلبن جي فراواني

englishMeaning: The speed or pace at which a piece of music is played. The rate or speed of motion or activity. The characteristic rhythm or pattern of an activity. The general pace or timing of something.

englishMeaning: Relating to worldly rather than spiritual matters. Connected with or limited by time. Relating to the temples of the head. Lasting for a limited time rather than eternal. Secular or non-religious in nature.
