sindhiMeaning: روحاني معاملن جي بجاءِ دنياوي معاملن سان لاڳاپيل، وقت سان ڳنڍيل يا محدود، مٿي جي مندرن سان لاڳاپيل، ابدي جي بجاءِ محدود وقت لاءِ رهندڙ، فطرت ۾ سيڪيولر يا غير مذهبي
urduMeaning: روحانی معاملات کی بجائے دنیاوی معاملات سے متعلق، وقت سے جڑا ہوا یا محدود، سر کے مندروں سے متعلق، ابدی کی بجائے محدود وقت کے لیے رہنے والا، فطرت میں سیکولر یا غیر مذہبی

englishMeaning: For a limited period of time, not permanently. In a way that lasts for only a short time. For the time being or in the meantime. Until something more permanent is arranged. Not lasting or intended to last indefinitely.
synonyms: Briefly, Momentarily, Short-term, Provisionally, For now, For the time being, Transiently
antonyms: Permanently, Forever, Indefinitely, Long-term, Continually, Constantly, Always
examples: The road is temporarily closed for repairs. She is temporarily staying with her parents. The office will be temporarily relocated during renovations. His vision was temporarily blurred after the accident.
sindhiMeaning: محدود عرصي لاءِ، مستقل طور تي نه، اهڙي طريقي سان جيڪو صرف ٿورڙي وقت لاءِ هلي، في الوقت يا ان وچ ۾، جيستائين ڪجهه وڌيڪ مستقل ترتيب نه ڏني وڃي، نه رهڻ وارو يا اڻڄاتل وقت تائين رهڻ جو ارادو
urduMeaning: محدود عرصے کے لیے، مستقل طور پر نہیں، ایسے طریقے سے جو صرف تھوڑے وقت کے لیے رہے، فی الوقت یا اس درمیان میں، جب تک کچھ زیادہ مستقل ترتیب نہ دیا جائے، نہ رہنے والا یا نامعلوم وقت تک رہنے کا ارادہ

englishMeaning: The quality or state of being temporary or lasting for only a limited time. The characteristic of not being permanent. The condition of being transient or short-lived. The nature of existing for a brief period.
synonyms: Impermanence, Transience, Brevity, Ephemerality, Fleetingness, Short-livedness, Instability
antonyms: Permanence, Durability, Stability, Longevity, Constancy, Endurance, Perpetuity
examples: The temporariness of life makes every moment precious. She accepted the temporariness of her living situation. The temporariness of the job made him keep searching for something permanent. We must embrace the temporariness of all worldly things.
sindhiMeaning: عارضي هجڻ يا صرف محدود وقت لاءِ رهڻ جو معيار يا حالت، مستقل نه هجڻ جي خاصيت، عارضي يا مختصر عرصي واري هجڻ جي حالت، مختصر عرصي لاءِ موجود هجڻ جي طبيعت
urduMeaning: عارضی ہونے یا صرف محدود وقت کے لیے رہنے کا معیار یا حالت، مستقل نہ ہونے کی خاصیت، عارضی یا قلیل المدتی ہونے کی حالت، مختصر عرصے کے لیے موجود ہونے کی نوعیت

englishMeaning: Using very few words; brief and to the point. Short in a way that seems rude or unfriendly. Expressed in a compact and economical style. Abrupt and lacking warmth in speech or writing.
synonyms: Brief, Concise, Curt, Succinct, Laconic, Pithy, Blunt, Abrupt
antonyms: Verbose, Lengthy, Wordy, Rambling, Long-winded, Polite, Elaborate
examples: His reply was terse and left no room for discussion. She sent a terse message saying only that she was busy. The manager gave a terse account of the incident. I was surprised by his terse manner on the phone.
sindhiMeaning: مختصر ۽ سڌو سنئون، ٿورن لفظن ۾ ڳالهه ڪندڙ، اهڙو جواب جيڪو مختصر هجڻ سبب اڻ وڻندڙ لڳي، جامع ۽ بي جا لفظن کان خالي، رکو ۽ بي مروت انداز
urduMeaning: مختصر اور دو ٹوک، کم الفاظ میں بات کہنے والا، ایسا جواب جو مختصر ہونے کے باعث رُوکھا لگے، جامع اور غیر ضروری الفاظ سے پاک، سپاٹ اور بے مروت انداز

englishMeaning: In a brief and direct manner using few words. In a short way that may sound abrupt or unfriendly. Concisely and without unnecessary detail. Curtly, with little politeness or explanation.
synonyms: Briefly, Concisely, Curtly, Bluntly, Succinctly, Abruptly, Laconically
antonyms: Verbosely, At length, Politely, Elaborately, Wordily, Expansively
examples: He answered tersely and returned to his work. The spokesman tersely denied the allegations. She tersely told them the meeting was over. The note was written tersely, without any greeting.
sindhiMeaning: مختصر ۽ سڌي انداز ۾، ٿورن لفظن سان، رکي نموني، بنا اضافي تفصيل جي، بي مروتيءَ سان جواب ڏيندي
urduMeaning: مختصر اور دو ٹوک انداز میں، کم الفاظ کے ساتھ، رُوکھے پن سے، غیر ضروری تفصیل کے بغیر، بے مروتی سے جواب دیتے ہوئے

englishMeaning: The quality of using very few words. Brevity of expression in speech or writing. Abruptness that can seem unfriendly. Economy of language that leaves out all unnecessary detail.
synonyms: Brevity, Conciseness, Succinctness, Curtness, Bluntness, Pithiness
antonyms: Verbosity, Wordiness, Prolixity, Long-windedness, Elaboration
examples: The terseness of his reply surprised everyone. Her writing is admired for its terseness and clarity. There was a certain terseness in the official statement. He apologised for the terseness of his earlier email.
sindhiMeaning: اختصار، ٿورن لفظن ۾ ڳالهه ڪرڻ جي خاصيت، ڳالهائڻ يا لکڻ ۾ جامعيت، رکائپ جيڪا بي مروت لڳي، غير ضروري تفصيل کان پاڪ انداز
urduMeaning: اختصار، کم الفاظ میں بات کہنے کی خوبی، گفتگو یا تحریر میں جامعیت، رُوکھا پن جو بے مروت محسوس ہو، غیر ضروری تفصیل سے پاک اندازِ بیان

englishMeaning: A fourteen-sided polygon with fourteen angles. A geometric shape with fourteen straight sides and fourteen vertices. Any flat shape with fourteen corners and fourteen edges.
synonyms: Fourteen-sided polygon, Tetrakaidecagon, Tetradecagonal shape, Fourteen-gon
antonyms: Circle, Triangle, Square, Simple shape, Irregular shape
examples: A regular tetradecagon has fourteen equal sides and angles. The decorative plate featured a tetradecagonal border. Mathematicians study the symmetry properties of tetradecagons. The pavilion was built with a tetradecagonal base.
sindhiMeaning: چوڏهن رخن ۽ چوڏهن ڪنڊن وارو هڪ شڪل، چوڏهه سڌي پاسن ۽ چوڏهه نقطن وارو جيوميٽري شڪل، چوڏهه ڪنڊن ۽ چوڏهه ڪنارن وارو ڪو به برابر شڪل
urduMeaning: چودہ اضلاع اور چودہ زاویوں والی شکل، چودہ سیدھی اطراف اور چودہ نقاط والی ہندسی شکل، چودہ کونوں اور چودہ کناروں والی کوئی بھی چپٹی شکل

englishMeaning: A three-dimensional solid with four triangular faces. A polyhedron with four vertices, six edges, and four faces. The simplest form of pyramid with a triangular base. A regular tetrahedron has all faces as equilateral triangles.
synonyms: Triangular pyramid, Four-faced polyhedron, Triangular-based pyramid
antonyms: Cube, Sphere, Prism, Many-faced polyhedron
examples: A tetrahedron is the simplest polyhedron. A regular tetrahedron has four identical faces. The molecular structure forms a tetrahedron. Calculate the volume of the tetrahedron.
sindhiMeaning: ٽن طرفن وارو ٺوس شڪل جنهن ۾ چار مثلثي منهن هجن، هڪ ڪثير السطوح جنهن ۾ چار نقطا  ڇهه ڪنارا ۽ چار منهن هجن، هرم جو سڀ کان سادو روپ جنهن جو مثلثي بنياد هجي، هڪ باقاعده ٽيٽراهيڊرون جا سڀ منهن برابر پاسن وارا مثلث هوندا آهن
urduMeaning: تین جہتی ٹھوس شکل جس میں چار مثلثی چہرے ہوں، ایک کثیر السطوح جس میں چار نقاط  چھ کنارے اور چار چہرے ہوں، اہرام کی سب سے سادہ شکل جس کی مثلثی بنیاد ہو، ایک باقاعدہ ٹیٹراہیڈرون کے تمام چہرے مساوی الاضلاع مثلث ہوتے ہیں

englishMeaning: An inherited blood disorder characterized by abnormal hemoglobin production. A genetic condition causing reduced oxygen-carrying capacity in blood. A disease resulting in anemia of varying severity. A hereditary disorder common in Mediterranean, Middle Eastern, and Asian populations.
synonyms: Hereditary anemia, Genetic blood disorder, Mediterranean anemia, Cooley's anemia
antonyms: Normal hemoglobin, Healthy blood, Non-thalassemic
examples: Thalassemia is an inherited genetic disorder. She requires regular blood transfusions due to thalassemia. Thalassemia carriers may have mild anemia. Genetic counseling is recommended for thalassemia families.
sindhiMeaning: هڪ موروثي رت جي خرابي جنهن ۾ غير معمولي هيموگلوبن جي پيداوار شامل آهي، هڪ جينياتي حالت جيڪا رت ۾ آڪسيجن کڻڻ جي صلاحيت کي گهٽائي، هڪ بيماري جنهن جو نتيجو مختلف شدت جي خون جي گهٽتائي آهي، هڪ موروثي خرابي جيڪا ميڊيٽرينين، وچ اوڀر ۽ ايشيائي آبادي ۾ عام آهي
urduMeaning: ایک موروثی خون کی خرابی جس میں غیر معمولی ہیموگلوبن کی پیداوار شامل ہے، ایک جینیاتی حالت جو خون میں آکسیجن لے جانے کی صلاحیت کو کم کرے، ایک بیماری جس کا نتیجہ مختلف شدت کی خون کی کمی ہے، ایک موروثی خرابی جو بحیرہ روم، مشرق وسطیٰ اور ایشیائی آبادیوں میں عام ہے

englishMeaning: A decisive trial that proves the true value or quality of something. A situation that shows whether a person or thing is genuine. The final proof of worth or ability. A conclusive test of success.
synonyms: Decisive test, Crucial trial, Litmus test, Proof, Ordeal, Touchstone, Trial, Benchmark
antonyms: Rough guess, Trivial test, Preliminary trial, Formality, Assumption
examples: The next election will be the acid test for the new party. The acid test of a teacher is how weak students improve. This match is the acid test of their training. Real friendship faces its acid test in bad times.
sindhiMeaning: اهڙي فيصلي ڪن آزمائش جيڪا ڪنهن شيءِ جي اصل قدر يا معيار کي ظاهر ڪري، اهڙي صورتحال جيڪا سچائي پرکي، لياقت يا قابليت جو حتمي ثبوت، ڪاميابيءَ جي پڪي پرک
urduMeaning: ایسی فیصلہ کن آزمائش جو کسی چیز کی اصل قدر یا معیار ظاہر کرے، ایسی صورتِ حال جو کھرے اور کھوٹے میں فرق کر دے، صلاحیت یا قابلیت کا حتمی ثبوت، کامیابی کی قطعی جانچ

englishMeaning: The overall weight of the available evidence when both sides are compared. A judgment about which side of an argument is supported by stronger evidence. The greater probability suggested by considering all the facts together.
synonyms: Weight of evidence, Preponderance of evidence, Overall proof, Body of evidence
antonyms: Lack of evidence, Insufficient proof, Inconclusive evidence, Doubt
examples: The balance of evidence suggests that the treatment is effective. On the balance of evidence, the committee accepted the researcher's conclusions. Scientists weighed the balance of evidence before issuing their report. The balance of evidence points to human activity as the main cause of climate change.
sindhiMeaning: ٻنهي پاسن جي شاهدين جو مجموعي وزن، ڪهڙي پاسي جون شاهديون وڌيڪ مضبوط آهن ان جو فيصلو، سڀني حقيقتن کي نظر ۾ رکي وڌيڪ امڪان
urduMeaning: دونوں فریقوں کے شواہد کا مجموعی وزن، کس فریق کے شواہد زیادہ مضبوط ہیں اس کا فیصلہ، تمام حقائق کو مدنظر رکھتے ہوئے زیادہ امکان

englishMeaning: The likelihood that something is more probably true than not. A legal standard of proof used in civil cases, meaning more likely than not. The greater chance of one explanation being correct when compared with another.
synonyms: Likelihood, Greater probability, Preponderance of probability, More likely than not
antonyms: Beyond reasonable doubt, Improbability, Unlikelihood, Certainty
examples: On the balance of probability, the court found the company responsible. The judge ruled that, on the balance of probability, the accident was caused by negligence. In civil cases, claims are decided on the balance of probability. The balance of probability suggests the missing documents were destroyed.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڳالهه جي صحيح هجڻ جو وڌيڪ امڪان، سول ڪيسن ۾ ثبوت جو قانوني معيار، هڪ تشريح جي صحيح هجڻ جو ٻئي جي مقابلي ۾ وڌيڪ امڪان
urduMeaning: کسی بات کے درست ہونے کا زیادہ امکان، سول مقدمات میں ثبوت کا قانونی معیار، ایک تشریح کے درست ہونے کا دوسری کے مقابلے میں زیادہ امکان

englishMeaning: An informal expression for an excellent person or thing. Used of someone who thinks very highly of themselves.
synonyms: The best, Excellent, First-rate, The bee's knees, Outstanding, Superb
antonyms: Mediocre, Poor, Second-rate, Ordinary, Inferior
examples: He thinks he is the cat's whiskers since his promotion. That new camera is the cat's whiskers. In her red dress she felt like the cat's whiskers. Their new stadium is the cat's whiskers.

englishMeaning: A time very long ago that is hard to remember clearly. A period in the far past that now seems vague. Long-ago times that are only faintly recalled. Used humorously to talk about something that happened many years ago.
synonyms: Long ago, Ancient times, Bygone days, Olden days, Yesteryear, Antiquity
antonyms: The present, Recent times, Nowadays, The near past, Today
examples: Those events belong to the dim and distant past. In the dim and distant past, people travelled by horse. He talked about his school days as if they were the dim and distant past. Such customs faded away in the dim and distant past.
sindhiMeaning: تمام گهڻو اڳ جو زمانو، اهو ماضي جيڪو چٽيءَ طرح ياد نه هجي، ڏورانهون ۽ ڌنڌلو ماضي
urduMeaning: بہت پرانا زمانہ، وہ ماضی جو واضح طور پر یاد نہ ہو، دور اور دھندلا ماضی

englishMeaning: Natural human sympathy, care, and compassion for others. A kind and gentle nature that shows itself in generosity. The instinctive tenderness that people feel towards one another. Warm-heartedness and goodwill towards fellow human beings.
synonyms: Compassion, Kindness, Humanity, Benevolence, Tenderness, Sympathy
antonyms: Cruelty, Callousness, Hard-heartedness, Malice, Indifference, Ruthlessness
examples: She is full of the milk of human kindness and never refuses to help. The disaster brought out the milk of human kindness in the whole city. He seems harsh, but there is the milk of human kindness in him. Their charity work shows the milk of human kindness.
sindhiMeaning: انسان جي فطري نرمي ۽ همدردي، ٻين لاءِ رحمدلي ۽ سخاوت، دل جي نرمي جيڪا ڀلائي ۾ ظاهر ٿئي، انسانن جي هڪ ٻئي لاءِ محبت ۽ خيرخواهي
urduMeaning: انسان کی فطری نرمی اور ہمدردی، دوسروں کے لیے رحم دلی اور فیاضی، دل کی نرمی جو بھلائی میں ظاہر ہو، انسانوں کی ایک دوسرے کے لیے محبت اور خیرخواہی

englishMeaning: The pleasant feeling and rewards that come with achieving success. The enjoyment of fame, wealth, or recognition after hard work. The attractive sense of triumph experienced after winning.
synonyms: Taste of victory, Glory, Triumph, Fame, Acclaim, Recognition
antonyms: Bitter taste of defeat, Humiliation, Failure, Disgrace
examples: After years of struggle, she finally enjoyed the sweet smell of success. The team savoured the sweet smell of success in the dressing room. He wrote about the sweet smell of success in his memoir. Winning the contract gave them the sweet smell of success.
sindhiMeaning: ڪاميابيءَ جو مٺو مزو ۽ لطف، محنت کان پوءِ شهرت ۽ دولت جو احساس، فتح جي خوشي ۽ سرور
urduMeaning: کامیابی کا میٹھا لطف اور مزہ، محنت کے بعد شہرت اور دولت کا احساس، فتح کی خوشی اور سرشاری

englishMeaning: The time when one century ends and the next begins. The years just before and after a change of century. A period marking the transition between two centuries. Around the year that closes or opens a century.
synonyms: Century's end, Century's beginning, Transitional period, Turning point of an era
antonyms: Mid-century, Middle of the era, Present day
examples: The factory was built at the turn of the century. At the turn of the century, travel by ship was common. Fashion changed greatly at the turn of the century. The novel is set at the turn of the century in Lahore.
sindhiMeaning: صديءَ جي تبديليءَ جو وقت، هڪ صدي پوري ٿيڻ ۽ ٻي شروع ٿيڻ جو زمانو، صدين جي وچ وارو دور
urduMeaning: صدی کے بدلنے کا وقت، ایک صدی کے اختتام اور دوسری کے آغاز کا زمانہ، صدیوں کے درمیان کا دور

englishMeaning: The time when one year ends and the next begins. The period around New Year. The changeover between two calendar years. Late December and early January.
synonyms: New Year, Year's end, Year's beginning, Changeover of years
antonyms: Mid-year, Middle of the year, Any other season
examples: The project will begin at the turn of the year. Sales usually rise at the turn of the year. They returned home at the turn of the year. Prices are expected to change at the turn of the year.
sindhiMeaning: سال جي تبديليءَ جو وقت، نئين سال جي شروعات وارو زمانو، هڪ سال پورو ٿيڻ ۽ ٻئي جي شروعات جو عرصو
urduMeaning: سال کے بدلنے کا وقت، نئے سال کے آغاز کا زمانہ، ایک سال کے اختتام اور دوسرے کے آغاز کا عرصہ

englishMeaning: A system of government in which religious leaders rule in the name of God or a deity. A state governed according to religious law and the guidance of clerics. A country or society where political authority and religious authority are combined in the same institution.
synonyms: Religious rule, Clerical government, Hierocracy, Divine rule, Ecclesiastical state
antonyms: Democracy, Secular state, Republic, Atheocracy, Civil government
examples: The country was ruled as a theocracy for several centuries. In a theocracy, religious law shapes every state policy. Historians compared the ancient theocracy with modern democracies. Critics warned that the reforms could turn the state into a theocracy.
sindhiMeaning: اهڙي حڪومت جنهن ۾ مذهبي اڳواڻ خدا جي نالي تي حڪمراني ڪن, مذهبي قانون موجب هلندڙ رياست, ديني ۽ سياسي اقتدار جو ميلاپ, ملائيت جي بنياد تي قائم نظام حڪومت
urduMeaning: ایسا نظام حکومت جس میں مذہبی رہنما خدا کے نام پر حکمرانی کریں, مذہبی قانون کے مطابق چلنے والی ریاست, دینی اور سیاسی اقتدار کا اجتماع, مذہبی پیشوائیت پر مبنی حکومت

englishMeaning: A ruler or leader who governs in the name of God or a religion. A person who supports or belongs to a system of religious government. A member of a ruling class made up of priests or clerics.
synonyms: Religious ruler, Cleric, Priest-ruler, Hierarch, Spiritual leader
antonyms: Democrat, Secularist, Republican, Liberal, Civil leader
examples: The theocrat justified every law by quoting scripture. Power in that era rested with a small circle of theocrats. He was accused of behaving like a theocrat rather than a statesman. The theocrats resisted every attempt at secular reform.
sindhiMeaning: اهو حڪمران جيڪو خدا يا مذهب جي نالي تي حڪومت ڪري, مذهبي حڪومت جو حامي, ديني اڳواڻن جي طبقي جو فرد, ملائيت جو علمبردار
urduMeaning: وہ حکمران جو خدا یا مذہب کے نام پر حکومت کرے, مذہبی حکومت کا حامی, دینی پیشواؤں کے طبقے کا فرد, مذہبی اقتدار کا علمبردار

englishMeaning: Relating to a government ruled by religious leaders or religious law. Describing a state in which political power is exercised in the name of a deity. Having the characteristics of a theocracy.
synonyms: Religious, Clerical, Ecclesiastical, Priestly, Hierocratic
antonyms: Secular, Democratic, Civil, Liberal, Non-religious
examples: The country adopted a theocratic constitution after the revolution. Theocratic rule left little space for political opposition. Historians studied the theocratic structure of the ancient kingdom. Critics called the proposed law theocratic in spirit.
sindhiMeaning: مذهبي حڪومت سان لاڳاپيل, اهڙي رياست جيڪا ديني قانون تحت هلي, ملائي نظام سان تعلق رکندڙ, خدائي حڪمرانيءَ جي دعويٰ ڪندڙ
urduMeaning: مذہبی حکومت سے متعلق, ایسی ریاست جو دینی قانون کے تحت چلے, مذہبی نظام حکومت سے تعلق رکھنے والا, خدائی حکمرانی کا دعویٰ کرنے والا

englishMeaning: A precision surveying instrument used to measure horizontal and vertical angles. An optical device mounted on a tripod and used by surveyors and engineers to map land and set out construction work. A telescope-based tool essential in civil engineering and geodesy.
synonyms: Surveying instrument, Transit, Level, Measuring device, Geodetic tool
antonyms: Guesswork, Estimation, Naked-eye measurement
examples: The surveyor set up his theodolite at the corner of the plot. A theodolite gives far more accurate readings than a simple compass. Students learned to level a theodolite during the field class. The engineer used a theodolite to mark the road alignment.
sindhiMeaning: زمين ماپڻ وارو هڪ درست اوزار, افقي ۽ عمودي زاوين کي ماپڻ وارو آلو, انجنيئرن ۽ سروير جي ڪم ايندڙ دوربين وارو اوزار, ٽنگڻي تي رکيل ماپ جو آلو
urduMeaning: زمین کی پیمائش کا ایک درست آلہ, افقی اور عمودی زاویے ناپنے والا آلہ, انجینئروں اور سرویئروں کے کام آنے والا دوربین نما اوزار, تپائی پر نصب پیمائشی آلہ

englishMeaning: A mathematical statement that has been proven based on previously established statements. A general proposition not self-evident but proved by reasoning. A rule or principle in mathematics or logic. A formula or result that can be demonstrated as true.
synonyms: Mathematical principle, Proven statement, Formula, Proposition, Rule, Axiom (when proven)
antonyms: Conjecture, Hypothesis, Assumption, Unproven claim, Theory

englishMeaning: To carve or shape wood by cutting small pieces from it with a knife. To cut thin slices from a piece of wood as a pastime. To reduce something gradually in size, amount, or number. To pare down step by step.

antonyms: Build up, Increase, Add to, Expand, Enlarge, Augment, Accumulate
examples: He sat on the porch whittling a small wooden bird. The old man whittled a walking stick from a branch. They whittled the shortlist to five candidates. Rising costs have whittled our savings.
sindhiMeaning: چاقوءَ سان ڪاٺ ڪوري شڪل ڏيڻ، ننڍا ٽڪرا ڪٽي ڪاٺ گھڙڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ کي آهستي آهستي گھٽائڻ، ٿورو ٿورو ڪري ڪٽڻ

englishMeaning: To reduce something slowly and steadily until little remains. To wear down a quantity, right, or advantage bit by bit. To gradually destroy or erode something over time. To spend time idly cutting wood.
synonyms: Erode, Reduce, Diminish, Wear down, Eat away, Deplete, Chip away, Undermine
antonyms: Strengthen, Increase, Build up, Preserve, Boost, Restore, Reinforce
examples: Inflation has whittled away the value of their pension. New rules slowly whittled away workers' rights. His confidence was whittled away by constant criticism. The lead was whittled away in the final minutes.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ کي آهستي آهستي گھٽائيندي ختم ڪري ڇڏڻ، ٿورو ٿورو ڪري ڪمزور ڪرڻ، وقت سان گڏ حق يا فائدو ختم ڪرڻ، رفتي رفتي زوال آڻڻ
urduMeaning: کسی چیز کو آہستہ آہستہ کم کرتے ہوئے ختم کر دینا، تھوڑا تھوڑا کر کے کمزور کرنا، وقت کے ساتھ حق یا فائدہ ختم کرنا، رفتہ رفتہ زوال لانا

englishMeaning: Used to ask about the identity of a person or people. Used to introduce a clause that gives more information about a person. Referring to the person or people mentioned earlier. The subject form used for people in questions and clauses.
synonyms: Whoever, Which person, That, Whosoever
antonyms: None (function word), Whom (object form), No one
examples: Who is standing at the door right now? The man who helped us was a retired teacher. Nobody knew who had left the message. Who wants to join the trip on Sunday?
sindhiMeaning: ڪير، ڪنهن شخص جي سڃاڻپ بابت سوال ڪرڻ وارو لفظ، جيڪو، جنهن شخص، اڳ ۾ ذڪر ٿيل ماڻهوءَ بابت وڌيڪ ڄاڻ ڏيندڙ لفظ

englishMeaning: The object form of 'who', used to refer to the person receiving the action. Used in formal English after verbs and prepositions. Used to ask which person is affected by an action. Introducing a clause about a person as the object.
synonyms: Which person, That, Whomsoever
antonyms: Who (subject form), None (function word), No one
examples: To whom should I address this letter? The candidate whom we interviewed was very impressive. She is the person with whom I shared the office. Whom did they finally select for the position?

urduMeaning: کس کو، جس کو، 'who' کی مفعولی شکل، رسمی انگریزی میں فعل یا حرف جار کے بعد استعمال ہونے والا لفظ

englishMeaning: Used to ask who something belongs to. Showing possession or ownership by a person. Used to introduce a clause describing something belonging to someone. The possessive form of 'who' and sometimes of 'which'.
synonyms: Of whom, Belonging to whom, Of which
antonyms: None (function word), Nobody's, Unowned
examples: Whose bag has been left on the table? The writer whose novel won the prize will speak tonight. She met a family whose children study abroad. Whose turn is it to present the report?
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن جو، ڪنهن جي، جنهن جو، ملڪيت يا تعلق ظاهر ڪندڙ لفظ، 'who' جي ملڪيتي صورت
urduMeaning: کس کا، کس کی، جس کا، ملکیت یا تعلق ظاہر کرنے والا لفظ، 'who' کی ملکیتی شکل

englishMeaning: An opinion or idea accepted by a large number of people. A view that is common within a society or group. A popular assumption that may or may not be true. Conventional wisdom shared by the majority.
synonyms: Common belief, Popular opinion, Conventional wisdom, General view, Received wisdom, Consensus, Prevailing notion
antonyms: Rare view, Minority opinion, Heresy, Unpopular idea, Fringe theory, Dissent
examples: It is a widely held belief that breakfast is the most important meal. The study challenged a widely held belief about memory. That widely held belief has little scientific support. Many widely held beliefs change as knowledge grows.
sindhiMeaning: عام طور تي مڃيل خيال يا عقيدو، گهڻن ماڻهن ۾ رائج راءِ، اهڙو مفروضو جيڪو مشهور هجي پر ضروري ناهي سچو هجي، اڪثريت جي گڏيل سوچ
urduMeaning: عام طور پر تسلیم شدہ خیال یا عقیدہ، بہت سے لوگوں میں رائج رائے، ایسا مفروضہ جو مشہور ہو مگر ضروری نہیں کہ درست ہو، اکثریت کی مشترکہ سوچ

englishMeaning: A clever or deceitful trick used to persuade or trap someone. Cunning behaviour intended to deceive. To lure or entice someone by cleverness or charm. To pass time pleasantly, often in the form 'wile away'.

examples: He used every wile he knew to get out of the punishment. The old trader was famous for his wiles in the marketplace. She wiled him into signing the papers without reading them. The feminine wiles of the character drive the whole play.
sindhiMeaning: چالاڪي يا ٺڳيءَ وارو حيلو، دوکو ڏيڻ جي هوشياري، ڪنهن کي چالاڪيءَ سان ڦاسائڻ يا مائل ڪرڻ، وقت خوشگوار نموني گذارڻ

englishMeaning: Deliberate and intentional, especially in doing something wrong. Stubbornly determined to have one’s own way. Refusing to listen to advice or instruction. Done knowingly with full awareness of consequences.

antonyms: Accidental, Unintentional, Obedient, Compliant, Docile, Involuntary
examples: The court called it a wilful violation of the law. He is a wilful child who never listens to his parents. Her wilful neglect of duty led to dismissal. The damage was found to be wilful rather than accidental.
sindhiMeaning: ڄاڻي واڻي ڪيل، خاص ڪري ڪا غلطي، ضدي ۽ پنهنجي مرضي هلائيندڙ، نصيحت نه ٻڌندڙ، پوري ڄاڻ سان ڪيل عمل

englishMeaning: Ready and happy to do something without objection. Prepared to agree or cooperate readily. Done or given by choice rather than by force. Showing eagerness to help or take part.

antonyms: Unwilling, Reluctant, Hesitant, Averse, Opposed, Disinclined
examples: She is always willing to help her classmates. He was willing to accept the new terms of the contract. They gave their willing support to the campaign. Are you willing to work on Sunday?
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن ڪم لاءِ تيار ۽ راضي، بغير اعتراض جي مدد ڪرڻ وارو، پنهنجي مرضيءَ سان ڪيل، شوق سان حصو وٺندڙ
urduMeaning: کسی کام کے لیے تیار اور راضی، بغیر اعتراض مدد کرنے والا، اپنی مرضی سے کیا گیا، شوق سے حصہ لینے والا

word: With one’s tongue in one’s cheek
englishMeaning: In a way that is not meant to be taken seriously. Speaking with humorous or ironic insincerity. Saying something jokingly while appearing serious.

antonyms: Seriously, Sincerely, Earnestly, Genuinely, In earnest
examples: He praised the plan with his tongue in his cheek. Her compliment was clearly made with tongue in cheek. The article was written with tongue in cheek and should not be taken literally. He said it with his tongue in his cheek, and everyone laughed.

synonyms: On the verge of, Close to, Nearly, Almost, A hair's breadth from
antonyms: Far from, Nowhere near, Distant from, Well short of
examples: They came within a whisker of winning the title. The car passed within a whisker of the wall. She was within a whisker of breaking the record. We were within a whisker of missing the flight.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ کي حاصل ڪرڻ يا ٿيڻ کان تمام ٿورو پري, تمام ننڍي فرق سان

sindhiMeaning: بي خيالي ۾ خيالي پلاءُ پچائڻ، ڌيان ڀٽڪڻ يا خيالن ۾ گم ٿي وڃڻ، اجايو ۽ بي مقصد سوچ ويچار، حقيقت کان پري خيالي سوچ، پنهنجي ماحول کان بي خبر ٿي سوچن ۾ گم رهڻ

englishMeaning: To work extremely hard and for long hours. To labour continuously with great effort and little rest. To exhaust oneself through heavy or tiring work. To toil constantly in order to achieve something.

antonyms: Idle, Loaf, Laze, Relax, Slack off, Rest
examples: He works like a dog to support his large family. During harvest season the farmers work like dogs. She worked like a dog to finish the project on time. They worked like dogs all summer to build the house.

antonyms: Wilderness, Sanctuary, Empty place, Quiet room, Natural habitat

englishMeaning: Using more words than are necessary to express a meaning. Containing redundant repetition of an idea. Relating to unnecessary wordiness in speech or writing. Marked by superfluous expressions.
synonyms: Redundant, Wordy, Verbose, Repetitive, Tautological, Prolix
antonyms: Concise, Brief, Succinct, Terse, Economical, Pithy
examples: The phrase free gift is pleonastic. Editors removed the pleonastic phrases from the draft. His pleonastic style tires the reader. Avoid pleonastic expressions in formal reports.
sindhiMeaning: ضرورت کان وڌيڪ لفظ استعمال ڪندڙ، اجائي ورجاءُ وارو، لفظي ڀرتيءَ وارو، غير ضروري ڊگهو انداز
urduMeaning: ضرورت سے زیادہ الفاظ استعمال کرنے والا، بے جا تکرار والا، لفظی بھرتی سے بھرپور، غیر ضروری طوالت والا

englishMeaning: A space completely filled with matter, as opposed to a vacuum. A meeting attended by all members of a body. An enclosed chamber holding air at higher pressure in a ventilation system. A full assembly or gathering.
synonyms: Full assembly, General meeting, Fullness, Full session, Air chamber
antonyms: Vacuum, Void, Emptiness, Subcommittee, Partial meeting
examples: The party held a plenum to approve the new policy. Physicists once argued that space was a plenum. Cool air is pushed through the ceiling plenum. All delegates attended the annual plenum.
sindhiMeaning: مڪمل ڀريل جڳهه (خلا جي ابتڙ)، سڀني ميمبرن جو گڏيل اجلاس، هوا واري نظام ۾ دٻاءُ وارو خانو، مڪمل اجتماع
urduMeaning: مکمل بھرا ہوا مقام (خلا کے برعکس)، تمام ارکان کا مشترکہ اجلاس، ہوا کے نظام میں دباؤ والا خانہ، مکمل اجتماع

englishMeaning: The use of more words than needed to convey a meaning. A redundant phrase such as burning fire. A figure of speech involving deliberate repetition for emphasis. Unnecessary wordiness in expression.
synonyms: Redundancy, Tautology, Verbosity, Wordiness, Repetition, Prolixity
antonyms: Conciseness, Brevity, Succinctness, Economy of words, Terseness
examples: The expression I saw it with my own eyes is a pleonasm. Teachers warn students against pleonasm in essays. Poets sometimes use pleonasm for emphasis. His report was spoiled by constant pleonasm.
sindhiMeaning: اجائي لفظن جو استعمال، غير ضروري ورجاءُ وارو جملو، زور ڏيڻ لاءِ ڄاڻي واڻي ڪيل ورجاءُ، لفظي ڀرتي
urduMeaning: غیر ضروری الفاظ کا استعمال، بے جا تکرار والا جملہ، زور دینے کے لیے جان بوجھ کر کی گئی تکرار، لفظی بھرتی

englishMeaning: A repeated or extra performance given after the main show. A demand by an audience for more, usually by shouting. To call for or perform an additional piece. Used as an exclamation meaning perform it again.
synonyms: Repeat performance, Curtain call, Extra number, Reprise, Again
antonyms: Finale, Conclusion, End, Exit, Silence, Booing
examples: The band played two songs as an encore. The audience shouted encore at the end of the concert. She was encored three times that evening. His piano encore delighted the whole hall.
sindhiMeaning: پروگرام کان پوءِ ٻيهر يا اضافي پرفارمنس، سامعين پاران وڌيڪ جي فرمائش، ٻيهر پيش ڪرڻ، ٻيهر ٻيهر چوڻ
urduMeaning: پروگرام کے بعد دوبارہ یا اضافی پرفارمنس، سامعین کی جانب سے مزید کی فرمائش، دوبارہ پیش کرنا، ایک بار پھر کہنا

englishMeaning: An instrument that shows direction using a magnetic needle. A tool with two hinged legs used for drawing circles. The range or scope of something such as knowledge or activity. To encircle, surround or achieve something.
synonyms: Direction finder, Magnetic needle, Dividers, Scope, Range, Extent, Encircle
antonyms: Aimlessness, Disorientation, Limitlessness, Release, Free, Uncover
examples: The hikers used a compass to find their way. Draw the circle with a compass and ruler. That subject lies beyond the compass of this book. High walls compass the old garden.
sindhiMeaning: ڏس ڏيکاريندڙ اوزار (قطب نما)، دائرا ٺاهڻ وارو پرڪار، ڪنهن شيءِ جو دائرو يا حد، گهيرو ڪرڻ يا حاصل ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: سمت بتانے والا آلہ (قطب نما)، دائرے بنانے والا پرکار، کسی چیز کا دائرہ یا حدود، گھیرنا یا حاصل کرنا

word: It takes one to know one
englishMeaning: A person who recognizes a particular bad quality in someone else often has that quality themselves. The expression is usually used as a humorous or defensive reply to an insult.
synonyms: Pot calling the kettle black, Hypocrite, Self-accusation, Tit for tat
antonyms: Fair-mindedness, Self-awareness, Innocence
examples: “You are being selfish.” “It takes one to know one,” she replied with a smile. He called me a gossip, but it takes one to know one. The phrase “it takes one to know one” turned the insult into a joke. When the critic accused others of laziness, someone whispered, “It takes one to know one.”
sindhiMeaning: جيڪو عيب ڪنهن ۾ سڃاڻي ٿو، اهو عيب پاڻ ۾ به هوندو آهي، طعني جو مزاحيه جواب
urduMeaning: جس شخص میں کوئی عیب پہچاننے کی صلاحیت ہو، اکثر وہ عیب خود اس میں بھی ہوتا ہے، طعنے کا مزاحیہ جواب

word: There is no smoke without fire
englishMeaning: A rumor or sign of trouble may have some truth behind it. Suspicious reports should not always be dismissed without investigation.
synonyms: Where there is smoke, there is fire, Rumor, Suspicion, Sign, Evidence
antonyms: Baselessness, Certainty of innocence, Clear evidence of no wrongdoing
examples: People say there is no smoke without fire, so the manager investigated the complaint. Although the rumor may be exaggerated, there is no smoke without fire. Her sudden resignation made colleagues wonder whether there was no smoke without fire. The police took the allegation seriously because there is no smoke without fire.
sindhiMeaning: دونهين کان سواءِ دونهون نٿو نڪري، افواهه پٺيان ڪا نه ڪا حقيقت هوندي آهي
urduMeaning: دھوئیں کے بغیر آگ نہیں ہوتی، افواہ کے پیچھے کچھ نہ کچھ حقیقت ہو سکتی ہے

englishMeaning: Formerly. Once. At an earlier time, usually in literary or old-fashioned language.
synonyms: Formerly, Once, Previously, In the past, Erewhile
antonyms: Now, Currently, Hereafter, In the future
examples: Whilom, the village stood beside a much smaller river. The whilom champion now coaches young athletes. This was whilom a busy market, but it is quiet today. In the poem, the knight recalls his whilom glory.
sindhiMeaning: اڳ ۾، ڪنهن وقت، اڳوڻو
urduMeaning: پہلے، کبھی، کسی زمانے میں

englishMeaning: To be completely expected. To cause no surprise because the facts or circumstances already suggested it.
synonyms: Be expected, Be predictable, Be unsurprising, Be anticipated
antonyms: Be shocking, Be unexpected, Take by surprise, Astonish
examples: Her promotion came as no surprise because she had worked hard for years. It came as no surprise when the team won the final. The delay came as no surprise after the heavy snowfall. His decision to resign came as no surprise to his closest colleagues.
sindhiMeaning: ڪا به حيرت نه ٿيڻ، اڳواٽ متوقع هجڻ
urduMeaning: حیرت کی بات نہ ہونا، پہلے سے متوقع ہونا

englishMeaning: In a straight line between two places, without following roads or natural obstacles. Used to describe the shortest geographical distance.
synonyms: In a straight line, Directly, By the shortest route, Geographically
antonyms: By road, Indirectly, Along the winding route, With detours
examples: The village is only five miles away as the crow flies. As the crow flies, the airport is close, but the road takes much longer. The two towns are ten kilometers apart as the crow flies. Our houses are near each other as the crow flies, although a hill lies between them.
sindhiMeaning: سڌي ليڪ ۾ فاصلو، رستن جي پرواهه کان سواءِ سڌو فاصلو
urduMeaning: سیدھی لکیر میں فاصلہ، سڑکوں یا رکاوٹوں کو نظرانداز کرتے ہوئے کم ترین فاصلہ

englishMeaning: A period of two weeks. Fourteen consecutive days.
synonyms: Two weeks, Fourteen days, Two-week period
antonyms: Instant, Moment, Eternity, Long period
examples: The course lasts a fortnight. We will return in a fortnight. She spent a fortnight visiting relatives in the countryside. The notice must be submitted within a fortnight.
sindhiMeaning: ٻه هفتا، چوڏهن ڏينهن
urduMeaning: دو ہفتے، چودہ دن

englishMeaning: Easily affected, influenced, harmed, or infected by something. Open to a particular influence or impression.
synonyms: Vulnerable, Prone, Liable, Sensitive, Receptive, Impressionable
antonyms: Resistant, Immune, Protected, Insensitive, Unaffected
examples: Young plants are susceptible to frost. He is susceptible to persuasive advertising. People with weak immune systems may be susceptible to infection. The old bridge is susceptible to damage during storms.
sindhiMeaning: جلدي متاثر ٿيندڙ، آساني سان بيماري لڳندڙ، اثر قبول ڪندڙ
urduMeaning: جلد متاثر ہونے والا، آسانی سے بیماری لگنے والا، اثر قبول کرنے والا

englishMeaning: Having the power or function of causing something. Relating to the cause of an event or condition. In grammar, a form that shows one person makes another person do something.
synonyms: Causal, Causing, Productive, Responsible, Determinative
antonyms: Noncausal, Preventive, Resulting, Incidental
examples: Scientists searched for the causative factor behind the disease. The report identified smoking as a causative agent. “Have” can be used in a causative construction. The doctor explained the causative link between the exposure and the illness.
sindhiMeaning: سبب بڻجندڙ، ڪنهن نتيجي جو ڪارڻ، گرامر ۾ ڪنهن کان ڪم ڪرائڻ وارو

englishMeaning: Excessive and immoral indulgence in sensual pleasures. Wild behavior involving heavy drinking, sexual excess, or other moral wrongdoing.
synonyms: Dissipation, Vice, Immorality, Excess, Licentiousness, Profligacy
antonyms: Temperance, Morality, Moderation, Discipline, Self-control
examples: The novel describes a life of wealth and debauchery. The ruler’s debauchery angered the poor citizens. They rejected the party culture of drinking and debauchery. Years of debauchery damaged his health and reputation.
sindhiMeaning: بدڪاري، عياشي، حد کان وڌيل اخلاقي بي راهه روي
urduMeaning: بدکاری، عیش پرستی، اخلاقی بے راہ روی اور عیش و عشرت میں حد سے بڑھ جانا

englishMeaning: Intentionally. Deliberately. With a specific aim or plan rather than by accident.
synonyms: Intentionally, Deliberately, Knowingly, On purpose, By design
antonyms: Accidentally, Unintentionally, Inadvertently, Accidentally
examples: She purposely arrived early to get a good seat. He purposely left the door open for the dog. The editor purposely used simple language. I did not break the vase purposely.

urduMeaning: جان بوجھ کر، ارادتاً، کسی مقصد کے ساتھ

englishMeaning: The reason for which something exists or is done. A desired result or aim. A person’s sense of determination or resolve. To intend or design something for a particular use.
synonyms: Aim, Goal, Objective, Intention, Reason, Function, Resolve
antonyms: Meaninglessness, Aimlessness, Pointlessness, Accident, Disinterest
examples: The purpose of this meeting is to solve the problem. She found a clear purpose in helping children. The tool was designed for a specific purpose. He purposefully set aside money for his education.

urduMeaning: مقصد، ارادہ، وجہ، عزم، کسی کام کے لیے مقرر کرنا

englishMeaning: In a deliberate and intentional manner. In a way that shows clear purpose, determination, or meaning.
synonyms: Deliberately, Intentionally, Determinedly, Meaningfully, With purpose
antonyms: Accidentally, Aimlessly, Randomly, Hesitantly, Unintentionally
examples: She walked purposefully toward the stage. The designer purposefully left space around the image. He spoke purposefully so that everyone understood the message. The team purposefully focused on the most urgent task.

urduMeaning: جان بوجھ کر، مقصد کے ساتھ، عزم اور ارادے سے

englishMeaning: Unhealthy or harmful to health. Not clean, safe, or suitable for living or working.
synonyms: Unhealthy, Unsanitary, Harmful, Unwholesome, Noxious
antonyms: Salubrious, Healthy, Sanitary, Wholesome, Beneficial
examples: The workers lived in insalubrious conditions. Experts warned that the insalubrious air could cause illness. The abandoned building was damp and insalubrious. They moved away from the insalubrious neighborhood.
sindhiMeaning: غير صحتمند، صحت لاءِ نقصانڪار، گندو يا غير محفوظ
urduMeaning: غیر صحت مند، صحت کے لیے نقصان دہ، گندا یا غیر محفوظ

englishMeaning: Impossible to defend or explain as reasonable, fair, or acceptable. Not supported by a valid reason.
synonyms: Indefensible, Unreasonable, Inexcusable, Unwarranted, Unacceptable
antonyms: Justifiable, Defensible, Reasonable, Excusable, Warranted
examples: The violence was cruel and unjustifiable. The company called the price increase unjustifiable. His absence without notice was unjustifiable. There is no unjustifiable reason for treating staff unfairly.

englishMeaning: Able to be defended or explained as reasonable, fair, or acceptable. Supported by a valid reason or evidence.
synonyms: Defensible, Reasonable, Valid, Warranted, Excusable, Legitimate
antonyms: Unjustifiable, Indefensible, Unreasonable, Unwarranted, Illegitimate
examples: The decision was justifiable under the circumstances. Her anger was justifiable after the unfair accusation. The expense is justifiable because it improved safety. The officer gave a justifiable explanation for the delay.

synonyms: Lump, Piece, Block, Portion, Segment, Cut
antonyms: Whole, Particles, Shred, Atomize, Unite
examples: He ate a chunk of bread with the soup. A large chunk of the budget went to repairs. Cut the vegetables into small chunks. The rock broke into a chunk of stone.
sindhiMeaning: وڏو ٽڪرو، ڳنڍ، وڏي مقدار جو حصو، ٽڪرن ۾ ڪٽڻ

englishMeaning: To purify or separate a liquid by heating it and then cooling the vapor. To extract the essential meaning or qualities of something. British spelling of distill.
synonyms: Purify, Refine, Extract, Concentrate, Summarize, Condense
antonyms: Contaminate, Dilute, Complicate, Expand, Mix
examples: The plant distils fresh water from seawater. The report distils years of research into a clear summary. Lavender oil is distilled from the flowers. Good teaching distils complex ideas into simple examples.
sindhiMeaning: ٻاڦ ذريعي صاف يا جدا ڪرڻ، خلاصو ڪڍڻ، نچوڙ حاصل ڪرڻ

synonyms: Purify, Refine, Extract, Concentrate, Summarize, Condense
antonyms: Contaminate, Dilute, Complicate, Expand, Mix
examples: The laboratory distills alcohol for the experiment. She distilled the main argument into one sentence. The machine distills polluted water. The teacher distilled the lesson into three key points.
sindhiMeaning: ٻاڦ ذريعي صاف يا جدا ڪرڻ، نچوڙ يا خلاصو ڪڍڻ

englishMeaning: Swollen, enlarged, or stretched because of pressure, gas, fluid, or internal expansion. Extended beyond the normal size or shape.
synonyms: Swollen, Bloated, Expanded, Enlarged, Stretched
antonyms: Collapsed, Shrunken, Deflated, Contracted, Compressed
examples: His distended stomach hurt after the meal. The balloon was distended with air. The patient had a distended abdomen. The distended river threatened to overflow its banks.

urduMeaning: پھولا ہوا، سوجا ہوا، دباؤ یا گیس کی وجہ سے معمول سے بڑا

englishMeaning: A liquid obtained by distillation. A purified or concentrated product produced from a mixture.
synonyms: Extract, Condensate, Purified liquid, Concentrate, Product
antonyms: Residue, Waste, Impurity, Mixture, Diluent
examples: The distillate was collected in a clean glass flask. The chemist tested the distillate for impurities. The plant produces a fragrant distillate from rose petals. This distillate is more concentrated than the original mixture.

englishMeaning: The process of purifying or separating liquids by heating, vaporizing, and condensing them. The extraction of an essential or concentrated part of something.
synonyms: Purification, Separation, Refining, Extraction, Condensation
antonyms: Mixing, Contamination, Dilution, Combination, Impurity
examples: Distillation is used to separate alcohol from water. The laboratory demonstrated the process of fractional distillation. Oil distillation produces several useful fuels. The article is a careful distillation of the author’s ideas.

englishMeaning: A formal evening suit, usually black or dark, worn with a dress shirt and bow tie. Formal clothing for men, especially at weddings or ceremonies.
synonyms: Dinner jacket, Formal suit, Evening suit, Black tie attire
antonyms: Casual wear, Sportswear, Informal clothing, Everyday clothes

sindhiMeaning: رسمي شام وارو سوٽ، ڪارو تقريب وارو لباس
urduMeaning: رسمی شام کا سوٹ، عموماً سیاہ تقریب یا شادی کا لباس

englishMeaning: Voluntarily. On one’s own initiative, without being asked or forced. A Latin legal phrase meaning that a court or authority acts on its own motion.
synonyms: Voluntarily, Spontaneously, On one’s own motion, Independently
antonyms: Under compulsion, Involuntarily, Under instruction, Coercively
examples: The judge raised the issue sua sponte. The committee acted sua sponte to protect the students. She sua sponte offered to organize the event. The court dismissed the case sua sponte after reviewing the record.
sindhiMeaning: پنهنجي مرضي سان، پاڻمرادو، بغير چوڻ جي
urduMeaning: اپنی مرضی سے، از خود، بغیر کہے یا مجبور کیے

englishMeaning: On its own initiative. Without a formal request from the parties, especially when a court or authority begins action independently. Often written suo motu.
synonyms: Suo motu, Sua sponte, Independently, On its own initiative
antonyms: On request, Under instruction, Compulsorily, In response to a petition
examples: The court took suo motu notice of the matter. The regulator opened an inquiry suo motu. The judge issued a suo motu order to protect the witness. The authority acted suo motu after seeing the public report.

englishMeaning: Relating to both social and economic conditions or factors. Connected with the way society and the economy influence one another.

antonyms: Non-economic, Purely social, Unrelated, Individual-only
examples: The study examined the socio-economic effects of unemployment. Education can improve a family’s socio-economic position. The policy targets socio-economic inequality. Researchers collected socio-economic data from rural households.

synonyms: Formal tie, Neck bow, Ribbon tie
antonyms: Open collar, Casual shirt, Untied neckwear
examples: He wore a red bow tie with his dinner jacket. The child learned how to tie a bow tie. Her bow tie matched her dress. A bow tie is traditional formal wear for some ceremonies.
sindhiMeaning: ڳچيءَ تي ٻڌڻ وارو ڪمان جهڙو ٽائي، رسمي ٽائي

englishMeaning: To bend the head or upper body as a sign of respect or greeting. To accept or submit to a demand, rule, or influence.
synonyms: Bend, Nod, Salute, Submit to, Yield to, Comply with
antonyms: Defy, Resist, Reject, Challenge, Oppose
examples: The performers bowed to the audience. He refused to bow to political pressure. She bowed to the king as a sign of respect. The company finally bowed to public demand.
sindhiMeaning: جهڪڻ، احترام ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ڳالهه کي مڃڻ يا آڻ مڃڻ

englishMeaning: To kneel or bend low in respect, worship, or submission. To accept someone’s authority or power completely.
synonyms: Kneel, Prostrate, Worship, Submit, Surrender, Yield

urduMeaning: جلد ہونے والا، قریب الوقوع، آنے والا

englishMeaning: To drive or strongly encourage someone to take action. To force or motivate something to move forward.
synonyms: Drive, Motivate, Urge, Compel, Prompt, Propel
antonyms: Deter, Discourage, Restrain, Hinder, Prevent
examples: A desire to help others impelled her to volunteer. The evidence impelled the police to investigate. His conscience impelled him to tell the truth. Rising costs impelled the company to change its strategy.
sindhiMeaning: اڀارڻ، مجبور يا مضبوط ترغيب ڏيڻ
urduMeaning: محرک بننا، کسی کو عمل پر آمادہ یا مجبور کرنا

englishMeaning: Equipment, baggage, or other things that make movement difficult. Burdens or obstacles that hinder progress.
synonyms: Baggage, Burden, Obstacle, Hindrance, Encumbrance, Luggage
antonyms: Aid, Assistance, Support, Advantage, Facilitation
examples: The hikers left unnecessary impedimenta behind. Heavy luggage became impedimenta during the climb. Bureaucracy can become impedimenta to innovation. She removed every piece of impedimenta from the narrow path.
sindhiMeaning: سامان يا بار جيڪو هلڻ ۾ رڪاوٽ بڻجي، رڪاوٽون
urduMeaning: ایسا سامان یا بوجھ جو حرکت مشکل بنائے، رکاوٹیں

englishMeaning: Impossible to pass through, enter, or see through. Impossible to understand or solve because it is extremely difficult or obscure.
synonyms: Unpierceable, Impassable, Inaccessible, Incomprehensible, Unreadable
antonyms: Penetrable, Accessible, Clear, Understandable, Permeable
examples: The fortress was protected by an impenetrable wall. Thick fog made the forest impenetrable to sight. His explanation was impenetrable to beginners. The security system is designed to be impenetrable.
sindhiMeaning: ناقابل دخول، جنهن مان لنگهي يا سمجهي نه سگهجي
urduMeaning: ناقابلِ نفوذ، جس میں داخل ہونا یا اسے سمجھنا بہت مشکل ہو

englishMeaning: The quality of being impossible to enter, pass through, see through, or understand. Resistance to penetration or explanation.
synonyms: Inaccessibility, Opacity, Incomprehensibility, Resistance, Solidity
antonyms: Accessibility, Clarity, Permeability, Openness, Transparency
examples: The impenetrability of the armor protected the vehicle. Readers complained about the impenetrability of the technical article. The forest’s impenetrability slowed the search. Researchers tested the material’s impenetrability to water.
sindhiMeaning: داخل نه ٿيڻ جي حالت، ناقابل فهمي، سخت مزاحمت
urduMeaning: داخل نہ ہونے یا سمجھ میں نہ آنے کی کیفیت، نفوذ کے خلاف مزاحمت

englishMeaning: In a way that cannot be entered, passed through, seen through, or understood. So obscurely or densely that understanding is difficult.
synonyms: Inaccessibly, Obscurely, Densely, Opaquely, Unintelligibly
antonyms: Clearly, Openly, Transparently, Understandably, Simply
examples: The author writes impenetrably about the theory. The cave was impenetrably dark. The hedge grew impenetrably thick. The legal document was written impenetrably for ordinary readers.
sindhiMeaning: ناقابل دخول يا ناقابل فهم نموني، ايترو پيچيده جو سمجهڻ ڏکيو هجي
urduMeaning: ایسے انداز میں جس میں داخل ہونا یا سمجھنا ممکن نہ ہو، انتہائی پیچیدگی سے

englishMeaning: Not feeling regret or remorse for wrongdoing. Unrepentant and unwilling to change one’s behavior.
synonyms: Unrepentant, Remorseless, Uncontrite, Defiant, Unapologetic
antonyms: Penitent, Repentant, Remorseful, Contrite, Apologetic
examples: The impenitent criminal showed no regret. He remained impenitent after hurting his colleague. Her impenitent attitude angered the victims. The judge noted that the offender was still impenitent.
sindhiMeaning: بي توبه، پشيمان نه ٿيندڙ، پنهنجي غلطي تي نادم نه
urduMeaning: بے توبہ، پشیمان نہ ہونے والا، اپنی غلطی پر نادم نہ ہونا

englishMeaning: Not complete, flawless, or entirely correct. Having faults, weaknesses, or defects. Not yet perfected.
synonyms: Flawed, Faulty, Incomplete, Defective, Limited
antonyms: Perfect, Flawless, Complete, Accurate, Ideal
examples: The plan is imperfect but workable. We live in an imperfect world. The vase has an imperfect shape. Her English is imperfect, but her meaning is clear.
sindhiMeaning: نامڪمل، عيب وارو، مڪمل نه
urduMeaning: نامکمل، عیب دار، بے نقص نہ ہونے والا

englishMeaning: A fault, defect, or weakness. The state of being incomplete or not perfect.
synonyms: Flaw, Defect, Fault, Blemish, Shortcoming, Limitation
antonyms: Perfection, Flawlessness, Excellence, Completeness, Virtue
examples: The small imperfection made the handmade bowl unique. Everyone has some imperfection. The inspector found an imperfection in the surface. The artist embraced the imperfection of natural materials.
sindhiMeaning: عيب، نقص، نامڪملي
urduMeaning: عیب، نقص، نامکمل ہونے کی حالت

englishMeaning: In a way that is too slight, gradual, or subtle to be noticed. Without being detected by the senses or attention.
synonyms: Unnoticeably, Imperceptibly, Gradually, Subtly, Barely
antonyms: Noticeably, Clearly, Suddenly, Markedly, Obviously
examples: The temperature rose imperceptibly during the afternoon. The colors changed imperceptibly from blue to green. His accent improved imperceptibly over the year. The boat moved imperceptibly away from the shore.
sindhiMeaning: اهڙي نموني جو محسوس نه ٿئي، آهستي ۽ لڪل نموني
urduMeaning: اس طرح کہ محسوس نہ ہو، نہایت معمولی یا بتدریج انداز میں

englishMeaning: Having a fault, defect, weakness, or mistake. Not perfect, reliable, or completely correct.
synonyms: Defective, Faulty, Imperfect, Unsound, Mistaken
antonyms: Flawless, Sound, Correct, Reliable, Perfect
examples: The report was based on flawed data. Their flawed plan failed under pressure. The argument is logical but flawed. The bridge design was flawed from the beginning.
sindhiMeaning: عيب وارو، نقص ٿيل، غلطين سان ڀريل
urduMeaning: عیب دار، نقص والا، غلطیوں سے بھرا ہوا

englishMeaning: Without any faults, defects, mistakes, or imperfections. Perfectly executed or exceptionally smooth.
synonyms: Perfect, Impeccable, Faultless, Excellent, Unblemished
antonyms: Flawed, Defective, Imperfect, Faulty, Damaged
examples: She gave a flawless performance. The jeweler displayed a flawless diamond. His explanation was clear and flawless. The team completed a flawless operation.
sindhiMeaning: بي عيب، مڪمل، ڪا غلطي نه رکندڙ
urduMeaning: بے عیب، مکمل، جس میں کوئی غلطی یا نقص نہ ہو

englishMeaning: In a perfect way, without mistakes or defects. With exceptional smoothness, accuracy, or skill.
synonyms: Perfectly, Impeccably, Faultlessly, Smoothly, Accurately
antonyms: Poorly, Faultily, Imperfectly, Clumsily, Incorrectly
examples: The choir performed flawlessly. She executed the plan flawlessly. The machine worked flawlessly throughout the test. He explained the process flawlessly to the new staff.
sindhiMeaning: بي عيبي سان، مڪمل نموني، بغير غلطي جي
urduMeaning: بے عیبی سے، مکمل طور پر، بغیر غلطی کے

englishMeaning: Having a pleasant and strong taste. Full of flavor and enjoyable to eat or drink.
synonyms: Flavorful, Tasty, Delicious, Savory, Appetizing
antonyms: Flavorless, Tasteless, Bland, Insipid, Unappetizing
examples: The chef prepared a flavoursome vegetable curry. This soup is light but very flavoursome. Fresh herbs make the dish more flavoursome. We enjoyed a flavoursome meal at the village restaurant.
sindhiMeaning: سواد وارو، ذائقي سان ڀرپور
urduMeaning: ذائقے دار، خوش ذائقہ، ذائقے سے بھرپور

englishMeaning: A substance added to food or drink to give it a particular taste or smell. The act of adding flavor.
synonyms: Flavor, Seasoning, Essence, Spice, Extract, Additive
antonyms: Plainness, Blandness, Neutrality, Unseasoned food
examples: Vanilla is a common flavouring in cakes. The manufacturer uses natural fruit flavouring. Add a little flavouring to the milk. The soup needs no extra flavouring.
sindhiMeaning: ذائقو ڏيڻ وارو مادو، کاڌي ۾ سواد شامل ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: ذائقہ دینے والا مادہ، کھانے یا مشروب میں ذائقہ شامل کرنا

englishMeaning: The particular taste of food or drink. A distinctive quality or atmosphere. To give something a particular taste or character.
synonyms: Taste, Savor, Essence, Character, Season, Infuse
antonyms: Tastelessness, Blandness, Neutrality, Dislike
examples: The soup has a rich flavour. I prefer the lemon flavour of this drink. The experience added a new flavour to the story. Herbs flavour the rice beautifully.
sindhiMeaning: ذائقو، سواد، خاص انداز يا ڪيفيت ڏيڻ
urduMeaning: ذائقہ، مزہ، خاص انداز یا کیفیت دینا

englishMeaning: Having little or no taste or distinctive quality. Bland and lacking flavor.
synonyms: Tasteless, Bland, Insipid, Unseasoned, Dull
antonyms: Flavorful, Tasty, Savory, Delicious, Distinctive
examples: The soup was watery and flavourless. The doctor recommended a flavourless diet for a few days. Without spices, the beans tasted flavourless. The critic called the speech dull and flavourless.
sindhiMeaning: بي ذائقو، سواد کان خالي
urduMeaning: بے ذائقہ، ذائقے سے خالی، پھیکا

englishMeaning: Having a rich, pleasant, or distinctive taste. Full of flavor and satisfying to eat or drink.
synonyms: Flavorful, Tasty, Delicious, Rich, Savory, Aromatic
antonyms: Flavorless, Bland, Tasteless, Insipid, Dull
examples: The flavourful sauce transformed the simple pasta. These tomatoes are ripe and flavourful. She cooked a flavourful stew with herbs and vegetables. The tea is strong, fragrant, and flavourful.
sindhiMeaning: ذائقي سان ڀرپور، سوادي، مزيدار
urduMeaning: ذائقے سے بھرپور، خوش ذائقہ، لذیذ

englishMeaning: A Latin phrase meaning "reduction to the absurd". A method of disproving a statement or argument by showing that it logically leads to a ridiculous or impossible conclusion. An argument form that demonstrates a proposition is false because its consequences are absurd.
synonyms: Reduction to the absurd, Proof by contradiction, Argumentum ad absurdum, Disproof by absurdity
antonyms: Direct proof, Affirmative argument, Constructive proof
examples: The lawyer used reductio ad absurdum to dismantle the witness's claim. By reductio ad absurdum, if everyone lied, no statement could ever be believed. The professor demonstrated the fallacy through reductio ad absurdum. Reductio ad absurdum is a powerful tool in mathematical proof.
sindhiMeaning: لاطيني جملو جنھجو مطلب آهي "بي معقوليت تائين گهٽائڻ"، ڪنھن بيان يا دليل کي غلط ثابت ڪرڻ جو طريقو جيڪو ڏيکاريندو ته اھو منطقي طور بي معقوليت يا ناممڪن نتيجي تائين پهچي ٿو، اھڙي استدلال جي صورت جيڪا ٿي ثابت ڪري ته خيال غلط آھي ڇاڪاڻ ته ان جا نتيجا بي معقول آھن
urduMeaning: لاطینی جملہ جس کا مطلب ہے "بے معقولیت تک گھٹانا"، کسی بیان یا دلیل کو غلط ثابت کرنے کا طریقہ جو دکھاتا ہے کہ یہ منطقی طور پر بے معقولیت یا ناممکن نتیجے تک پہنچتا ہے، ایسی استدلال کی صورت جو ثابت کرتی ہے کہ خیال غلط ہے کیونکہ اس کے نتائج بے معقول ہیں

englishMeaning: A direct vote in which all the eligible people of a country or region are asked to decide on a single political question. A general vote by the electorate on an important issue of public policy, such as a constitutional change. The process of putting a proposed law or decision to the public for approval or rejection. Any occasion on which people are given the chance to express their opinion on a particular matter. An informal test of public opinion about a person, policy, or government.
synonyms: Plebiscite, Public vote, Ballot, Poll, Popular vote, Vote, Election, Survey of opinion
antonyms: Appointment, Decree, Dictatorship, Imposition, Executive order, Autocracy
examples: The government held a referendum on the new constitution. Voters rejected the proposal in a national referendum. A referendum will decide whether the region becomes independent. Many people treated the local election as a referendum on the mayor's performance.
sindhiMeaning: عوامي راءِ شماري، ڪنهن اهم قومي يا آئيني مسئلي تي عوام جو سڌو ووٽ، ڪنهن تجويز يا قانون کي منظور يا رد ڪرڻ لاءِ ڪرايل ووٽنگ، ماڻهن جي راءِ معلوم ڪرڻ جو طريقو، ڪنهن حڪومت يا پاليسي بابت عوامي راءِ جو امتحان
urduMeaning: ریفرنڈم، رائے شماری، کسی اہم قومی یا آئینی مسئلے پر عوام کا براہِ راست ووٹ، کسی تجویز یا قانون کو منظور یا مسترد کرنے کے لیے کرائی جانے والی ووٹنگ، عوامی رائے معلوم کرنے کا طریقہ، کسی حکومت یا پالیسی کے بارے میں عوامی رائے کا امتحان

englishMeaning: To mention or speak about someone or something. To direct someone or something to another person, place, or authority for help, information, or a decision. To look at a book, note, or source in order to get information. To describe or relate to something in particular. To hand over a matter to an official body for consideration.
synonyms: Mention, Cite, Allude, Direct, Send, Consult, Point, Indicate, Relate, Submit
antonyms: Ignore, Overlook, Omit, Withhold, Conceal, Disregard, Suppress
examples: Please refer to page ten for the full details. The doctor decided to refer him to a specialist. She did not refer to the argument again. The committee will refer the matter to the board.
sindhiMeaning: ذڪر ڪرڻ يا حوالو ڏيڻ، ڪنهن ٻئي ڏانهن موڪلڻ يا رجوع ڪرائڻ، معلومات لاءِ ڪتاب يا نوٽ ڏسڻ، ڪنهن شيءِ سان تعلق رکڻ يا اشارو ڪرڻ، ڪو معاملو ڪنهن اختياريءَ واري اداري ڏانهن موڪلڻ
urduMeaning: ذکر کرنا، حوالہ دینا، کسی کو کسی دوسرے کے پاس بھیجنا یا رجوع کرانا، معلومات کے لیے کتاب یا نوٹ دیکھنا، کسی چیز سے تعلق رکھنا یا اشارہ کرنا، کوئی معاملہ کسی مجاز ادارے کو بھیجنا

englishMeaning: To speak about or write about someone or something briefly, without giving many details. To refer to a person, fact, or thing in passing. A short remark or statement about someone or something. A formal recognition or honourable reference given to someone for good work. To name someone in a list or record.
synonyms: Refer to, Cite, Note, Remark, State, Name, Allude to, Indicate, Reference, Acknowledge
antonyms: Omit, Ignore, Conceal, Hide, Suppress, Overlook, Withhold, Forget
examples: He did not mention the meeting to anyone. She made only a brief mention of the incident. Did I mention that we are moving next month? The soldier received an honourable mention for his bravery.
sindhiMeaning: مختصر ذڪر ڪرڻ، ٿورو ڳالهائڻ يا لکڻ، ڪنهن جو نالو کڻڻ، هلندي هلندي حوالو ڏيڻ، مختصر تذڪرو يا بيان، ڪنهن سٺي ڪم تي سرڪاري طور تي ساراهه يا اعتراف
urduMeaning: ذکر کرنا، مختصراً بیان کرنا یا لکھنا، کسی کا نام لینا، ضمناً حوالہ دینا، مختصر تذکرہ یا بیان، کسی اچھے کام پر باقاعدہ اعتراف یا ستائش

englishMeaning: To ask someone for advice, information, or an opinion before making a decision. To look at a book, map, watch, or record in order to get information. To discuss something with someone in order to reach a decision together. To work as an expert adviser for a company or organisation. To seek professional help, especially from a doctor or lawyer.
synonyms: Ask, Seek advice, Confer, Discuss, Refer to, Check, Advise, Deliberate, Talk over
antonyms: Ignore, Disregard, Decide alone, Dictate, Command, Neglect
examples: You should consult a doctor about that pain. Let me consult the map before we turn left. The management failed to consult the staff before the change. She consults for several technology companies.
sindhiMeaning: صلاح وٺڻ، مشورو ڪرڻ، ڪنهن ماهر کان راءِ گهرڻ، معلومات لاءِ ڪتاب نقشو يا رڪارڊ ڏسڻ، فيصلي لاءِ گڏجي بحث ڪرڻ، ڪنهن اداري کي ماهراڻي صلاح ڏيڻ، ڊاڪٽر يا وڪيل کان رجوع ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: مشورہ کرنا، صلاح لینا، کسی ماہر سے رائے طلب کرنا، معلومات کے لیے کتاب نقشہ یا ریکارڈ دیکھنا، فیصلے کے لیے مل کر بات چیت کرنا، کسی ادارے کو ماہرانہ مشورہ دینا، ڈاکٹر یا وکیل سے رجوع کرنا

englishMeaning: A curve that winds around a central point while moving continuously away from or towards it. Shaped like a coil or winding curve. To move in a continuous curve around a central point, especially while rising or falling. To increase or decrease rapidly and in an uncontrolled way. A continuous harmful rise or fall in prices, wages, or a situation.
synonyms: Coil, Helix, Whorl, Curl, Twist, Wind, Soar, Escalate, Snowball
antonyms: Straight line, Stabilise, Steady, Level off, Decline slowly, Straighten
examples: The smoke rose in a slow spiral above the fire. The staircase has a beautiful spiral design. Prices continued to spiral out of control. His health began to spiral downwards after the accident.
sindhiMeaning: چوٽيءَ وانگر ويڙهيل يا گول ڦرندڙ ليڪ، پيچدار يا ڪنڊل نما شڪل، مرڪز جي چوڌاري ڦرندي مٿي يا هيٺ وڃڻ، تيزيءَ سان بي قابو ٿي وڌڻ يا گهٽجڻ، قيمتن يا حالتن ۾ لاڳيتو خراب ٿيندڙ سلسلو
urduMeaning: مرغولہ، گول گھومتی ہوئی لکیر، پیچ دار یا کنڈلی نما شکل، مرکز کے گرد گھومتے ہوئے اوپر یا نیچے جانا، تیزی سے بے قابو ہو کر بڑھنا یا گھٹنا، قیمتوں یا حالات میں مسلسل بگاڑ کا سلسلہ

englishMeaning: To mention or speak about someone or something. To look at something such as a book, note, or website in order to get information. To describe or apply to a particular person or thing. To use a name or word for someone or something. To turn to a source or authority for guidance.
synonyms: Mention, Cite, Allude to, Consult, Look up, Speak of, Denote, Indicate, Concern
antonyms: Ignore, Overlook, Omit, Disregard, Avoid mentioning
examples: He referred to his notes during the presentation. The report refers to several recent studies. Who exactly are you referring to? This rule refers only to full-time employees.
sindhiMeaning: ذڪر ڪرڻ يا حوالو ڏيڻ، معلومات لاءِ ڪتاب نوٽ يا ويب سائيٽ ڏسڻ، ڪنهن خاص شخص يا شيءِ سان لاڳو ٿيڻ، ڪنهن لاءِ ڪو نالو يا لفظ استعمال ڪرڻ، رهنمائي لاءِ ڪنهن ماخذ ڏانهن رجوع ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: ذکر کرنا یا حوالہ دینا، معلومات کے لیے کتاب نوٹ یا ویب سائٹ دیکھنا، کسی خاص شخص یا چیز پر لاگو ہونا، کسی کے لیے کوئی نام یا لفظ استعمال کرنا، رہنمائی کے لیے کسی ماخذ سے رجوع کرنا

englishMeaning: To mention or look again at something that was said, written, or decided earlier. To send a matter back to a person or group for further discussion or a fresh decision. To relate to something that happened in the past. To check an earlier source again in order to confirm information.
synonyms: Return to, Revisit, Look back at, Recall, Send back, Review, Reconsider
antonyms: Move on, Skip, Forget, Ignore, Proceed, Finalise
examples: Let me refer back to the point I made earlier. The chairman referred the proposal back to the committee. She kept referring back to her childhood in the interview. Please refer back to chapter two for the definitions.
sindhiMeaning: اڳ ۾ چيل يا لکيل ڳالهه ڏانهن ٻيهر اشارو ڪرڻ، ٻيهر ڏسڻ يا حوالو ڏيڻ، ڪو معاملو ٻيهر غور لاءِ واپس موڪلڻ، ماضيءَ جي ڪنهن ڳالهه سان تعلق رکڻ، تصديق لاءِ اڳوڻي ماخذ ڏانهن موٽڻ
urduMeaning: پہلے کہی یا لکھی گئی بات کی طرف دوبارہ اشارہ کرنا، دوبارہ دیکھنا یا حوالہ دینا، کوئی معاملہ دوبارہ غور کے لیے واپس بھیجنا، ماضی کی کسی بات سے تعلق رکھنا، تصدیق کے لیے پہلے کے ماخذ کی طرف لوٹنا

englishMeaning: To call someone or something by a particular name, title, or description. To use a specific word or phrase when speaking about a person or thing. To describe someone or something in a certain way. To be commonly known by a certain name.
synonyms: Call, Name, Term, Label, Describe as, Style, Dub, Designate
antonyms: Misname, Leave unnamed, Ignore, Mislabel
examples: The students always referred to him as Sir. This period is often referred to as the golden age. She prefers to be referred to as a writer, not a poet. Locals refer to the building as the old mill.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي ڪنهن خاص نالي يا لقب سان سڏڻ، ڪنهن لاءِ خاص لفظ يا اصطلاح استعمال ڪرڻ، ڪنهن کي ڪنهن خاص انداز ۾ بيان ڪرڻ، عام طور تي ڪنهن نالي سان سڃاتو وڃڻ
urduMeaning: کسی کو کسی خاص نام یا لقب سے پکارنا، کسی کے لیے مخصوص لفظ یا اصطلاح استعمال کرنا، کسی کو کسی خاص انداز میں بیان کرنا، عام طور پر کسی نام سے جانا جانا

englishMeaning: To send a person to another individual or place for expert help, treatment, or advice. To direct someone to a source of information. To pass a person's case on to a specialist or higher authority. To recommend someone to another person or organisation.
synonyms: Send, Direct, Recommend, Pass on, Guide, Point, Transfer
antonyms: Keep, Retain, Handle personally, Withhold, Turn away
examples: My doctor referred me to a heart specialist. The teacher referred the student to the school counsellor. He referred us to the manual for further instructions. The agency referred her to a local employer.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن کي ماهراڻي مدد يا علاج لاءِ ٻئي ڏانهن موڪلڻ، ڪنهن کي معلومات جي ماخذ ڏانهن رهنمائي ڪرڻ، ڪنهن جو ڪيس ماهر يا مٿانهين اختياريءَ ڏانهن موڪلڻ، ڪنهن جي سفارش ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: کسی کو ماہرانہ مدد یا علاج کے لیے کسی دوسرے کے پاس بھیجنا، کسی کو معلومات کے ماخذ کی طرف رہنمائی کرنا، کسی کا معاملہ ماہر یا بالادست اتھارٹی کو بھیجنا، کسی کی سفارش کرنا

englishMeaning: To send a matter, case, or question to a person or body that has the authority to deal with it. To pass a decision on to a higher level for consideration. To submit an issue formally for judgement or discussion. To hand a problem over to an expert or official group.
synonyms: Submit, Hand over, Pass on, Send, Transfer, Assign, Delegate
antonyms: Settle, Decide, Resolve personally, Withhold, Retain
examples: The council referred the dispute to an independent panel. She referred the complaint to her supervisor. The case was referred to the high court. They referred the design question to the engineers.
sindhiMeaning: ڪو معاملو يا مسئلو اختيار رکندڙ شخص يا اداري ڏانهن موڪلڻ، فيصلي لاءِ مٿانهين سطح ڏانهن پيش ڪرڻ، ڪو سوال باقاعده غور لاءِ جمع ڪرائڻ، مسئلو ماهرن يا سرڪاري اداري حوالي ڪرڻ
urduMeaning: کوئی معاملہ یا مسئلہ بااختیار شخص یا ادارے کو بھیجنا، فیصلے کے لیے بالادست سطح پر پیش کرنا، کوئی سوال باقاعدہ غور کے لیے جمع کرانا، مسئلہ ماہرین یا سرکاری ادارے کے حوالے کرنا

englishMeaning: Happening at a lucky or very suitable time, as if arranged by God or fate. Fortunate and timely in a way that seems more than mere chance. Relating to divine care, guidance, or protection. Bringing unexpected help exactly when it is needed.
synonyms: Fortunate, Lucky, Timely, Opportune, Heaven-sent, Auspicious, Fortuitous, Blessed
antonyms: Unlucky, Unfortunate, Untimely, Disastrous, Ill-timed, Calamitous
examples: Their arrival was providential, as we had run out of water. A providential change in the weather saved the harvest. It was providential that a doctor was on the train. He called his escape providential rather than lucky.
sindhiMeaning: خوش قسمتيءَ وارو، خدا جي مهربانيءَ سان صحيح وقت تي ٿيندڙ، غيبي مدد وارو، اهڙو موقعو جيڪو اتفاق کان وڌيڪ لڳي، رباني رهنمائي يا حفاظت سان لاڳاپيل
urduMeaning: خوش قسمت، عین وقت پر ہونے والا، خدا کی مہربانی سے آنے والا، غیبی مدد سے متعلق، ایسا اتفاق جو محض اتفاق نہ لگے، ربانی رہنمائی یا حفاظت سے متعلق

englishMeaning: Unlucky and deserving of pity. Suffering repeated misfortune through no fault of one's own. Unfortunate in a way that often seems helpless or pitiful. Having bad luck in a situation one cannot control.
synonyms: Unlucky, Unfortunate, Ill-fated, Wretched, Luckless, Doomed, Pitiable, Miserable
antonyms: Lucky, Fortunate, Blessed, Successful, Prosperous, Favoured
examples: The hapless traveller lost his passport on the first day. A hapless goalkeeper watched the ball slip through his hands. She felt sorry for the hapless victims of the flood. The hapless team lost every match of the season.
sindhiMeaning: بدنصيب، بدقسمت، ترس جوڳو، مسلسل مصيبت ۾ ڦاٿل، لاچار ۽ بي وس شخص، بغير ڪنهن ڏوهه جي نقصان سهندڙ
urduMeaning: بدنصیب، بدقسمت، قابلِ رحم، مسلسل مصیبت میں گھرا ہوا، لاچار اور بے بس، بغیر کسی قصور کے نقصان اٹھانے والا

englishMeaning: Having a single set of unpaired chromosomes in a cell. Describing a cell or organism with half the usual number of chromosomes. A cell, such as a sperm or egg cell, that contains one set of chromosomes. Relating to the single chromosome condition found in gametes.
synonyms: Monoploid, Single-set, Gametic, One-chromosome-set
antonyms: Diploid, Polyploid, Triploid, Tetraploid
examples: Sperm and egg cells are haploid. The haploid number in humans is twenty-three. Fertilisation joins two haploid cells to form a diploid one. Many fungi spend most of their life cycle in a haploid state.
sindhiMeaning: هڪ سيٽ ڪروموزوم رکندڙ خليو، عام تعداد کان اڌ ڪروموزوم وارو، اهڙو خليو جهڙو نطفو يا انڊو، جنسي خليي جي هڪ هيري واري حالت سان لاڳاپيل
urduMeaning: ایک سیٹ کروموسوم رکھنے والا خلیہ، معمول سے نصف کروموسوم والا، ایسا خلیہ جیسے مادۂ تولید یا بیضہ، جنسی خلیوں کی یک لڑی حالت سے متعلق

englishMeaning: Having two complete sets of chromosomes, one from each parent. Describing a cell or organism with paired chromosomes. A cell that contains the full number of chromosomes typical of a species. Relating to the normal chromosome condition of most body cells.
synonyms: Double-set, Paired, Two-set, Somatic
antonyms: Haploid, Monoploid, Gametic, Polyploid
examples: Human body cells are diploid. A diploid cell contains forty-six chromosomes in humans. The zygote is diploid because it receives chromosomes from both parents. Most animals are diploid organisms.
sindhiMeaning: ٻه سيٽ ڪروموزوم رکندڙ خليو، ماءُ ۽ پيءُ کان هڪ هڪ سيٽ حاصل ڪندڙ، جوڙيدار ڪروموزوم وارو، جسم جي عام خلين واري حالت
urduMeaning: دو سیٹ کروموسوم رکھنے والا خلیہ، والدین میں سے ہر ایک سے ایک سیٹ حاصل کرنے والا، جوڑی دار کروموسوم والا، جسم کے عام خلیوں کی حالت سے متعلق

englishMeaning: An official document or certificate showing that a person has completed a course of study. A qualification awarded by a college, school, or training institution. A certificate given as evidence of success in an examination or programme. A course of study leading to such a certificate.
synonyms: Certificate, Qualification, Credential, Degree, Award, Testimonial, Parchment
antonyms: Failure, Disqualification, Rejection, Incompletion
examples: She received a diploma in graphic design last year. He hung his diploma on the office wall. The college offers a two-year diploma in nursing. A diploma is not the same as a full degree.
sindhiMeaning: سند، ڊپلوما، تعليمي سرٽيفڪيٽ، ڪنهن ڪورس مڪمل ڪرڻ جو سرڪاري ثبوت، ڪاليج يا اداري پاران ڏنل قابليت جو دستاويز، امتحان ۾ ڪاميابيءَ جو سرٽيفڪيٽ

englishMeaning: A very large plant-eating dinosaur with a long neck, a long whip-like tail, and four thick legs. A genus of huge sauropod dinosaurs that lived in the late Jurassic period. A fossil skeleton or model of such a dinosaur displayed in a museum.
synonyms: Sauropod, Dinosaur, Prehistoric reptile, Brontosaur, Long-necked dinosaur
antonyms: Mammal, Modern animal, Carnivore, Small reptile
examples: The museum displays a huge Diplodocus skeleton in its main hall. A Diplodocus could grow more than twenty-five metres long. Children gathered around the model of the Diplodocus. The Diplodocus used its long neck to reach low plants.
sindhiMeaning: هڪ تمام وڏو گاهه کائيندڙ ڊائناسور جنهن جي ڳچي ۽ پڇ ڊگها هوندا هئا، جراسڪ دور جو وشال سوروپوڊ ڊائناسور، عجائب گهر ۾ رکيل اهڙي ڊائناسور جو پڃرو يا نمونو

englishMeaning: A large extinct reptile that lived on the earth millions of years ago. Any member of the extinct group of reptiles that dominated the Mesozoic era. A person, idea, or thing that is very old-fashioned and no longer useful. Someone who refuses to accept modern methods or change.
synonyms: Prehistoric reptile, Saurian, Fossil, Relic, Antique, Old-timer, Has-been
antonyms: Modern creature, Innovator, Trendsetter, Progressive, Newcomer
examples: Dinosaurs disappeared from the earth millions of years ago. My son is fascinated by dinosaur bones. Some critics called the old machine an industrial dinosaur. He is a dinosaur who still refuses to use email.
sindhiMeaning: ڊائناسور، لکين سال اڳ رهندڙ وڏو ناپيد ٿي ويل ريڙهندڙ جانور، ميسوزوئڪ دور جي جانورن جو فرد، پراڻي سوچ وارو شخص يا شيءِ جيڪا هاڻ ڪم جي ناهي، تبديليءَ کي قبول نه ڪندڙ ماڻهو
urduMeaning: ڈائناسور، لاکھوں سال پہلے پایا جانے والا بہت بڑا معدوم رینگنے والا جانور، میسوزوئک دور کے جانوروں میں سے ایک، فرسودہ سوچ رکھنے والا شخص یا بے کار پرانی چیز، تبدیلی کو قبول نہ کرنے والا شخص

englishMeaning: Expressing blame, criticism, or disapproval of someone's behaviour. Showing gentle but clear disapproval. Scolding someone in a mild and often kindly way. Intended to correct a fault by pointing it out.

antonyms: Approving, Praising, Encouraging, Complimentary, Supportive, Admiring
examples: She gave him a reproving look across the table. His reproving tone made the children fall silent. The teacher wrote a short reproving note in the margin. He raised a reproving finger at the noisy students.

urduMeaning: ملامت کرنے والا، سرزنش آمیز، ناپسندیدگی ظاہر کرنے والا، نرمی سے ٹوکنے یا تنبیہ کرنے والا، غلطی بتا کر اصلاح کرنے والا

englishMeaning: In a way that shows blame, criticism, or disapproval. With a tone or expression that gently scolds someone. In a manner intended to correct another person's behaviour. Disapprovingly but usually without anger.

antonyms: Approvingly, Admiringly, Encouragingly, Warmly, Praisingly

urduMeaning: ملامت آمیز انداز میں، سرزنش کے ساتھ، ناپسندیدگی ظاہر کرتے ہوئے، نرمی سے ٹوکتے ہوئے، اصلاح کی نیت سے تنبیہ کرتے ہوئے

englishMeaning: A country that is governed by elected representatives and an elected leader rather than a king or queen. A state in which supreme power is held by the people through their chosen representatives. A form of government without a monarch, usually headed by a president. A group or community seen as having its own independent character.
synonyms: Democracy, Commonwealth, State, Nation, Federation, Free state, Polity
antonyms: Monarchy, Kingdom, Empire, Dictatorship, Autocracy, Tyranny

urduMeaning: جمہوریہ، ایسا ملک جہاں عوام کے منتخب نمائندے حکومت کرتے ہوں، بادشاہت سے آزاد ریاست، ایسا نظام جس کا سربراہ صدر ہو، عوامی اقتدار پر مبنی ریاست

englishMeaning: Relating to or supporting a republic as a form of government. A person who believes that a country should be a republic rather than a monarchy. Belonging to or supporting the Republican Party in the United States. A member or supporter of that political party.

antonyms: Monarchist, Royalist, Loyalist, Imperialist, Autocratic

sindhiMeaning: جمهوريت جو حامي، جمهوريه سان لاڳاپيل، بادشاهت جي بدران جمهوري نظام چاهيندڙ شخص، آمريڪا جي ريپبلڪن پارٽيءَ سان لاڳاپيل يا ان جو ميمبر
urduMeaning: جمہوریہ سے متعلق، جمہوری نظام کا حامی، بادشاہت کے بجائے جمہوریہ چاہنے والا شخص، امریکہ کی ریپبلکن پارٹی سے متعلق یا اس کا رکن

englishMeaning: The main meal of the day, eaten either in the middle of the day or in the evening. A formal evening meal held for guests or to mark a special occasion. The food that is served at such a meal. An organised social event centred on an evening meal.

englishMeaning: Relating to a diocese, the district under the care of a bishop. Belonging to or controlled by a diocese. A bishop who has charge of a diocese. Concerning the administration or affairs of a diocese.

englishMeaning: The plates, dishes, bowls, and other items used for serving and eating a meal. A matching set of crockery used at the dining table. Tableware intended especially for dinner. Household items used for presenting food at meals.
synonyms: Crockery, Tableware, China, Dishes, Plates, Servingware, Kitchenware
antonyms: Cutlery, Cookware, Utensils, Glassware

englishMeaning: By means of something, especially through great effort or persistence. As a result of a particular quality, action, or force. Because of the power or influence of something. Through the use of a particular method or means.

antonyms: In spite of, Despite, Without, Regardless of, By chance
examples: By dint of hard work, she finished the project on time. He succeeded by dint of sheer determination. The team won by dint of superior fitness. By dint of long practice, he became an excellent speaker.
sindhiMeaning: ڪنهن شيءِ جي ذريعي، خاص ڪري سخت محنت يا مسلسل ڪوشش سان، ڪنهن خوبي يا طاقت جي نتيجي ۾، ڪنهن خاص طريقي جي استعمال سان

englishMeaning: By continuing to do a particular action, usually with great effort. Through the process of repeatedly performing something. As a result of persistent activity or practice. By managing to do something over a period of time.
synonyms: By means of, Through, As a result of, Owing to, By virtue of, Thanks to
antonyms: Despite, In spite of, Without effort, By luck, Accidentally
examples: By dint of working late every night, he met the deadline. She learned the language by dint of listening to the radio daily. By dint of saving carefully, they bought their first home. He passed the exam by dint of studying every weekend.

englishMeaning: A small hollow mark or dent made in a surface by a blow or pressure. Force, effort, or means by which something is achieved, chiefly used in the phrase by dint of. To make a dent or hollow mark in something. A slight depression left after something has been pressed.
synonyms: Dent, Hollow, Depression, Mark, Indentation, Force, Means, Power

englishMeaning: Shaking or trembling, especially of the voice. Sounding unsteady and weak because of age, fear, or emotion. Not firm or steady in movement or tone.

antonyms: Steady, Firm, Strong, Confident, Stable, Assured

sindhiMeaning: لرزندڙ يا ڏڪندڙ خاص ڪري آواز، عمر  ڊپ يا جذبات سبب ڪمزور ۽ ٿڙڪندڙ لڳندڙ، غير مضبوط ۽ اڻ ٿلهو آواز يا حرڪت

englishMeaning: In a way that shows or causes a feeling of sickness in the stomach. In a manner marked by nausea or the urge to vomit. In an uneasy, uncomfortable, or slightly nervous way.
